title: Agentic Design Exploration: How LA28 and Autodesk
abstract: Agentic design exploration marks a new frontier in sustainable architecture, shaped through partnerships like Autodesk and LA28. In this real-world case study, you’ll see how the approach aligned design, cost, and climate goals. By combining domain expertise with AI workflows, the team addressed ambitious targets using agent-based tools across the project's site, building, and assembly scales—integrating codes, performance, and program needs. These workflows enabled rapid generation and refinement of design options, helping identify high-performing, buildable solutions earlier, reducing carbon and costs. You’ll compare where AI-driven workflows succeed, where they fall short, and how to apply them at scale.
speakers: Arthur Harsuvanakit, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: AU Merch Store
abstract:
Take AU Home With You.

Visit the all-new AU Merch Store for exclusive Autodesk apparel, premium swag, and limited-edition AU collectibles. Celebrate the ideas, innovations, and connections that brought us together and grab a piece of the experience before it's gone.

Designed for the builders, makers, innovators, and visionaries shaping tomorrow.

title: Accelerating Manufacturing Design: Unlocking the Top 10 Hidden Productivity Tools in AutoCAD Mechanical
abstract: Most manufacturing teams use AutoCAD daily but overlook the AutoCAD Mechanical toolset included in their subscription. This session will showcase 10 productivity features that cut repetitive drafting: intelligent commands with associative centerlines, automated hidden-line management, parametric content libraries, power dimensioning with tolerances, detail view automation, GD&T and welding symbols, integrated BOM with balloons, enterprise standards enforcement, built-in engineering calculators, and associative 2D documentation of Inventor 3D models. Through live demos and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain hands-on techniques to reduce cycle times, enforce ISO/ANSI compliance automatically, and bridge 2D-3D workflows using tools you already own.
speakers: Sridhar Subramani, Sr. Principal Product Owner, Autodesk

title: AEC Meets GIS: Autodesk Platform Services Viewer and Esri's MapLibre SDK for Construction and Asset Intelligence
abstract: Esri's MapLibre GL JS software development kit (SDK) brings ArcGIS power to open-source maps: feature layers, vector tiles, terrain, geocoding, spatial analysis, and routing. Now add the Autodesk Platform Services Viewer rendering intelligent models directly into that same canvas. It’s a match made in heaven for construction and asset management. This session will show how Esri and Autodesk are converging on MapLibre to deliver unified AEC-GIS experiences. Esri demonstrates their SDK's visualization and analysis—POIs, feature styling, elevation, and basemaps—while Autodesk fuses Revit models into the scene via shared WebGL rendering with synchronized cameras. Together, we build a complete construction-site intelligence view: geospatial context meets BIM precision, in about 300 lines of code.
speakers: George Owen, Product Engineer — Developer Experience team, Esri
Michael Beale, SWE, AWS

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma Build
abstract: From punch lists to submittals and RFIs, your tools must be jobsite-ready and drive project progress. Strong field execution and project management rely on connected, efficient workflows. Join the Autodesk Forma Project Management and Field Delivery teams for a deep dive into what’s new and what’s next for project management and field across Forma Build Essentials, Forma Build, and the Forma Mobile app. See how we’re designing core field and project management tools that help teams plan, execute, and close work on-site, in the trailer, and in the office. Learn how data flows between field and project workflows to improve visibility, accountability, and decisions. And see how your feedback is shaping the roadmap, including Autodesk AI.
speakers: Emilio Mercado, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Sagi Zeberger, Group Product Manager, Autodesk
David Kadyshewich, Group Product Manager, Autodesk
Courtney Wright, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Adam Arcus, Senior Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma Data Management
abstract: Connected project data is the foundation of Autodesk Forma. Join this roadmap session to see how Autodesk is advancing Autodesk Forma Data Management as the common data environment (CDE) that connects teams, workflows, and phases across the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) lifecycle. The product team will share the latest developments, what’s coming next, and the future direction of Forma Data Management.
speakers: Justin Lipsey, Senior Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk
Joan Allen, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk
Audrey Boguchwal, Senior Group Product Manager, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Forma - Cost Management + GCPay and Payapps
abstract: Construction teams need strong project financial controls to reduce risk and protect the bottom line. Join this session to learn how Autodesk is evolving cost management across Autodesk Forma Build, GCPay, and Payapps to deliver greater visibility, accuracy, and confidence. We’ll cover what’s new and what’s coming next across budget and change management, forecasting, and payment workflows. And we’ll explore how these solutions work together to create a more connected financial ecosystem. Get a behind-the-scenes look at our product strategy and key investments focused on helping teams manage costs more proactively, reduce financial risk, and improve project outcomes.
speakers: Cassie Bustos, Principal Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk
Mark Ballinger, Dir, Product Strategy, PayApps, Autodesk
Ian Turner, Group Product Manager, Autodesk
Evan Zachmann, Sr Product Strategy  Manager, GC Pay, Autodesk

title: Agentic AI for Next‑Generation AEC Workflows
abstract:
This session will be presented by Greg Schleusner, AIA, owner of 2611 Labs, former Principal Director of Design Technology at HOK, and Adjunct Assistant Professor at Columbia University.

Lightweight laptops with large, unified memory pools have crossed an important threshold: they can now run capable AI assistants locally. For AEC professionals, this creates something fundamentally different from a chatbot or copilot that waits for prompts and returns suggestions. A local assistant can remain connected to design tools, carry out multi-step assignments in the background, and even create new utilities when existing tools fall short—all without an internet connection or sending project data to the cloud.

This session will demonstrate the power of  such an assistant by combining state-of-the-art models, tool integrations, workflows, and agent harnesses into a practical working example of the power of one machine.  It will also examine the larger shift this makes possible: as models and inference software improve, the hardware you can buy today, becomes increasingly capable. We are only beginning to understand what becomes possible when every practitioner can have a private, persistent, and extensible AI collaborator working alongside them.
speakers: Ken Denton, Global Segment Lead AEC / PD&M, HP

title: Agentic AI in Action: How Autodesk and AWS Build Intelligent Agents for Design and Make
abstract: Autodesk and AWS are building agentic AI to design and construct at scale. Autodesk has deployed several AI agents—orchestrated through Autodesk Assistant, powered by Amazon Bedrock, and connected via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In this session, we’ll dive deeper into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: an agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating highly effective agents securely at scale using any framework and foundation model. Learn real-world patterns that combine MCP, AgentCore, and generative AI services for construction and manufacturing. Whether you're starting your AI journey or scaling intelligent systems, you’ll walk away with actionable insights and tools to accelerate innovation.
speakers: Zaiba Jamadar, Senior Solutions Architect, AWS
Anuj Butail, Principal Solutions Architect, AWS
Taha Topiwalla, Principal Account Manager, AWS

title: Agentic AI Running Project Workflows in Autodesk Forma with MCP
abstract: This session will explore how PEC is implementing agentic AI to run real project workflows within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). By using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a governed orchestration layer, AI agents can securely connect to Autodesk APIs, query live project data, perform QA/QC checks, and execute tasks across project systems. You’ll see how this architecture moves beyond automation into true workflow execution—enabling scalable, consistent, and intelligent project delivery. We’ll share real-world examples, implementation strategies, and lessons learned to help teams begin adopting AI-driven workflows today.
speakers: Farzad Towhidi, Senior Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Luis Salmeron, Senior Digital Systems Engineer, Professional Engineering Consultants (PEC)

title: Agents of Change: Mastering Agentic AI and MCP Workflows for the Multi-Discipline AEC Firm
abstract: The AEC industry is undergoing a paradigm shift where the lines between software developers, industry groups, and design firms are blurring. This session explores how AI strategies are being collaboratively shaped to move beyond basic research into high-impact implementation within multi-discipline engineering environments. We will examine the evolution of AI maturity, moving from foundational context engineering to the deployment of agentic services and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) that automate complex engineering tasks. Drawing on real examples, business leaders will gain a clear view of the emerging landscape and a practical way to balance AI’s potential against the demands of modern design practice.
speakers: Michael Gustafson, SVP of Strategic Growth, QNECT LLC
Andrew Sundal, Structural Engineer/Comp Design Specialist, HGA

title: AI Agents Meet APS: From Forma Building Design to Operational Digital Twin
abstract: Most digital twin projects stall at the same point: There’s no 3D model. Point cloud scanning takes weeks—too heavy for operational use cases like workplace booking or shop-floor monitoring. But we’ve found a faster path: Design buildings in Autodesk Forma Building Design, process them server-side via the Autodesk Platform Services Automation API for Revit, then use agentic AI workflows via Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enrich the model with workplaces and connected production data. It takes hours instead of months. Through video walk-throughs and live demos, we’ll show two use cases we’re deploying this year—replacing our own third-party desk-sharing tool, and building a manufacturing digital twin. You’ll leave with a replicable pattern for AI-enabled design-to-operate workflows.
speakers: Frank Otto, Product Owner - Platform, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH

title: AI and the Architect: Designing Human-AI Workflows That Preserve Authorship
abstract: When Stantec deployed AI agents on a 190,000-square-foot health care project, this question stopped being theoretical: Where does AI execution end and architect authorship begin? This session—co-presented by Stantec's senior BIM administrator and SWAPP's CEO—will walk through the actual decisions made on that project. We’ll look at which documentation tasks the AI was allowed to execute, which were held back for human review, and what happened when AI agents moved a fixture during an ADA compliance check. You’ll leave with a workflow categorization framework that separates judgment-dependent work from execution-dependent work, applied live to 20 common tasks, plus the standards-governance playbook used to keep firm authorship intact under AI execution.
speakers: Kari Schutte, Regional Digital Delivery Lead, US South, Stantec
Eitan Sarfati, CEO, SWAPP.AI

title: AI: A Practical Guide to Implementation and Risk Management
abstract: This talk will offer a clear, practical road map for using AI without sleepwalking into liability minefields. Drawing on real disputes, emerging case law, and live industry data, we’ll explain where AI can go wrong in design, delivery, and operations, and what this means for contracts, professional duties, and insurance. Using vivid, real-world examples of AI hallucinations, flawed outputs, and disputed responsibility, we’ll demystify what good practice looks like in reality. You’ll learn how to cut through AI hype, how to embed internal processes and procedures, and how to structure effective internal training and implement proportionate governance, assurance, and documentation that satisfy clients, regulators, and insurers while still enabling innovation.
speakers: May Winfield, Global Director of Legal + Digital Risks, Buro Happold

title: AI Assistants Connected by Claude MCP and GPT Agents Using Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Autodesk Platform Services Workflows
abstract: Autodesk Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) and Revit hold powerful data, yet teams still spend hours on model QA, quantity takeoffs, and reporting. In this two-presenter session, we build a practical AI assistant for Revit and Forma Data Management on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), driven from both Claude and GPT. A Revit add-in bridges natural language drives structured, deterministic tool calls instead of unreliable prompt-only behavior.
speakers: Manuel Meneses, Business Intelligence & Data Analytics, Independent
Enrique Meneses, BIM Administrator, Bayer

title: AI Changes the Cost Curve but Connected Data Changes Value Creation
abstract: AI is often discussed in terms of efficiency, but the bigger shift may be how connected data improves the quality, consistency, and usefulness of expert delivery. This session will share Norconsult’s perspective on how AI and connected data are beginning to influence decision support, delivery workflows, and client value across architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). We’ll explore why the impact goes beyond isolated productivity gains, where connected data makes AI more relevant in practice, and what leaders should consider as technology starts to affect how value is created in engineering and project delivery. The session will focus on practical implications and lessons emerging from real industry needs.
speakers: Knut Ramstad, CTO and Partner, Registered Architect, Nordic Office of Architecture
Marius Jablonskis, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult ASA

title: AI-Connected Workflows: Fusion, Claude, and MCP 101
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion, Claude, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) can work together to create smarter, more connected engineering workflows. This introductory session will explore how conversational AI can assist with design, automation, scripting, documentation, and workflow generation inside Fusion environments, while MCP enables secure connections between AI, tools, and data sources. Attendees will learn foundational concepts, practical integration examples, and real-world use cases that demonstrate how AI-driven workflows can improve productivity, collaboration, and decision-making across product development and manufacturing.
speakers: Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk

title: AI Data Check for Civil 3D: Validating Models Against Project Requirements via APS
abstract: This session will present a platform built through vibe coding using Autodesk Platform Services APIs, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and AI code generation to automate the full data validation cycle for Civil 3D models. The platform pulls files from Forma, extracts metadata via the Model Derivative API, and ingests project requirement PDFs. An AI layer converts PDFs into structured validation rules, then runs them against the model to produce a detailed conformity report, flagging gaps, mismatches, and missing attributes without manual checks. The session will also cover key lessons from development, AI-driven architecture, and real-world use cases showing practical impact at scale.
speakers: Mohamad M. KASSIR, Regional Digital Manager, Egis

title: AI Data Ready: From Design to Construction to Operations
abstract: Design and construction projects involve diverse tools and stakeholders across phases, creating fragmented, inconsistent data and documentation. This session will show how we establish an AI-ready data foundation from day one using the Autodesk Forma Assets module, enabling a continuous digital thread from design through construction to operations. We’ll demonstrate how standardized data from Revit models and equipment lists—aligned with CSI MasterFormat and UniFormat—connects design, procurement, project controls, commissioning, and operations. By treating models and metadata as lifecycle deliverables, we reuse and enrich data instead of recreating it—with Forma serving as the central platform for integrated, reliable, AI-ready project data.
speakers: Gilbert Kwan, BIM Business Process Owner, Amgen
Stacy Goins, Senior Manager, Engineering Projects, Amgen
Victor Strausbaugh, Engineering Projects Sr Mgr, Amgen

title: AI-Driven Digital Twins: Standardizing and Scaling Mission-Critical Infrastructure
abstract: The rapid growth of data centers is challenging traditional approaches to design and delivery. Project-by-project workflows are no longer scalable, leading to inefficiencies and inconsistent outcomes. This session will explore how AI-driven digital twins—developed through Autodesk Tandem software and enabled by collaborative workflows in Autodesk Forma—can support a scalable and repeatable approach to mission-critical infrastructure. You’ll learn how to connect early-stage planning, detailed design, and operations into a continuous data-driven process. And you’ll see how to replicate solutions across multiple sites while maintaining performance, quality, and speed.
speakers: Juliana Mizumoto, Head of Bid Management, Start Campus

title: AI for Ideation: Telling a good story with Generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services (APS)
abstract: Imagine this scenario: You’re a developer and a user identifies a problem that, when solved, could save hundreds of hours per project. Moreover, there doesn’t appear to be a solution on the market that solves this problem adequately, so you get to build something. In an industry where users are more likely to buy a story than a product, how do we tell a good story? This discussion will center around our approach to collaboratively translating ideas into prototypes. We’ll use generative AI and Autodesk Platform Services as our low-barrier-to-entry tools for the code, and demonstrate the value of building trust in the solution by building it together.
speakers: Andrell Laniewicz, East Region RBG Digital Delivery Lead, HDR
Zachary Smith, Autodesk Platform Developer, HDR

title: AI from Anywhere: Building Secure Hybrid AI Workflows for Autodesk Users
abstract:
AI is transforming design workflows, but many firms face the same challenge: how do you encourage innovation while maintaining data privacy, security, governance, and control of escalating cloud costs?
In this session, Lenovo explores how architects, engineers, and designers are building AI capability from the ground up using a hybrid approach that combines Autodesk cloud services, AI PCs powered by Intel Core Ultra processors, local AI inference, remote workstations, and centralized AI resources. Learn how organizations are creating safe environments for AI experimentation, enabling teams to test ideas using real project data, evaluate business value, and scale successful workflows with confidence.
Discover how firms are empowering users to innovate from anywhere while balancing performance, flexibility, security, and cost.
Key message: Experiment locally. Collaborate globally. Scale in the cloud.
speakers: Mark Hirst, World Wide Solutions Manager, Lenovo

title: AI-Powered Inventor: Design Faster, Work Smarter
abstract: In this session, discover how AI assistance is transforming Inventor workflows from concept to production. See how Autodesk Assistant uses natural language to analyze models, create model states, suppress components, generate parameters, and automate repetitive tasks—without leaving Inventor or writing code. Learn how AI works alongside Inventor software’s parametric, rules-based, simulation and documentation tools to accelerate design, improve manufacturability, and reduce errors in complex assemblies. Walk away with practical insights to boost productivity and design smarter, faster.
speakers: Maulik Patel, Sr. SW Eng. Test, Autodesk
Rena Andrews, Senior Software QA Engineer, Autodesk

title: AI-Ready AECO: A 90-Day Revit and Autodesk Forma Data Management Scorecard
abstract: Architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) firms want better automation, reporting, and AI outcomes. But inconsistent Revit parameters, unmanaged content, weak naming standards, and disconnected Autodesk Forma Data Management workflows often get in the way. This session will give BIM, virtual design and construction (VDC), and digital practice leaders a practical 90-day scorecard for identifying the data that matters most, scoring current-state readiness, and prioritizing what to fix first. You’ll see how to evaluate model health, content governance, metadata, coordination workflows, and handoff structure so you can build a realistic road map for stronger delivery, better collaboration, and future AI readiness.
speakers: Michael Echave, Design Revenue Manager, ATG

title: AI-Ready Workstations: Powering the Next Generation of Autodesk Workflows in AEC
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming the AEC space. Bringing new capabilities to Autodesk applications such as Revit, AutoCAD, Forma, Construction Cloud, and emerging AI-powered design and productivity tools. Realizing the full value of these innovations requires more than software—it demands modern, AI-capable hardware.

This session explores how workstation architecture, including high-performance CPUs, professional GPUs, dedicated AI accelerators, and optimized memory and storage configurations, enables faster design iteration, intelligent automation, real-time visualization, and enhanced collaboration. Attendees will learn how AI workloads are changing hardware requirements across BIM, CAD, visualization, simulation, and reality capture workflows, and how to future-proof their technology investments. Join us to discover why AI-ready workstations are becoming an essential foundation for the next generation of Autodesk-powered AEC projects.
speakers: Rob Jamieson, Senior ISV Manager-ADM, AMD
Stephanie Berger, ACS Technical Manager, HP

title: AI Without Chaos: AutoCAD and Revit Plug-In Development with Spec-Driven Development
abstract: AI coding tools are changing how software is developed in architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). Inconsistent outputs, lack of standards, and tight coupling to platform APIs often lead to fragile and unstable plug-ins. This class will introduce Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as a practical, tool-agnostic approach to bring structure and reliability to AI-assisted development. Instead of prompts and chat history, SDD uses persistent specifications as the source of truth. Using plug-ins in AutoCAD and Revit software, we’ll demonstrate how to separate business logic from platform-specific implementations. You’ll learn how SDD can use modern AI tools such as OpenAI Codex to transform AI from a source of chaos into a controlled software development asset.
speakers: Fernando Malard, Chief Technology Officer, ofcdesk, LLC

title: APS GraphQL in Production: AEC & MFG Patterns from Analytics to AI Agents
abstract: Autodesk's Data Model APIs for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) and manufacturing (MFG) use GraphQL—unlocking richer integrations and AI-powered workflows. But GraphQL differs from REST in ways that quietly break production systems. Our team has shipped analytics dashboards, workflow automation, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, letting AI agents query live design data. We've hit the pitfalls so you don't have to. This session will deliver production-proven patterns: query design for AEC/MFG data models, partial-success error handling, enterprise authentication, mutation patterns, and AI-agent enablement via MCP. We’ll also highlight the underused GraphQL capabilities in the User Profile API. Real examples. Real lessons. Patterns that work from day one.
speakers: Kevin Vandecar, Sr Mgr, Technology Consulting, Autodesk

title: Ask the Experts Panel: AI in AutoCAD and Civil 3D, From Today's Tools to Tomorrow's Workflows
abstract: Curious how AI is actually showing up in AutoCAD, AutoCAD Web, and Civil 3D, and where it's headed next? In this interactive "Ask the Experts" panel, our experts will go beyond the hype to talk about how AI is starting to change the way design work gets done. We'll explore where AI shows up in your workflows today, how Autodesk Assistant is evolving with Model Context Protocols (MCPs) to support faster, smarter decisions, and what's coming as AI becomes a more active partner in the design process across desktop and web. Expect a candid conversation about the opportunities, the open questions, and how you can start putting AI to work right now. The session is moderated, with plenty of time for audience questions, so come ready to ask.
speakers: Anum Mithani, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Alëna Iouguina, Director, User Experience, AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Reality Capture, Autodesk
Peter Qian, Sr Director, Software Engineering, Autodesk
Sachin Singh, Senior Product Manager, AutoCAD Web, Autodesk

title: A Smarter Asset Strategy for Data Center Delivery with Autodesk Forma
abstract: Data center lifecycle transition is a critical milestone where minor handover gaps can cause multimillion-dollar operational delays. In mission-critical delivery, establishing an institutional data-center asset strategy must begin well before closeout. This session will examine how Autodesk Forma serves as a strategic driver for rigorous data-center asset planning, complex systems architecture organization, and comprehensive operational readiness throughout design and construction. Executives and project leaders will gain a high-level framework to align cross-functional data-center teams, mitigate handover liabilities, and secure high-fidelity facility intelligence for day-one operational excellence.
speakers: Matthew Harraka, Technology Consultant, Forma, ARKANCE
Bobby Hinojosa, Technology Consultant, ARKANCE

title: AU Clubhouse
abstract:
Join the club.

 

What if networking felt more like collaborating than mingling? AU Clubhouse is an interactive networking experience where the AU community comes together through team-based games designed to spark conversation and collaboration.

 

Connect with architects, engineers, designers, manufacturers, and developers from across industries as you solve puzzles in Solvers Club, draw and decode in Decoders Club, or put your knowledge to the test in Trivia Club.

 

It’s networking reimagined for people who learn by doing, and do their best work together.

 

Drop in anytime - no sign-up required. Visit the AU Clubhouse Welcome Desk outside the Expo Hall to get started.

abstract:
Take AU Home With You.

Visit the all-new AU Merch Store for exclusive Autodesk apparel, premium swag, and limited-edition AU collectibles. Celebrate the ideas, innovations, and connections that brought us together and grab a piece of the experience before it's gone.

Designed for the builders, makers, innovators, and visionaries shaping tomorrow.

title: AU Newbies Meetup
abstract: Welcome to the AU Newbies Meetup—designed specifically for first-time AU attendees. This engaging event will offer a unique opportunity to connect with community members, industry experts, and elite professionals who’ll provide invaluable insights into how to maximize your AU experience. Discover tips and tricks to navigate the conference, delve into the vast array of sessions and workshops, and learn how to use the networking opportunities that AU presents. Immerse yourself in the vibrant AU community, share your aspirations, and get personalized guidance on making the most of AU. Join us to kick-start your AU journey with confidence and excitement!
speakers: Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore
Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk

title: AutoCAD Electrical Meets Vibe Coding: Building a Complex Dashboard Without DAX/M Expertise
abstract: Turn messy AutoCAD Electrical data into a working dashboard—without deep Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) or Power Query expertise. This session will reveal a real-world journey using “vibe coding”: iterative problem-solving with AI, trial and error, and constant refinement. From duplicate tags and broken relationships to the rebuilding of structure and debugging in loops, every step reflects practical challenges and breakthroughs. Learn how structured thinking, smart prompting, and persistence can transform chaotic engineering data into meaningful insights—without waiting to become an expert.
speakers: Shinu Mathew, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk

title: AutoCAD Plant 3D Custom Plug-ins Save Our Customers Hundreds of Engineering Hours
abstract: Engineering teams often spend hundreds of hours on repetitive manual tasks during CAD design that can lead to inefficiencies and errors. In this class, discover how Autodesk Consulting works closely with customers to understand their unique needs and develop custom AutoCAD Plant 3D plug-ins and scripts that automate complex workflows, improve data quality, and accelerate project execution. Learn how Plant 3D extensibility can deliver measurable productivity gains in areas such as report generation, instrument patterns, P&ID and PFD management, custom data queries, instrument loops, pipeline management, and recovery of legacy drawings.
speakers: Nuria Martinez, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: AutoCAD Tips, Tricks, and the Most-Human Drafting Techniques
abstract: You keep asking your assistant to act like an Autodesk Expert Elite member specializing in AutoCAD software, but your artificially intelligent relationship with it remains … complicated. Because somewhere between the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the suspiciously effective large language model (LLM) that completes your sentences, your drawings still need a human. In this ninth installment of AU's top-rated AutoCAD Tips session, Autodesk Expert Elite Member Donnie "The CAD Geek" Gladfelter will deliver the most-human drafting techniques backed by the intelligence of AutoCAD 2027, including Geometry Cleanup, Smart Blocks, and Checkout that ends read-only standoffs. Plus, you’ll get deep cuts no chatbot can replicate. That's why yours flagged this session for excessive human productivity and hoped you'd never find it.
speakers: Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek

title: Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, Maya, and Flame: Building a Natural-Language AI-Driven VFX Pipeline
abstract: Fragmented VFX pipelines rely on manual asset handoffs, inconsistent data, and disconnected tools across tracking, digital content creation (DCC), and finishing. This session will demonstrate a connected workflow linking Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, Maya, and Flame software through a natural language-driven orchestration layer. Asset ideas defined by text or images are transformed into timely prototypes for rapid iteration, automatically loaded into Maya, published to Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, and rendered to Flame for downstream work. The session will break down architecture, data flow, and automation patterns, including safeguards for reliability. You’ll learn how to apply these patterns incrementally. A documented implementation supports exploration and reuse.
speakers: Abraham Borbujo, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
Fernando Novo Paz, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Forma R&D Meetup
abstract: Are you an administrator, manager, or user of Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)? Join the Autodesk Forma R&D Meetup! You’ll dive into candid conversations, share real-world experiences, and explore forward-thinking ideas that are shaping the future of construction technology—whether that involves Forma Data Management, Forma Build, Forma Design Collaboration, the Cost Management tool, or others. This meetup is designed for attendees to share insights as well as discuss best practices and exchange strategies for all things Autodesk Forma. Don’t miss this opportunity to learn, grow, and connect with a supportive community of industry and design professionals.
speakers: Cary Mandell, Principal Customer Advocate, Autodesk
Pete GilMurray, Sales Specialist, Enterprise Emerging Solutions, Autodesk
Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Forma Site Design for Infrastructure: Rapid Context and Site Setup
abstract: Autodesk Forma Site Design allows infrastructure professionals to take the lead in project setup by providing a high-fidelity data environment from the very beginning. This session will demonstrate how to jump-start projects by using open-source terrain, roadway, and property data to create a reliable conceptual foundation. We’ll explore how to define critical site zoning constraints—including property offsets and building height limits—to provide clear parameters for the building design team.  You will also learn how to apply preliminary grading design and add GIS data from the ArcGIS Connector. Finally, we will look ahead at the growing set of infrastructure capabilities coming to Forma, including new tools for urban street design and the upcoming integration with Civil 3D, and how adopting these cloud-first tools today positions your team to take full advantage of what's next.
speakers: Shelby L Smith, BIM Manager, Bohler
Hilde Bakkeli, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Forma Standardization at Scale: Jacobs’ Road to 30,000 Users
abstract: The idea of global standards for any large and diverse business is often a pipe dream. How can you empower people to work in similar ways when they’re located in all corners of the world, hold different roles, and work across many markets requiring unique solutions? We can’t promise the perfect answer, but we can promise that we gave it a shot and it’s going well. We hope to share our experiences, our strategy, and our tactics, and help others around the industry solve a complex problem. Whether it’s less than 100 people or more than 1,000, the value of working in a single source of truth in a consistent way pays dividends in the quality of your deliverables, the user experience, and the time you spend kicking off and managing a project. We hope to see you there!
speakers: Thomas Crawford, Director of Information Management, Jacobs
Margarita Kreternova, Digital Delivery Manager - Data Centers, JACOBS
Michael McKeon, Global Principal Civil Tools, Jacobs
Nathaniel Coombs, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
Bruce Johnson, BTS Autodesk Platform Lead, Jacobs Engineering Group

title: Autodesk Tandem Connect in Action: Integrate Systems, Trigger Workflows, Drive Operations
abstract: In this hands-on session, explore how Autodesk Tandem Connect enables truly operational digital twins by integrating real-time data with building assets. Participants will connect external systems, visualize performance through heat maps, integrate with CMMS platforms to generate work orders, and trigger automated alerts. Learn how to transform raw signals into actionable workflows that improve maintenance, reduce downtime, and drive smarter facility operations. This session will focus on practical implementation, showing how connected data can power real-world decisions and outcomes.
speakers: Derek Milz, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Autodesk VRED: Latest Real-Time Visualization Trends combined with AI Transforming Automotive Design
abstract: Autodesk VRED is known for rapidly adopting state of the art rendering technologies, open standards, and AI workflow tools. This Autodesk University session explores new key capabilities including Vulkan Ray Tracing, Gaussian Splat rendering, CloudXR streaming to Apple Vision Pro, and the use of constraints and physics. Learn how these technologies work together to deliver highly realistic visuals and physically plausible behavior for complex digital twins with minimal setup time. Discover how designers, engineers, and visual artists can accelerate projects, improve collaboration, and reduce costly errors early in the digital model. Ideal for visualization, XR, and automotive workflows focused on performance, realism, and scalability.
speakers: Victor Perez, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Pascal Seifert, Sr. Technical Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Automating ISO 7817 Compliance: A Practical Workflow Using Dynamo, Revit, and LLMs
abstract: Producing and controlling data from project models at a defined level is still largely a manual and error-prone process. This session will present ISO 7817 (Level of Information Need), the emerging standard beyond traditional Levels of Detail, and show how BIM execution plan requirements link to a Revit model. The session will explore a closed-loop workflow that tracks data from requirements to reporting. The method includes transferring information requirements from Microsoft Excel into Revit elements as parameters using Dynamo, guiding modelers by showing what data to input and why within element properties, collecting data back into Excel, and automatically generating performance reports by doing a row-by-row comparison of “Required” and “Provided” data using a large language model (LLM).
speakers: Idris Bahadur, Co-Founder Architect, ROP Architects

title: Better Together: Drainage Design Best Practices with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
abstract:
With the release of drainage tools for Civil 3D 2026, users are asking: How do these tools fit into Autodesk’s drainage design ecosystem? 

This session provides a clear, practical comparison of drainage tools for Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, including how each solution integrates into your workflows. This session will demonstrate how to combine Autodesk tools with open-source solutions and LLM’s to unlock new possibilities. We streamline the drainage design process by using API and Civil 3D tools for catchment delineation. 

Walk away with a practical understanding of the tools, with the ability to navigate Autodesk’s evolving drainage design landscape and leverage a hybrid ecosystem for scalable, intelligent design.
speakers: Hunter Sparks, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Beyond Automation: AI Collaboration with Autodesk Assistant
abstract: This session will demonstrate how the recently introduced Autodesk Fusion AI Assistant enhances product development. AI Assistant accelerates early-stage design exploration, development, and fabrication by translating text into CAD, automating workflows, and accelerating implementation. Case studies of consumer products will illustrate how AI Assistant improves efficiency, when traditional methods are more effective, and how to best combine both. The session will cover prompt engineering techniques that improve output quality. By adopting these workflows, teams can reduce repetitive tasks, improve iteration speed, and focus human expertise on higher-value design decisions, ultimately achieving faster, more informed results.
speakers: Alex Lobos, Director, School of Design, Rochester Institute of Technology

title: Beyond the BOM: Using PLM to Drive Modern Product Management
abstract: Product lifecycle management (PLM) is often treated as a system of record for BOMs—but leading teams are using it to drive product strategy, execution, and cross-functional alignment. In this session, we’ll show how to evolve PLM into a product management backbone that connects engineering, operations, and business decisions. You’ll learn practical workflows for managing product definitions, changes, and lifecycle data in a way that improves visibility, reduces delays, and enables better decision making. Walk away with patterns you can apply immediately to move beyond BOM management and unlock real business value from PLM.
speakers: Gus Quade, Sr. Technical Sales Specialist,  Fusion PLM, Autodesk

title: Beyond the PDF: Synchronizing Large-Scale Teams via the Autodesk-Forma-to-Autodesk-Workshop XR Pipeline
abstract: Strategic alignment: integrated workflows, convergence across tools (Forma + Revit + Workshop XR) to create impact. This focuses on "business outcomes" by eliminating the "render-review-rework" cycle. Coordination gaps between master planners and building designers often lead to costly rework during design development. Using the KEO project as a case study, this session demonstrates how to establish Autodesk Forma as a "single source of truth." We showcase a scalable strategy applied across our projects and a workflow demo where design constraints are pushed through Revit into Workshop XR for 1:1 scale review. Learn how this integrated approach allows global teams to make instant, data-backed decisions from massing and orientation to design details, ensuring total stakeholder alignment before construction.
speakers: Amar Hromo, Senior Architect, KEO International Consultants

title: BIM Intelligence Agent: Live QTO, Carbon, Cost, and Compliance from Autodesk Forma via AI and AEC Data Model
abstract: What if one AI prompt returned live QTO, carbon, cost, compliance, and a 4D schedule from your Revit models in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)—no exports or plug-ins? This session will present a working BIM Intelligence Agent built at the APS Accelerator Bangalore 2026 in four days, connecting to the AEC Data Model GraphQL API via Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Azure GPT-4.1. Ten BIM intelligence tools, all natural language. Real WSP project data live on screen will include: walls 1,860 square meters; floors 6,089 square meters; 380 tCO₂e carbon; $1.44 million cost; ISO 19650 compliance check; and a 38-week 4D schedule. One conversation, zero manual work. Learn the architecture, undocumented GraphQL patterns, 3LO OAuth flows, and 10 production bugs fixed. Code shared.
speakers: Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global
Vijaya Adigopula, Technical Director, WSP

title: Boosting Autodesk Development Using AI with AutoLISP and C# .NET
abstract: Learn how to use AI as a practical coding assistant to accelerate AutoCAD development. This 30-minute strategy session will show how AI can generate AutoLISP routines and C# .NET code, assist with debugging, and support code translation—enabling faster iteration and higher-quality results. Attendees will gain strategies to evaluate AI-generated code, integrate it into existing projects, and apply AI-assisted workflows effectively across both legacy and modern Autodesk development.
speakers: Todd Schmoock, Implementation Consultant, Graitec
James Johnson, Application Developer, Synergis Software

title: Break the Desktop Barrier: Dynamo in the Cloud for Scalable Revit and Civil 3D Automation
abstract: Ever ran the same Dynamo graph across multiple projects and waited hours while Revit or Civil 3D software was locked? What if you could hand it off instead? This session will dive into how Dynamo Switchboard enables cloud execution of Dynamo graphs across projects at scale. Rather than running workflows locally or building custom pipelines with Design Automation, you can now execute graphs through a simple, player-like interface. Learn how to run batch automations across multiple models without opening host applications, and review results through logs and the Dynamo graph web viewer. Through live demos, you’ll see how to launch runs and interpret results. We’ll also briefly explore connecting workflows with Autodesk Platform Services and AEC Data Models.
speakers: Achintya Bhat, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Bridge the Gap: Syncing Autodesk Forma, Procore, and HCSS with ProjectReady WorkBridge
abstract: Are you tired of manually re-entering data between Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Procore, and HCSS? ProjectReady WorkBridge eliminates that burden. In this live product demo, Topcon Solutions and ProjectReady will walk through three real-world workflows: bidirectional sync between Autodesk Forma and Procore for submittals, RFIs, issues, and photos; project data transfers from Procore to Autodesk Forma; and the connecting of HCSS HeavyBid to BuildingConnected for a seamless preconstruction-to-construction handoff. See WorkBridge's scheduling engine, audit logs, and no-data-at-rest architecture in action—and leave knowing how to connect your platforms and keep every team aligned.
speakers: Jordan Bullock, MBA, ACI, Manager, Design Software & Training, Topcon Solutions
Joe Giegerich, CEO, ProjectReady

title: Bridging BIM and Hydraulics: Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro for Smart Pressure Networks
abstract: Discover a new integration between Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro software that connects BIM-based pressure pipe network design with detailed hydraulic analysis. See how bidirectional data exchange helps teams create constructable 3D networks using real parts while validating pressure, flow, and performance in InfoWorks WS Pro. Learn how this workflow improves design quality, reduces rework, and supports more-cost-effective outcomes. An industry expert will share real-world workflows, key benefits, lessons learned, and practical recommendations for successful adoption.
speakers: Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Bridging the Knowledge Gap: An Open-Source RAG Approach to Reliable Revit Development
abstract: What if anyone could automate Revit software—without writing a single line of code? This session introduces an open-source AI agent that turns natural language into executable Revit operations. Built on retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), it retrieves knowledge from Revit API Docs, generates C# code, and executes it inside Revit in real time. Key highlights include the following: There are no hardcoded rules—the large language model (LLM) reasons from real API signatures. There are no preset commands—never-seen operations are reasoned and created on the fly. Successful operations solidify into reusable templates—non-developers replay them instantly. And there’s a live Revit connection via TCP JSON-RPC with Roslyn dynamic compilation. No C# experience or plug-in background is needed. And there’s no command library to maintain. Just describe what you want.
speakers: 兰辉 徐, Product Developmenter, TYDI

title: Builders in the AI Loop: How We Accelerate Construction and Preserve Judgement
abstract: AI is increasing output across construction teams, but many leaders are seeing a quieter problem: more-polished work, less ownership. With more options come harder decisions. This strategy talk will use one concrete story and a practical framework to show how to adopt AI without eroding the judgment that experienced builders, designers, and owners have earned the hard way. You’ll learn how to separate AI-assisted production from the human decision making that takes decades to develop. We’ll discuss how leaders in the industry add thinking checkpoints within workflows that make teams faster while preserving their precious (and playful) cognition.
speakers: Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Building an AI-Ready BIM Data Backbone with Autodesk APS
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations struggle to scale automation and AI because BIM data is fragmented, inconsistently governed, and tied to individual projects. This session will show how Drees & Sommer and AnkerDB built a centralized BIM data backbone using Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable reliable automation and consistent data quality at scale. The collaboration started as a rapid proof of concept at DevCon 2025, was validated across multiple projects, and is now scaling at the business-unit level. The session will explain how Autodesk Forma data, Autodesk Platform Services software, and downstream systems were connected to support automated validation, data enrichment, analytics, integrations, and AI-supported workflows for cost management and lifecycle assessment (LCA).
speakers: Valeriia Vlasenko, Expert, Drees & Sommer
Moritz Mombour, Head of Digitalization EPCM REI, Drees & Sommer SE

title: Building an Industry-Class Electrical Subcontractor Revit Template
abstract: In this session, we’ll walk through the process of building an electrical detailing and prefabrication Revit template that supports more than 50 detailers in multiple regions across the United States. Then we’ll examine what it takes to evolve it to the next level with EVOLVE Electrical.
speakers: Derek Renn, Director of BIM Technology, Bergelectric Corporation

title: Building an MCP Server for BIM: Connect Any AI to Live Autodesk Forma Models via AEC Data Model
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is transforming how AI assistants interact with engineering data. Instead of building separate apps, you expose your data as MCP tools—and any large language model (LLM) connects natively. In this session, we’ll show how WSP built a production MCP server using FastMCP and Python that exposes AEC Data Model GraphQL APIs as intelligent tools—enabling engineers to query live Autodesk Forma Revit models conversationally via the Claude Desktop app or GPT-4. Ask "What is the total embodied carbon for Level 3?" or "List all structural columns over 5m" and you’ll get live answers directly from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), with no separate UI. This was built and demonstrated at the Autodesk APS Accelerator Bangalore 2026. Attendees will leave with a replicable MCP server blueprint for Autodesk Forma.
speakers: Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global
Vijaya Adigopula, Technical Director, WSP

title: Building an Operational Digital Twin for a Health Care Facility
abstract: Discover how Healthworld Hospitals implemented a complete Autodesk and InnoMaint CMMS‑powered digital twin to transform facility operations and maintenance workflows. This session will showcase the end-to-end journey—from site survey, laser scanning, and as-built BIM creation to real-time asset monitoring, dashboard visualization, and data-driven decision making. Learn how the digital twin improved operational efficiency, reduced downtime, and enabled smarter, safer hospital management.
speakers: Naman Patwari, Head of Automation, Pinnacle Infotech
Barry Brunet, VP - Strategic Solutions, Pinnacle FutureBuild

title: Building at the Speed of Demand: A Data Center Meetup
abstract: Data center demand is accelerating at an unprecedented pace—bringing tight schedules, complex MEP coordination, constant change, and high-stakes commissioning. This meetup aims to be a curated networking space for owners, developers, designers, and builders to connect with peers and share practical thoughts on “what’s working” in the field. Join the conversation to exchange real-world strategies across delivery, standardization, prefabrication, design coordination, commissioning readiness, and transformation of project data into operational value. Whether you're scaling programs or managing aggressive timelines, you’ll leave with new connections, fresh ideas, and a clearer view of how others are accelerating delivery while managing risk.
speakers: Julia Cook, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Jayanth Iyengar, Sr Principal, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Sarah O' Sullivan, Senior Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk

title: Building Custom AEC Apps in Minutes: AI-Assisted Development with FORMA and VIKTOR.AI
abstract:
Design teams increasingly need trusted workflows that connect Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Platform Services (APS), agentic AI, engineering tools, proprietary company knowledge, and cloud automation to solve real project challenges. This session explores how organizations can use open APIs and modern development platforms to build custom applications and intelligent workflows around Forma Site Design and Building Design.

Attendees will learn how to integrate project data, automate engineering and design processes, connect cloud services, and extend Autodesk workflows with company-specific logic. We will also introduce the Autodesk Marketplace and discuss how developers can package and distribute solutions that strengthen the Autodesk ecosystem.

Using VIKTOR.AI as the application, workflow, and agentic automation layer, we will demonstrate how Autodesk technologies can be combined with AI, engineering software, and internal knowledge. We will show how organizations can move beyond isolated AI prompts by creating transparent, controlled, and verifiable workflows in which agents execute tasks, use engineering tools, and present traceable results for expert review.
speakers: Jordana Rosa, Autodesk
Peter Madlener, CEO, VIKTOR

title: Building Operational Twins with Indoor GIS: Where BIM, CAD, and Facility Data Go to Thrive
abstract: CAD and BIM have long served as foundational design and construction documentation, but their value often ends at project handoff. What if it didn't? Indoor GIS is a floor-aware system for visualizing, analyzing, managing, and navigating facilities. This session will demonstrate how AutoCAD, Revit, PDF, indoor reality, and imagery can be transformed into foundations for operational, living digital twins with ArcGIS Indoors. Learn how organizations support asset management, space planning, safety, and occupant experience while extending the life of design and construction data beyond project delivery. See how GIS integrates with Autodesk products, design and engineering data in Forma Data Management, and facility data to create long-term operational value.
speakers: Gokce Ozcelik, Sr. Product Manager - Indoor GIS, Esri
Michael Davidson, Product Manager, Esri
Will Isley, CTO - PS R&D Center, Esri

title: Building the Digital Thread: Connecting CRM, Vault PLM, MES, and ERP from Order to Delivery
abstract: Manufacturing organizations often struggle with disconnected systems across sales, engineering, and production. This class will show how Vault PLM software forms the backbone of a connected digital thread spanning customer relationship management (CRM), CAD, product data management (PDM), product lifecycle management (PLM), manufacturing execution systems (MES), and enterprise resource planning (ERP). Starting from a CRM order, we’ll demonstrate rule-based CAD automation, engineering data management in Vault, and seamless Item and BOM synchronization into Autodesk Fusion Manage—driven by the built-in connector. Design reviews are handled through a web interface powered by the Vault Data API, manufacturing execution runs in Autodesk Fusion Operations, and business data flows into ERP—event-driven and AI-assisted. See how Vault PLM bridges engineering and enterprise to streamline the journey, from order to delivery.
speakers: Markus Gundersen, Business Manager, COOLORANGE NORTHERN EUROPE
Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l.

title: Building the Digital Thread: M2X’s Path from Engineering to Manufacturing Scale
abstract: What breaks when a 10-person engineering team becomes a 70-person manufacturing organization? This session will explore M2X’s real-world journey scaling with Inventor, Vault, AutoCAD Plant 3D, and Autodesk Fusion Manage software. Learn how the team transitioned from ad hoc design workflows to structured data management and a connected PDM/PLM strategy. We’ll cover how to time tool adoption, avoid common scaling missteps, and enable cross-functional collaboration between engineering and production. You’ll gain practical frameworks to structure product data, build a digital thread, and support rapid growth—while improving quality, reducing rework, and maintaining control across the product lifecycle.
speakers: Justin Johnson, M2X Energy
Nicholas Schwartz, Chief Manufacturing Officer at M2X Energy, M2X Energy

title: Building the Talent Pipeline for Industrialized Construction
abstract: Ryan MacMahon, Senior Director and General Manager of Manufacturing Informed Design at Autodesk, and Chad Ray, Provost and Chief Campus Officer at Wake Technical Community College, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how education and industry are preparing the workforce for industrialized construction. The episode explores prefab, manufacturing, curriculum development, workforce readiness, and the future skills needed to transform how buildings are delivered.

title: Can AI Help Construction Understand the Jobsite in Real Time?
abstract: Chris Baze, Director of Construction Technology @ Hawaiian Dredging and Fikret Kalay, Director @ Autodesk Research join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss research exploring whether AI can create a continuously updated digital understanding of active construction sites. The conversation examines jobsite intelligence, digital twins, project readiness, risk detection, and how connected data could help project teams make better decisions before problems affect schedule and cost.

title: Civil 3D and Dynamo with ReCap 2026: Automating Tunnel Section Extraction and Comparison for Rehab
abstract: Tunnel rehabilitation projects lack a single, bulletproof workflow for comparing complex point cloud data with design corridors. Instead of chasing a one-size-fits-all solution, successful projects require selecting the right toolset for the specific job. This session explores the current state of the art in working with tunnel point cloud meshes using ReCap, Civil 3D, and Dynamo. Rather than presenting a single rigid path, we will dissect multiple methodologies, analyzing the practical pros and cons of each. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of what is realistically possible right now, how to automate section creation, and how to select the optimal workflow to balance accuracy against automation scale.
speakers: David Pastor, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
Goyo Grzeskow, Sr Enterprise Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: Collaborate Better with AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma Data Management: Share, Trace, Multi-User Markups, Checkout
abstract: See how AutoCAD software and Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) work together so your team can collaborate without confusion. This hands-on session will walk you through Share—sending view or edit links so others can open drawings in the browser or in AutoCAD on the web—and Trace—adding markups on a syncing overlay and bringing them into the main drawing. You’ll try multi-user markups so several people can add feedback to the same design from web and desktop, and see how to use checkout to reserve entities for edit, submit for review, then merge approved checkout back into the drawing. Whether you work in AutoCAD desktop, on the web, or with Forma Data Management, you’ll leave with a clear workflow to share, review, and manage drawings as a team.
speakers: Helen Chen, Principal QA Specialist, Autodesk

abstract:

title: Connected Buildings at Scale: From Construction to Operations
abstract: Construction and building operations remain disconnected across projects, limiting efficiency and long-term performance. This session will bring together leaders from Windover Construction, KONE, and STRABAG, along with Autodesk Research, to show how connected workflows improve delivery and operations. KONE systems move 2 billion people daily, demonstrating the impact of connected building systems at scale. Windover and STRABAG workflows, combined with prefab and vertical logistics, can reduce schedules by up to 30% during construction. In operations, linking real-time occupancy data and digital twins has achieved up to 36% in energy savings. You’ll gain strategies to connect BIM, construction, and operations into a continuous lifecycle.
speakers: Adam Allard, Senior Manager, Technical Environments, Autodesk
Fikret Kalay, Director, Research Science, Autodesk
Amr Raafat, Chief Innovation Officer (CIO), Windover Construction

title: Connected Carbon Data for Construction: API-Powered Decisions at Scale
abstract: Construction teams face growing pressure to make early, data-driven carbon decisions. Yet fragmented regional data sets limit consistency and scalability across tools. This session will explore how TBI, a leading construction firm, is advancing end-to-end carbon assessment by connecting data across planning, design, and preconstruction workflows. Using Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Forma Takeoff) and the Sustainability Data API, TBI will demonstrate how API-powered strategies enable early-stage carbon comparisons across multiple regions, reduce manual data handling, and scale assessments across projects. You’ll gain a strategic framework for driving better, data-informed decisions through connected, scalable carbon workflows.
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk

title: Connected Coordination Level 3: Elevate Clash Resolution Using the Power of Model Coordination in Autodesk Forma
abstract: In fast-paced digital project delivery, timely communication and clear accountability across teams are fundamental to effective clash resolution. In this Connected Coordination Level 3 lab, we’ll build on the 2025 session to demonstrate how a structured, closed-loop approach to issue management allows you to assign, notify, track, and resolve clashes while maintaining a fully auditable record of every action. In this lab, you’ll learn to pull clash issues directly into their Revit models to visualize conflicts and act to ensure transparency and efficiency among stakeholders. This lab will also build on exporting active clash data and integrating it with Power BI dashboards for real-time insights and better decision making.
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk

title: Connected Design: Real-World Collaboration Workflows Across Autodesk Forma and Revit
abstract: The way architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams work across tools has long been fragmented: models reimported manually, analyses running outside the authoring environment, and design intent lost at every handoff. Forma Connected Clients is here to change that. Two of the product managers behind Forma Connected Clients will share insights into the strategy and walk you through a real workflow connecting Autodesk Forma Site Design, Forma Building Design, Forma Board, and Revit software. Hear from customers on what's already shifting. See Autodesk Forma analyses spanning across design applications, keeping multiple models aligned without reimport, and collaborative live design review with Forma Board—all in one connected process.
speakers: Matt Arsenault, Principal Product Manager - Forma Connected Clients, Autodesk
Caoimhe Loftus, Product Manager, Forma Model, Autodesk

title: Connecting AECO Workflows End-to-End with the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud
abstract: See how architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams connect planning, design, coordination, and construction workflows in a single AI and data-driven environment using the Autodesk Forma industry cloud. This technical and practical deep dive will walk through real workflows—from site planning in Autodesk Forma to design in Revit software, coordination in Forma Design Collaboration, and execution in Forma Build. Learn how data flows through Autodesk Data Management as a common data environment, preserving decisions across phases with practical examples. Explore practical AI-powered use cases such as rapid design iteration, automated analysis, and model-based coordination. And discover how to reduce manual work, improve collaboration, and implement connected workflows across the AECO lifecycle.
speakers: Joey Matla, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Alejandra Beaujon, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Connecting BIM to Citizen-Scale Digital Twins: Sustainability, Compliance & Connected Infrastructure
abstract: SIMICO S.p.A delivered infrastructure to the 2026 Winter Olympics (Livigno, Cortina, Milano, Verona, Bormio) using a full Autodesk pipeline: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Autodesk Forma Build, Autodesk Platform Services, Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Navisworks software. Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Build managed cost, schedule, and field workflows. Autodesk Platform Services connected everything bidirectionally. This Autodesk-Azure dual common data environment (CDE) enabled a complex environment where BIM authoring changes synced with Forma cost tracking, Build field logs, and compliance docs. These pipelines preserved data integrity from Autodesk tools to digital XR experiences (VR/AR/pixel streaming), making the twin accessible to all stakeholders. Tailored as such, this system delivered an organic ecosystem, reducing risk and accelerating decisions on complex public infrastructure in Italy.
speakers: Francesco Cappilli, Head of Digital Engineering, Infrastrutture Milano Cortina 2026 Spa

title: Continuous vs. Periodic Clash Detection : Can Model Coordination and Autodesk AI replace Navisworks?
abstract: Is the Navisworks silo holding your project back? For 20 years, coordination was a "once a week" event locked on a desktop. No more. This session will explore the leap to continuous, cloud-native coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll dive into how Model Coordination democratizes BIM, using Autodesk AI and Autodesk Assistant to validate clashes against specs in real time. Learn to ditch static PDF reports for a closed-loop workflow that connects designers directly to fixes. We’ll settle the debate: Where does Model Coordination win, and when do you still need the Navisworks "power user" kit? Join us to build a road map for a faster, AI-augmented and integrated future. Stop clashing. Start coordinating.
speakers: Anas Poshekar, Associate Sr. BIM Coordinator, Burns & McDonnell India

title: Cracking the Code: Automating Block Editor Workflows with DocumentManager CommandAsync
abstract: Thirty-seven offices and seven unique borders. Discover how to eliminate hours of repetitive tasks by using AutoCAD software’s DocumentManager and asynchronous command execution to automate Block Editor operations. This session will demonstrate techniques for automatically managing the dynamic blocks with visibility states in these drawings using the Block Editor API. Learn how to combine Editor.CommandAsync, transaction management, and proper document locking to update these seven drawings based on a single database. This session will cover how to get the final solution, and attendees will walk away with the practical code patterns, debugging strategies, and approaches that transformed hours of manual updates into a process that takes just seconds.
speakers: Scott Mizsak, CAD Coordinator, Bolton & Menk

title: Create Your Own AI Assistant That Interacts with Revit and Other Programs at the Same Time
abstract: Current AI assistants for Revit software typically operate within a single application. This class will explore a different approach by creating a custom AI assistant that can interact with Revit and other programs simultaneously using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The assistant can be extended to interact with additional tool applications to help solve interoperability. When creating a custom AI assistant, the available actions are defined explicitly. You’ll configure which Revit functions are exposed to the assistant and which are not. For example, you can restrict commands that delete elements, remove views, or make unwanted model changes. No prior AI or server development experience is necessary.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: Data Center Design Automation: A New Paradigm for Feasibility and Early Design
abstract:
Data center projects must move faster while managing increasing complexity in power, cooling, and cost.
Traditional feasibility workflows are fragmented and slow, limiting iteration and delaying decisions. This session presents a new approach through a real customer case study, showing how integrating Podium with Autodesk Forma and Revit enables teams to move from site analysis to coordinated design in a single day. By automating layout generation and enabling rapid scenario testing, teams can evaluate more options, align stakeholders earlier, and reduce risk. Learn how feasibility becomes a fast, iterative, and data-driven process.
speakers: Nuno Mourao, Chief Software Architect, Podium.io

title: Data-Centered Delivery at Scale: Selective IFC Exports from Autodesk Forma Using Autodesk Data Exchange​
abstract: Ramboll’s shift to data-centered delivery moves beyond project-by-project file exchanges, transforming BIM data into a reusable, trusted, and scalable company-wide asset. This class will present a practical architecture and operating model to selectively export standardized IFC data from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) using Data Exchange, enabling analytics, integration, digital twins, and lifecycle information management.
speakers: Adrian Fernandez Sanchez, Product Owner Autodesk Transport, Rambøll Norge
Aleksandra Gorczyca, Principal Consulting Project Manager, Autodesk
Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk

title: Data-Driven Water Utilities: BIM-GIS Validation and Digital Twins at Gruppo CAP
abstract: Inconsistent data across the water lifecycle hinders operational resilience. This session will present the technical framework developed for Gruppo CAP (Milan) to bridge this gap using Autodesk Forma as a unified cloud environment. Starting from scan-to-BIM modeling of a water plant, we’ll detail a custom validation engine built on Autodesk Platform Services that automates model checking against asset information requirem`ents (AIR) standards via specialized scripts. We’ll explore how validated BIM data flows into Esri Utility Network to fuel InfoWorks ICM solutions for advanced hydraulic modeling. You’ll evaluate how this scalable architecture, in a large-scale utility, uses Power BI to transform data into a simulation-ready digital twin for smarter asset management.
speakers: Giuseppe Barberio, Head Of Digital Engineering & BIM, Gruppo CAP
Antonio Devito, Technical Director, One team

title: Day 1 Keynote
abstract:
What if every person, team, and project had more capacity to deliver?

Join Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost and CTO Raji Arasu to discover how Autodesk is helping customers move faster, reduce repetitive work, improve predictability, and unlock new value across design, make, and operate.

Through live demonstrations, you'll see how Autodesk AI and Industry Clouds are helping individuals work smarter, teams collaborate more effectively, and organizations turn ideas into outcomes with greater speed and confidence.

The keynote will also feature fireside chat between Andrew Anagnost and Clara Shih, founder of the New Work Foundation and a pioneering technology leader. Drawing on her experience leading AI initiatives at Salesforce and Meta, Clara will share insights on how agentic AI is transforming the way organizations work and how businesses can unlock new capacity by combining human expertise with AI.

Explore how Autodesk builds AI for the real world, grounded in the data, workflows, and controls you need to get more done, solve bigger challenges, and shape what comes next.
speakers: Andrew Anagnost, President and Chief Executive Officer, Autodesk
Raji Arasu, EVP, Platform Services and Emerging Technologies, and CTO, Autodesk
Clara Shih, Founder, New Work Foundation; Advisor and Founder of Business AI at Meta; ex-CEO, Salesforce AI

title: Demystifying AI: Find the sweet spot for starting up in AI using LLMs, Autodesk Assistant, and MCPs in your company
abstract: Learn how large language models (LLMs) and model content protocols (MCPs) work, when to use them, and how to get better results with effective prompting. See how STV began their journey into AI, and learn about their process. Explore practical ways to use Autodesk Assistant across tools and discover how AI is integrated into Forma to support design decisions. Walk away with real workflows, tips, and confidence to apply AI in your daily work. Learn how to use LLMs to create add ins, dynamo scripts, and general design automation.
speakers: David Banyard, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
STEPHANIE CATALINA, Principal Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk
Xiaoxuan Peng, Director of Digital Delivery, stv

title: Design-Driven Reinforcement in Revit: From Analysis Results to Automated Rebar and Documentation
abstract: Revit software is evolving into a design-driven environment for structural engineers, enabling a seamless transition from analysis to reinforcement and documentation. In this hands-on session, you’ll integrate results from FEM software—such as Robot Structural Analysis, GRAITEC Advance Design, or other tools—directly into Revit to perform code-based checks and generate reinforcement for concrete members, including beams, columns, footings, and walls. You’ll automate rebar cage generation, produce engineering reports, and generate drawings and schedules within a single BIM-integrated platform, reducing manual work, improving coordination, and ensuring compliance with US and European standards.
speakers: Irina Cojocaru, R&D Product Director, Graitec
Stevens Chemise, Product Manager, Graitec Innovation

title: Design Fast, Validate Smart: Extending InfoDrainage with Parametric Workflows in Civil 3D and InfoWorks ICM to Deliver Multiple Benefits
abstract: Early-stage drainage design prioritizes speed, using simplified assumptions to test options quickly. However, challenges such as combined sewer overflows (CSOs), flooding, biodiversity loss, and wider community outcomes are increasingly interconnected and require a more systems-based approach that extends beyond the traditional boundaries of the water sector. This session explores how connected digital workflows can support the identification, design, and validation of sustainable drainage interventions that deliver multiple benefits. Using an anonymized case study, attendees will see how opportunities can be rapidly explored through parametric site-design workflows in Civil 3D and InfoDrainage, then assessed through system-scale modelling in InfoWorks ICM to understand impacts on flood risk and CSO frequency, volume, and timing. The session focuses on balancing speed, rigour, and confidence in decision-making, helping practitioners understand how technology, systems thinking, and proportionate modelling can support more resilient and integrated outcomes for communities and the environment.
speakers: Pablo Souto, Global Discipline Leader - Water, Mott MacDonald Ltd
Juan Aguirrebengoa, Principal Civil Engineer CEng MICE, Mott MacDonald

title: Design Fast, Validate Smart: Extending InfoDrainage with Parametric Workflows in Civil 3D and InfoWorks ICM to Deliver Multiple Benefits

However, challenges such as combined sewer overflows (CSOs), flooding, biodiversity loss, and wider community outcomes are increasingly interconnected and require a more systems-based approach that extends beyond the traditional boundaries of the water sector.
