Pablo Souto, Global Discipline Leader - Water, Mott MacDonald Ltd

title: Designing for Everyone: How Mott MacDonald and Autodesk Are Advancing AEC Software Accessibility
abstract: Mott MacDonald and Autodesk are partnering to make architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) software more accessible for people with diverse needs. Through a joint accessibility working group, user research with colleagues with lived experience, and a pilot focused on inclusive design improvements, both organizations are shaping more-intuitive, barrier‑free workflows. This session will share practical lessons from our collaboration and provide a repeatable model for embedding accessibility into digital delivery.
speakers: Katrin Buehn, Director, Customer Relationship Mgmt, Autodesk
Tom Hughes, Head of Software Portfolio, Mott MacDonald
Ian Besford, Global Digital Delivery Leader, Mott MacDonald
Karla Ortloff, Director, User Experience, Autodesk
Conny Scheitz, VP, Platform Next, Autodesk

title: Designing for Inclusion: Solving Low-Battery Anxiety in AEC and Design and Make
abstract: What if your designs unintentionally limit who belongs in the spaces you create? This strategy talk reveals the hidden infrastructure gap behind “low battery anxiety” for power mobility users and why it matters to AEC and Design & Make professionals. Through Teresa Valenzuela’s story, discover how culture, empathy, and inclusive innovation can reshape design. Learn to uncover overlooked user needs, design for accessibility at scale, and apply practical strategies that expand access and participation. Walk away with actionable ways to embed accessibility and belonging into your next project.
speakers: Melody Lindenberger, Dir., Tax, Autodesk
Ian Pendlebury, Vice President Fusion Platform, Autodesk
Teresa Valenzuela, Founder | CEO, Well-Able Platforms
Alexis Womble, Senior Security Program Manager, Autodesk

title: Design Once, Use Forever: Automating Civil 3D Asset Data for Operations
abstract: As owners and operators increasingly rely on digital twins, geographic information systems (GIS), and asset management platforms, expectations for consistent, accurate, and information‑rich civil deliverables continue to rise. Yet many Civil 3D workflows still rely on manual asset attribution, introducing risk, rework, and inconsistency. This session will explore how Civil 3D and Dynamo can be used to automate asset attribution, using a real‑world airport-infrastructure case study with the Houston Airports System (HAS). You will learn how rule‑based logic, Civil 3D object intelligence, and standardized data schemas are used to populate attributes for linear and point‑based assets, then export attribution‑ready data for GIS and asset management systems.
speakers: Jelber Prado, BIM Manager | Infrastructure, Houston Airport System
George Cernetig, Sr. VDC Specialist, HNTB

title: Design Once, Use Many Times: The OpenBIM Strategies at the São Paulo Metro Company
abstract: Large rail and metro programs generate vast amounts of design data, yet information is often recreated or lost across phases and contracts. This session shows how infrastructure owners can apply OpenBIM strategies to truly “design once, use many times.” Based on real metro and railway programs, it demonstrates how open standards—especially IFC 4.3—enable consistent reuse of data from planning and design through construction, oversight, and long-term operations. Attendees will learn how owners can structure BIM requirements, governance models, and data workflows that support interoperability across multiple vendors and platforms, improving transparency, efficiency, and decision-making across the asset lifecycle.
speakers: Ivo Mainardi, BIM Manager, São Paulo Metro
Joyce Delatorre, Principal Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: Design. Optimize. Connect. Build Smarter Products with Autodesk Fusion.
abstract: Have you ever wanted to design a part but weren’t sure how to approach it using the available tools and materials? Would you like to analyze existing products to identify optimizations or potential failures before they occur—or transform current designs into smarter, more capable products? In this hands-on lab, we’ll use Autodesk Fusion to work more effectively across key stages of the product lifecycle—from initial concept to optimization and intelligent enhancement. Using a smart desk lamp as our example, we’ll explore three distinct workflows: designing a manufacturable component from scratch, analyzing and optimizing critical parts, and finally enhancing the product by integrating electronics to create a smarter, connected system.
speakers: Ignacio Madina, Sr Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk
David Sabaté, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: Design Requirements Verification with BIM Automation and AI Agents
abstract: Verifying that a building meets project requirements - room sizing, adjacencies, equipment, performance - is still largely manual. This session presents a pipeline automating design requirements verification on BIM models. Rule-based engines extract properties, compare them to the project brief, and flag deviations. AI agents augment this pipeline - not replacing verification, but assisting decision-making: interpreting ambiguous requirements and suggesting resolution paths. Attendees see a live walkthrough: model ingestion, rule matching, deviation reporting, and AI-assisted decision support. We share lessons learned at Egis, including data quality pitfalls and balancing automation with human judgment.
speakers: Alexandre HERSANT, Product Owner, Egis
Abdelhakim BENATTIA, BIM Developer, Egis

title: Digital Project Delivery, Forma Build Implementation
abstract: Our session will show how Autodesk Forma was implemented and governed on a live health care project, adapting workflows to project‑specific needs. We will demonstrate the application of standards during active delivery to maintain consistency and data integrity while teams adopt the platform and evolve digital practices in real time. You’ll learn how collaboration was structured across Autodesk, construction technology, operations, and BIM by deploying two Autodesk Forma Build projects to separate design coordination from construction execution, alongside targeted training. We’ll also cover license provisioning, role‑based access, content ownership alignment, and Power BI dashboards that deliver actionable insights for better decisions.
speakers: Rania Hassan, VDC Regional Manager, Ellisdon

title: Digital Transformation Is a Race Without a Finish Line
abstract: Olli Hyyppa, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at Arcadis, joins the Digital Builder podcast to discuss why digital transformation is no longer a destination, but a continuous process of reinvention. Drawing on a career spent leading transformation efforts across multiple organizations, Olli shares his perspective on navigating constant change, adapting to new technologies, and how leaders can think about transformation in a world where the pace of innovation continues to accelerate.

title: Don’t AI everything: Hybrid automation with APS and Revit.
abstract: Automation specialists are increasingly tasked with finding areas to implement AI. But how do we decide when AI is the correct tool and when deterministic automation serves better? Through a live demo of an AI-augmented building regulation compliance checker running on Autodesk Platform Services, we will explore a practical hybrid framework. The Automation API and Revit software handle rule evaluation through a deterministic engine. Large language models (LLMs) extract compliance rules from regulation documentation and explain failures in natural language. And the Viewer SDK provides visual context. We’ll demonstrate a human-in-the-loop approach and show how AI architecture adapts rapidly when regulations change or new markets require new rule sets.
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk
Neil Lee, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd
Will North, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd

title: Do You Trust Me? Building Trustworthy AI for Design and Engineering Workflows
abstract: As AI becomes embedded in design and engineering tools, the question isn’t just what it can do—it’s whether you can trust it. This session will cover practical ways to make AI more reliable, including handling proprietary versus common design data—and validating outputs. You'll learn practical tactics for increasing the trustworthiness of AI models, with a focus on real-world challenges like distinguishing proprietary intellectual property from common design elements and validating the accuracy of AI-generated outputs. We’ll explore assessing inputs, adding safeguards, and creating feedback loops to improve performance over time—so you can adopt and build AI responsibly without sacrificing quality or compliance.
speakers: Ousama Lakhdar-Ghazal, Director, Trusted AI & Privacy, Autodesk

title: Dr. Vibe: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Start Loving Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: This is a tale from a BIM manager’s foray into vibe coding—going from having no coding experience to building web applications that tap into the Autodesk Platform Services APIs to supercharge the capabilities of our Autodesk Forma-based CAD managers. Have you been curious about Autodesk Platform Services but haven’t pulled the trigger because you’re not “a developer”? With Dr. Claude’s help, you can be! Come to this session to learn tips on diving into the world of Autodesk Platform Services and large language models (LLMs). We’ll share lessons learned on working hand in hand with these LLMs in a safe and efficient way so that you can also share in this digital boon.
speakers: Winston Pagliaro, Civil Infrastructure BIM and VDC Specialist, HNTB

title: Eaton and Trane: 1-GW Data Center Codesign with BIM and Autodesk Forma
abstract: This class will showcase how Trane, Eaton, and Autodesk enable collaborative codesign for gigawatt-scale data centers using BIM and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). You will see how data center reference kits become live, cloud-based environments for real-time collaboration between owners, engineers, and contractors. These environments centralize BIM and engineering data into a shared source of truth, enabling coordinated design of mechanical and electrical systems at massive scale. The session will demonstrate how Autodesk Forma Build supports structured codesign workflows, role-based collaboration, and asset-centered data models. This approach enables faster iteration, reduced risk, and scalable delivery for data centers of 1 gigawatt capacity.
speakers: Justin Carron, Director of Segment Marketing, Eaton
Matt Lemay, Principal Account Executive, Enterprise, Autodesk
Victor Mirasola, General Manager - TRACE, Trane Technologies

title: EDU1455 Unlock the power of AI for AutoCAD 2027 Toolsets
abstract: Unlock the full potential of AI in AutoCAD 2027 toolsets. Building on our AU 2024 award-winning class, this session will explore how AI-powered tools revolutionize CAD, driving unmatched efficiency. Experience how AutoCAD 2027 software’s AI automates complex workflows—from intelligent object recognition and predictive drafting to real-time generative design. With automated dimensioning, predictive error-correction, and material optimization, you’ll slash design cycles. Use AI-driven simulation to stress-test designs against real-world scenarios, ensuring peak performance. Transform your workflow with seamless, AI-enhanced interoperability that bridges multidisciplinary teams. Future-proof your craft with smarter, faster, and more creative CAD.
speakers: Lina El-Khoury, BIM Strategy & Digital Solutions Consultant, LEK
Hung Nguyen, Technical Consultant, SolidCAD

title: End-to-End Drainage Design with Forma, InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
abstract:
InfoDrainage and Autodesk Forma will soon work together as part of a connected workflow for site drainage design. In this session, you'll work with Civil 3D and InfoDrainage models hosted in Forma, using live references such as surfaces and CAD background data to keep design information connected across applications. 

 Starting from a site design, you'll develop and optimize a drainage network in InfoDrainage, leveraging connected site data to accelerate hydrologic design. 

 The workflow continues with dynamic hydraulic simulation, exceedance assessment, and review of results, followed by compliance-ready reporting. The session concludes by synchronizing the completed drainage design back to Civil 3D, demonstrating a streamlined, connected workflow from site model to validated drainage design.
speakers: Javier Soto, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: End-to-End New Geolocation Solution Across Autodesk Platforms: From Civil 3D to Revit
abstract: Geolocation is essential for accurate positioning, data integration, and interoperability across architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) workflows. This session will introduce core concepts such as coordinate systems, datums, and spatial references—and show how they’re applied across Autodesk platforms. You will learn how to create and manage coordinate systems in Civil 3D software, define geolocation in Civil 3D and AutoCAD software, and understand how these support geographic information system (GIS) integration. The session will also cover legacy and modern geolocation workflows in Revit software, highlighting improvements in model alignment and interoperability. By connecting workflows across Civil 3D and Revit, this class will provide practical guidance on maintaining consistent geospatial positioning throughout a project’s lifecycle.
speakers: Frank Huang, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: Engineering Copilot: Real AI Workflows for Vault, BOMs, and Manufacturing Data
abstract: AI is everywhere—but how does it actually help engineering teams working with CAD, BOMs, and Vault software? This class will demonstrate real-world applications of AI on top of Vault, focusing on engineering and manufacturing processes. Using live examples, we’ll show how structured data such as eBOMs and mBOMs can be interpreted, transformed, and enriched using AI while keeping engineers in control. You’ll see how natural-language interfaces, rule-based automation, and AI-assisted decision making support tasks like BOM transformation, process planning, and validation. The session will highlight proven architectures, integration patterns, and limitations when introducing AI into Vault-based environments.
speakers: Christian Gessner, Head of Research and Innovation, coolOrange S.r.l.
Tyler Warner, Sr. Software Developer, IMAGINiT Technologies

title: Expo
abstract:
This is where AU comes to life.

Step inside the AU Expo and experience the future of design and make in motion. See live demos of Autodesk’s newest product offerings, connect with the Autodesk Community, recharge and network in our lounges, and explore breakthrough solutions from hundreds of innovative sponsors.

Whether you’re shaping buildings, infrastructure, teams, or transformation strategies, the Expo is your place to discover what’s next—and meet the people making it happen.

And don’t miss the AU Quest: a fun, interactive way to explore, connect, and uncover the best of the Expo.

Come curious. Leave inspired.

title: Expo Reception
abstract: Wrap up day one at the AU Expo Reception—an evening of great conversations, new connections with fellow attendees, and an opportunity to expand your professional network in a relaxed, social setting. Grab a drink and some snacks as you explore the showcase to discover the latest innovations and ideas all designed to inspire your next big breakthrough.

times.room: Venetian, Expo Hall C - Reception, level 2

title: Fall in Love with the Problem: Redefining Visual Storytelling
abstract:
The way we visualise and tell stories has evolved from static 2D rendering, to real-time 3D, to AI. The underlying problem these technologies serve has never gone away; it has changed shape as the needs of the industry have evolved.

In this session you will hear from Lumion’s Head of Product and explore the new ways of addressing, validating and building architectural solutions that are guided by customer feedback and experience.

As a live case study you will experience Project Compass, a brand new Lumion product being shown to the public for the first time at AU, which addresses an intrinsically important stage of the visual communication pipeline in your architecture portfolio. You will follow the whole journey, from ideation, identifying the problem, exploring the solution space, and most importantly validating the outcome with the wider industry.
speakers: David Weir-McCall, Head of Product, Lumion

title: First to the Chow Bowl: How Claiming Your Spot and Data Early Pays Off Throughout Coordination
abstract: Electrical VDC teams routinely enter coordination late, racing to populate models while other trades claim space first. This talk shows how Owen Electric used AI-powered conduit routing to shift that dynamic across three complex jobs in three months. Instead of manually entering electrical data, the team embedded that information from the start and then explored routing options allowing for faster decisions and optimal layout. The result: modeling time cut in half, tens of thousands of feet of conduit populated, in days rather than weeks, returning time back to specs, submittals, and constructability reviews. Attendees leave with a framework to walk into the first coordination meeting fully populated as well as practical tactics to build infill data early so a lean team can take on bigger, more complex scope and meaningfully grow capacity.
speakers: Aaron Szymanski, Chief Product Officer, Augmenta

title: Forma to Energy: AI-Powered Workflows for Carbon Insight
abstract: Energy and carbon analysis often arrives too late—after key decisions have been made. Despite tools like Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight software, most teams rely on manual, disconnected workflows that limit iteration. This session will introduce a connected, data-driven approach. By embedding performance data in BIM and using AI to generate simulation logic, teams can automatically produce carbon and energy analyses—earlier, more frequently, and without deep simulation expertise. Through a live demo, you’ll see design data flow from Autodesk Forma through Revit into automated workflows and into Insight for actionable results. Attend this class to learn how to replace one-off analysis with scalable, repeatable carbon workflows.
speakers: Tetsuya Hishida, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato
Chris Balbach, Director of R&D, Performance Systems Development of NY, LLC

title: From 2D to Digital Twin: Connecting Design to Oper
abstract: Retail construction still relies heavily on fragmented 2D documentation, creating a disconnect between design, construction, and operations. This session will explore how EssilorLuxottica is transforming that model by converting 2D assets into structured 3D BIM and building a connected digital lifecycle. By linking design data to Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and maintenance workflows, stores evolve from static deliverables into dynamic, data-driven digital twins. This session will present a scalable approach to connect design to operations, improve asset visibility, and enable predictive maintenance, turning retail environments into fully integrated intelligent assets.
speakers: Enrico Trovato, Head of AECO Automation & Intelligence, EssilorLuxottica

title: From AutoCAD Toolsets to Inventor: Enabling Connected Workflows with Desktop Connector and Forma
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD Electrical electromechanical workflows, AutoCAD Mechanical linked with Inventor software, and factory design workflows for seamless data exchange. Learn how to integrate layouts and models across tools, enabling accurate coordination from schematics to 3D design. Discover how cloud-based solutions like Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma improve collaboration, maintain data continuity, and reduce rework. Through practical examples, see how connected workflows enhance efficiency and accelerate project delivery.
speakers: Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Autodesk Forma to IFC Compliance: Automating BIM Validation in Railway Projects
abstract: Ensuring BIM data quality in railway infrastructure projects remains a challenge due to manual checks, inconsistent requirements, and lack of standardization. This session will present a real-world workflow using Civil 3D software for railway design, integrated with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), to automate IFC model validation using IDS. Starting from structured tabular requirements, we’ll demonstrate how to generate IDS files using Python and apply automated validation workflows. We’ll also compare this approach with commercial solutions and highlight trade-offs in scalability, control, and collaboration. Attendees will learn how to reduce manual effort, improve data consistency, and implement a scalable openBIM validation process for infrastructure projects.
speakers: Thiago Dantas, Project Manager, TPF
Juliana Scanoni, Innovation Manager, TPF
Juliana Scanoni
Melissa Yamada, BIM Manager, TPF Engenharia

title: From a Work-Around to a Real Workflow: Duct Bank Design in Civil 3D
abstract: Designing duct banks in Civil 3D software can be challenging due to limited out-of-the-box tools for multiconduit systems. This class will present a practical workflow for creating, managing, and visualizing duct banks using surfaces, corridor assemblies, and custom subassemblies and pipe network structures. You’ll go over custom duct bank subassemblies using Subassembly Composer, learning how to model subsurface duct banks, use the duct banks in construction documents, and export the models to Revit or Navisworks software to coordinate with other disciplines.
speakers: Vincent Sheehan, Sr. Designer, Timmons Group

title: From Borehole to Building: Advanced Ground Modeling Directly in Civil 3D with GeoDin Ground
abstract: Ground models are the missing link between site investigation and infrastructure design. Engineers make critical decisions on alignments, crossings, and foundations while the subsurface remains a black box—data arriving late, locked in static reports, or in formats incompatible with the design environment. GeoDin Ground for Civil 3D software is changing that. In this session, we’ll present the latest advances in 3D ground modeling inside Civil 3D, including direct AGS file ingestion and autoconversion—eliminating the need for a preexisting database and letting teams start directly with received data. You’ll see the ground take shape inside Civil 3D, evolving into a 3D model that drives critical design choices and reduces project risk from day one.
speakers: Devrez Karabacak, Head of Product, GeoDin, Fugro

title: From Capture to AI: How Data Enrichment Unlocks the Value of Motion
abstract: AI-powered animation is only as good as the data behind it, but most motion data wasn’t designed for AI. In this session, we’ll demonstrate a projection-mapped capture app that guides performers in real time to produce more-structured motion. As well as how Label Maker, a tool integrated within the Autodesk ecosystem, uses AI to turn raw motion data and videos into richly tagged, reusable data sets. You will walk away with a clearer picture of how to make motion data actually usable for AI, and how to rethink their pipelines to get there. The real value of motion data isn’t in the capture—it’s in the enrichment.
speakers: Olivier Zurcher, Animation Researcher (Technical Animator), Autodesk

title: From Change to Clarity: Better Multidiscipline Coordination Model in Revit and Autodesk Forma Data Management
abstract: Discover how to effectively use Revit software’s Coordination Model Changes to monitor and manage updates across disciplines. In this hands-on session, architects and engineers will learn practical methods to detect, review, and act on element changes directly within their models. The session will cover step-by-step workflows for identifying additions, deletions, and modifications, using visual cues, filters, and structured object data. You’ll also explore how to assess geometry, properties, and transformations of updated elements to support better decision making. By the end, you’ll be able to reduce manual coordination effort, improve accuracy, and confidently integrate change tracking into your daily Revit workflows.
speakers: Mihaela Stan, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
Leslaw Janus, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk

title: ​From Chaos to Control: ACC Model Coordination and API Strategies for Infrastructure Projects
abstract: In large-scale infrastructure, "coordination chaos" is a common reality. When teams use different tools and inconsistent methods, design mistakes are often caught too late. This leads to expensive rework, missed deadlines, and increased project risk. As projects grow across disciplines, keeping everyone aligned becomes a massive challenge. In this session, we’ll share how Ramboll tamed this complexity by building a standardized, scalable framework using Autodesk Forma industry cloud (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Using the 2025 IFC Viewer, Autodesk Platform Services, and Insight dashboards, Ramboll moved from disconnected software to a single, unified system. We’ve aligned our digital process with ISO 19650 to ensure data moves smoothly from one project phase to the next.
speakers: Maria Albízuri, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Adrian Fernandez Sanchez, Product Owner Autodesk Transport, Rambøll Norge

title: From Classroom to Jobsite: Building Design-to-Make Curriculum with Autodesk
abstract: How do you turn Design-to-Make workflows into job-ready curriculum? This panel brings together JARC, SEAF, Bechtel, and Autodesk to show how Fusion, Revit, and Autodesk Forma power scalable workforce training. Through real-world examples, see how learners move from concept modeling to fabrication and site execution using the same tools and data as in industry. Panelists will share how curriculum is structured, how employer input shapes projects, and how digital workflows enable delivery. Attendees will gain practical models to align training with production workflows and improve job readiness.
speakers: Kate McElligott, Workforce Innovation & Investment Lead, Autodesk
Jovan Madjovski, Vice President, CEED Global SME Green Advancement Initiative
Regan Brewer, President, Jane Addams Resource Corporation
Agata Zytniak, Senior Automation Engineer and Information Manager, Bechtel

title: From Construction to Operations: Delivering a Seamless Handover
abstract: This session explains how Lantis—client of a €10 billion infraproject—prepares a seamless and data‑rich handover from construction to operations and maintenance (O&M) by combining Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Datum, the Autodesk Data Model, and Autodesk Tandem software. Discover how structured asset requirements, Autodesk Forma‑based data validation, automated property mapping, and federated model workflows ensure consistent, complete, and BIM‑to‑O&M‑ready information. Investing in asset lifecycle management has a potential ROI of €40.74 million. Learn how Lantis uses open standards, QA/QC automation, and twin‑based asset structuring to transition thousands of deliverables into a usable digital twin ecosystem that supports long‑term maintenance, inspection, and operations.
speakers: Yanissa De Jonghe, Head of Digital & Data, Lantis
Guillaume Neyrinck, Senior Technical Success Manager, Autodesk

title: From Data Exchange to Spatial Computing: Building Immersive Autodesk Platform Services Experiences
abstract: Explore how Autodesk Platform Services enables a new class of immersive design applications. This session will dive into the Autodesk Data Exchange API and the Geometry Utilities SDK, showing how to extract, transform, and stream architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data into custom 3D experiences. Using a real-world example on Apple Vision Pro, we’ll demonstrate how subsets of Revit models can be converted into lightweight, queryable geometry and rendered in spatial computing environments. You’ll gain practical insights into data pipelines, geometry processing, and performance considerations for building production-ready immersive apps on top of Autodesk Platform Services.
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk
Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk

title: From Design Intent to Preconstruction Reality: Closing the Carbon Data Handover Gap
abstract: Decarbonization is accelerating across the built environment, yet the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry lacks consistent ways to manage carbon data across project phases. Through a collaboration led by the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) and Autodesk, 11 leading AEC firms are working to define and improve how carbon data transitions from design to preconstruction. Based on applied learnings, this panel will examine data challenges in the preconstruction handoff, including gaps in material quantities, nonmodeled elements, specifications, and assumptions—and we’ll highlight emerging best practices and recommendations. Gain practical strategies for your projects and ways to improve carbon data consistency, transparency, and decision making across phases.
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk

title: From Emerging Tech to Enterprise Adoption: Autodesk & Arcadis Shaping the Future of AEC
abstract: How does a 36,000-person design and engineering firm decide what new technology is worth adopting? In this fireside chat, leaders from Autodesk and Arcadis discuss what it really takes to introduce emerging tools into a global AEC practice. The conversation covers the promise of Autodesk Forma Site Design and Building Design, and a candid look at how both parties are testing and shaping these products together.

title: From Fragmented Inputs to Actionable Design Intent
abstract: Design teams rarely start with a complete and coherent requirements package. Instead, they work with fragmented inputs such as briefs, standards, legacy specifications, expert assumptions, performance targets, and evolving stakeholder constraints. This session will explore how AI-enabled workflows—combining information normalization, uncertainty quantification, human-in-the-loop review, retrieval-augmented generation, threshold-based routing, and decomposition/aggregation—can convert incomplete information into actionable, traceable design intent. Although developed in product design and simulation, the insights directly transfer across industries.
speakers: Nigel Morris, Sr. Manager, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: From Fragmented Workflows to a Digital Thread: Scaling Modular Construction with PLM at Faith
abstract: Faith Technologies Incorporated (FTI) is rapidly scaling its modular construction and manufacturing operations. But disconnected systems, manual workflows, and poor data governance created barriers to growth. In partnership with Symetri, Faith is implementing a PLM-driven digital thread connecting Vault software, Autodesk Fusion Manage, Inventor software, and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) systems. This transformation enables centralized data, automated design-to-fabrication workflows, and enterprise collaboration. This session will explore how Faith is moving from siloed processes to a connected, scalable ecosystem to accelerate productization and support rapid growth.
speakers: Darren Hartenstine, Senior Solutions Consultant, Symetri USA
Caleb Goins, Application Support Manager, FTI

title: From Good Intentions to Sustainable Decisions
abstract: Most sustainability strategies never make it into daily work. Teams struggle to turn ambition into decisions, data flows, and repeatable processes. This session will explore three sustainability workflows that are actually working today: design-phase carbon estimation, AI-enabled inspection, and material selection informed by connected product and carbon data. We’ll examine how these workflows are structured, where they break, and what it takes to implement them across tools, teams, and data sources—drawing on examples from technology partners such as One Click LCA and VAPAR. You’ll leave with a practical framework for turning sustainability goals into operational workflows.
speakers: Becky Burns, Sustainability Technical Partner Program Manager, Autodesk
Amarpreet Singh, Team Lead, North America, One Click LCA
Michelle Aguilar, CTO, VAPAR

title: From Innovyze to Tandem: Digital Twins & AI for Climate‑Resilient Water Infrastructure
abstract: Water infrastructure is entering a decisive decade. In 2026, utilities face climate volatility, aging assets, regulatory pressure, and rising expectations for resilient, transparent service. Traditional approaches based on static hydraulic models and reactive operations are no longer sufficient. This keynote will explore how connected digital twins and AI are reshaping water infrastructure across the full lifecycle—from planning and design to operations and maintenance. It will present a practical workflow showing how Innovyze modeling outputs evolve into a live operational digital twin in Autodesk Tandem software, enabling continuity from design to asset maintenance, and supporting predictive, risk‑based decision making.
speakers: Priyanka Talkal, Associate-Water, WSP

title: From Inventor Design to Machined Part: Building a Real Digital Thread with Autodesk Fusion CAM
abstract: In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a real machined project designed in Inventor and programmed in Autodesk Fusion Manufacturing Extension. Follow the complete workflow: creating and iterating the part in Inventor, uploading to Fusion, applying toolpaths, generating G-code, and efficiently updating toolpaths after design changes using simple refreshes. We’ll cover both the cloud approach (AnyCAD linked references and Desktop Connector) and the enterprise version using Vault Professional software for controlled releases and revision management. We’ll share the actual files, challenges encountered, key lessons, and measurable time savings. You’ll leave with actionable steps to build an effective digital thread between design and manufacturing teams.
speakers: Edward Rose, Client Success Manager - Adoption Programs, Symetri

title: From Legacy to Next Generation: Modernizing HEC-RAS Model Libraries into Cloud-Ready InfoWorks ICM
abstract: Many water authorities have built extensive HEC-RAS model libraries that remain valuable but are hard to standardize, scale, and adapt. This session will show how Türkiye’s General Directorate of Water Management is transforming legacy river models into a next-generation InfoWorks ICM environment for higher precision, performance, and future cloud use. We will outline a modernization strategy covering geometry transfer, standardization, terrain integration, and numerical stability. A benchmark shows improvement: 1 million cells, diffusion wave, 173 hours versus 7.5 million cells, shallow water, 22 hours. The result is faster, more accurate, and operational—enabling automation, scalability, and real-time readiness.
speakers: Mustafa DAL, HEAD OF DEPARTMENT, GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF WATER MANAGEMENT
Cihat ADSIZ, Section Manager, General Directorate of Water Management
Özgüray AYDIN, General Manager, Viasu Teknoloji

title: From Massing to Metrics: Integrating Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights for Outcome-Based Design
abstract: Around 80% of a building’s environmental impact is determined in the first 20% of design, yet this phase often relies on intuition rather than data. This presentation will introduce GHD’s outcome-based workflow that embeds predictive AI and cloud simulation into early design, providing carbon insights when decisions matter. Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) enables real-time evaluation of wind, thermal comfort, and early embodied carbon from simple massing models. As designs progress, Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (formerly Autodesk Insight) calculates energy-use intensity and examines trade-offs between operational and embodied carbon. The result is an iterative, data-driven approach that integrates carbon performance into design and enables credible sustainability narratives from project inception.
speakers: Jessica Carson, Architect, GHD Design
Isaac McCormack, Architect, GHD Design
Michael from Chile Sturm, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: From Messy to Meaningful: Ground Truth, Update-Ready Site Context in Revit
abstract: Accurate site context is essential for coordination, yet many teams struggle with fragile or inconsistent site models in Revit. This session presents reliable workflows for building and maintaining site context using common upstream sources, including Forma Site Design generated Revit files, Civil 3D published surfaces, and native Revit tools such as TopoSolids and Building Pads. The focus is on stability and change management – showing how to keep site models update ready as upstream data evolves, while supporting design development, visualization, and downstream coordination with minimal rework or model failure. We'll walk through four practical workflows for bringing site context into Revit and discuss where each one shines and where each one breaks.
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec
Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec

title: From Model to Diagram: Automating Electrical One-Line Generation in Revit
abstract: Clear diagrams are critical for translating MEP designs into something contractors can build in the field. However, creating those diagrams is often a slow, manual process—drawing connection lines, placing detail items, and constantly checking the diagram against the model. Electrical one-line diagrams are prime examples, regularly taking several hours to draft for each project. What if that process could happen automatically? This session will demonstrate how you can use model data to generate clean, accurate one-line diagrams with the click of a button. Using pyRevit as the backdrop, we’ll walk through the process of transforming structured model information into fully drafted diagrams—reducing hours of manual drafting down to seconds.
speakers: Zach Bratcher, AI Integrator, DBR Engineering

title: From More Data to Better Data: Rethinking Information in AEC
abstract: Join Eddy Krygiel from AEC Data Strategy on this episode of the Digital Builder podcast to explore why more data doesn’t automatically mean better data. Learn how AEC firms and owners are tackling the challenge of managing information quality at scale, the growing role of data specialists and more intentional approaches to keeping information accurate and aligned, and why trusted data is becoming essential as AI and automation create new opportunities across AEC.

title: From Pilot to Competitive Advantage: Scaling Generative Design with Autodesk Forma and Infraspace
abstract:
Infrastructure projects face increasing demands for faster delivery, lower costs, and more sustainable outcomes. Meeting these demands requires teams to work smarter, deliver higher-quality designs, and make better decisions within tight project deadlines.

Following last year's session, Infraspace and Norconsult will share how they have moved from promising pilots to production use of generative design in real transportation and energy projects.

Powered by Infraspace and integrated with Autodesk Forma, they will demonstrate how engineering teams can streamline planning and early design, and reduce iteration time from weeks to minutes through automated generation of design alternatives for roads and other infrastructure assets.

Through real-world project examples, you will learn how generative design augments engineering expertise, improves project outcomes, and provides a competitive advantage through faster, better-informed design decisions.
speakers: Kristoffer Spendrup Bugge, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult
Andreas Kjølseth, Founder & CEO, Infraspace

title: From PlanGrid to Platform: How a Specialty Contractor Built an Enterprise Data Strategy on Autodesk Forma
abstract: When we, one of the larger MEP design-build contractors on the US West Coast, decided to replace PlanGrid, our mission was clear: We want to update our tool suite, and quickly standardize data quality across all projects. But a platform decision is more than just a tool swap. This session will walk you through the generalized strategic framework that we used to evaluate, select, and roll out Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) as the enterprise backbone for both office and field teams. Learn how a three-stage rollout from exploration, a year-long pilot with rigorous standardization, and a fine-tuned enterprise deployment delivered measurable results: unified dashboards, and a data foundation that helps us to build custom solutions with Autodesk Platform Services.
speakers: Niklas Janetzky, Technology Strategy Manager, Pan-Pacific Mechanical

title: From Plant Design to Product Passport: Extending PLM and Autodesk Fusion Manage Across the Full Lifecycle
abstract: By 2027, every manufacturer selling into the European market will be required to provide a Digital Product Passport (DPP)—and most are not ready. This session will show how Autodesk Fusion Manage software can close that gap, while also solving a longer-standing problem: disconnected data between process plant design and PLM. You'll see how equipment data from AutoCAD Plant 3D projects on Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) can automatically populate Fusion Manage BOMs—eliminating manual handoffs between plant design and PLM. And you’ll see how that same structure can generate EU-compliant DPPs on demand, without duplicate data entry—connecting project context from Autodesk Forma with product lifecycle data where it belongs. Both extensions are built on Autodesk Platform Services APIs and demonstrated live.
speakers: Zoé Bezpalko, Sr. Manager, Sustainability Innovations, Autodesk
Andreas Nicolescu, Principal Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: From Plan to Pour: Aurigo Primus Plan and Autodesk Forma for Asset Owners
abstract: Bridge the gap between capital planning and project execution. Led by Aurigo's director of product, this technical deep dive will explore Primus Plan and its powerful integration with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll showcase our AI-powered what-if scenario planning, demonstrating how to optimize multi-year capital portfolios before pushing them to downstream construction management. Walk through the technical architecture and data flows that move infrastructure projects from early-stage planning straight into execution within Autodesk Forma. Learn how to eliminate data silos, maximize funding, and maintain total visibility across the entire project lifecycle.
speakers: Johann Potgieter,  Director of Product, Aurigo Software Technology

title: From Prompts to Project Outcomes: Using Autodesk Assistant in Autodesk Forma
abstract: AI is now embedded directly into Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) through Autodesk Assistant. But its real value comes from how it improves decisions, not just how it responds to prompts. This session will show how to use Autodesk Assistant in real workflows, grounded in the shared data and industry context that power Autodesk Forma. Through practical examples, we’ll explore how teams can use AI to support design exploration, generate project insights, and streamline everyday tasks without leaving their workflows. You’ll learn how to structure effective prompts, refine responses, and build on outputs to turn AI-generated information into actionable decisions. We’ll also cover where Autodesk Assistant delivers the most value today and where its limitations lie.
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend
Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+

title: From Prompt to Production: Designing Furniture at the Speed of AI with Fusion
abstract: Designing and manufacturing furniture often relies on disconnected tools and repetitive work. This session will explain how to create a connected, end-to-end workflow using the Autodesk Fusion platform. Starting from simple prompts, Autodesk Assistant accelerates design and enables fast creation of parametric furniture models. This workflow will show how models are refined for engineering, prepared for manufacturing with integrated CAM tools, and transferred to production using Autodesk Fusion Operations software—while Autodesk Fusion Manage ensures process and data continuity from request to delivery. It will also highlight how design intent is preserved and how a single data environment reduces errors.
speakers: Melike Ozdemir, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Reality to Simulation: Capturing, Predicting & Replaying the Experience of Design with APS & AI
abstract: How do you capture or predict the human experience of design and replay it to build empathy and drive better design decisions? This session will present a technical workflow spanning three research projects: real-world experience capture (The Bentway, Toronto), XR-based capture in virtual environments, and agentic simulation of human behavior. Learn how Autodesk Platform Services powers a system where human-experience data—whether captured using sensors, or in VR, or predicted using AI—can be replayed by designers to better appreciate the diversity of the human experience of design. We’ll explore the technology that will power future human-experience-driven workflows, from sensors and VR headsets to knowledge graphs and vision language models.
speakers: Kean Walmsley, Dir., Systems Design/Architecture Engrg, Autodesk

title: From Revit Projects and Simple Renderings to Interactive and Immersive VR Apps
abstract: Project presentations in AutoCAD or Revit software are essential for the technical development of construction. However, what truly captivates the end client is the visual experience. Today, simple renders or videos are no longer enough. The real difference is telling a story through the project or allowing the client to explore the environment interactively, visiting and engaging with the space through virtual reality or immersive applications. This transforms the presentation into a memorable and engaging experience.
speakers: ALAN ARAUJO, Architect, Bee1

title: From Revit Stills to Stories: AI Video Workflows for Architectural Communication
abstract: Architects increasingly need to communicate design intent through motion before there is time or budget for traditional animation and for audiences who do not read drawings. This session shows how approved design assets from Revit based rendering views, diagrams, sketches, physical model, photos, can become short AI-assisted motion assets for design reviews, competitions, and client presentations. Attendees will learn a repeatable still-to-video workflow, see where AI video supports architectural communication and where it falls short, and apply QA guardrails for review and trust before using outputs in practice. A 5 minute case study assembled from 30 AI-assisted clips will also demonstrate how short generations become a coherent story.
speakers: Qian Huang, Design Technology Specialist, HOK

title: Full Project Delivery with Autodesk Forma Build: From CDE to QA/QC, EDMS, and Handover
abstract: Project delivery is often fragmented across systems, with disconnected data between common data environments (CDEs), QA/QC, electronic document management systems (EDMSs), and handover processes creating inefficiencies and delays. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma Build enables full project delivery through a connected data platform, integrating workflows across RFIs, Submittals, NCRs, snags, scheduling, and QA/QC closeout. You’ll learn how to structure and manage data from design through construction to achieve progressive closeout and successful handover. Real-world examples will demonstrate how connected workflows improve data quality, reduce rework, and enable earlier, more reliable project completion.
speakers: Juan Camilo VALDES, Digital Engineering & Quality Lead, HEB (Vinci)
William L. Guauque Castaneda, Digital Delivery Manager, HEB Construction - VINCI NZ

title: General Contractor Meetup
abstract: Join us in a session designed to connect general contractors around the United States so they can exchange best practices, wins, and lessons learned that enhance the construction customer experience. This is a place to network with like-minded contractors and owners to share ideas and dive deeper into workflows you wouldn’t normally find in an Autodesk webinar. We want to connect YOU with your peers to elevate the way you manage your facilities, helping Autodesk create the most valuable tool for your needs—based on your feedback, presented by your peers.
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk
LaShawn Hodge, Principal Account Services Rep, Autodesk
Jared McKibben, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Get Connected: Simplify Navigation of Project Tools for Everyone
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore how trade contractors can provide streamlined navigation to the applications and platforms used by field, project management, and safety teams, ensuring each team member can easily obtain and share the information needed to perform their roles. We’ll review the solution Cupertino Electric uses on our projects, and outline the core functionality required to replicate this approach, regardless of vendor or specific products.
speakers: Kelli Lubeley, Construction Technology Manager, Cupertino Electric Inc

title: Get started with iLogic Configuration - Learn Configurator workflows by Building one
abstract: Change a few parameters and watch your Inventor model reconfigure itself! Configuration is the dream! However, applying configurations to some models can be migraine-inducing. Let’s start with assemblies built for configuration. In this hands-on lab, you’ll experience assemblies prepared for configuration from the beginning. Through guided exercises, you’ll explore model-building best practices for configuration with Inventor iLogic. You'll experience driving top-down design changes, adding and removing components, and learning how to incorporate Model States and iLogic. You’ll leave with an understanding of model configuration best practices, including checklists and guidance to apply to your own configuration projects.
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk

title: Get the Most Out of the Drainage Tools in Civil 3D
abstract: Moving data back and forth between multiple design and modeling programs can be time-consuming and prone to error. The Civil 3D drainage design environment addresses this by allowing engineers to model complete stormwater systems in one place. This session will demonstrate a practical workflow for building a drainage network using the rainfall manager, catchments, channels, ponds, and underground storage components. You’ll learn how to define rainfall events, generate runoff through catchments, create storage and conveyance elements, and run hydraulic analyses to evaluate system performance.
speakers: Brian Hailey, CAD Manager, GEI Consultants

title: Get Workforce Ready with Autodesk Certifications!
abstract: Certification is more than a badge—it’s a signal of capability and a demonstration of skills applied in real industry workflows. Employers are looking for people who can step into projects and make an impact. As tools and workflows continue to evolve especially with the growing influence of AI- demonstrating applied capability is becoming even more important. That’s why certification is shifting from a one-time milestone to something more continuous part of how professionals build, demonstrate, and validate their skills over time. We will explore how to navigate Autodesk certifications from foundational to professional levels, align them to career goals, and use preparation to build skills that translate into effectiveness on the job.
speakers: Dania Eter, Principal Autodesk Certification Program, Autodesk

title: Global Autodesk Group Network (AGN) Digital Meetup
abstract: Want to learn more about our Autodesk Group Network program? Whether you're looking to start a new group or help your existing one grow and gain visibility, join our session hosted by Sam Karas, Community Program Manager.

title: Go Slow to Go Fast: Dome Construction’s Real-World Roadmap to Autodesk Forma Build
abstract: Dome Construction's transition to Forma Build wasn't planned; it was driven by clients. As owners across Life Sciences, Technology, and Foodtech began requiring Autodesk Build, the question quickly shifted from if to how fast. Leadership set a two-year mandate. This session shares Dome's real journey from pilot to rollout: uncovering platform gaps, navigating commercial strategy, and building a change approach grounded in "doing it right." Instead of rushing, Dome adopted a Lean mindset (go slow to go fast) waiting for field readiness before go-live. Through close collaboration with Autodesk, Dome is shaping a practical, experiential roadmap for contractors facing similar mandates, backed by real lessons and early results from live projects.
speakers: John Mack, Construction Technology Consultant, Dome Construction
Jason Dodds, Principal Business Consultant, Construction, CDE & Data Strategy, Autodesk

title: How AI Agents are reshaping the way AEC works
abstract: Architecture and engineering firms are going agentic. The ones moving now will set the pace for everyone else. This session will get into what that actually means for your practice, with a concrete plan you can act on immediately. An agent isn't a smarter chatbot. It's a system you give instructions, skills, tools, and context—and then trust to do real work. Chello, Mosaic's AI planning assistant, shows what that looks like in practice: it watches project deadlines, catches scope creep before it eats your profit, forecasts workload and revenue, and keeps the whole firm's plan current, so leadership is always in control and never caught off guard. We'll cover how agents connect to your existing systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP), how to capture your firm's expertise so it scales across every team member, and when to build versus buy. The firms that get this right will operate at a level their competitors can't match. This session will be your starting point.
speakers: John Meyer, Founder & CEO, Mosaic

title: How Cleveland Construction Added AI-Powered Submittal and Drawing Reviews to Autodesk Forma
abstract: When Cleveland Construction migrated from Procore to Autodesk, company leaders saw an opportunity to build an intelligent document pipeline and agentic workflows on top of the wealth of data they run their business on in Autodesk. In this session, Elliot Christiansen, SVP of operations at Cleveland Construction, will share how his team configured their Autodesk environment to enable AI-powered workflows that automatically review submittals against specs and new bulletins against previous ones. Brandon Ramsey, VP of customer success from Trunk Tools, an App Marketplace Partner, will join Elliot to share Cleveland's winning playbook to transition from handshakes to driving deep adoption across their project teams.
speakers: Elliot Christiansen, Sr. Vice President of Operations, Cleveland Construction, Inc.

title: IFC 4.3 for Infrastructure: From Export to Digital Delivery
abstract: IFC 4.3 enables open data exchange for infrastructure, yet many teams struggle to turn IFC exports into information that projects can rely on. This session will move beyond export steps and focus on using IFC effectively on infrastructure projects. You’ll learn how IFC 4.3 works once it leaves Civil 3D software, including how models are governed, versioned, reviewed, and trusted. Topics will include model view definitions, the IFC Reference View for civil infrastructure, and common mistakes that reduce value. The session will also introduce Autodesk Forma Data Management as a practical way to manage IFC delivery at scale, supporting controlled sharing and review. You’ll leave with guidance on positioning IFC as a trusted project resource.
speakers: Morgan Smith, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Salwan Abbosh, IDT Lead, Ramboll

title: Industrialized Construction at Scale: Data-Driven Sustainability for Modular Systems
abstract: How can industrialized construction, intelligent data, and integrated workflows turn sustainability from a reporting burden into a scalable design strategy? In this session for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) leaders and delivery teams, Max Bögl Group will share how one company manages the value chain—from raw material sourcing and design to off-site production, delivery, assembly, and maintenance—to deliver modular buildings and bridge systems with measurable sustainability outcomes. As we use projects from Germany and the Netherlands, you’ll see how standardized, parametric products, connected models, and automated assessments help teams compare options faster, respond to strict European requirements, and build the data foundation for future AI-supported design decisions.
speakers: Mergim Hoti, BIM Specialist, Max Bögl Nederland B.V.

title: Innovators Stage | AECO Design Slam: Designing the Future of Event Cities
abstract: Can great urban design turn a global event into a permanent destination? Watch two teams compete live as they reimagine the corridor between Allegiant Stadium and the Las Vegas Strip into a climate-smart, hospitality-driven district designed for the FIFA World Cup™ and beyond. Using Autodesk Forma, Forma Building Design, sustainability analysis, and AI visualization, competitors will create bold concepts that improve mobility, enhance the fan experience, and deliver lasting value for residents and visitors. You'll see every decision happen live—and cast the vote that crowns the Design Slam champion.
speakers: Jake Storey, Manager, Field Events, AMER, Autodesk
Ali Nasiri, Director of Computational Design, Flad Architects
Thesla Collier, Design Technology Manager, HNTB

title: Innovators Stage | Preserving What Matters: Digital Innovation and the Future of Historic Stewardship
abstract: Historic landmarks carry memory, identity, and community—but preserving them is increasingly complex as age, climate, and visitor demand put new pressure on cultural sites. The session will open with the premiere of a short documentary offering an intimate look at Fallingwater, Frank Lloyd Wright’s architectural masterpiece, and the people, partnerships, and technology working together to preserve a UNESCO world heritage site. Following the screening,  Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystems Sales, Autodesk, will moderate a conversation to explore how craft, expertise, and connected technologies are transforming preservation from reactive repair to proactive, data-informed stewardship. Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, will share the realities of stewarding this iconic landmark and balancing preservation for future generations. Touf Hassoun, CEO of CASE Technologies, will discuss how reality capture, digital twins, and AI are helping preservation teams better understand and protect historic places. Ramesh Sridharan, Director of Reality Solutions, Autodesk will share Autodesk's perspective on how connected platforms, data, and emerging technologies are enabling new approaches to preserving our built heritage.
speakers: Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystem Sales, Autodesk
Ramesh Sridharan, Director, Reality Solutions, Autodesk
Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater
Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies

title: Innovators Stage | Preserving What Matters: Digital Innovation and the Future of Historic Stewardship
abstract:
Historic landmarks carry memory, identity, and community — but preserving them is increasingly complex as age, climate, and visitor demand put new pressure on cultural sites. Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, will share what it takes to steward one of Frank Lloyd Wright’s masterpieces for future generations. Touf Hassoun, CEO of Case Technologies, will discuss how reality capture, digital twins, and AI are helping preservation teams better understand and protect historic places. Autodesk Chief Customer Officer Elisabeth Zornes will moderate a conversation on how craft, expertise, and technology can move preservation from reactive repair to proactive, data-informed stewardship with innovation at the center.

Short documentary
speakers: Ramesh Sridharan, Director, Reality Solutions, Autodesk
Rachel Tuller, VP, Global Partner Ecosystem Sales, Autodesk
Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater
Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies

title: Innovators Stage | The Power of Storytelling in a Data-Driven World
abstract: Whether you're proposing a new product, presenting a design, or helping clients imagine a better future, storytelling is often what moves ideas from possibility to reality. In today's data-driven world, storytelling has become an essential skill for anyone who wants to gain influence, inspire action, and help others see what's possible. In this engaging session, Tom Kelley shares memorable examples from business, design, and innovation, along with practical techniques for transforming data and insights into stories that resonate with colleagues and decision-makers. Along the way, you'll have a live "thumbs up or thumbs down" moment, as you help decide which topic Tom explores next. You'll leave with practical storytelling tools and a fresh perspective on how compelling stories help turn promising ideas into reality by first helping other people imagine a future that doesn't yet exist.
speakers: Tom Kelley, Founder & Advisor, D4V (Design for Ventures)
