title: Innovators Stage | What Pacesetters know that others don’t: Insights from the 2027 State of Design & Make
abstract: Join Autodesk’s Vikram Dutt and a lively panel of customers as they unpack the most surprising findings from our fourth annual State of Design & Make report. We’ll challenge assumptions, debate what the data really means, and explore the trends shaping the future of AEC, design & manufacturing, and media & entertainment industries. See how the landscape is evolving, discover who’s pulling ahead, and find out whether your organization is keeping pace—or setting it.
speakers: Solomon Jagwe, 3D Artist/Creative Director, Sowl Studios
Vikram Dutt, Vice President, Industry & Portfolio Marketing, Autodesk
Hickiran Tolgay, Founding Partner, Codeo
Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD

title: Innovators Stage | What Pacesetters know that others don’t: Insights from the 2027 State of Design & Make
abstract: Join Autodesk’s Vikram Dutt and a lively panel of customers as they unpack the most surprising findings from our fourth annual State of Design & Make report. We’ll challenge assumptions, debate what the data really means, and explore the trends shaping the future of AEC, design & manufacturing, and media & entertainment industries. See how the landscape is evolving, discover who’s pulling ahead, and find out whether your organization is keeping pace—or setting it.
speakers: Solomon Jagwe, 3D Artist/Creative Director, Sowl Studios
Vikram Dutt, Vice President, Industry & Portfolio Marketing, Autodesk
Hickiran Tolgay, Founding Partner, Codeo
Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD

title: Inside Forma Building Design
abstract: What if building design could be more fluid, intelligent, and connected from the start? Get an inside look at Forma Building Design, Autodesk’s upcoming detailed design solution that brings intuitive modeling and integrated analytics together. Explore how teams can create purposeful designs with real-time performance insights and generative AI, work flexibly across parametric, manual, and AI-assisted tools, and bring BIM and non-BIM contributors together in one cloud workspace. Discover how integration with Revit helps teams transition smoothly to BIM, reducing rework while preserving design intent.

title: Inside the Factory Experience: How We Design Hands-On Manufacturing for AU
abstract: The Factory Experience gives AU attendees a hands-on way to build a simple electronic device—but creating that experience requires coordination across design, manufacturing, and delivery. This panel will bring together Autodesk and industry partners to share how the Factory Experience is conceived, developed, and brought to life on the expo floor. Panelists will discuss how teams align on design intent, navigate real-world production constraints, and deliver a scalable, repeatable experience for AU attendees. Topics will include cross-company collaboration, prototyping-to-production workflows, and the role of emerging technologies like AI. You’ll gain insight into how complex systems are transformed into engaging educational experiences.
speakers: Brittany Evans, Senior Technology Consultant, Autodesk
Phil Eichmiller, Principal SW Eng. Test, Autodesk
Jonathan Odom, Community Manager, Fusion, Autodesk
Rhett Moore, Director, Digital Design & Eng. Content, Avnet, Inc.
Brian DeSmith, Senior Solutions Engineer, Xometry

title: Integrated Real-Time MIDP using Autodesk Forma Reviews and Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: Keeping a Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP) accurate on live projects is one of the biggest challenges for BIM managers and project managers. Issuing incomplete or unreviewed deliverables puts contracts at risk. In this class, we’ll show how Autodesk Platform Services Webhooks and the Reviews tool in Autodesk Forma transform the MIDP into a live system that validates deliverable metadata against information requirements and confirms review status before submission. Using real project examples and proven metrics, we’ll show how this ensures 100% compliance with contractual deliverables, eliminates manual tracking, and mitigates the risk of noncompliant submissions. Join us to learn how to build a QA/QC system that keeps your MIDP accurate, connected, and audit ready.
speakers: Mateusz Lukasiewicz, Associate Director - Digital Technology, KEO International Consultants

title: Integrating Nature-Based Solutions in Civil 3D and
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are reshaping how civil teams deliver resilient water infrastructure. Yet integrating watershed-scale insights into detailed design remains a challenge. This session will show how The Nature Conservancy applied targeted training and InfraWorks and Civil 3D software to connect regional watershed analysis with site-level engineering workflows. Learn how to translate watershed data into design inputs, develop NbS concepts into constructible models, and maintain data continuity across planning and design phases. See how connected workflows improved cross-team collaboration, enabled earlier decision making, and reduced project risk in real-world water infrastructure projects.
speakers: Carlos Rogeliz, Technical Director – N4W Facility, The Nature Conservancy

title: Inventor Meetup: What’s Working, What’s Not, What’s Next
abstract: Do you want to talk about what’s working in Inventor, what creates friction, and what should come next? Join the Inventor Meetup for a conversation with Autodesk’s Inventor product team and fellow users. Share experiences, compare challenges, discuss workflow practices and solutions, and explore the future of Inventor through automation tasks (iLogic, drawings), Model States, Vault-connected workflows, Content Center and data governance, AI-assisted productivity, and performance at scale. Come for honest discussion, practical insight, fresh perspectives from peers, and the opportunity to influence future priorities for Inventor in a more direct, collaborative way. Whether you’re a long-time user or a newer voice, your perspective matters.
speakers: Dan Szymanski, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Riya Ghosh, Sr Customer Advocate, Autodesk

title: Lessons from AI-Driven Software Engineering That Can Improve Design and Make Productivity
abstract: As generative AI begins to automate software engineering, new principles are emerging that also apply to Design and Make processes. AI-enabled development shifts the focus toward clear requirements, structured documentation, and rigorous validation to guide and verify generated outputs. While execution becomes increasingly automated, professional oversight remains critical to ensure reliability and quality. This talk will explore how these lessons can transform Design and Make workflows—enabling faster design execution with AI while elevating the importance of design and manufacturing specifications, thoughtful application of AI where it adds value, and expert-driven verification to build trust in AI-enabled workflows.
speakers: Anthony Ruto, Senior Director, Research Engineering, Autodesk
Andy Harris, Director, Research, Autodesk

title: Level Up Your Corridors: Unlocking Advanced Civil 3D Modeling Techniques
abstract: Think Civil 3D corridors are just for roads? Time to think again. Corridors have a secret life as high-performance grading machines for infrastructure design. In this technical deep dive, we’ll push familiar Civil 3D tools to their limits to solve complex geometry. Through scenarios like cul-de-sacs, knuckles, parking lot grading, and driveway connections, you’ll see how dynamic corridor models maintain design control in both site and roadway environments. We’ll demonstrate advanced workflows for modeling precision and show how Subassembly Composer extends these possibilities. Gain the expertise to build adaptable models that reduce manual rework and streamline digital delivery for every project.
speakers: Shelby L Smith, BIM Manager, Bohler
Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.

title: Live XR Coordination: In-Person BIM Reviews with Workshop XR, ACC, and Web Participants
abstract: Step beyond screen-based coordination and see how immersive design reviews can drive faster decisions in the room. In this in-person session, you’ll learn how Tetra Tech uses Autodesk Workshop XR, Autodesk Construction Cloud, and mixed headset/web participation to review BIM models at full scale, validate designs against existing conditions, and capture issues live. Through practical workflows and project examples, we’ll show how to connect Revit, Navisworks, and segmented mesh data into repeatable XR review sessions that improve stakeholder alignment, reduce late-stage surprises, and support more efficient project delivery.
speakers: SEBASTIEN CLICHE, BIM Manager & Innovation, Technology Expert, Tetratech
Chris Fries, Design Technology Manager, Tetra Tech

title: Lunch
abstract:
Midday is made for good food and good company. Join fellow attendees for lunch and enjoy a relaxed break before the afternoon sessions begin.

 

Thank you to our lunch sponsors: Dell Technologies, HP, and Lenovo.

title: Lunch & Learn: More Performance, Less Power Needed: Lowering the Hidden Cost of Workstations
abstract:
The workstations that run your Autodesk software require high performance CPUs and one of the most important advancements in CPU technology have to do with improvements in the power-to-performance ratio. In other words, the newest Intel CPUs are able to do more but need less power. That might not be an aspect of your technology stack cost, you've considered before.  

In this session, hear from Dell, Intel and industry experts on real world examples of this power-to performance improvements lowering power bills and increasing on-prem compute density all while giving your Autodesk users a system that is fast and effective for their design and engineering work.
speakers: Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato
Trey Morton, Sr. Principal Engineer, Tech Marketing, Dell Technologies

title: Making AI Stick in Estimating
abstract:
AI is changing estimating today, and will continue to evolve workflows in the future. The challenge is knowing which opportunities are worth pursuing. 

Drawing on 14 months of real-world implementation, this session shares a practical framework for identifying AI use cases with the greatest potential based on three factors: impact, frequency, and visibility. It then tackles what happens after a solution works: driving adoption, creating repeatable processes, establishing ownership, and scaling across the team.

Attendees will leave with a framework for prioritizing AI opportunities and a roadmap for turning individual wins into lasting, scalable workflows.
speakers: Brad Klick, Estimating Manager, Victaulic

title: Mastering Autodesk Fabrication: Advanced ITM Content Management Tips and Strategies
abstract: Managing Fabrication ITM content effectively is critical to keeping projects on track and teams working efficiently. This session will cover advanced strategies for connector naming and connectivity, helping you build smarter, more consistent content from the ground up. We'll explore tips and tricks using a hybrid workflow—using MEP Content Editor in the cloud alongside local products like Fabrication CADmep, Fabrication ESTmep, and Fabrication CAMduct—to build and manage content with precision. You'll also learn how to execute mass content changes while modeling jobs are in progress, minimizing disruption and avoiding costly errors. Walk away with strategies you can implement immediately.
speakers: Darren J Young, Consultant, Self Employed
Scott Hendricks, Owner, Virtual Building Supply

title: Maximizing Autodesk Platform Services Value: Smarter Usage, Greater Control, AI-Ready Scale
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services continues to evolve to better support how customers build, scale, and optimize applications in an increasingly AI-driven world. APIs and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) are becoming foundational to agentic AI workflows, making it more important than ever to understand and optimize Autodesk Platform Services use. This session will highlight the features Autodesk Platform Services is building to help you make the most of cloud APIs and MCPs, whether developing directly on Autodesk Platform Services or integrating through third-party applications. You’ll also see new capabilities that provide greater visibility and control, including Autodesk Platform Services reporting, cost management tools, and AI-powered usage prediction through Autodesk Assistant. Join us to learn how to scale with confidence and maximize value from Autodesk Platform Services.
speakers: Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: MCP on Autodesk Platform: Three Production Servers Across the Full Stack
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the layer that lets AI agents access Autodesk tools, data, and APIs through a standardized interface. The firms building this infrastructure today will define the standard—not just use it. This session will go deep on three production MCP servers: revitDeploymentMCP (CI/CD pipeline as four AI-callable tools), a Dynamo MCP server (exposing Dynamo scripts for AI orchestration), and an Autodesk Platform Services Data Pipeline server (chaining the Model Derivative API, the Data Management API, and the Design Automation API without auth failures or silent webhook drops). Each server is examined at the architecture, implementation, and deployment levels. You’ll receive complete implementation patterns for all three.
speakers: Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap
Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap

title: Multi-AI-Agent BIM Orchestration: Building Autonomous Query. Check. Fix Loops for Revit.
abstract: What if your Revit model could check itself—and fix what it finds—autonomously? This session will introduce a multi-agent system where specialized AI agents collaborate in a loop: a Query agent will read model data via Model Context Protocol (MCP), a QC agent will check it against configurable standards, and a Design agent will propose corrections - each previewed, human-approved, and audited before any write. The cycle will repeat until the model passes. We’ll demo three live scenarios: Naming Convention Fix, Parameter Completeness, and Geometry Checking - built with Revit MCP Server, Forma MCP, Python, LangGraph, and configurable YAML rules. We'll also cover transaction management, convergence control, and the points where human oversight remains essential.
speakers: Phuc Le, Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: No Line of Sight, No Leveling: Syncing Field Reality to Revit with Topcon Origo
abstract: Traditional field layout is a disconnected process plagued by line-of-sight obstructions, tedious equipment leveling, and office-to-field data gaps. When conditions shift on chaotic jobsites, the central design model is left completely out of date. This fast-paced, 20-minute session closes the loop entirely. See how to generate precise field points using Autodesk Point Layout (APL), execute high-precision layout with the Topcon Origo ecosystem—requiring zero equipment leveling or line-of-sight constraints—and seamlessly pull "as-staked" and field conditions directly back into your model using ClearEdge3D Tools for Revit. Stop fighting site obstructions—learn to build a true two-way Revit workflow.
speakers: William Palmgren, Product Business Owner, Topcon Positioning Group

title: Nomic at Scale: How AEC Firms Are Operationalizing AI
abstract: Autodesk tools generate some of the most complex documentation in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), yet reviewing and coordinating it still takes hours of manual effort, with errors slipping through. Join Nomic for a live 20-minute demo of purpose-built vision-language models that catch issues earlier, reduce rework, and give teams back time on every project. We'll show three workflows running on real AEC projects: 1) Drawing QA/QC: catching coordination issues and cross-discipline conflicts before they become RFIs or change orders; 2) Submittal reviews: extracting, comparing, and validating data against specs with findings cited to source; 3) Automated code compliance: surfacing violations on sheets early in design, referenced to applicable code sections. Each demo will pair with real ROI data from firms running Nomic in production, so you’ll leave with a clear picture of what deployment delivers. Nomic's AI is built for drawings, specs, and complex documentation: inspectable, governable, and grounded in your project data.
speakers: Andriy Mulyar, CEO and Founder, Nomic

title: One Digital Playbook – Scaling Lessons Across Level Crossing Removal
abstract: This session will explore how Auckland’s road-rail level crossing program used the Autodesk platform to deliver complex infrastructure under a fast‑tracked delivery program. Using Autodesk Forma as a common data environment, the team standardized site visit reporting with Forma Build, automated asset data management through Autodesk APIs, and enhanced design quality with improved clash detection workflows. Design models were integrated with site time‑lapse imagery using Viewer APIs and augmented reality to improve construction insight. The program also used Revit software to produce high‑quality renders, video fly‑throughs, and 3D‑printed pedestrian bridge models, improving stakeholder engagement and decision making.
speakers: Jack Donaghy, Digital Lead, Beca Ltd

title: Operationalizing Autodesk Forma: Lessons from Scaling Infrastructure Delivery
abstract: Heirloom Carbon, a direct air capture (DAC) company, shares how its infrastructure team turned Autodesk Forma (including Forma Data Management, Forma Build, and Forma Takeoff) into a reliable, daily delivery platform. Like many architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams, they faced inconsistent onboarding, fragmented document control, and unclear governance across projects. This session will break down how the team established a scalable common data environment (CDE) through standardized templates, permissions, and workflows issues. You’ll see how they improved collaboration, reduced rework, and increased delivery capacity, and you’ll understand what failed or took longer than expected. Walk away with a practical playbook to configure and standardize Autodesk Forma for consistent, scalable project delivery.
speakers: Allison Maclellan, Design Manager, Heirloom Carbon Technologies

title: People and AI: Building Your Workforce Planning Strategy in the Agent Era
abstract: Construction companies are navigating more workforce challenges than ever—and those staying ahead are doing it with a powerful combination of technology, data, and AI. But the game’s changing. A new era of AI agents is shifting workforce planning from reactive to strategic—giving contractors instant command of their people data, smarter staffing decisions, and a clearer view of what's on the horizon. Join David Pimiskern, Bridgit’s VP of strategy and operations, for an in-depth look at how North America's leading contractors are building their workforce planning strategies for the agent era—and what it means to put AI to work without losing the human expertise at the center of it all. You’ll leave with a fresh perspective on where construction workforce planning is headed, and what forward-thinking leaders are doing today to stay ahead of the curve.
speakers: David Pimiskern, VP, Strategy & Operations, Bridgit

title: People Before Platforms: How Gamuda Made Change Stick with Autodesk Forma
abstract: Digital transformation in construction fails far more often than it succeeds, largely due to resistance to change, legacy system complexity, and poor adoption planning. In this AU class, we’ll explore how Gamuda successfully navigated these challenges while scaling Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) across a global construction organization. Using real examples from Gamuda’s journey, this session will focus on aligning leadership, empowering champions, and supporting end users through continuous training and engagement. We'll examine how Gamuda addressed cultural resistance, integrated Autodesk Forma with legacy systems using open APIs, and implemented robust data governance aligned to ISO 27001 standards.
speakers: Jowenn Lua, Sr Principal, Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Arthur Mun Siew Meng, Group Digital Engineering Acting Sn Manager, Gamuda
Kelsey Stein, Sr Manager, Consulting Services, Autodesk

title: Perfect Quality Control with Autodesk Forma Construction Connect: How Integrated Data Delivers a 45% Workload Reduction
abstract: This session will present a practical case in which Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) connects project data across design, preconstruction, procurement, cost, and construction workflows. Traditionally, inspections required time-consuming drawing checks, record creation, document handling, and information sharing. In this initiative, models, drawings, inspection records, and progress data are centrally managed in Forma Build, enabling standardized inspections and real-time collaboration. Automated status updates and stakeholder communication through Autodesk Forma Construction Connect reduce document search time, support early issue detection, and cut overall workflow effort by 45%. Success depends not only on technology, but also on the right team structure to support common data environment (CDE) operations.
speakers: hideaki takimoto, Senior Manager, TAKENAKA Corporation

title: Pipe Design in InfoWorks ICM: Penalty Configuration and Automatic Constraint Relaxation
abstract: This hands-on lab will teach you the practical use of the InfoWorks ICM Network Design logic for both stormwater and sanitary networks. Through guided exercises, you’ll configure design constraints, explore the new penalty configuration parameters and the concept of automatic relaxation of constraints, apply design locks and backdrops, build and edit pipe network catalogs and selection lists, and interpret the design report to diagnose infeasible pipes. During the session, you’ll use the Rational Method and intensity-duration-frequency (IDF) curves to calculate peak flows for stormwater design. And then you’ll move to sanitary design using population-based peak flows with validation and troubleshooting best practices so you can apply InfoWorks ICM design logic confidently.
speakers: Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
Ahmed Elsayed, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk

title: PLM Summit | Connected Data and Change-Management Process
abstract: Discover our successful transition from a heavily customized, end-of-life forms automation system—processing more than 600 engineering change orders (ECOs) annually—to Autodesk Fusion Manage integrated with Vault Professional software. Learn how we mitigated critical system-failure risks that could have doubled annual change-process costs from ~$130,000 to more than $250,000 and disrupted on-time shipments of multimillion-dollar orders worldwide. Explore the enhanced change-management capabilities we now benefit from, including task and milestone assignments, approval tracking, and metric dashboards. We’ll also share our road map and planned next steps for expanding into quality processes linked to product data as well as future enterprise resource planning (ERP) integration.
speakers: Justin Williams, Engineering Manager, Humanetics

title: PLM Summit | Driving Business Impact with PLM: A Customer Panel Discussion
abstract: Hear directly from leading organizations across industries as they share how PLM is helping them transform the way they work. In this dynamic panel, customers will discuss how they connect data, streamline processes, and improve collaboration to tackle real business challenges. From accelerating time to market to improving product quality and reducing costs, you’ll gain practical insights into what’s working, what they’ve learned, and how they’re achieving measurable results. Whether you're early in your connected data and processes journey or you’re looking to scale, this session will offer actionable takeaways. This session is part of the PLM Summit—a curated learning and networking experience. To explore related sessions, select “PLM Summit” track.
speakers: Josh Smith, Engineering Manager, UMD AUTOMATED SYSTEMS
Thomas Ward, Engineering Manager, Made By Gather
Andrew Pitman, Application & Data Lead, Spirax Group
Dimitri Van Nuland, Project Manager Digitization, Reynaers Aluminium
Mike Vesperman, Director, Expansion & Strategic Accounts, Autodesk

title: PLM Summit | From Fragmented Workflows to a Digital Thread: Scaling Modular Construction with PLM at Faith
abstract: Faith Technologies Incorporated (FTI) is rapidly scaling its modular construction and manufacturing operations. But disconnected systems, manual workflows, and poor data governance created barriers to growth. In partnership with Symetri, Faith is implementing a PLM-driven digital thread connecting Vault software, Autodesk Fusion Manage, Inventor software, and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) systems. This transformation enables centralized data, automated design-to-fabrication workflows, and enterprise collaboration. This session will explore how Faith is moving from siloed processes to a connected, scalable ecosystem to accelerate productization and support rapid growth.
speakers: Darren Hartenstine, Senior Solutions Consultant, Symetri USA
Caleb Goins, Application Support Manager, FTI

title: PLM Summit | Lifting the Weight of Product Development at Overhead Door
abstract: Learn how Overhead Door shaved 18 months off its new product development (NPD) timeline. What once averaged 30 months now follows a standardized phase-gated process in Autodesk Fusion Manage to be completed in under 12 months—with most projects tracking ahead of schedule. This session will explore this journey of improving resource visibility, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and creating leadership visibility into bottlenecks.
speakers: Greg Fineran, Project Manager, Overhead Door Corporation
Todd Clark, Senior Engineering Manager, Overhead Door

title: PLM Summit | Welcome with Srinath Jonnalagadda, Vice President, Data Management, Autodesk
abstract: Kick off the PLM Summit with a high-impact keynote from Srinath Jonnalagadda, vice president of Data Management at Autodesk. He’ll dive into how organizations are tackling disconnected systems, data complexity, and relentless pressure to move faster. You’ll also gain insights into how Autodesk is addressing these challenges head-on—advancing connected data and process strategies and using the power of AI. This session will set the tone by spotlighting key themes, challenges, and opportunities you’ll explore during the PLM Summit. Lunch will be served immediately following the session in the same room, so plan to stay and join us.
speakers: Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Powering Paperless Contractor Submissions and Tracking Across 50 Million Square Feet with Autodesk Forma and Data Analytics
abstract: Disconnected contractor submissions and manual tracking reduce visibility, slow approvals, and limit scalability. In this session, you’ll learn how a paperless submission framework was deployed across a 50-million-square-foot portfolio using Autodesk Forma. Integrated workflows were established using Submittals, RFIs, and Forms to standardize contractor interactions, enable consistent data capture, and ensure full traceability. Through APIs, disparate data sources were unified and transformed into intelligent data models that power advanced dashboards. Discover how this approach delivers real-time submission tracking, improved transparency, and faster data-driven decisions—providing a scalable blueprint for digital transformation at an enterprise level.
speakers: Japneesh Singh, Deputy Manager, DLF
Ritesh Mittal, General Manager, DLF Limited

title: Precast Concrete Solutions: Achieving Convergence Through Revit-Inventor Data Exchange
abstract: In this session, you’ll learn how to move beyond drawing-based coordination and establish a connected design-to-manufacturing workflow based on data convergence. Through an actual project of a general contractor operating a precast concrete plant, this session will explain how Revit and Inventor software were integrated via Autodesk Forma and Informed Design to enable the convergence of design and manufacturing data. You will see how configurable and reusable manufacturing models are created, and how data can flow consistently from BIM to production. The session will demonstrate how this convergence-driven approach reduced workload by more than 40%, and how it provides practical insights that designers and manufacturing engineers can apply to reduce rework, improve quality, and strengthen cross-team collaboration.
speakers: 岩倉巧 TakumiIwakura, BIM Manager, HAZAMA ANDO CORPORATION
Shuhei Tazawa, Associate Professor, Toyo University

title: Predict Before You Model: How We Built an ML-Powered MEP Estimating Bot Trained on 300+ Real Projects
abstract: What if you could generate a reliable MEP cost estimate before modeling a single element in Revit software? That’s exactly what we built: a Python-based estimation bot trained on more than 300 real MEP projects from our historical data. Instead of relying on disconnected spreadsheets or manual takeoffs, the bot uses pattern recognition to generate estimates at the proposal stage before BIM begins. Our solution achieves more than 95% accuracy versus final costs, and it reduces estimation time by more than 70%. In this session, we’ll show how we structured the data, trained the model, and integrated it into our workflow. You’ll leave this session with a practical framework to turn historical data into a predictive asset.
speakers: Gustavo Gusmão, BIM Solution Architect, ENG
Gabriel Campos, BIM Solution Architect, ENG BIM

title: Predict Before You Model: How We Built an ML-Powered MEP Estimating Bot Trained on 300+Real Projects
abstract: What if you could generate a reliable MEP cost estimate before modeling a single element in Revit software? That’s exactly what we built: a Python-based estimation bot trained on more than 300 real MEP projects from our historical data. Instead of relying on disconnected spreadsheets or manual takeoffs, the bot uses pattern recognition to generate estimates at the proposal stage before BIM begins. Our solution achieves more than 95% accuracy versus final costs, and it reduces estimation time by more than 70%. In this session, we’ll show how we structured the data, trained the model, and integrated it into our workflow. You’ll leave this session with a practical framework to turn historical data into a predictive asset.
speakers: Gustavo Gusmão, BIM Solution Architect, ENG
Gabriel Campos, BIM Solution Architect, ENG BIM

title: Preparing Construction Data for AI
abstract: Everyone wants AI in construction. Almost no one has data ready for it. Poor structure, inconsistent metadata, and fragmented workflows hold most teams back. This session will share real-world lessons from Stowe Australia, implementing Autodesk Forma as a common data environment (CDE) to fix that problem. Learn how ISO 19650 principles, standardized templates, and disciplined workflows turn messy project information into structured, usable data. The result? A scalable foundation for analytics, automation, and AI across projects, teams, and the wider business.
speakers: Matt Fern, National Digital Engineering Manager, Stowe Australia

speakers: Matt Fern, National Digital Engineering Manager, Stowe Australia

title: Preparing LAX for the 2028 Olympics: AI-Powered Digital Twins with Autodesk Tandem MCP
abstract: With the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) is modernizing to handle millions of visitors. Managing billions in capital assets across disconnected BIM, CMMS, and GIS systems is no longer viable. In this session, Mingxun Zou, James Awe and Michael Beale will reveal how Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) built an AI-powered digital twin platform. We'll demonstrate the following: An Autodesk Tandem MCP server enabling natural language queries, a Python/Grasshopper automation extracting asset attributes to GeoJSON, and a real-time MapLibre visualization. Building on an Esri Dev Summit 2026 presentation, we'll show the evolution from manual CAD exports to AI-driven facility intelligence. Through live coding, you'll build the same integrations—preparing LAX for its Olympic moment.
speakers: James Awe, Sr Distinguished Architect, Head of Tandem Connect, Autodesk
Mingxun Zou, BIM Administrator, Los Angeles World Airports
Michael Beale, SWE, AWS

title: Production-Ready Auth for MCP Servers: A Practical Deep Dive for Autodesk Platform Services Developers
abstract: Designing secure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that integrate with Autodesk Platform Services requires choosing and implementing the right authentication strategy for each use case. This session will provide a technical deep dive into recommended MCP auth patterns, including 2-legged versus 3-legged flows, user-delegated access, and service-to-service scenarios. We’ll examine trade-offs, token handling, and common pitfalls. We’ll then walk through practical implementation patterns based on real examples from the Autodesk Platform Services MCP server reference. You’ll leave with actionable guidance for building secure, production-ready integrations.
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk
Akash Srivastava, Manager, Software Development, Autodesk

Akash Srivastava, Manager, Software Development, Autodesk

title: Reliable Techniques for Complex Drawings and Detailing in Inventor
abstract: You update your Inventor model and suddenly your drawing is a complete mess! Your views, sections, and details have moved all over the sheet, and your dimensions are pink with confusion! (This always seems to happen at 4 PM on a Friday.) In this class, you’ll learn how updating a drawing can be as predictable and efficient as any other part of your design process. The class is a continuation of the AU classes “Reliable Modeling Techniques for Complex Part Design in Inventor” and “Reliable Techniques for Complex Assembly Design in Inventor.”
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk

title: Rendering Reality: The Rise of Gaussian Splats
abstract: Join industry experts from design visualization and VFX as they explore how Gaussian Splats and solutions from Autodesk Interactive Media & Entertainment are transforming digital workflows. Learn what these techniques are, how they enable highly accurate digital twins and immersive world building, and where they fit in real-world production pipelines. Through examples and firsthand insights, speakers will share what excites them about this approach—along with the practical pros, cons, and challenges of adopting it.
speakers: Logan Foster, Product Owner, Autodesk

title: Restructuring Your Construction Data for the Future
abstract: This session will explore how construction teams can transform fragmented project data into a connected, intelligent workflow using Revit, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and Autodesk Tandem. You’ll learn how to overcome common challenges such as data silos, inconsistent standards, and manual processes, and replace them with integrated pipelines for quantities, progress tracking, and digital twins. You’ll discover practical strategies for structuring data, automating workflows, and preparing your organization for AI-driven construction delivery.
speakers: Josh Weese, Director of Construction Services, ATG USA

title: Rethinking the Construction Workforce for the Next Decade
abstract: Brad Buckles, VP of Technology & Innovation of CPPI, and Mallorie Brodie, CEO and Co-Founder of Bridgit, return to the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how workforce challenges have evolved over the past six years. The conversation explores labor shortages, workforce planning, experience gaps, retention, AI, and what construction leaders must do to attract, develop, and support the next generation of industry talent.

title: Revit Family Building for Facility Management 101
abstract: Do you want to learn how to build families properly? Do you want to know how to build them with custom parameters? Do you want to know how to build them for facilities management use? If so, this class is for you. If not, come anyway and learn something cool and fun. Unlock the power of creating your own custom content. In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn about the art of building Revit families from the ground up, specifically tailored for facility management. We’ll guide you through setting up the framework, crafting geometry, adding character, and defining custom parameters. By the end, you’ll know how to schedule your data and use these families to streamline your facility management workflows.
speakers: Dzan Ta, Autodesk Technical Specialist, Symetri
AU Speaker, Test
ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM
Howard Munsell, Sr. Design Application Specialist II, Whitman Requardt & Assoc

title: Revit MEP Fundamentals and New Tricks
abstract: Many teams still rely on outdated Revit MEP habits that slow coordination and create inconsistent models. This session will cover how to build a strong foundation in spaces, connectors, systems, circuits, and documentation. Then we’ll show how recent Revit improvements support better analysis, clearer panel and circuit workflows, improved analytical visibility for duct and pipe systems, and a smoother path from design to fabrication. We’ll share practical methods that help newer users build confidence and experienced users work faster, model more accurately, and reduce rework.
speakers: Matthew Collier, Technical Product Manager, IMEG Corp.
Sean Fruin, Mechanical Applications Product Owner, IMEG

title: Right Knowledge, Right Time: Transforming Scattered Training into Scalable Learning
abstract: Engineering firms struggle to scale technology training beyond one-off classes and static PDFs, especially when teams are fully billable and tool stacks evolve rapidly. At Thornton Tomasetti, the CORE technology team addresses this by combining Eagle Point Software's Pinnacle Series with Glean—an AI-powered enterprise search platform—to transform fragmented standards, institutional knowledge, and vendor content into structured, role-based learning journeys. This session will show you how workflow-integrated training and enterprise search deliver the right guidance at the moment of need, embedding learning into daily work, and improving adoption, consistency, and future competency pathways.
speakers: Joshua Bradshaw, Director CORE Delivery, Thornton Tomasetti
Mike Federspiel, Customer Success Manager, Eagle Point Software
Mary Forbes, Customer Success Team Lead, Eagle Point Software

title: Rule-Driven Building Design: Connecting Structural Analysis, Autodesk Forma, and Informed Design
abstract: Learn how to automate decision making in type 5 designs by connecting structural analysis, product data, and off-site construction workflows across the Autodesk platform. This class will demonstrate how to integrate a Structural Analysis Design Engine (SADE) with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to automate shear wall placement, then propagate those requirements through Informed Design to drive product behavior. Using the Informed Design API and parametric logic authored in Inventor software, we’ll embed structural intelligence into configurable wall panels assigned to Autodesk Forma masses—enabling consistent, data-driven outcomes from early design through fabrication.
speakers: steve dewitt, Owner, Custom Building Configurators
Kelly Justin Wilson, Founder, SADE

title: Rule-Driven Building Design: Connecting Structural Analysis, Autodesk Forma, and Informed Design
abstract: Learn how to automate decision making in type 5 designs by connecting structural analysis, product data, and off-site construction workflows across the Autodesk platform. This class will demonstrate how to integrate a Structural Analysis Design Engine (SADE) with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to automate shear wall placement, then propagate those requirements through Informed Design to drive product behavior. Using the Informed Design API and parametric logic authored in Inventor software, we’ll embed structural intelligence into configurable wall panels assigned to Autodesk Forma masses—enabling consistent, data-driven outcomes from early design through fabrication.
speakers: Steve Dewitt, Independent Contractor, Autodesk

title: Sabesp Digital Transformation: Largest Water CAPEX in the Southern Hemisphere Powered by Autodesk Portfolio
abstract: Come to this session to hear how Sabesp powers a $15 billion+ CAPEX program, universalizing water and sewer systems for 28 million people across 375 municipalities with more than 1,100 work fronts. Over five years, custom Civil 3D/Revit/AutoCAD Plant 3D libraries and Autodesk Forma Data Management (engineering CDE) enable full intelligent modeling of water intake, transport, treatment, reservoirs, distribution, sewage collection, pumping stations, and effluent treatment plants (ETPs)—replacing 2D workflows. Forma Data Management and Autodesk Forma Build orchestrate CAPEX, from planning to commissioning. Autodesk Forma Design Collaboration streamlines model coordination. Water solutions—including InfoDrainage, InfoWorks WS Pro, and SCM6—handle hydraulic modeling and rehab planning. ArcGIS supports CAPEX spatialization and BIM publishing. Pioneering AI via Autodesk Platform Services automates Sabesp standards compliance checking.
speakers: Marcel Costa Sanches, Engineering Corporate Director, SABESP

title: Same Building, Different Data: Why Owners and Construction Still Miss Each Other
abstract: Everyone says they’re delivering “the data”—but whose data is it really? Construction teams manage RFIs, submittals, schedules, and models to get the building delivered. Owners need something very different: trusted, structured asset data they can use on day one—and for the next 30 years. In this panel, we’ll break down the disconnect between construction data and owner data, discuss why handover still fails, and examine what operational readiness actually looks like. From defining asset requirements early to validating data in the field, we’ll challenge assumptions and share what it takes to move from project closeout to lifecycle value. Because delivering everything isn’t the same as delivering what matters.
speakers: Andy Burg, Vice President, Messer Construction
Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS
Julie Jernigan, Digital Delivery Leader - Buildings, RS&H
Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk
Robert Brown, Sr. Project Controls Systems Manager, DFW Airport

title: Save Time and Improve Quality: Dynamic Factory Design with Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim Integrations
abstract: Discover how combining Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim software transforms facility design through seamless integration of 2D layouts, 3D models, and process simulation. This case study will demonstrate significant time savings by eliminating redundant updates across platforms and enabling engineering teams to make objective, data-driven decisions with less rework. This class will present the end-to-end Factory Design Utilities workflow, showing how AutoCAD, Inventor, Revit, and FlexSim software work together to enable rapid, realistic simulations and models. Engineers from Jacobs will share real project examples demonstrating ROI, cost savings, and how simulations validate designs, communicate decisions, and extend value into production planning and continuous improvement.
speakers: Justin Freeman, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Tyler Morrison, Industrial Systems Global Principal, Jacobs

title: Scaling Rail Data at MRS Logística: From Fragmented Workflows to Real-Time Intelligence
abstract: In a reality of more than 200 railway infrastructure projects running simultaneously, data fragmentation is not a risk—it’s inevitable. This technical deep dive will show you how MRS Logística tackles this challenge by refining BIM requirements and building a standardized common data environment (CDE) in Autodesk Forma. From issues and daily reports to audits, model coordination, cost, and schedule, workflows are structured and connected at scale. Discover how Autodesk Assistant enables structured analysis and how the Insight Builder tool turns connected data into real-time intelligence—driving consistency, reliability, and faster decision making across projects.
speakers: Rafael Braida, Infrastructure Specialist - BIM Manager, MRS Logística

title: Shift to Next-Generation Construction: From Connected Processes to Predictive Decision Making
abstract: During construction, fragmented information and decision making across multiple teams remain a major challenge. At Daiwa House, Autodesk Forma projects are launched across more than 400 design and construction projects each year, supporting collaboration across departments. About 130 of these projects use Autodesk Forma Site Design to establish concurrent processes from the early design stage and reduce information gaps. Building on this track data, we’re developing an integrated construction platform for schedule and cost forecasting and recommendations. The goal is to connect these predictions and make decision making itself more predictable. This session will present future processes, technology, and organizational change for next-generation construction.
speakers: Yui Kikuchi, Chief, Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.
Yoshinori 慶典, Chief, Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.
Takuya Ogawa, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Stop Calculating. Start Designing for Biodiversity Net Gain.
abstract: Biodiversity net gain is rapidly becoming a regulatory requirement across global markets, yet most assessments still rely on disconnected spreadsheets, manual calculations, and static reporting—creating risk, inefficiency, and limited design insight. In this session, Ramboll will share its "nature as an asset" perspective and explore evolving biodiversity frameworks across the United Kingdom, European Union, and United States. We’ll examine limitations of traditional workflows and demonstrate how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), integrated with ArcGIS, enables geometry-driven habitat unit calculations via Ramboll's Biodiversity Calculator. Discover how digitalizing biodiversity assessment enables proactive, data-informed design—improving accuracy, transparency, and long-term project value.
speakers: Paul Reed, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk
Vikki Patton, Global Biodiversity Metrics Lead, Ramboll

title: Stop Filling Out Forms: Auto-Generating Autodesk Forma Forms at Scale
abstract: Every construction project uses forms, but creating and managing them manually can quickly become time-consuming and inconsistent across teams. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) forms can be automatically generated and populated using Forma Construction Connect (formerly ACC Connect) and Workato. Learn how automation can trigger forms from project events such as inspections, workflows, or schedule activities, and prefill information from project data and external systems. Using real project examples, we’ll demonstrate how automated form generation can reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and ensure critical project information is captured accurately across large construction portfolios.
speakers: Dominic Martens, Group Construction Technology Manager, Icon Construction

title: Stop Rebuilding Your Project: The Autodesk Forma Lifecycle Challenge—From AI Planning to Built Outcomes
abstract: Projects shouldn’t feel like starting over at every phase—yet they often do, leading to lost data, and rework. This interactive lab tackles that challenge through a full lifecycle experience with Autodesk Forma. Experience how one connected workflow can take a project from AI-powered site planning in Forma Site Design, through data management and collaboration, to construction outcomes. Along the way, you'll step into different project roles, experience real-world scenarios, make critical decisions, and achieve the best results across the lifecycle. You won’t just learn the workflow—you’ll experience it, making it memorable and directly applicable to your projects.
speakers: Beatriz Davi Medola, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Danielle Foss, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Ignacio Suque, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk

title: Stop Searching, Start Knowing: Item-Driven Classification in Vault
abstract: Learn how to bring structure, clarity, and powerful searchability to your engineering data using Vault Items as the foundation for classification. Many organizations rely on files and folders to organize models, drawings, and documents, but this approach can quickly become difficult to manage as data grows. By using Items, you can create a consistent classification framework in a more meaningful way.
speakers: Bill Shaner, CAD Administrator, FS Elliott

title: Stop Sharing Screens – Start Sharing Space: Practical XR for Model Coordination
abstract: Immersive technologies are often promoted as the future of model coordination, yet most teams remain stuck in screen sharing and pilot demos. This session challenges that pattern, presenting a practical playbook for using shared immersive space as a deliberate coordination tool rather than a novelty. Through real project scenarios, it shows when XR enables faster understanding and better decisions, when desktop review works better, and how to structure immersive meetings so technical and non-technical stakeholders collaborate effectively. Hardware, visualization, and platforms matter – but only when paired with clear intent, facilitation, and decision focused workflows.
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec
Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec

title: Stop Sharing Screens – Start Sharing Space: Practical XR for Model Coordination
abstract: Immersive technologies are often promoted as the future of model coordination, yet most teams remain stuck in screen sharing and pilot demos. This session challenges that pattern, presenting a practical playbook for using shared immersive space as a deliberate coordination tool rather than a novelty. Through real project scenarios, it shows when XR enables faster understanding and better decisions, when desktop review works better, and how to structure immersive meetings so technical and non-technical stakeholders collaborate effectively. Hardware, visualization, and platforms matter – but only when paired with clear intent, facilitation, and decision focused workflows.
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec
Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec

title: Strengthening Your Core: Working with AutoCAD Core Console
abstract: Process hundreds—or even thousands—of drawings in a fraction of the time using the AutoCAD Core Console, a powerful headless version of AutoCAD software built for high-performance batch automation. This session will go beyond theory to show how you can use the AutoCAD Core Console to execute scripts, run custom applications, and automate repetitive CAD tasks without ever opening the AutoCAD interface. You will learn how to build scalable workflows that dramatically reduce manual effort while improving consistency across large drawing sets.
speakers: Matt Miyamoto, ISD Professional Services Manager, IMAGINiT Technologies

title: Subassembly Composer and Corridor Transitions for Repeatable Complex Road Design
abstract: In more-complicated designs, users can see efficiency gains from using customized subassemblies that do the work of multiple assembly regions. In this lab, users will experience using Subassembly Composer to create a subassembly that uses a Decision function to facilitate multiple end conditions along a design with a single assembly or region. Then, using that custom subassembly in Civil 3D software, we’ll use the Corridor Transition tools to adjust the design with a high level of control.
speakers: Ben Wardell, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Russ Nicloy, Civil Solutions Specialist, MACER Technologies, Inc.

title: Symetri Presents: The Revit Family Feud
abstract: Survey says... there's a better way to work in Revit. Join Heather Volk and Abra Cooley for an interactive game-show-style workflow challenge that puts common project tasks, coordination issues, and productivity bottlenecks center stage. Through real-world MEP scenarios, attendees will compare traditional and optimized workflows while estimating the time and effort behind everyday Revit tasks. Using Revit, Naviate MEP, and Naviate Accelerate, this engaging session will combine live demonstrations, audience participation, and friendly competition to showcase practical ways to improve efficiency, reduce rework, streamline coordination, and increase productivity.
speakers: Heather Volk, Strategic Implementation Manager - MEP, Symetri
Abra Cooley, Strategic Implementation Manager - MEP, Symetri

title: Taming 3D Scans: STL Model Cleanup Using Meshmixer Then Moving to Autodesk Fusion for Reverse Engineering
abstract: 3D scanning is more accessible than ever, with consumer and prosumer scanners flooding the market. But the real challenge begins after the scan is complete. Raw STL files are often heavy, messy, and filled with artifacts—especially when capturing organic subjects like the human body. In this session, we’ll dive deep into Meshmixer software, the ultimate Swiss army knife for STL manipulation. We’ll cover essential scan triage, basic cleanup, and targeted reconstruction techniques to repair complex holes and smooth organic artifacts. Then we’ll transition into Autodesk Fusion software to enable reverse engineering workflows. We’ll explore techniques to accurately build and drive solid parametric models on top of your scanned data.
speakers: Nicholas Kloski, Co-Founder, HoneyPoint3D, LLC

title: That's YOUR Opinion: Revit Workflow Point / Counter Point
abstract: Opinions can be wonderful things. Don’t rule anything out because you’ve never tried it before. From the best use of curtain walls to using AI and cloud services, everyone has their own opinions on how things should be done. Some work. Some work better. Some don’t work at all. Follow along as we discuss and flesh out workflows and some best practices. A lot of these are tools you use every day when designing and innovating. But are you using them correctly? Is there something else you could be doing, or is there a better way to do it? Join Matt Preston and Howard Munsell as they provide their unique perspectives on daily tools.
speakers: Howard Munsell, Sr. Design Application Specialist II, Whitman Requardt & Assoc
Matthew Preston, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman Requardt & Associates, LLP
John Selbe, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman, Requardt & Associates, LLP

title: That's YOUR Opinion: Revit Workflow Point / Counter Point
abstract: Opinions can be wonderful things. Don’t rule anything out because you’ve never tried it before. From the best use of curtain walls to using AI and cloud services, everyone has their own opinions on how things should be done. Some work. Some work better. Some don’t work at all. Follow along as we discuss and flesh out workflows and some best practices. A lot of these are tools you use every day when designing and innovating. But are you using them correctly? Is there something else you could be doing, or is there a better way to do it? Join Matt Preston and Howard Munsell as they provide their unique perspectives on daily tools.
speakers: Howard Munsell, Sr. Design Application Specialist II, Whitman Requardt & Assoc
Matthew Preston, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman Requardt & Associates, LLP
John Selbe, Senior Design Application Specialist I, Whitman, Requardt & Associates, LLP

title: The AI-Ready Project: How to Structure Information That Agents Can Actually Use
abstract:
AI is only as good as the data behind it - but what does that actually mean in practice? As AI continues to reshape the AECO industry, firms are beginning to realize that success depends on more than adopting the latest tools. How do you structure, connect, and manage project information so it's ready for the next wave of AI, especially agentic AI that needs to act on information, not just retrieve it? 

In this session, we'll move beyond the theory and into the practical steps firms can take today to make project information AI-ready, helping position your organization for what's next instead of scrambling to catch up.
speakers: Benjamin Bazso, CTO, Newforma

title: The AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027 Treasure Chest: Unlocking Collaborative Efficiency in Process Plant Design
abstract: Discover the revolutionary innovations in AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027 software that will transform the way you work in process plant design. Experience the new isometric sheet collection, where you’ll get an entire line number in a single isometric drawing. Streamline your work with improved AutoCAD P&ID Modeler, including the completion rate and status. Take advantage of P&ID enhancements such as the ability to substitute several components in one single step using the Property Palette. And learn more about several additional new features in AutoCAD Plant 3D 2027. This session will give you practical insights into how you can use these innovations to make your daily tasks more efficient and successfully complete your projects.
speakers: Bernd Gerstenberger, Principal Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk

title: The Design and Make Marketplace: Perspectives That Scale
abstract: Autodesk is building the Design and Make Marketplace to power a new era of AI-driven automation—connecting customers to both Autodesk and third-party capabilities in a unified experience. This panel will bring together perspectives from across that ecosystem: an end user discovering and combining solutions, a publisher building and monetizing capabilities, an enterprise leader managing adoption at scale, and Autodesk shaping the platform. Together, they’ll explore how AI-powered services, agents, and workflows are discovered, acquired, and used—and what it takes to make solutions from multiple providers work seamlessly. Learn how this shift is redefining how work gets done.
speakers: Vasini Govindarajan, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Prashant Potadar, Manager - App Store Operations, Autodesk
Brent Scannell, Group Product Manager, Autodesk

title: The Foster + Partners Journey to ISO 19650 Certification and BSI Kitemark—Enabled by Autodesk Forma
abstract: Achieving BSI Kitemark certification for ISO 19650 Information Management as a Lead Appointed Party requires sustained effort, careful governance, and consistent project delivery. This session will explain how Foster + Partners undertook the work required to achieve certification, embedding ISO 19650 principles into everyday practice across complex, multidisciplinary projects. It will outline key steps taken, including defining roles, establishing proportionate information-management processes, developing project-ready documentation, and evidencing consistent application across live projects. The session will also explore challenges such as scaling processes and meeting audit expectations, giving you a view of how to prepare effectively for certification.
speakers: Lola Carbajal Moro, Digital Delivery, Foster + Partners
Daniel Roca Monteagudo, Senior BIM & Design Systems Coordinator, Foster + Partners

title: The Future of Drainage Workflows with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
abstract: Join this session with Autodesk Water experts exploring site drainage design workflows using Civil 3D and InfoDrainage. This session brings together proven approaches to show how Autodesk Water Infrastructure solutions work together to support efficient, data driven drainage design.

title: The Good, the Bad, and the Wildcard: Big Lessons from Autodesk Forma Cost Management Implementation
abstract: Cost management implementations don’t fail on software—they fail on assumptions. This session will break down the good, the bad, and the wildcard moments from real-world deployments, highlighting what actually drives success (and what quietly derails it). From aligning workflows between field, PMs, and accounting to managing data structure, contracts, and change processes, we’ll share practical lessons learned from implementing cost management in live projects. You’ll walk away with clear strategies to improve adoption, avoid common pitfalls, and confidently lead your own implementation.
speakers: Ariel Castillo, Subject Matter Expert, Preconstruction, Autodesk
Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Brad Buckles, VP, Technology and Innovation, Charles Perry Partners, Inc.
Tim Kelleher, Ops. Standards and Innovation Manager, Brinkman Construction Inc.

title: The Hidden Cost of Information Silos
abstract: The average AECO firm manages nearly 87 different software applications. At the same time, construction professionals spend more than 14 hours every week searching for information, resolving conflicts, and correcting mistakes. Coincidence? Probably not. As technology stacks continue to grow, so does the challenge of finding trusted project information when it matters most. In this session, we'll explore the hidden cost of disconnected information and why creating a consolidated view of truth has become essential for improving collaboration, reducing project risk, and giving teams confidence they're making decisions with the right information.
speakers: David Wagner, Vice President of Product Marketing, Newforma
Carl Veillette, CPO, Newforma

title: The New Backbone of Pfizer's Data Infrastructure
abstract: The new backbone of Pfizer’s data management brings transformation in how engineering data is managed. By a strategic data migration into Autodesk Vault and Forma, legacy information has been consolidated into a more structured, reliable system. Previously fragmented datasets are organized, enabling cleaner access, better traceability, and improved governance. This modernization enhances project communication and collaboration across teams, ensuring stakeholders are aligned throughout the engineering project lifecycle. With streamlined file handover processes and centralized control, project management becomes more efficient. Vault and Forma establish a robust foundation that supports scalability and consistency across Pfizer’s operations.
speakers: Justin Dewell, Engineering Systems Senior Associate, Pfizer
STEPHANIE CATALINA, Principal Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk
Brian Schanen, Principal Business Consultant, PLM/PDM, Autodesk

title: The Stack Inversion Is Real: How AI Is Changing What CAD Managers Actually Do
abstract:
AI tools are not just adding new features to CAD workflows. They are changing where the real work happens.

Some tasks that used to require deep CAD knowledge can now be researched, diagnosed, or automated faster than before. At the same time, more decisions about standards, support, compliance, and workflow ownership are landing on the CAD manager’s desk.

This session looks at what is actually changing in day-to-day CAD management, including advanced support research, complex CAD issue diagnosis, CER crash analysis, CAD standards compliance, and using real project and support data to develop better best practices. We will focus on the skills that are becoming more valuable and how to prepare your team before the shift catches you off guard.
speakers: Shaan Hurley, Engineering Software Lead, DOWL

title: The Superb Guide to Easy Revit Rides On!
abstract: The award-winning Superb Team continues with enhanced insights into the ever-expanding world of Revit software and its friends. Our lively conversation spiced with weird, wild, witty, and wonderful war stories will energize you with the latest and greatest developments in Revit 2027 and Autodesk Forma industry cloud. Discover wild and wonderful things to do with Revit using native tools or third-party software for reality capture, visualization, and AR/XR. Use interoperability with add-ins and other authoring and visualization software. Get a glimpse of the future with innovative use cases using AI. Discover more ways and means to enhance productivity. Join us for wise and fun pointers on how to be a fearlessly productive Revit Warrior.
speakers: Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim

title: The Truth Is Out There, But So Is the Nonsense: AI Tips & Tricks for iLogic and the Inventor API
abstract: You've seen how iLogic can tame tedious tasks and make you more efficient. Now AI promises to go even further, writing your rules, navigating the Inventor API, and transforming your automation overnight. Sounds great, right? Here's the truth: Great results from AI are out there, but so is the AI-induced nonsense. You might have seen AI confidently generate code that doesn't work. Or watched it invent API methods that don't exist. The promise is real. But so are the hallucinations, the dead ends, and the frustrations of vibe coding. Come to this session to cut through the hype with tips, tricks, and insights for getting real results from AI, knowing when to trust it, when to push back, and how to build automation that fulfills the prompt.
speakers: Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries

title: Totally Carbon: Customizing Forma Carbon Insights to Your Project Needs
abstract: It's never polite to ask a Revit model its carbon—but now your 75% CD model is being asked for its embodied carbon estimates to establish LEED v5 benchmarks. Don't fret! Forma Carbon Insights (formerly Autodesk Insight) can give you real-time data without slowing your model's production team. Using the Total Carbon Analysis dashboard in Forma Carbon Insights, you can take all the work you’ve already done and transform it into carbon data. Then, you can dedicate some time to the online dashboard, refining carbon inputs without waiting for Revit buffer time or changing your family types. With your knowledge of local laws, client goals, and national averages, you can build out a holistic visual communications tool that toggles between options and their associated carbon costs in real time.
speakers: Annabelle Swain, BIM Manager, Dattner Architects
Dana Moore, Project Architect, Dattner Architects

title: Turning BIM into AI-Powered Digital Twins: Real-Time Predictive Maintenance with IoT
abstract: Intelligent models are often underused after design, remaining static and disconnected from real-world operations. This session will present a real-world deployment in a metropolitan rail system, where BIM is transformed into a live, AI-powered predictive maintenance platform. Using IFC-based workflows derived from Revit software, models are converted into lightweight, web-ready formats and integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data at the asset level. An AI layer enables anomaly detection and failure prediction, reducing unplanned downtime and improving maintenance efficiency. You will gain a practical understanding of how to extend BIM into an operational digital twin and implement scalable, data-driven maintenance strategies.
speakers: Tolga Bozkurt, AI Digital Twin & IoT Specialist, Metro Istanbul

title: Understanding Project and Executive Insights with Insight Builder
abstract: This hands-on lab will help users understand how to begin using the Insight Builder tool within the Project and Executive Insights to obtain project and portfolio level reporting for RFIs, Submittals, Issues, and Cost data. We’ll walk through the following: accessing Insight Builder; building your first Insight Builder dashboard; generating visualizations from key project data; creating pixel-perfect reports to automate PDF generation of weekly reports; and sharing data to project teams. This session will focus on digesting Build data across many projects and helping users find ways to present key insights across projects and portfolios. If you’re looking to level up your analytics skills, this class will help you get started on your data journey.
speakers: William Fiallos, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
John Prior, Sr Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk
Sheryl Yang, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Unified Production Environment: How AI and Data Transformed Ramboll’s Engineering
abstract: Ramboll is reinventing itself as a data-centered, AI‑powered engineering firm. Through its Together for Better Outcomes (T4BO) partnership with Autodesk, Ramboll has productized a unified production environment (UPE) to accelerate AI adoption. By embedding the Autodesk AI tool Autodesk Assistant into daily workflows, productivity increases while more-sustainable client value is delivered. This session will show how data-centered design and AI‑assisted engineering are transforming project delivery and ways of working, reinforcing Ramboll’s role as a partner for sustainable change. We’ll share tangible outcomes, such as higher delivery quality, deeper sustainability insights, and increased project capacity without adding headcount.
speakers: Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk
David Thomson, Principle Product Owner Digital Design, Ramboll

title: Unleashing Dynamo with Autodesk Assistant and MCP: From Intent to Inspectable Graphs
abstract: Dynamo is evolving from manual graph authoring to intent-driven co-creation. In this session, you’ll see how Autodesk Assistant can drive Dynamo through the Dynamo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to create, modify, and run graphs using natural language—while keeping results deterministic, inspectable, and shareable. We’ll walk through real examples: generating a graph from a workflow description, refactoring an existing graph, and validating outputs. You’ll learn where MCP fits in the Dynamo stack, what makes tool-based AI safer than free-form code generation, and which patterns keep AI-assisted automation maintainable across teams.
speakers: John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk
Achintya Bhat, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Unlocking Autodesk Assistant: Secrets of World-Class Data Management with Vault, Common Data, & PLM
abstract: World-class implementations don’t happen by accident—they’re built on deep knowledge of how to make Autodesk tools work together intelligently. In this no-fluff session, Allen Gager will reveal the secrets every expert knows for maximizing Autodesk Assistant across the Autodesk platform while building a robust common data environment (CDE) powered by Vault and Vault PLM software. Discover how to use Autodesk Assistant (now integrated in Vault 2027, Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, Autodesk Forma, and beyond) as your always-on, context-aware AI partner. Learn natural language techniques to find files faster, automate routine tasks, get in-context guidance, query project data, and even drive simple automations—without ever leaving your workflow.
speakers: Allen Gager, Applications Expert - MSD, Rand
Tyson Copa, Platform Specialist, IMAGINiT Technologies

title: Unlocking Connected Workflows: Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Fusion Manage
abstract: This session will explore how the Vault Connector enables connected workflows between Vault, Autodesk Forma, and Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping organizations bridge the gap between engineering data and enterprise lifecycle processes. We’ll begin with an overview of the latest enhancements to the Vault Connector for Fusion Manage, highlighting improvements introduced in recent Vault releases. We’ll then move into a deep dive on the new Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma, exploring how it enables seamless data exchange between design environments and cloud platforms. You will gain insights into integration workflows and real-world use cases. The session will conclude with an interactive Q&A session.
speakers: Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
Younes Yammouri, Director, Product Management, Autodesk

title: Unlocking Connected Workflows: Vault Connector for Forma and Fusion Manage
abstract: This session will explore how the Vault Connector enables connected workflows between Vault, Autodesk Forma, and Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping organizations bridge the gap between engineering data and enterprise lifecycle processes. We’ll begin with an overview of the latest enhancements to the Vault Connector for Fusion Manage, highlighting improvements introduced in recent Vault releases. We’ll then move into a deep dive on the new Vault Connector for Autodesk Forma, exploring how it enables seamless data exchange between design environments and cloud platforms.
