speakers: Younes Yammouri, Director, Product Management, Autodesk
Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk

title: Unlocking the CADD Manager’s Bag: What's Inside? Keys to Navigate Disruption and Speed Transformation.
abstract: Today’s CADD manager isn’t carrying the same old bag. Step inside the modern toolkit where digital strategy, change leadership, and transformation know-how sit right alongside technical expertise. This fast‑paced, story‑driven session will reveal how CADD managers across industries are shedding the “CAD cop” stereotype and emerging as influential technology leaders who shape business outcomes. You’ll hear examples of teams that moved from reactive chaos to confident, future‑focused momentum by redefining the role and embracing disruption. If you’re ready to elevate your impact and lead your organization through digital change with clarity and confidence, this session will show you exactly what’s possible—and what belongs in your upgraded bag.
speakers: Joseph Gaffney, Director of Design Technology Services, Colliers Engineering & Design

title: Using Autodesk Forma Takeoff for Carbon Offset and Sustainability Requirements
abstract: As more projects are being mandated to demonstrate reduced carbon impact during construction, managing contractors are now tasked with finding solutions to easily calculate and track the change in materials that affect Green Star ratings for their clients. This presentation will show you how Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) can use the project models using Forma Takeoff and the EC3 plug-in to effectively report and track carbon offsets to international standards.
speakers: Nathan Love, Construction BIM Manager, Multiplex
Adam Sheather, Sr Principal, Solution Architect – APAC Lead Technical Advisory, Autodesk

title: Using Autodesk Forma to Modernize Digital Delivery and Information Management in Public Transit
abstract: Join us for an in-depth demonstration of a real-world approach to modernizing digital delivery for a public transit agency that delivers one of the largest US infrastructure expansion programs. This session will explore how Autodesk Forma is being used to support ISO 19650-aligned workflows by addressing the challenges of legacy CAD and Revit record data. The discussion will focus on improving data consistency, enabling earlier information alignment, and transforming record documentation into operationally useful data beyond project closeout.
speakers: Casey Gallagher, AEC Technology Specialists, Sound Transit
Greg Smith, Digital Delivery Lead, Mott MacDonald

title: Using MCP to Build Self-Improving AEC Data Workflows
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data stays raw because processing it manually does not scale. This session will demonstrate a working pipeline where AI classifies documents, extracts structured information, enriches records, and validates outputs at every stage. Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI agents to Revit, Autodesk Platform Services, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), letting them read and write connected data across tools in a single workflow. A live walk-through of a real pipeline used on AEC projects will show how feedback loops capture user corrections so results improve with every iteration. You will leave with a reusable architecture pattern you can adapt to your own challenges, from tender analysis to intelligent models to construction submittals.
speakers: Nabil Sadeg, CTO, Nacorm

title: Vault 2027: What’s New and Where We’re Headed
abstract: Vault software continues to evolve to support modern engineering and enterprise needs. And Vault 2027 delivers focused improvements in workflow efficiency, productivity, and platform integration. In this 60‑minute session, we’ll explore what’s new in Vault 2027. You’ll learn how these enhancements support real‑world CAD, engineering, and IT workflows. And you’ll see how they fit into enterprise environments. We’ll also look ahead at the Vault roadmap, highlighting strategic themes and future direction. Learn how customer feedback helps shape Vault and how to prepare your organization for what’s coming next.
speakers: Irvin Hayes, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Vaultify Your Inventor Add-In
abstract: Learn how to “Vaultify” an existing Inventor add-in by integrating Vault API functionality. This session will focus on adding Vault connectivity and using Vault data directly within Inventor to enhance your design workflows. You’ll see how to search for existing parts using both system and user-defined properties, helping reduce duplicate designs and improve reuse of existing data. We’ll also explore how this approach can support smarter decision making during design, streamline processes, and lay the foundation for more-advanced Vault-driven automation within your custom add-ins.
speakers: Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc.

title: Vault on Autopilot: AI-Driven PDM Automation Across Lifecycle, Revisions, and ERP
abstract: Vault Professional software manages thousands of engineering workflows—but property assignment, lifecycle transitions, revision management, approval routing, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) synchronization remain manual. Every operation is predictable and rule-governed. This session will deliver AU 2026's Intelligent Data theme in practice: an AI agent connected to the Vault API monitoring product data management (PDM) events and executing the right action autonomously via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent loop. The large language model (LLM) interprets PDM state against business rules, and the API executes without manual intervention. In controlled workflows, this has reduced administrative overhead by up to 70%. You’ll leave with an ROI-prioritized implementation road map.
speakers: Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap
Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap

title: Vault Professional Mastery: 13 Modern Tips to Supercharge Your Workflow
abstract: Stop clicking through menus and start maximizing your data. In this fast-paced, 30-minute session, we’ll dive into 13 high-impact tips and tricks for Vault Professional software that often go overlooked. From optimizing lifecycles and advanced searching to using the latest "modern" features in the 2027 release, these hacks are designed to eliminate bottlenecks and supercharge your daily workflow. Whether you’re a CAD manager or a power user, you’ll leave with a practical toolkit to automate repetitive tasks, improve data security, and get the most out of your Vault environment.
speakers: Radu Stancescu, CAD Specialist, Permasteelisa North America | Benson
Raffaele Sammarco, Principal Consulting Project Manager, Autodesk
Douhet Wilcox, CAD Lead, Permasteelisa North America | Benson

title: What Becomes Possible When Fabricators Join the Design Process? A Design-to-Fabrication BIM Study.
abstract: Designers make responsible decisions on details—but fully reflecting fabricators' knowledge of real production difficulty and cost is not straightforward. Quantities often emerge only once drawings reach the contractor. What becomes possible when fabricators engage as technical consultants during design? This session shares a joint study with a steel fabricator. Positioning Revit as a single source of truth, connection rules for diaphragms and splices were implemented as components in Tekla via IFC, automating detail generation and takeoff. Fabricators proposed cost improvements; designers made the final geometry decisions. We also examine data retention, the limits of automation, and role boundaries—showing both what became possible and the challenges that remain.
speakers: Takashi Fukushima, STRUCTURAL ENGINEER, Nikken Sekkei

title: What's New in Revit 2027 for Structural Professionals: Hands-On Lab
abstract: As structural projects move from analysis and design intent into detailing and fabrication readiness, teams often struggle with rework, inconsistent model behavior, and repetitive documentation tasks. In this 90-minute lab, you’ll create analytical models with improved automation, editing, loads, and boundary conditions. You’ll also apply new rebar modeling techniques and detailing workflows, work with detailed steel modeling, and automate element numbering with rule-based controls. Guided exercises will demonstrate how these capabilities improve analytical model accuracy and editability, strengthen reinforcement definition and documentation, reduce manual effort, and support more-reliable downstream delivery.
speakers: Tomasz Fudala, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect – AECO, Autodesk

title: When BIM and GIS Stay Connected: Esri and Autodesk’s Path to True Cloud Interoperability
abstract: Discover how Esri and Autodesk are advancing BIM and GIS interoperability through their strategic alliance. Today, teams rely on manual conversion, translation, and duplicate publishing to bring BIM into GIS context - creating friction, slowing decisions, and making it harder to trust the right information is available when needed. This session explores the art of the possible: a future where BIM and GIS data stay connected across Autodesk and Esri environments. Attendees will see how evolving interoperability efforts can reduce handoff friction, improve continuity, and make it easier to bring BIM into GIS and GIS into BIM. Join us to learn about the patterns enabling true cloud-to-cloud workflows!
speakers: Nora Nanov, Product Manager, Esri
Michael Davidson, Product Manager, Esri

title: When the Airport Disappears: Building a Smarter ATL with Autodesk Tandem
abstract: How do you keep the world’s busiest airport running so smoothly that passengers never notice the infrastructure behind it? Chris Harmon of WSP shares how Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is bringing 100 years of data together with Autodesk Tandem to better understand assets, anticipate issues, and connect operations back to planning and design, all while keeping the passenger experience at the center.

title: Which Revit Structural Model to Use for Analysis? Analytical or Physical or Both?
abstract: This class will explore whether structural analysis workflows in Revit software should rely on the analytical model, the physical model, or a hybrid of both. Traditionally, structural analysis platforms use only the analytical model to translate geometry and structural properties from Revit. Why limit workflows to just the analytical model? With analytical and physical models now able to act independently, users can choose which representation best fits their needs. This class will compare approaches and evaluate when each method—or a combined strategy—provides the most reliable and efficient structural analysis workflow. We’ll also explore customizing structural analysis tools to accept physical model geometry.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: Which Revit Structural Model to Use for Analysis? Analytical or Physical or Both?

speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: Why AI Struggles in Real-World Making—And How to Make It Work
abstract: AI has transformed design and simulation, yet its role in real-world making—where materials, tolerances, and human judgment converge—remains emergent. Fabrication is variable, unforgiving, and governed by physics that challenge AI tools. This panel will explore the current state of AI in manufacturing and construction, focusing on how agentic systems can augment, not replace, skilled practitioners. Drawing on applied research from the Autodesk Technology Centers, we’ll share how we train AI on real fabrication data, develop physics-informed models, and test intelligent, automated manufacturing workflows. Join experts across domains to examine how human-AI collaboration can drive impactful outcomes from factory floors to jobsites.
speakers: Kelvin Hamilton, Sr. Manager, Technology Consulting, Autodesk
Nathan Kutz, Director of Physics Informed AI, Autodesk
Fope Bademosi, Circular Economy and Construction Researcher, Autodesk
Adam Allard, Senior Manager, Technical Environments, Autodesk

title: Why Rhumbix Is Critical to Autodesk Forma
abstract: Autodesk Forma industry cloud connects design, preconstruction, and field coordination within a single platform. But one critical layer has been missing: real-time workforce data from the field. Labor is the largest cost on most construction projects—and the least measured. That’s why Autodesk acquired Rhumbix. In this session, we’ll explain the strategic vision behind the acquisition and why Rhumbix is essential to the future of Autodesk Forma. You’ll learn what field and resource management data Rhumbix captures and how it will flow into the Forma platform to support cost, schedule, estimating, and planning workflows, enabling a more complete field-to-finance operation for construction.
speakers: Zach Scheel, Director, Construction Strategy, Autodesk
Sidharth Haksar, VP,  Construction Strategy and Industry Partnerships, Autodesk

title: Why Universities Aren't Teaching the Offsite Industry We're Building—And the Solution
abstract: The offsite construction industry is scaling, but the graduates entering it have been trained for a world of bespoke ETO delivery. No accredited degree program teaches configure-to-order workflows, manufacturing product definition, modular interface standards, or offsite logistics. The industry is hiring for skills that schools don't yet teach. This session will present the MBI-CfOC Offsite Construction Accreditation Initiative—a joint effort between the Modular Building Institute and the Center for Offsite Construction to establish the first accredited degree pathway for the industrialized construction workforce. With materials nearly complete and first accreditation discussions happening, let's understand what the next generation of offsite-trained talent will know, and how to build a firm that can absorb them.
speakers: Jason Van Nest, Executive Director, Center for Offsite Construction

title: XR Meetup: real conversations about extended reality
abstract: Join the 5th Annual Extended Reality (XR) Meetup for an open, interactive conversation on how people are using virtual, augmented, and mixed reality technologies today. Hear real experiences from across industries about what’s working, where XR fits, and what people are still figuring out. This is a space to connect with your people: ask questions, share insights, and connect with others exploring XR. Whether you are just getting started or building on existing workflows, you will leave with practical insights, new connections, and a clearer view of how XR is being used right now.
speakers: Mingus New, Customer Community Manager, Workshop XR, Autodesk

title: Your Bottlenecks Are Showing: 10 Lessons from Thousands of Product Design and Development Companies
abstract: Designing great products is difficult. Successfully taking those products to market on time and under budget is even harder. After working with thousands of product design and engineering businesses, clear patterns have emerged between teams that struggle and those that consistently deliver. In this fast-paced 30-minute session, we’ll break down 10 key lessons that separate successful teams from the rest. We’ll dive into what worked for them as well as what didn’t. You’ll leave with practical strategies to reduce delays, improve alignment, and move from concept to production with greater speed and increased confidence. If you’re a business owner or business leader who wants to fast-track your company’s success, this session is for you.
speakers: Jason Lichtman, Principal Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk

title: Your Firm's Brain: AI-Powered Knowledge Repositories for Smarter Project Execution
abstract: Architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) firms accumulate irreplaceable institutional knowledge—buried in drawings, RFIs, submittals, intelligent models, and lessons learned no one reads twice. Drawing on firsthand conversations with North American AEC firms, we’ll demonstrate how retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), multimodal AI, and lightweight agents—layered on Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and Autodesk Platform Services—can mine project data to surface precedent details, validate firm standards, classify specifications, predict RFI risk, and accelerate new-hire onboarding. You’ll leave with a practical implementation road map, governance and data-readiness checkpoints, build-versus-buy decision criteria, and three pilot patterns proven on real Revit, Civil 3D, and Autodesk Forma workflows.
speakers: Peter Pincic, Global Director - Software, AI, Enterprise, Neilsoft
Pravin raijade, CTO - Software, Neilsoft

title: Advanced Maya and Unreal Integration for Game Cinematics: Motion Capture, Characters, and VFX
abstract: This class will present an intermediate-to-advanced workflow integrating Maya software and Unreal Engine software to create more-complex and exciting game cinematics—including characters animated with motion capture, manually animated vehicles, particles, and dynamics. This class will show you how to create and layout an advanced game cinematic in Maya, preparing it for export to Unreal Engine. Then we will show you how to import and set up the exported Maya scene in Unreal Engine, setting up materials, cameras, mocap, particles, and dynamics. Finally, we’ll implement industry-standard best practices while working between Maya and Unreal Engine, and rendering the final cinematic in Unreal Engine. This hands-on class has the indie game dev and 3D artist in mind.
speakers: Marcio Goncalves, Assistant Professor of Game Art and Design, State University of New York - Empire State

title: AECO Data Community Meetup: AEC Data Model Fan Club
abstract: Do you get a thrill from liberating data from files, models, and all the places it hides? Do dashboards, connectors, and clean schemas spark joy? Then come hang out with your fellow data enthusiasts! We’re gathering AEC data pros, beginners, and the data curious. This one-hour session is designed to celebrate real-world wins, discuss future visions, talk open standards, and everything in between. Whether you’re a seasoned AEC Data Model expert or just dipping your toes into structured data goodness, you’re invited to join us in person to trade war stories, compare best practices, and generally geek out together. Calling all fans of the AEC Data Model API, Content Catalog, Datum, Model Analytics, and Parameters Service.
speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk
Alexine Gordon-Stewart, Sr Manager, Chief of Staff, Autodesk

title: AECO Roadmap: Vision and Strategy
abstract: The AECO industry is entering a new era where granular data, connected workflows, and AI are transforming how projects are planned, delivered, and operated. This session explores Autodesk’s AEC vision for a unified cloud foundation that helps teams define outcomes earlier, carry context across the lifecycle, and make better decisions from day one. With a focus on outcome-based BIM, Autodesk is advancing an approach where data is more meaningful, accessible, and actionable. This enables stronger alignment, better visibility, and improved coordination, while laying the groundwork for intelligent guidance and automation across the project journey.
speakers: Jen Suerth, Senior Director, Construction Strategy, Autodesk
Theo Agelopoulos, VP AEC Design Strategy, Autodesk
Julie Chen, Sr. Dir., Strategic Business Dev., Autodesk

speakers: Nicolas Mangon, VP, AEC Industry Strategy, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Architecture
abstract: Designing for impact means designing with agility, insight, and collaboration. In this session, Autodesk product and strategy leaders will share what’s new, and what’s coming next, for architects across Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Autodesk’s cloud collaboration tools. Learn how we’re advancing workflows from planning and schematic design to performance analysis, documentation, and multidisciplinary coordination. See how deeper connections between desktop tools and the Forma industry cloud, through the Forma Connected Client initiative, can help teams move data, context, and insights across solutions, reducing rework, supporting sustainability, and unlocking creativity.
speakers: Lauren Poon, Senior Product Line Manager, Architecture, Autodesk
Matt Arsenault, Principal Product Manager - Forma Connected Clients, Autodesk
Daniel Gameiro, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Andrea Vallés, Senior Architecture Industry Strategy Manager, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: AutoCAD
abstract: Get a front-row seat to what’s next for AutoCAD software. In this session, the AutoCAD product team will walk you through the latest enhancements and offer a preview of upcoming features that are redefining design and drafting. From improved collaboration tools to AI-powered productivity boosts, you’ll see how Autodesk is evolving AutoCAD to meet the needs of today’s and tomorrow’s complex projects. You’ll also get insight into the product strategy guiding our development, and see how your feedback is helping shape what’s coming next.
speakers: Dan Whitcombe, Senior Group Product Manager, Autodesk
Tedman Martinez, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Anum Mithani, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Shiva Kashalkar, Senior Director, Product Management, AIR, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma for Model Management
abstract: Models should not live in silos. They should drive decisions. This session will explore how Autodesk connects BIM and virtual design and construction (VDC) workflows across design and construction, from early concept through handover and beyond. Learn how teams can better coordinate, collaborate, and use models across tools and roles. We’ll share what’s coming in Autodesk Forma to make models more usable, accessible, and valuable in both the field and the office. Explore the recent and future capabilities for Autodesk Forma Design Collaboration, Autodesk Forma for Model Management, and Navisworks Manage users to better coordinate models and collaborate across teams.
speakers: Marco Ramolla, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk
Monserrat Elaskar, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
Paul Walker, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Tori Anderson, Product Marketing Manager, Construction, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Civil Infrastructure
abstract: Infrastructure projects are growing in scale, complexity, and urgency—and Autodesk is evolving to meet that challenge. In this session, you’ll hear from the teams behind Civil 3D, InfraWorks, ReCap, and Collaboration for Civil 3D as they share what’s new and what’s next for civil engineers and infrastructure professionals. Learn how modeling, analysis, and collaboration workflows are evolving to support more-sustainable, connected, and efficient project delivery. You’ll also get an early look at features in development and have the opportunity to provide input that will help shape Autodesk’s infrastructure roadmap.
speakers: Andrew Milford, Sr. Group Product Manager, Infrastructure and APAC Product Lead, Autodesk
Can Anbarlilar, Sr. Group Product Manager, Infrastructure Product Line and Strategic Projects, Autodesk
Prakriti Khanna, Sr. Group Product Manager, Collaboration Product Line, Autodesk
Shiva Kashalkar, Senior Director, Product Management, AIR, Autodesk
Tim Yarris, Sr. Group Product Manager, Civil 3D and Infrastructure Product Line, Autodesk

title: Agentic AI Running Project Workflows in Autodesk Forma with MCP
abstract: This session will explore how PEC is implementing agentic AI to run real project workflows within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). By using a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a governed orchestration layer, AI agents can securely connect to Autodesk APIs, query live project data, perform QA/QC checks, and execute tasks across project systems. You’ll see how this architecture moves beyond automation into true workflow execution—enabling scalable, consistent, and intelligent project delivery. We’ll share real-world examples, implementation strategies, and lessons learned to help teams begin adopting AI-driven workflows today.
speakers: Luis Salmeron, Senior Digital Systems Engineer, Professional Engineering Consultants (PEC)
Farzad Towhidi, Senior Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk

title: Agents of Change: Mastering Agentic AI and MCP Workflows for the Multidiscipline AEC Firm
abstract: The AEC industry is undergoing a paradigm shift where the lines between software developers, industry groups, and design firms are blurring. This session explores how AI strategies are being collaboratively shaped to move beyond basic research into high-impact implementation within multi-discipline engineering environments. We will examine the evolution of AI maturity, moving from foundational context engineering to the deployment of agentic services and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) that automate complex engineering tasks. Drawing on real examples, business leaders will gain a clear view of the emerging landscape and a practical way to balance AI’s potential against the demands of modern design practice.
speakers: Michael Gustafson, SVP of Strategic Growth, QNECT LLC
Andrew Sundal, Structural Engineer/Comp Design Specialist, HGA

title: AI-Assisted AutoLISP in AutoCAD: A Practical Workflow for Nonprogrammers
abstract: Most AutoCAD users never touch AutoLISP. So many small, repetitive design tasks stay manual. This session will show how AI-assisted AutoLISP workshops helped rail engineers who have little or no coding experience build useful automations themselves. You’ll discover how to identify good automation candidates, prompt AI for workable routines, validate and refine the results, and add lightweight governance through version control and testing. The outcome? Faster design work, more self-sufficient teams, and a practical path from AI curiosity to repeatable workflow improvement.
speakers: Fabian Raaijman, Team Lead of Rail Digital Engineering, Haskoning

title: AI Changes the Cost Curve. But Connected Data Changes Value Creation.
abstract: AI is often discussed in terms of efficiency, but the bigger shift may be how connected data improves the quality, consistency, and usefulness of expert delivery. This session will share Norconsult’s perspective on how AI and connected data are beginning to influence decision support, delivery workflows, and client value across architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO). We’ll explore why the impact goes beyond isolated productivity gains, where connected data makes AI more relevant in practice, and what leaders should consider as technology starts to affect how value is created in engineering and project delivery. The session will focus on practical implications and lessons emerging from real industry needs.
speakers: Knut Ramstad, CTO and Partner, Registered Architect, Nordic Office of Architecture
Marius Jablonskis, Digital Transformation Leader, Norconsult ASA

title: AI Data Check for Civil 3D: Validating Models Against Project Requirements via Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: This session will present a platform built through vibe coding using Autodesk Platform Services APIs, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and AI code generation to automate the full data validation cycle for Civil 3D models. The platform pulls files from Forma, extracts metadata via the Model Derivative API, and ingests project requirement PDFs. An AI layer converts PDFs into structured validation rules, then runs them against the model to produce a detailed conformity report, flagging gaps, mismatches, and missing attributes without manual checks. The session will also cover key lessons from development, AI-driven architecture, and real-world use cases showing practical impact at scale.
speakers: Mohamad M. KASSIR, Regional Digital Manager, Egis

title: AI-Enabled Design for Excellence: Advancing Industrialized Construction from Design to Fabrication
abstract: This session introduces a next-generation design for excellence (DfX) framework for industrialized construction, which combines design for manufacturing, assembly, disassembly, and sustainability into an AI-enabled decision-making system. This framework seeks to shift construction from a project-based approach to a performance-driven, product-based approach, focusing on constructability and lifecycle optimization early in the design phase. Demonstrated through a pilot building in six stages—loading, learning, programming, assembly, experimentation, and exhibition—it incorporates computational design, large-scale 3D concrete printing, robotic assembly, and prefabrication, and serves as a living laboratory for advancing industrialized construction systems.
speakers: Karla Saldana, Assistant Professor, University of Florida

title: AI-Powered Visual Storytelling for AEC Projects
abstract: Autodesk Flow Studio software is a generative solution in the Autodesk Media & Entertainment Collection. This software helps artists produce layout, create content, and drive home visuals across film, television, and games. This solution can also be used in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) space to help standup Revit content and aid with visuals to maximize customer impact.
speakers: Duane Rutkowski, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: AI-Ready BIM Foundation: Push-Button Cross-Discipline Automation with Revit MCP, Dynamo, and pyRevit
abstract: The first days of a building project are consumed by repetitive start-up tasks across architecture and MEP teams—validating models, aligning levels and grids, creating spaces, and generating documentation. This session will show how teams can reduce start-up from 40 staff hours to under 60 minutes using Revit MCP, Dynamo, and pyRevit software. Revit MCP validates levels, grids, rooms, and naming conventions through natural-language queries. Dynamo then synchronizes linked architectural data into MEP models, while pyRevit batch tools automate spaces, views, sheets, and standards-compliant documentation. You’ll leave with a scalable cross-disciplinary framework that improves coordination quality and builds an AI-ready BIM foundation.
speakers: Mayank Sharma, Director, Virtual Design and Construction, Mazzetti
Julide Bozoglu, Director of Technology, Goettsch Partners

title: Animation in Maya with AI: Creating a Game Cinematic with MotionMaker
abstract: MotionMaker is an exciting new feature released with Maya 2026 software. It uses the power of AI to help 3D artists animate characters and creatures quickly and efficiently. This is AI at its best—not trying to replace the 3D artists but helping them. This class will introduce you to MotionMaker and teach you how to use it to create an exciting game cinematic. First, you’ll learn what MotionMaker is and how it compares to other tools. Then, you’ll learn the basic elements and components of the MotionMaker interface. Finally, we’ll use MotionMaker to create an exciting game cinematic, taking advantage of the three proxy characters available (biped, canine, and horse)—and then we’ll export the game cinematic to a game engine.
speakers: Marcio Goncalves, Assistant Professor of Game Art and Design, State University of New York - Empire State

title: An Owner’s Digital Blueprint for Airports: Mandated BIM, GIS‑Led Master Planning, and Digital Twins
abstract: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) is building a unified digital ecosystem by mandating BIM across all projects and adopting geographic information system (GIS) as the foundation for master planning. Progress toward digital twins is independently certified through global, standards‑driven bodies such as the BSI Kitemark. AAHL is proud to have the world’s first and second airports certified to BSI Kitemark Stage 2 for Design and Construction, and to be the first organization globally with all seven airports achieving Stage 3. This session will demonstrate how scan‑to‑BIM and full airside scan‑to‑GIS establish accurate digital baselines to govern and protect the aerodrome, improving design coordination, safety compliance, and operational and long‑term expansion through BIM‑GIS integration.
speakers: Rahul Khanna, Head of Design & Master Planning, Adani Airport Holdings Limited
Malishka Gupta, BIM Manager, ADANI GROUPS

title: An Owner’s Digital Blueprint for Airports: Mandated BIM, GIS‑Led Master Planning, and Digital Twins
abstract: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) is building a unified digital ecosystem by mandating BIM across all projects and adopting geographic information system (GIS) as the foundation for master planning. title: An Owner's Playbook for a Common Data Environment
abstract: Most common data environments (CDEs) are set up for the delivery team. They solve coordination during design and construction, then get handed to the owner who lives in them for decades. The folder structures and workflows that suited the project rarely fit how a facilities team works. This session will be a practical guide for owners. We'll cover what to specify before a project starts, the contract language that protects your access to the data, where standard handovers break down, and how to organize information so it stays useful over the life of the asset. You'll leave with a checklist you can apply to your next project, whether you're standing up a CDE for the first time or trying to fix one you inherited.
speakers: Jon Dalton, Sr. BIM Manager, NV5

title: AU Clubhouse
abstract:

Designed for the builders, makers, innovators, and visionaries shaping tomorrow.

title: Autodesk Community Meetup: Meet Expert Elites
abstract: Looking to deepen your connection with the Autodesk community? Join us for an exclusive meetup where you can engage with Autodesk's esteemed subject matter experts: Autodesk Expert Elites. These exceptional individuals are recognized for their significant contributions in sharing product knowledge, best practices, and expertise—playing vital roles in helping our customer community thrive. During this event, you'll hear insightful tips and experiences straight from Expert Elites, enhancing your understanding of Autodesk products. Don't miss this opportunity to connect, ask questions, and learn from community leaders in a collaborative environment. We look forward to seeing you there!
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend
Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Community User Group Meetup
abstract: The Autodesk Community User Group Meetup is your chance to connect with group leaders and members, learn how to start your own group, and understand the value these communities offer. Hear about best practices for running successful user groups, and make connections that will enhance your experience at AU and beyond. Join us to share knowledge, grow your network, and become part of a thriving community.
speakers: Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching
Sam Karas, Program Manager - Community, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Forma Isn’t the Hard Part. Leading Through Change Is.
abstract: Implementation of Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) is often treated as the finish line, when it’s only the starting point. The real challenge is leading through continuous change—balancing field needs, data, and evolving technology. This session will share how a shift toward proactive engagement, stronger internal alignment, and deeper partnership with Autodesk transformed how we operate and scale Autodesk Forma. By combining field feedback with user data, we built an operating model that supports better decisions and long-term success. You’ll leave with a strategic lens and practical approach to leading Autodesk Forma beyond implementation.
speakers: Lil Magallanes, Construction Technology Program Manager, DPR Construction

title: Autodesk Forma to Energy: AI-Powered Workflows for Carbon Insight
abstract: Energy and carbon analysis often arrives too late—after key decisions have been made. Despite tools like Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight software, most teams rely on manual, disconnected workflows that limit iteration. This session will introduce a connected, data-driven approach. By embedding performance data in BIM and using AI to generate simulation logic, teams can automatically produce carbon and energy analyses—earlier, more frequently, and without deep simulation expertise. Through a live demo, you’ll see design data flow from Autodesk Forma through Revit into automated workflows and into Insight for actionable results. Attend this class to learn how to replace one-off analysis with scalable, repeatable carbon workflows.
speakers: Chris Balbach, Director of R&D, Performance Systems Development of NY, LLC
Tetsuya Hishida, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato

title: Autodesk Fusion Roadmap
abstract: Explore the future of product development with Autodesk Fusion. This roadmap session will provide insight into where Fusion is headed across design, manufacturing, data, and AI-driven workflows. You’ll get an early look at upcoming innovations, strategic priorities, and how Autodesk is evolving Fusion to help teams work in a more connected, intelligent, and efficient way across the entire product development process. This session is ideal for anyone interested in understanding the future of Autodesk Fusion.
speakers: Daniel Graham, VP, Manufacturing, Autodesk
Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk
Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Fusion Roadmap
abstract: Explore the future of product development with Autodesk Fusion. This roadmap session will provide insight into where Fusion is headed across design, manufacturing, data, and AI-driven workflows. You’ll get an early look at upcoming innovations, strategic priorities, and how Autodesk is evolving Fusion to help teams work in a more connected, intelligent, and efficient way across the entire product development process. This session is ideal for anyone interested in understanding the future of Autodesk Fusion.
speakers: Daniel Graham, VP, Manufacturing, Autodesk
Srinath Jonnalagadda, VP, Data Management, Autodesk
Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Operations Roadmap: What's new and next in Operations
abstract: In this roadmap session, we'll explore why operations is emerging as the next frontier of digital transformation and how Autodesk is helping organizations move from disconnected systems to connected operations that continuously learn and improve. We'll share the vision behind Autodesk Operations, the market forces reshaping the industry, and the latest innovations across FlexSim, Fusion Operations, Autodesk Tandem, Autodesk Connect and more. You'll gain insight into how Autodesk is connecting Design, Make, and Operate to close the loop across the asset lifecycle, transforming operational knowledge into actionable insights that improve future decisions, optimize performance, and drive continuous improvement. Discover how this connected approach creates greater lifecycle visibility, builds operational intelligence, and lays the foundation for more predictive, proactive, and ultimately autonomous operations.
speakers: Robert Bray, VP, Tandem Platform, Autodesk
Seth Hindman, Sr Director, Product Management, Industry Strategy, & XD, Autodesk
Tim Kelly, Director, Tandem Platform Strategy, Autodesk

title: Autodesk VRED: Latest Real-Time Visualization Trends combined with AI Transforming Automotive Design
abstract: Autodesk VRED is known for rapidly adopting state of the art rendering technologies, open standards, and AI workflow tools. This Autodesk University session explores new key capabilities including Vulkan Ray Tracing, Gaussian Splat rendering, CloudXR streaming to Apple Vision Pro, and the use of constraints and physics. Learn how these technologies work together to deliver highly realistic visuals and physically plausible behavior for complex digital twins with minimal setup time. Discover how designers, engineers, and visual artists can accelerate projects, improve collaboration, and reduce costly errors early in the digital model. Ideal for visualization, XR, and automotive workflows focused on performance, realism, and scalability.
speakers: Pascal Seifert, Sr. Technical Product Manager, Autodesk
Victor Perez, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Women’s Network Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.
speakers: Christi Clay, Senior Program Manager, Autodesk

title: Beyond Copilots: Agentic AI Workflows for Design and Engineering
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly evolving from chat assistants into autonomous workflow agents capable of completing meaningful engineering tasks. For design and engineering organizations, the greatest opportunity isn't replacing designers—it's eliminating the repetitive work that consumes the time of design technologists, and other highly skilled experts.
This session explores running secure, high-performance agentic workflows with local AI models alongside Autodesk applications on Dell Pro Max and Precision workstations powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and NVIDIA Grace Blackwell AI superchips. Local open models keep sensitive design data and IP on-premises, reduce inference costs, and deliver always-on, low-latency automation.
Through practical Autodesk-focused examples, we'll demonstrate AI agents that review models against CAD and BIM standards, validate customer requirements, automate quality control, generate documentation, and orchestrate multi-step engineering workflows.
speakers: Sean Young, Director of AEC, NVIDIA

title: Beyond Design: The Evolving Role of Architects and Engineers in the Age of AI
abstract: Hear directly from technology leaders at some of the most innovative architectural/engineering firms (HKS Architects, PBK Architects, TYLin Group) as they share how AI is reshaping practice at scale. This panel will explore how global architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations are integrating AI into design, engineering, and delivery workflows—moving from pilots to enterprise adoption.  Panelists will share real-world use cases, lessons learned, and the organizational changes required to successfully scale innovation. The discussion will also examine how the role of architects and engineers are evolving and the skills that will be critical for success in an AI-driven future.  You’ll gain practical insights into how leading firms are using AI and power of technology to drive efficiency, improve decision making, and stay competitive in a rapidly changing industry.
speakers: Deepika Khowal, Principal Account Executive, Enterprise, Autodesk
Steve Cayea, CIO, TYLin International
Lauren Collier, Chief Technology Officer, PBK
Natasha Luthra, Chief Technology Officer, HKS
Sam Omans, Head of AI Growth Strategy, Autodesk

title: Beyond the BOM: Using PLM to Drive Modern Product Management
abstract: Product lifecycle management (PLM) is often treated as a system of record for BOMs—but leading teams are using it to drive product strategy, execution, and cross-functional alignment. In this session, we’ll show how to evolve PLM into a product management backbone that connects engineering, operations, and business decisions. You’ll learn practical workflows for managing product definitions, changes, and lifecycle data in a way that improves visibility, reduces delays, and enables better decision making. Walk away with patterns you can apply immediately to move beyond BOM management and unlock real business value from PLM.
speakers: Gus Quade, Sr. Technical Sales Specialist,  Fusion PLM, Autodesk

title: Beyond the Migration: From Discovery to Momentum
abstract: Migrating an organization to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) requires a sophisticated balance of technical automation and cultural change management. This session will explore the comprehensive migration journey at VanKirk Electric, focusing on the development of internal AI-assisted tools to automate legacy project transfers. We’ll detail how we addressed complex technical hurdles—such as long-file-path limitations—while coordinating across departments to ensure the new environment met the specific needs of every team. Furthermore, we’ll showcase our "ACC Training Hub," a centralized Microsoft SharePoint ecosystem designed to drive high adoption rates through on-demand training, support ticketing, and peer-to-peer engagement forums.
speakers: David Smith, Technology Integration Manager, Vankirk Electric

title: Beyond the Migration: From Discovery to Momentum
abstract: Migrating an organization to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) requires a sophisticated balance of technical automation and cultural change management. This session will explore the comprehensive migration journey at VanKirk Electric, focusing on the development of internal AI-assisted tools to automate legacy project transfers. We’ll detail how we addressed complex technical hurdles—such as long-file-path limitations—while coordinating across departments to ensure the new environment met the specific needs of every team. speakers: David Smith, Technology Integration Manager, Vankirk Electric

title: Beyond Tool Adoption: Orchestrating Change with Autodesk Forma
abstract: Is adopting digital solutions and AI alone truly sufficient? This session will offer a point of view on how we scaled digital delivery across an organization of more than 5,000 engineers. As highlighted in Autodesk’s State of Design and Make, owners are increasingly demanding outcomes enabled by data-driven decision making. To connect digital initiatives to these outcomes, we’ll show how Autodesk Forma acts as a foundation for aligning value streams and driving organizational transformation. You will gain two vision frameworks that enable transformation in conditions of rapid change and ambiguity, along with real-world examples of how Forma accelerated consensus-building and supported owner decision making on complex projects.
speakers: Koichi Murata, Sr Principal, Solutions Architect, Autodesk
Arisa Takahashi, Manager, Obayashi Corporation
Gen Morimoto, Archi / Data Engineer, Obayashi Corp.

title: BIM Meets Real World: Geospatial Data Integration Best Practices
abstract: To plan, design, build, and manage projects suited to a more sustainable and resilient future, owners and design teams need spatial context of the built and natural environment in their workflows. The Esri-Autodesk partnership delivers out-of-the-box tools and capabilities that bridge BIM and geographic context, putting location at the center of informed decision making. This session will explore the range of available integration approaches, strategies for enriching existing workflows rather than disrupting them, downstream considerations that also benefit early conceptual design, and real-world governance practices that can make or break a successful integration.
speakers: Erika Bocian, Principal Consultant, ESRI
Shiori Sasaki, Senior Consultant, Esri

title: BIM Rebar Revolution: Information Management Standard for Rebar and Its Impact on Chilean Industry
abstract: Is it possible to eliminate uncertainty between structural design and the fabrication plant? This session will reveal the milestone of creating the first BIM information management standard for reinforced concrete, a strategic development transforming productivity in Chile. We’ll analyze how the ecosystem—integrated by the new national standard, AEC Rebar, the ICDM web platform, and Nexo BIM Power Data—achieves a robust and auditable data flow. Through real-world success cases, we’ll demonstrate how automation from Revit to industrial fabrication eliminates critical interpretation errors, optimizes the procurement cycle, and finally connects all stakeholders in a high-efficiency digital environment.
speakers: Manuel Saavedra, CEO, AEC Shift
Ivana Kermen, Principal Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Alejandro Marinelli, Principal Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: BIM to EAMS: Building the Bridge Between Digital Delivery and Asset Lifecycle Management
abstract: The most powerful moment in digital delivery isn't when the model is complete. It's when an owner traces a work order back to a verified asset record and makes a better decision because the data was there. This session will show how to make that moment possible. Drawing on large-scale aviation and transportation infrastructure experience, you’ll learn to structure BIM/CIIM deliverables that deliver value beyond handover. Asset data schemas, COBie deliverables, and Revit models connected through Autodesk Forma become the foundation for an operational ecosystem where owners and delivery teams share a single source of truth, driving smarter operations and measurable facility performance for the life of the asset.
speakers: Matt Anderle, AVP, Director of Digital Strategy, AECOM
Chris France, Digital Operations Manager, AECOM

title: Boosting Autodesk Development Using AI with AutoLISP and C# .NET
abstract: Learn how to use AI as a practical coding assistant to accelerate AutoCAD development. This 30-minute strategy session will show how AI can generate AutoLISP routines and C# .NET code, assist with debugging, and support code translation—enabling faster iteration and higher-quality results. Attendees will gain strategies to evaluate AI-generated code, integrate it into existing projects, and apply AI-assisted workflows effectively across both legacy and modern Autodesk development.
speakers: James Johnson, Application Developer, Synergis Software

title: Braindate
abstract:

Share expertise, solve real-world challenges, discover new ideas, and make meaningful connections with attendees who are passionate about the same topics you are - from AI and automation to digital twins, BIM workflows, and more.

 

Visit My AU Portal to start Braindating!

times.room: Venetian, Expo Hall C - Braindate Lounge, level 2

title: Breakfast
abstract: Grab coffee and a bite to eat to fuel your second day at AU.

title: Breaking Down Silos: Modernizing AutoCAD-Inventor-Revit Interoperability with Data Exchange
abstract: For EFCO's team of 250 engineers, moving design data across AutoCAD, Inventor, and Revit software meant constant rework, misaligned models, lost parameters, and no path to incremental updates. By adopting Data Exchange, EFCO built a consistent, update-aware pipeline that scales reliably across the firm’s full team. But the real power of this story extends beyond EFCO: Its workflow is a blueprint for any industry where manufacturing and architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams must collaborate across domains. You’ll leave this session with practical techniques for modernizing multitool workflows and a model for enabling seamless cross-domain collaboration, from design to construction.
speakers: Jonathan Crowson, CAD Support Manager, EFCO Corp.
Gaurav Bhamre, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Trevor Love, CAD Administrator, EFCO Corp.

title: Bridging BIM and Hydraulics: Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro for Smart Pressure Networks
abstract: Discover a new integration between Civil 3D and InfoWorks WS Pro software that connects BIM-based pressure pipe network design with detailed hydraulic analysis. See how bidirectional data exchange helps teams create constructable 3D networks using real parts while validating pressure, flow, and performance in InfoWorks WS Pro. Learn how this workflow improves design quality, reduces rework, and supports more-cost-effective outcomes. An industry expert will share real-world workflows, key benefits, lessons learned, and practical recommendations for successful adoption.
speakers: Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Ahmed Elsayed, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk
Mahmoud Najmeddine, BIM Manager, Khatib and Alami

title: Bridging the Field-to-Office Gap: Centralizing Workflows in Autodesk Forma
abstract: Moving from decentralized PDFs and paper to a unified digital ecosystem requires more than just software—it requires a cultural shift. This session explores how the Convention Center project transformed fragmented punch lists and labor tracking into streamlined Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) workflows.
speakers: Shree Kabra, Digital Technology Specialist, AECOM - Hunt
Brandon Kisner, Quality Superintendent, Penta Building Group

title: Building a CIP Concrete Dashboard with Autodesk Data Exchange and Autodesk Power BI Connector
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn how to build an on-demand model-driven data dashboard for your project teams using the Autodesk Data Exchange API and Autodesk Power BI Connector. Model-driven data dashboards will give your project teams on-demand access to model-based information and will help them forecast their jobsite needs. By building model-driven, filterable dashboards, you empower your team members by placing at their fingertips the data they require daily to run a lean and efficient jobsite.
speakers: Ihsan Gin, Regional BIM/VDC Manager, Baker Construction - Eastern US Commercial

title: Building an AI-Ready BIM Data Backbone with Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) organizations struggle to scale automation and AI because BIM data is fragmented, inconsistently governed, and tied to individual projects. This session will show how Drees & Sommer and AnkerDB built a centralized BIM data backbone using Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable reliable automation and consistent data quality at scale. The collaboration started as a rapid proof of concept at DevCon 2025, was validated across multiple projects, and is now scaling at the business-unit level. The session will explain how Autodesk Forma data, Autodesk Platform Services software, and downstream systems were connected to support automated validation, data enrichment, analytics, integrations, and AI-supported workflows for cost management and lifecycle assessment (LCA).
speakers: Moritz Mombour, Head of Digitalization EPCM REI, Drees & Sommer SE
Valeriia Vlasenko, Expert, Drees & Sommer

title: Building Insight: Using FARO Reality Capture, Qbitec Visualization, and Autodesk Solutions to Drive Better Decision Making
abstract: Every project starts with assumptions—but misalignment with reality leads to costly rework. What if decisions were grounded in real-world conditions from day one? This session will present a practical AECO workflow from field to design, showing how reality capture combined with ReCap, Revit, AutoCAD, and Autodesk Forma becomes a true decision engine. Discover how point clouds and 360-degree imagery enable early validation, risk identification, and trusted data integration into design environments. With FARO Sphere XG, Qbitec, and FARO As-Built, learn how to accelerate modeling, improve coordination, and reduce uncertainty—empowering teams to shift from reactive problem-solving to proactive, confident project delivery.
speakers: Ritesh Chandawar, Lead Product Manager - AECO, FARO Insight, a business of AMETEK Inc.
Irene Radcliffe, Product Manager, AEC Software, FARO Insight

title: Building Resilient Communities: A Collaborative Revit 2027 Sample Model
abstract: Following the 2025 Los Angeles fires, The Foothill Catalog Foundation and Autodesk partnered to accelerate rebuilding through a collection of preapproved residential designs. This session will go behind the scenes of creating the new Revit 2027 residential sample model that is part of this catalog. We’ll explore the unique collaboration between a nonprofit and Autodesk to develop the design with interchangeable options. Discover the challenges of balancing municipal standards with modeling best practices, and see the "split" where the model evolved into both a product asset and a real-world home. Join representatives from The Foothill Catalog Foundation and Autodesk to learn how Revit can transform residential workflows and empower communities. Build better, together.
speakers: Paul Aubin, Author/Consultant, Paul F Aubin Consulting Services, Inc.
Harlan Brumm, Director, Product Management, Revit Core Capabilities & Collaboration Services, Autodesk
Rachel Martinelli, Co-Founder / Board Member, Foothill Catalog Foundation

title: Building Smarter with AI in Construction
abstract: Join Tomer Rosenthal, Principal Product Manager for AI at Autodesk, to explore and demo practical AI-powered workflows that help construction teams make faster, more informed decisions, reduce manual effort, and turn project data into actionable insights. And learn how smarter, more connected ways of working can help teams deliver better project outcomes.

title: Building the AI Ecosystem for Better Engineering in AEC
abstract: Ben Cochran, Vice President of Engineering at Autodesk, and Peter Madlener, CEO of VIKTOR, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how AI is moving beyond experimentation and into real engineering workflows. The episode explores AI agents, connected ecosystems, domain expertise, trust, automation, and how organizations are beginning to transform practical business processes using emerging AI capabilities.

title: Business Intelligence Without Leaving Your Browser: Autodesk Forma Data into Microsoft Fabric
abstract: Long gone are the days of CSV files and IT requests to download software to create your dashboards and reports. Also long gone is the need for a data scientist to help you start taking advantage of YOUR data. During this technical deep dive, we’ll walk you through the fundamentals of bringing your Autodesk Forma data into Power BI via Microsoft Fabric without ever leaving your preferred internet browser. From there we’ll share some tips and tricks to kick-start your dashboarding journey. Your data pipeline to business intelligence has never been more direct, and we hope to teach you just how easy it is to start building your own reports in the cloud. From blank canvas to a dashboard in under 60 minutes - let us shepherd you into the new era of data and reporting.
speakers: Nathaniel Coombs, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
Santhosh Krishna Sekar, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
Joe Fields, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, AEC Analytics, Autodesk

title: Carbon Intelligence in the Cloud: Connecting ORIS to Autodesk Forma and Your Enterprise Data Ecosystem
abstract: Carbon assessment still happens outside the tools where infrastructure teams actually work. In this panel discussion, Autodesk, Ramboll, and ORIS explore what it looks like when that changes, bringing carbon intelligence directly into the cloud environment where project data already lives. Drawing on a concrete project from Ramboll, panelists will share how their team embedded carbon workflows into their existing Autodesk Forma environment without disrupting data governance or forcing manual exports. The conversation will surface the technical and practical realities of connecting carbon assessment to the project data ecosystem, from integration architecture to day-to-day workflow impact.
speakers: Jón Gunnar Hilmarsson, Chief BIM Manager, Ramboll
Sheena Zhang, Sr. Manager, AECO Sustainability Strategy, Autodesk
Guilhem de Montaignac, BIM Advocate & Software Engineer, ORIS
Nolwenn LANCIEN, Head of partnership, ORIS Material Intelligence

title: Catch a first look: The Future of Street Design
abstract:
Get a live look at new street design capabilities in Autodesk Forma. See how we’re expanding Forma into street and roadway design and how these new capabilities will connect with Civil 3D.

Whether you’re a civil engineer, road engineer, transportation planner, or similar, discover how Forma can help you explore more options, identify risks earlier, and align your team around a strong design direction—faster and with greater confidence.

title: Change Orders: Chaos to Order
abstract: Before adopting Cost Management, our change order process lived primarily in Microsoft Excel. Looking back, it’s honestly impressive (and a little terrifying) that it worked at all. Moving to Cost Management allowed us to standardize the process and drive more-consistent outcomes. But giving up the flexibility and freedom of spreadsheets left many of our project managers feeling stuck. In this class, we’ll show how we use the Change Order tools in Cost Management to simplify the process without losing the flexibility our teams need. You’ll learn how we balance structure where it matters and flexibility where it doesn’t—streamlining workflows in a way that improves PM productivity and keeps them happy, without sending them back to Excel.
speakers: Tim Kelleher, Ops. Standards and Innovation Manager, Brinkman Construction Inc.

title: Collaborating at the Heart of Design and Manufacturing
abstract: Discover the inspiring collaboration of Team Bath Heart and Autodesk at the Autodesk Technology Centre in Birmingham, merging creativity with advanced technology to create a revolutionary artificial heart. Team Bath Heart is a multidisciplinary engineering team from the University of Bath in England. Two-time champions of the international Heart Hackathon, the team is pioneering innovations in artificial-heart design—combining advanced simulation, manufacturing, and biomedical insight to push the boundaries of medical engineering. The team uses the Autodesk Fusion collaborative features, CAM profiling, and generative design tools to accelerate the design, testing, and prototyping of their next-generation artificial heart.
speakers: James Wainwright, Technical Lead, Team Bath Heart
Aksharaa Gupta, Team Lead, University of Bath- Team Bath Heart

title: Community Meetup: Media and Entertainment - Creators & Artists
abstract: The media and entertainment industry is evolving rapidly, driven by advances in AI, emerging technologies, shifting audience expectations, and new creative possibilities. Join us for a meetup where industry professionals come together to explore how creators, studios, and production teams are adapting, innovating, and thriving in this dynamic landscape. Designed for artists, creators, producers, technologists, and other media and entertainment professionals, this event is a chance to network, exchange ideas, and discover trends shaping the future of content creation, storytelling, and production.
speakers: Joaquim Moral, Senior Community Manager, Autodesk
Didier Raphael Ramirez Darjo, Autodesk Expert Elite, Independent consultant
Felipe Fierro, Film Director - Autodesk Expert Elite, Pigmalion Animation Studio
