Elmer Muñoz, Profesor e Investigador, Expert Elite Member

title: Community watch party: Day 2 Keynote in English by The Big Room
abstract:
Hello everyone!

We invite you to join us for the Day 2 Keynote, live from AU 2026 in Las Vegas.

Join us in the Zoom room with several members of the Expert Elite program and Autodesk's Community Manager, Alex Eckhart. We'll be watching this session together and chatting live.

title: Connecting BIM to Citizen-Scale Digital Twins: Sustainability, Compliance, and Connected Infrastructure
abstract: SIMICO S.p.A delivered infrastructure to the 2026 Winter Olympics (Livigno, Cortina, Milano, Verona, Bormio) using a full Autodesk pipeline: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Autodesk Forma Build, Autodesk Platform Services, Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Navisworks software. Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Build managed cost, schedule, and field workflows. Autodesk Platform Services connected everything bidirectionally. This Autodesk-Azure dual common data environment (CDE) enabled a complex environment where BIM authoring changes synced with Forma cost tracking, Build field logs, and compliance docs. These pipelines preserved data integrity from Autodesk tools to digital XR experiences (VR/AR/pixel streaming), making the twin accessible to all stakeholders. Tailored as such, this system delivered an organic ecosystem, reducing risk and accelerating decisions on complex public infrastructure in Italy.
speakers: Francesco Cappilli, Head of Digital Engineering, Infrastrutture Milano Cortina 2026 Spa

title: Converge at Sweco How Integrated Workflows & XR Enhanced, Revolutionized a Multidisciplinary Project
abstract: Can a multidisciplinary team across countries and companies deliver a better wastewater treatment plant, faster, by working as one? At AU 2026, Sweco’s Zinta Rize shares the Kongsberg WWTP: a project that doubled capacity while meeting strict EU standards. Using Plant 3D, Revit, Civil 3D, and ACC as a single source of truth, plus VR reviews in Autodesk Workshop XR, the team broke silos and improved coordination. Results: 25% efficiency gain, 15% less 3D effort, and major reductions in 2D drafting. Discover how integrated BIM, cloud workflows, and immersive collaboration enabled smarter decisions, faster delivery, and a more sustainable, future-ready facility.
speakers: Zinta Rize, Water and Wastewater Engineer, Sweco Norge
Jani Pehkonen, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Dara Treseder on Building Trust, Brands, and Leadership in an AI World
abstract: Dara Treseder, Chief Marketing Officer at Autodesk, returns to the Digital Builder podcast to discuss what it takes to build trust and brand relevance in the era of AI. The conversation explores authenticity, thought leadership, marketing strategy, reputation building, and why organizations of all sizes must find new ways to stand out as information becomes increasingly abundant and accessible.

title: Data-Rich: Meeting the Model Standard Owners Now Expect
abstract:
What an owner expects inside the model has changed dramatically in recent years. The model has stopped being just a coordination artifact, it feeds prefab, production tracking, field deliverables, and facilities maintenance. On mission-critical work, and especially data centers, the stakes climb even higher because electrical infrastructure sits on the critical path and schedules leave no room for delay. The gap between a standard model and what is expected now shows up as measurable hours per project, and it lands hardest on teams that are already running at capacity.

This session draws on patterns Augmenta is seeing across a wide range of mission critical projects, breaking down how teams are meeting demand by generating data rich models from the start rather than back filling detail under deadline pressure.
speakers: Francesco Iorio, CEO, Augmenta Inc

title: Day 2 Keynote
abstract: Hear from Autodesk’s industry leaders as they bring Autodesk’s AI into sharper focus through the lens of your industries: design and manufacturing; architecture, engineering, construction; operations; and media and entertainment. Learn how the capabilities introduced on Day 1 translate into real-world productivity gains, more connected workflows, and new opportunities for you to create and build more.
speakers: Andrew Anagnost, President and Chief Executive Officer, Autodesk
Amy Bunszel, EVP, Architecture, Engineering, and Construction Solutions, Autodesk
Diana Colella, EVP, Interactive Graphics, Media & Entertainment, Autodesk
Stephen Hooper, Senior Vice President, Autodesk Operations Solutions, Autodesk
Jeff Kinder, EVP, Product Development and Manufacturing Solutions, Autodesk

title: Day 2 Keynote
abstract: Hear from Autodesk’s industry leaders as they bring Autodesk’s AI into sharper focus through the lens of your industries: design and manufacturing; architecture, engineering, construction; operations; and media and entertainment. Learn how the capabilities introduced on Day 1 translate into real-world productivity gains, more connected workflows, and new opportunities for you to create and build more.
speakers: Andrew Anagnost, President and Chief Executive Officer, Autodesk
Amy Bunszel, EVP, Architecture, Engineering, and Construction Solutions, Autodesk
Diana Colella, EVP, Interactive Graphics, Media & Entertainment, Autodesk
Stephen Hooper, Senior Vice President, Autodesk Operations Solutions, Autodesk
Jeff Kinder, EVP, Product Development and Manufacturing Solutions, Autodesk

title: Decision-Driven Parametric Tunnel Design Using Shared Project Data
abstract: Many tunnel projects rely on static design approaches that limit the ability of stakeholders to anticipate construction risks and adapt to evolving constraints. This session will present a decision-driven parametric design approach for tunnel and cross-passage modeling using shared project data accessible to stakeholders. Based on a real tunnel project in the United Kingdom, we’ll demonstrate how Dynamo-driven workflows enable rapid iteration of design scenarios and validation of geometric constraints. The session will also highlight collaboration between design and construction teams using shared linear references. We’ll also share how value was assessed, including reduced design iterations, improved risk anticipation, and faster decision making.
speakers: Mikhail SEMENENKO, BIM Manager, Bouygues Construction
Nicolas RAGEUL, Digital Transformation Leader, Bouygues TP

title: Delivering Kentucky Lock with BIM, GIS, and Federated Models: A USACE Case Study
abstract: The Kentucky Lock Addition Project is a high-priority U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) effort requiring coordination across multiple districts, agencies, and contractors. This session will provide a technical deep dive into how BIM, CAD, and GIS were integrated through an Advanced Modeling Project Execution Plan (PxP) to support design, coordination, and construction. Using tools that include Civil 3D, Revit, Inventor, and Navisworks software, teams developed federated models for clash detection, sequencing, and as-built deliverables. You will see how model-based workflows improved coordination, reduced errors, and supported better decision making across the project lifecycle.
speakers: Chris Miller, CAD-BIM Regional Technical Specialist, US Army Corps of Engineers

title: Design and Manufacturing Community Meetup
abstract: The design and manufacturing industry is experiencing rapid advancements, driven by innovative technology and evolving market demands. Join us for a meetup where industry professionals will come together to explore how designers and manufacturers are navigating, innovating, and excelling in this dynamic landscape. Tailored for designers, engineers, and other industry professionals, this event will provide a unique opportunity to network, share insights, and discover the latest trends shaping the future of design and manufacturing. Be part of the conversation and engage with fellow experts to collectively push the boundaries of our industry.
speakers: Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc.
Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk

title: Designing 3D Spaces using AI World Models
abstract: Existing AI image and video models allow for rapid iteration from text or concepts to images and videos but can only produce 2D outputs allowing for limited downstream interaction and editing. World models such as World Labs’ Marble can create complete and visually rich 3D environments in minutes from just a handful of real images, concept sketches, 360 panoramas, or a 3D layout. This session will walk through a variety of workflows combining AI image models and Marble together to rapidly build, edit, and visualize 3D worlds, as well as ways to export the resulting 3D Gaussian splat files into other tooling for further iteration.
speakers: Ben Mildenhall, Cofounder, World Labs

title: Designing 3D Spaces using AI World Models
abstract: Existing AI image and video models allow for rapid iteration from text or concepts to images and videos but can only produce 2D outputs allowing for limited downstream interaction and editing. World models such as World Labs’ Marble can create complete and visually rich 3D environments in minutes from just a handful of real images, concept sketches, 360 panoramas, or a 3D layout. This session will walk through a variety of workflows combining AI image models and Marble together to rapidly build, edit, and visualize 3D worlds, as well as ways to export the resulting 3D Gaussian splat files into other tooling for further iteration.
speakers: Ben Mildenhall, Cofounder, World Labs

title: Designing for Agriculture at Scale: Autodesk Tools for Crop Productivity and Processing
abstract: Smallholder farmers face climate volatility, energy constraints, and post-harvest loss. Yet many products are not designed for their realities. This session will show how Kheyti and S4S Technologies apply Autodesk tools—including Revit, Robot Structural Analysis, Autodesk Fusion, and Inventor with Autodesk CFD—to design greenhouse systems, agrivoltaics, and food processing technologies that improve yield and income reliability, reduce energy and material use, and minimize crop loss. You’ll gain practical approaches for embedding human-centered design into engineering workflows, building internal technical capability through pro bono and E4C support, and applying Autodesk-enabled methods to drive resilience, sustainability, and equitable impact at scale.
speakers: Ayush Sharma, Co-Founder & COO, Kheyti
Vaibhav Tidke, CEO and co-founder, S4S Technologies

title: Designing the Digital Factory for Process Plants: Bridging AEC and Manufacturing Workflows
abstract: Process plant projects require tight alignment between plant design and manufacturing. Yet, these areas are often disconnected, causing rework, delays, and fabrication errors. This session will show how design decisions impact manufacturing using a water treatment plant example. We’ll demonstrate how Autodesk’s Architecture, Engineering & Construction Collection and Product Design & Manufacturing Collection create a connected, design-led workflow from layout to fabrication. The session will also highlight common breakdowns in design-to-manufacturing workflows and how Autodesk Platform Services and structured data improve collaboration. This session is relevant for water treatment, energy, and industrial facilities industries.
speakers: Peter De Strijker, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Bas Claassen, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Did We Build What We Designed? Using AI and Autodesk Forma to Prevent Material Risk and Rework Failures.
abstract: Construction projects do not fail because of design. They fail when what gets built does not match specifications. Rework costs about 9% of US project budgets—more than $30 billion annually—driven mainly by design errors, omissions, and specification mismatches, worsened by poor data and fragmented communication. Wrong or unverified materials cause rework, delays, disputes, margin loss, and safety risks. This session will show how to intervene earlier by closing the loop between design intent and construction reality using AI and Autodesk Forma. You will see real-time material verification, automatic issue detection, and proactive risk management, with insights from a customer co-presenter.
speakers: Blake Jackson
Joe Butterworth, Head of Growth, NA, Qualis Flow

title: Digital Factory Summit | Autodesk Forma: The Common Data Environment for Gigafactory Development
abstract: In this session, we’ll go over how to use Autodesk Forma projects for managing the design of gigafactories and comparable megaprojects. Learn how Tesla brings together inputs from manufacturing teams, design groups, and construction management into one common repository to streamline project delivery. Explore how cloud-workshared Revit projects organize inputs from AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and other industry CAD tools to bring manufacturing context into your Revit files, and send factory context to your manufacturing teams or vendors. Finally, see how tools within Forma allow for coordination, clash resolution, and field documentation to support successful project execution.
speakers: Mark Rickabaugh, Lead, VDC & Reality Capture, Tesla
Genavera Gannon, Staff Engineering Program Manager, Tesla

title: Digital Factory Summit | Digital Twins Unplugged: Platforms, Practices, and Lessons from the Field
abstract: Digital twins are moving from concept to reality, but success looks different for every organization. This session will bring owners, operators, technologists, and consultants together to discuss moving from digital models to operational twins. Panelists will highlight different types of digital twins, from simulation-based twins like FlexSim to operational and asset-based twins like Autodesk Tandem, enabling connected asset data and certainty from design through operations. The discussion will compare platform ecosystems, use cases, and scaling strategies across the asset lifecycle. You can expect examples, lessons learned, and open dialogue on what works and what doesn’t, while connecting with peers shaping the future of digital twins.
speakers: Farzad Moghbel, VP of Technology Products, Michael Baker International
Marin Pastar, VP, Digital Practice Executive, Michael Baker International
Marc Banning, Senior Business Development Executive, Autodesk
Andrew Davis, Regional Technology Lead - Canada, Jacobs
Jacob Noltner, Section Leader, Mechanical Engineer, Jacobs

title: Digital Factory Summit | From Reactive to Resilient: How MaintainX Is Powering Intelligent Maintenance
abstract:
Keeping operations running has never been more critical. Maintenance and
operations leaders must maximize asset performance, reduce downtime, control costs, and do
more with leaner teams - all while keeping production moving.

Join leaders from MaintainX, now an Autodesk company, to explore how leading manufacturers are rethinking maintenance as a driver of operational performance and a competitive differentiator. Drawing on insights from thousands of customers, this session will share how data from frontline workers, real-time machine connectivity, and artificial intelligence (AI) help frontline teams improve asset reliability, increase productivity, and make faster, more informed decisions.

You'll learn how digital maintenance platforms help teams reduce unplanned downtime,
standardize work, and turn operational data into actionable insights. This session will also cover what's next for intelligent maintenance and asset management  - and why manufacturers are making this a priority today.
speakers: Ozella Bowman, Sr Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk
Colin Morris, Head of Solutions Consulting, MaintainX, Autodesk

title: Digital Factory Summit | From Spreadsheets to Simulation: M2X's Journey of Factory Simulation with FlexSim
abstract: This project addresses the challenge of optimizing a highly labor-intensive manufacturing process for GTM systems at M2X Energy, where welding and pipe fabrication dominate both cycle time and total hours. Traditional spreadsheet-based analysis lacks the ability to capture dynamic interactions between resources, workflows, and constraints. Using FlexSim software, we built a discrete-event simulation of the factory to model real-world operations, identify bottlenecks, and make accurate process decisions based on data. Combined with design inputs such as weld reduction strategies, this approach enables data-driven decisions to reduce manufacturing hours, improve throughput, and support scalable factory and product design.
speakers: Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Nicholas Schwartz, Chief Manufacturing Officer at M2X Energy, M2X Energy

title: Digital Project Delivery. Autodesk Forma Build Implementation.
abstract: Our session will show how Autodesk Forma was implemented and governed on a live health care project, adapting workflows to project‑specific needs. We will demonstrate the application of standards during active delivery to maintain consistency and data integrity while teams adopt the platform and evolve digital practices in real time. You’ll learn how collaboration was structured across Autodesk, construction technology, operations, and BIM by deploying two Autodesk Forma Build projects to separate design coordination from construction execution, alongside targeted training. We’ll also cover license provisioning, role‑based access, content ownership alignment, and Power BI dashboards that deliver actionable insights for better decisions.
speakers: Rania Hassan, VDC Regional Manager, Ellisdon

title: Digital Twin for Factories: Enabling Smart, Connected, and Collaborative Manufacturing
abstract: Manufacturing companies face inefficiencies from disconnected systems across factory design, engineering, and shop-floor operations. This session will demonstrate how a digital twin approach using Autodesk Tandem software integrates BIM-based factory models with live production data for smarter decisions. For greenfield projects, FlexSim integration enables simulation of layouts, production lines, and material flows before execution, optimizing throughput and reducing project risk. Energy Monitoring and Management System (EMMS) integration adds early visibility into energy and sustainability. For brownfield plants, connecting programmable logic controllers (PLCs), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), and a manufacturing execution system (MES) creates a unified operational view, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and bottleneck identification.
speakers: Santosh Kulkarni, President - Software Engineering Services, Neilsoft
Aniruddha Phatak, AVP-Strategic Market Development (Software), Neilsoft
Varun Bansal, AVP - Strategic Market Development (MFG), Neilsoft

title: Digital Twins in Practice: A Blueprint for Moving from Design to Operations
abstract: Digital twins promise to connect design and operations, but what does it take to make this real? In this session, Johnson Controls and ARKANCE will share how they helped a customer transition from disconnected intelligent models to a scalable digital twin through aligned roles, workflows, and cross‑industry collaboration. Learn how to prepare BIM data for operations by structuring Revit deliverables for Autodesk Tandem software and downstream workflows, including auditing, cleanup, and standardization. We’ll also cover integrating Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, mapping physical assets, and building a practical sensor strategy. Finally, we’ll explore long‑term success factors, including governance, ownership, maintenance, and stakeholder adoption to ensure your digital twin delivers lasting value.
speakers: Mohamed Abdelhameid, Digital Sales Director, Johnson Controls
Troy Gates, Senior Solutions Consultant, ARKANCE
Nick Miller, Pre-Sales Director, ARKANCE

title: Discover Forma: From Site to Building Design
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Forma is transforming planning and building design. See how Forma Site Design brings AI-powered workflows, real-time analysis, and collaboration to early-stage planning, and how Forma Building Design extends that journey with intuitive modeling, integrated analytics, and connected workflows with Revit.

title: Does Your Workstation GPU Still Make the Cut? How Local AI Is Raising the Bar for Autodesk Workflows.
abstract:
The workstation GPU that handles your Revit models and 3ds Max renders may be showing its age — not because Autodesk got more demanding, but because AI did.

Local AI tools are rapidly becoming part of how design and engineering professionals work: generating concepts, automating repetitive tasks, and running inference without sending sensitive project data to the cloud. These workloads are GPU-hungry, and they compete directly with your Autodesk applications for the same critical resource: graphics memory.

In this session, we'll give Autodesk users a practical framework for understanding GPU memory requirements across the workflows that matter to them. You'll see how real Autodesk applications perform under varying VRAM configurations, what happens when local AI enters the picture, and where the common pain points emerge. We'll also look at what the next generation of workstation GPUs brings to the table — and whether an upgrade is warranted or premature.
speakers: Ken Denton, Global Segment Lead AEC / PD&M, HP
Michael Katz, Sr Manager Software Development, AMD

title: Don’t AI Everything: Hybrid Automation with Autodesk Platform Services and Revit
abstract: Automation specialists are increasingly tasked with finding areas to implement AI. But how do we decide when AI is the correct tool and when deterministic automation serves better? Through a live demo of an AI-augmented building regulation compliance checker running on Autodesk Platform Services, we will explore a practical hybrid framework. The Automation API and Revit software handle rule evaluation through a deterministic engine. Large language models (LLMs) extract compliance rules from regulation documentation and explain failures in natural language. And the Viewer SDK provides visual context. We’ll demonstrate a human-in-the-loop approach and show how AI architecture adapts rapidly when regulations change or new markets require new rule sets.
speakers: Will North, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd
Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk
Neil Lee, Director, Design Automation Systems Ltd

title: Downstream Starts Upstream: How Governance Turns Project Data into Operational Value
abstract: For too long, BIM data quality for operations has been treated as a downstream problem—discovered late, remediated manually, and handed over with gaps that limit long-term value. In reality, these are rarely technical failures, but governance failures. This class will explore how organizations can shift from reactive records remediation to upstream prevention by introducing a BIM governance coordinator role: bridging client requirements, internal standards, and multidisciplinary delivery teams to ensure expectations are understood, tracked, and enforced throughout the project lifecycle—turning BIM deliverables into more-reliable operational assets.
speakers: NATALIA CASTILLO, Workplace Strategy Director RM and BIM, CBRE
Robert S. Olsen, Senior Director, CBRE

title: Drilling Down with BIM: Automating Tunnels and Rock Bolts in a Hydropower Megaproject
abstract: Large-scale underground infrastructure projects push BIM workflows to their limits, especially when dealing with tens of kilometers of tunnels and tens of thousands of repetitive elements. This session will present a real-world case study from a major Australian hydropower project where BIM was implemented across both design and construction phases. We’ll focus on the processes developed to efficiently model more than 40 kilometers of tunnels and more than 35,000 rock bolts, ensuring consistency, performance, and constructability. By combining Revit, Civil 3D, Dynamo, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), we established automated workflows for geometry generation, data structuring, and model coordination.
speakers: Emmanuel CHOCQ, Head of BIM Department, Tractebel
Maher DJEDIDI, BIM Manager, TRACTEBEL

title: Driving Certainty On-Site: 4D Workflows for Program, Progress, and Risk to Managing Contractors
abstract: A key industry challenge is accessing reliable, real‑time progress data, which is critical to reducing the risk of project overruns and cost escalation. This presentation will show how managing contractors can use data within design models and Autodesk Forma to deliver effective 4D workflows. We’ll showcase practical uses of Autodesk Forma and Revit software to plug into construction software that provides more-accurate site data, enabling teams to confidently measure progress against program.
speakers: Quoc Pham, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
Nathan Love, Construction BIM Manager, Multiplex

title: Dr. Vibe: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Start Loving Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: This is a tale from a BIM manager’s foray into vibe coding—going from having no coding experience to building web applications that tap into the Autodesk Platform Services APIs to supercharge the capabilities of our Autodesk Forma-based CAD managers. Have you been curious about Autodesk Platform Services but haven’t pulled the trigger because you’re not “a developer”? With Dr. Claude’s help, you can be! Come to this session to learn tips on diving into the world of Autodesk Platform Services and large language models (LLMs). We’ll share lessons learned on working hand in hand with these LLMs in a safe and efficient way so that you can also share in this digital boon.
speakers: Winston Pagliaro, Civil Infrastructure BIM and VDC Specialist, HNTB

title: Electrical Analytical Systems and Loads
abstract: Electrical engineers are often forced to make major design decisions early, with limited information and rapidly changing project conditions. In this hands-on lab, you will use Revit Electrical Analytical Systems tools to create connected, data-rich workflows for schematic and early design. You’ll define analytical area loads and analytical equipment loads, create analytical equipment, and connect and evaluate loading scenarios to make better design decisions with minimal model information for better project outcomes. Using these tools early in your design process can give you better understanding of current loading scenarios and help you plan for future expansions with minimal effort.
speakers: Jacob Miller, Electrical Applications Product Owner, IMEG

title: Enabling Next-Generation Autodesk Workflows: Can a Slim Mobile Workstation Really Keep Up with Your Autodesk Work?
abstract:
As AI, visualization, and increasingly complex 3D workflows reshape how teams design, review, render, and simulate, professionals need more than raw specifications—they need a system that performs reliably wherever work happens.

 

Join us and an Autodesk industry expert from the Elite Experience program for a real-world look at modern mobile workstation workflows across Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD, and Fusion. The session will share firsthand experience using a slim mobile workstation as a primary device, including the performance, responsiveness, mobility, battery-life, and day-to-day usability factors that matter beyond a benchmark score.

Attendees will learn how to evaluate the right balance of CPU, GPU, memory, storage, and connectivity for their own workloads; when local, cloud, or hybrid workflows make sense; and how to identify where a hardware upgrade will deliver meaningful value
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel
Lindsay M Benjamin, ISV Partner Marketing Manager, INTEL CORPORATION
Catherine Rocha, Platform Readiness Lead, Intel

title: End-to-End Drainage Design with Autodesk Forma, InfoDrainage, and Civil 3D
abstract:
InfoDrainage and Autodesk Forma will soon work together as part of a connected workflow for site drainage design. In this session, you'll work with Civil 3D and InfoDrainage models hosted in Forma, using live references such as surfaces and CAD background data to keep design information connected across applications. 

 Starting from a site design, you'll develop and optimize a drainage network in InfoDrainage, leveraging connected site data to accelerate hydrologic design. 

 The workflow continues with dynamic hydraulic simulation, exceedance assessment, and review of results, followed by compliance-ready reporting. The session concludes by synchronizing the completed drainage design back to Civil 3D, demonstrating a streamlined, connected workflow from site model to validated drainage design.
speakers: Javier Soto, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
Daniel'le DeVoss, Drainage Technical Account Specialist, Autodesk

title: Expo
abstract:
This is where AU comes to life.

Step inside the AU Expo and experience the future of design and make in motion. See live demos of Autodesk’s newest product offerings, connect with the Autodesk Community, recharge and network in our lounges, and explore breakthrough solutions from hundreds of innovative sponsors.

Whether you’re shaping buildings, infrastructure, teams, or transformation strategies, the Expo is your place to discover what’s next—and meet the people making it happen.

And don’t miss the AU Quest: a fun, interactive way to explore, connect, and uncover the best of the Expo.

Come curious. Leave inspired.

title: Feature, Add-In, or AI? Should You Buy, Build, or Hack in 2026?
abstract: AI is changing how work gets done in architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO), but it’s also complicating the path forward. Do you wait for a feature, bolt on an add-in, or hack together an AI solution? In this panel, industry experts will respond to real-world scenarios and rapid-fire questions. Drawing from experience across platforms, add-ins, and AI workflows, they’ll weigh trade-offs between features, integrations, and fast AI solutions, including what works, what breaks, and what creates risk. This session is for teams working within real constraints. Whether you have development resources or you’re figuring it out on your own, you’ll leave better equipped to decide what to buy, what to build, and when a quick solution makes sense.
speakers: Carl Storms, Technical Success Manager, Newforma
Mostafa EL AYOUBI, CEO, Oorkestra Online
Michael Kilkelly, Senior BIM Developer, Ulteig
John (JT) Pierson, Product Manager, Autodesk
Brodi Scott, Research, Development and Innovation Manager, BIM One

title: Find Answers, Not Artifacts: One Search Across All Your Project Systems
abstract: Your firm already holds the answer to almost every question your teams ask. It's buried in specs, RFIs, submittals, drawings, and contracts across hundreds of projects. The problem was never a lack of data. It was getting an answer without digging for the artifact. This session shows what changes when AI is grounded in your real project data. We start simple, asking a question of one folder. Then we go historical: what did we spec for the curtain wall on our last three hospital projects? Then live across your active systems. The part that separates this from every generic AI demo: you watch permissions respected in real time. Change who's asking, and the answers change with them.
speakers: Philip Townsend, Principal Solutions Architect, Egnyte Inc.
Aaron Vorwerk, AEC Practice Leader, Architects + Owners, Egnyte

title: Fireside Chat with the Inventor Product Team
abstract: Sit down with the Inventor product team and discuss your most-pressing issues, concerns, and questions about Inventor. Many Inventor team members will be available to answer your questions. What are the best practices for maximizing your Inventor use? How are Inventor projects prioritized and chosen for each release? Where is Inventor going in the near future? AI, Model States, Drawings, Sheet Metal, Autodesk Fusion versus Inventor—all your favorite topics will be open for discussion.
speakers: Steven Dennis, Sr Principal Engineer, Autodesk
Patrick Cataldo, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk
Andrew Faix, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk
Johnson Shiue, Sr. Principal SW Eng. Test, Autodesk
Dan Szymanski, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk

title: From 2D to Digital Twin: Connecting Design to Operations in Retail Lifecycle with BIM, IoT, and AI
abstract: Retail construction still relies heavily on fragmented 2D documentation, creating a disconnect between design, construction, and operations. This session will explore how EssilorLuxottica is transforming that model by converting 2D assets into structured 3D BIM and building a connected digital lifecycle. By linking design data to Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and maintenance workflows, stores evolve from static deliverables into dynamic, data-driven digital twins. This session will present a scalable approach to connect design to operations, improve asset visibility, and enable predictive maintenance, turning retail environments into fully integrated intelligent assets.
speakers: Caterina Peretti, Global Innovation Manager, EssilorLuxottica
Giorgio Radojkovic, Global Engineering & Innovation, Essilorluxottica
Enrico Trovato, Head of AECO Automation & Intelligence, EssilorLuxottica

title: From Capture to AI: How Data Enrichment Unlocks the Value of Motion
abstract: AI-powered animation is only as good as the data behind it, but most motion data wasn’t designed for AI. In this session, we’ll demonstrate a projection-mapped capture app that guides performers in real time to produce more-structured motion. As well as how Label Maker, a tool integrated within the Autodesk ecosystem, uses AI to turn raw motion data and videos into richly tagged, reusable data sets. You will walk away with a clearer picture of how to make motion data actually usable for AI, and how to rethink their pipelines to get there. The real value of motion data isn’t in the capture—it’s in the enrichment.
speakers: Olivier Zurcher, Animation Researcher (Technical Animator), Autodesk
Larasika Nadela, Machine Learning Developer, Autodesk

title: From Chaos to Clarity: The Data Exchange Strategy Behind a $1.3 Billion Dubai Harbour Icon
abstract: What happens when intelligent data connects teams who’ve never spoken the same language? On a $1.3-billion Dubai Harbour tower, we built an integrated workflow unifying BIM, planning, and commercial teams. The planning schedule defines the data standard, enforced through Autodesk Forma Library parameters. Data Exchange extracts data live from Revit into Power BI—no exports, no delays, no conflicts. Commercial teams get a weekly dashboard filterable by work package with a live 3D model view. Quantities are now a click away, even on your tablet. Leave with a replicable framework connecting decision makers using live collaboration and Revit, Forma Library, Data Exchange, and Power BI—proven on one of the Middle East's most ambitious towers.
speakers: Ahmad ElGammal, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk Forma, Autodesk
Derek Bourke, Digital & BIM Manager, Khansaheb Civil Engineering

title: From Chat to Commands to Agents: The Evolution of AI Automation in Revit for AEC Teams
abstract: AI in AEC is moving fast, but most teams are still stuck at the chat window. This session maps the three stages of AI maturity in BIM workflows: conversational chat, saved commands, and agents. Using real deployments inside Autodesk Revit, we'll show how firms turn one-off AI prompts into reusable commands their whole team can run (think add-ins created in minutes, not months), and how agent-based systems go further: planning multi-step work, using tools, and even creating new tools when a workflow demands it. Drawing on lessons from enterprise teams automating modelling, documentation, and QA/QC, we'll cover what worked, what failed, and how to judge where your organization sits on the chat-to-agent curve. You'll leave with a practical framework for scaling AI beyond individual experiments to team-wide automation and how agents can provide adoptive solutions to workflows.
speakers: Ali Najmi, Director, BIMLOGIQ

title: From Disconnected Tasks to Standardized Construction Workflows: Connected by Autodesk Forma with a Database
abstract: Construction work often struggles not because information is missing, but because tasks, people, and decisions remain disconnected. Has the push for accurate data increased input and broken workflows? This isn’t anyone’s fault. It happens when work isn’t connected properly—and that’s where Autodesk Forma helps. This session will show how Autodesk Forma links technical feedback, project coordination, and management information. In one workflow, standardizing how information reached the right people at the right time reduced office-side coordination by 70%, site response effort by 50%, and initial review meeting time by 20%. We’ll also show how this approach supports repeatable workflows and easier transfer of technical knowledge.
speakers: Saori 櫻井, Project Manager, Shimizu Construction Co., Ltd.

title: From Existing to Extraordinary: Reinventing Renovations with Autodesk Forma Site Design, Revit, and Dynamo
abstract: Renovation projects are often slowed by fragmented data and limited early-stage insight, leading to rework and inefficient decisions. This session will demonstrate how Autodesk Forma Site Design and Dynamo automate data-driven workflows and enable early-stage analysis within Revit software. By connecting design to execution, teams reduced manual effort, accelerated scenario evaluation, and improved coordination across multiple buildings. You’ll learn how to structure connected workflows that support scalable, data-driven renovation strategies and deliver measurable improvements in speed, consistency, and sustainability.
speakers: Isabella Nascimento, Technical Specialist, PARS

title: From Ground Data to Cost Certainty: Outcome-Based Excavation Analysis in Forma with GroundIQ
abstract:
Early-stage site design moves fast, but ground conditions rarely keep up. Excavation costs are a top risk driver, yet reliable estimates arrive long after key decisions are made. 

This session demonstrates outcome-based BIM in practice: directly from Forma, GroundIQ generates a 3D ground model from site investigation data and delivers excavation volumes and cost estimates automatically without specialist intervention. 

Attendees see a live demo: footprint placed, ground intelligence derived, cost insight surfaced instantly. BIM that connects subsurface conditions to project outcomes.
speakers: Nigel Peters, Senior Product Manager - Rail, Autodesk
Arno Koldewee, Head of Product, Fugro
Ben Wardell, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: From Image to Groom: AI Workflows for Production-Ready Character Hair
abstract: As media and entertainment pipelines accelerate, digital hair creation still requires hours of work, with artists meticulously crafting guide curves and tuning modifiers to match reference. This session will demonstrate a research prototype of an AI-powered tool for Maya software that converts one or more images into fully editable grooms. We’ll show how this approach reduces grooming time by up to five times through automation of repetitive work, and how it integrates with simulation and downstream departments. We’ll also detail our wholly owned, synthetic data strategy for training AI models designed for transparency and control. See this workflow in action and understand how image-to-groom can accelerate your character production workflows.
speakers: Hilmar Koch, Director, M&E Research, Autodesk
Derek Cheung, Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Autodesk

title: From Intelligent Model to Environmental Outcomes: AI-Powered Tools for RE2020 Compliance
abstract: How do you turn an intelligent model into a lever for real environmental performance? At the Chabanne office, we developed a suite of custom Revit plug-ins directly connected to live environmental databases (INIES/RE2020). This enabled our teams to query material carbon data, track biosourced ratios, and monitor energy indicators directly inside the model in real time. This outcome-based BIM helped us across different projects—especially Thoiry's Kindergarten—to reach Passivhaus-level energy needs, exceed the RE2020 2028 carbon threshold, and achieve 1.5 times the Level 3 biosourced label. Through Autodesk Platform Services, plug-ins, Autodesk Forma, Forma Site Design, Forma Building Design, Model Context Protocol (MCP), API, and AI, the intelligent model turned into a decision-making engine for our whole team.
speakers: Alexandre PARENA, BIM MANAGER / COORDINATOR, CHABANNE

title: From Inventor Design to Machined Part: Building a Real Digital Thread with Autodesk Fusion CAM
abstract: In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a real machined project designed in Inventor and programmed in Autodesk Fusion Manufacturing Extension. Follow the complete workflow: creating and iterating the part in Inventor, uploading to Fusion, applying toolpaths, generating G-code, and efficiently updating toolpaths after design changes using simple refreshes. We’ll cover both the cloud approach (AnyCAD linked references and Desktop Connector) and the enterprise version using Vault Professional software for controlled releases and revision management. We’ll share the actual files, challenges encountered, key lessons, and measurable time savings. You’ll leave with actionable steps to build an effective digital thread between design and manufacturing teams.
speakers: Edward Rose, Client Success Manager - Adoption Programs, Symetri

title: From Legacy to Cloud: Enterprise Migration Strategies for Civil Infrastructure to Autodesk Forma
abstract: Civil infrastructure firms manage complex portfolios across fragmented legacy environments like network drives, ProjectWise, Microsoft SharePoint, and BIM 360. Transitioning to Autodesk Forma Data Management establishes a unified, cloud-native ecosystem. But doing so at scale introduces high operational risks. How do you migrate massive Civil 3D data sets without disrupting active data shortcuts and xrefs? Where do heavy InfraWorks models and point clouds reside? What is the governance strategy for historical deliverables? This session will deliver a strategic, repeatable migration playbook engineered for complex multi-office environments. Moving beyond theory, we’ll provide a tool-by-tool, phased workflow. You’ll learn how to audit file dependencies across legacy storage, map structures to the Autodesk Forma architecture, and execute staged migrations that maintain business continuity. You’ll leave with an enterprise decision framework and an immediate deployment checklist.
speakers: Drew Theis, Technology Consultant, ARKANCE

title: From Messy to Meaningful: Ground Truth, Update-Ready Site Context in Revit
abstract: Accurate site context is essential for coordination, yet many teams struggle with fragile or inconsistent site models in Revit. This session presents reliable workflows for building and maintaining site context using common upstream sources, including Forma Site Design generated Revit files, Civil 3D published surfaces, and native Revit tools such as TopoSolids and Building Pads. The focus is on stability and change management – showing how to keep site models update ready as upstream data evolves, while supporting design development, visualization, and downstream coordination with minimal rework or model failure. We'll walk through four practical workflows for bringing site context into Revit and discuss where each one shines and where each one breaks.
speakers: Joseph Huang, Principal, Architect, BIM Design Team Lead, Stantec
Raghavendra Bhat, Principal, Sr. BIM Integration Specialist, Stantec

title: From POC to Product: Building an AI-Powered Revit App
abstract: Go behind the scenes on the development journey of an AI-powered generative design tool for architecture and MEP. See the unfiltered reality of evolving a simple proof of concept into a full-fledged product that converts text prompts and reference images directly into native Revit geometry that streams live into Enscape, where you can visualize, adjust, and iterate in real time. We’ll share the conflicts, pivots, and technology decisions that got us across the finish line, pulling back the curtain on what it really takes to deliver a truly innovative product that provides real efficiency gains for architects and engineers in an architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) technology landscape where AI is compressing years of technology change into months.
speakers: Roderick Bates, Senior Director, Product Operations, Chaos

title: From Promises to Performance: Hands-On Workplan Commitments and Metrics in Autodesk Forma Build
abstract: Construction teams often struggle to translate high-level schedules into reliable short-term execution. While master schedules define what should happen, they rarely capture what actually gets done on-site. In this hands-on lab, you will explore how to use Workplan Commitments and Metrics in Autodesk Forma Build to improve planning reliability, accountability, and performance tracking. Through guided exercises, you will do the following: create and manage short-term work plans, assign ownership and commit to tasks, track execution using Percent Plan Complete (PPC), analyze root causes for delays, and improve planning outcomes. By the end of the session, you will understand how to move from reactive scheduling to data-driven planning.
speakers: Ovais Mattoo, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
Dhruvesh Shah, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Reality to Simulation: Capturing, Predicting, and Replaying the Experience of Design with APS and AI
abstract: How do you capture or predict the human experience of design and replay it to build empathy and drive better design decisions? This session will present a technical workflow spanning three research projects: real-world experience capture (The Bentway, Toronto), XR-based capture in virtual environments, and agentic simulation of human behavior. Learn how Autodesk Platform Services powers a system where human-experience data—whether captured using sensors, or in VR, or predicted using AI—can be replayed by designers to better appreciate the diversity of the human experience of design. We’ll explore the technology that will power future human-experience-driven workflows, from sensors and VR headsets to knowledge graphs and vision language models.
speakers: Kean Walmsley, Dir., Systems Design/Architecture Engrg, Autodesk
Andrés Sebastián Diaz Vargas, Systems Engineer I  COP, Autodesk

title: From Revit Stills to Stories: AI Video Workflows for Architectural Communication
abstract: Architects increasingly need to communicate design intent through motion before there is time or budget for traditional animation and for audiences who do not read drawings. This session shows how approved design assets from Revit based rendering views, diagrams, sketches, physical model, photos, can become short AI-assisted motion assets for design reviews, competitions, and client presentations. Attendees will learn a repeatable still-to-video workflow, see where AI video supports architectural communication and where it falls short, and apply QA guardrails for review and trust before using outputs in practice. A 5 minute case study assembled from 30 AI-assisted clips will also demonstrate how short generations become a coherent story.
speakers: Qian Huang, Design Technology Specialist, HOK

title: From Scans to Decisions: Turning Reality Capture into Actionable Digital Twins with AI
abstract: Are your scans just visuals or are they driving real project decisions? Reality capture is widely used, but most workflows stop at geometry, leaving critical insights untapped. This session will demonstrate how to transform scan data into actionable digital twins by integrating Revit, Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), and asset data workflows. Learn how AI can detect deviations, connect model elements to structured data, and surface insights that influence coordination, cost, and project outcomes. If your scans aren’t informing decisions, you’re missing their true value. This session will show how to unlock the potential of scanned data and workflow.
speakers: Prashanth Dommeti, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Shubhamkar Bapat, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: From Silos to Shared Insight: How Construction Teams Deliver Better Outcomes
abstract:
Projects aren’t delayed by effort—they’re slowed by disconnects. When teams work in separate systems, visibility drops, costs drift, and decisions lag.

 

Join leaders from Reef Capital Partners, Jacobsen Construction, Gaylor Electric, and UPS to learn how they’re using Autodesk Forma to bridge these gaps. Discover how owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors are leveraging Forma—including new Bridge functionality—to connect workflows, improve cross-organizational collaboration, and enable more data-driven cost management.

 

Walk away with practical ways to improve coordination and drive better project outcomes.
speakers: Saadet Yilmaz, VP of Development, Reef Capital Partners
Christy Steffen, Assistant Director of Gaylor University, Gaylor Electric
Tawnya Reitz, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Heather Soderquist, VP, Construction Innovation, Jacobsen Construction
Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS

title: From Sketch to BIM: Forma Building Design and Revit
abstract: Discover how Forma Building Design and Revit 2027 connect in a sketch-to-BIM workflow that keeps design intent intact. See how teams can move from conceptual massing into early schematic design, explore options with environmental analysis and unit metrics and layouts, and continue development in Revit with site context and connected Forma scenarios. We’ll also show how Revit users can run environmental analysis, such as wind, directly in Revit—giving teams the flexibility to start in Forma or Revit, depending on their workflow.

title: From Unique to Scalable: Modular School Design with BIM, Industrialization and Resilience
abstract: After the 2024 floods in southern Brazil, the Rio Grande do Sul State faced an urgent challenge: how to deliver public schools faster with quality and at scale. This session presents the Escola+ project, a modular and standardized school model developed using BIM. Instead of unique designs, schools are assembled from a catalog of more than 60 modules that can be combined to meet different educational and site requirements. Using Autodesk Revit and Forma, the digital workflow integrates design data, cloud collaboration, and data-driven decision-making, accelerating project delivery while improving coordination, consistency, and predictability. Attendees will learn how modular BIM workflows can help scale resilient public-school infrastructure.
speakers: Gabriela Hoffmann Fiuza, Coordinator, Secretariat of the State of RS
Júlia Akemi Motoshima, BIM Manager, Secretariat of the State of RS

title: Future-Proof Modeling: Building Universal Pipeline Assets with USD in Maya
abstract: Modeling is no longer just about clean quads and edge loops—it’s about data integrity for a global pipeline. As studios transition to OpenUSD, Maya artists must evolve their workflows to ensure assets are portable and performant. In this technical deep dive, we’ll move beyond basic topology to explore the authoring of "smart" USD assets. We’ll cover the latest Maya 2026 USD modeling tools, demonstrating how to manage complex hierarchies, variants, and metadata within a single file. You will learn how to optimize meshes for seamless deformation across platforms and avoid common pitfalls in a multisoftware environment. Stop modeling for a single scene—start building assets that thrive in a universal production ecosystem.
speakers: Kaan Zorlu, Lead 3D Artist, Leo Production

title: Generative Design for Smart Catenary Systems Using Adaptive Parametric Families
abstract: Designing overhead catenary systems is highly constrained and repetitive. This session will introduce a generative workflow that automates catenary design using an advanced Revit adaptive parametric family capable of handling more than 350,000 configuration combinations. The family embeds engineering logic and formulas that evaluate geometry, spans, clearances, and structural conditions to automatically select the optimal mast configuration. Attendees will learn how Generative Design or Dynamo drives this parametric engine, enabling the model to adjust the catenary mast as track geometry changes. The result is a smart, self‑adapting catenary system that reduces manual work and increases design reliability across long rail corridors.
speakers: Ayman SALEH, BIM R&D Manager, Colas Rail

title: Generative Design for Smart Catenary Systems Using Adaptive Parametric Families
abstract: Designing overhead catenary systems is highly constrained and repetitive. This session will introduce a generative workflow that automates catenary design using an advanced Revit adaptive parametric family capable of handling more than 350,000 configuration combinations. The family embeds engineering logic and formulas that evaluate geometry, spans, clearances, and structural conditions to automatically select the optimal mast configuration. speakers: Ayman SALEH, BIM R&D Manager, Colas Rail

abstract:
Turn your AU 2026 experience into recognition you can use right away. Complimentary onsite Autodesk certification testing gives eligible* attendees the opportunity to validate their expertise, showcase real-world skills, and earn an industry-recognized digital credential.

 

Whether you're looking to advance your career, strengthen your team's capabilities, or set yourself apart from the competition, certification is a meaningful way to invest in your future.

title: Hand-Key Gameplay Animation Workflow Using Autodesk Maya and Flow Studio
abstract: In this session, we'll take a deep dive into how AI can help your team’s animators in a nondestructive and efficient way. We’ll cover how to use Autodesk Flow Studio software as a base and bring that into Maya software for the regular hand-key stylized animation workflow for gameplay animations—later exporting it to Unreal Engine to create a gameplay-ready asset. This workflow can also be used for film and TV animations.
speakers: Alex Ferreira Simoes, Senior Gameplay Animator & Director, Riot Games - Agora Community
Brendan Russert, Senior Animator, Riot Games

title: Harnessing AI for AECO: Live Workflows Connecting Design, Engineering, and Fabrication
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping AECO, but most solutions remain disconnected from engineering and fabrication workflows where technical decisions are made. Through live demonstrations, this session will show AI embedded within production environments, leveraging engineering standards, deterministic calculation engines, fabrication rules, and BIM data. Explore AI-assisted model management, load generation, detailing, and cross-platform workflows enabled through AI skills and APIs/MCPs, delivering reliable, auditable results while keeping engineers and fabricators in control.
speakers: Manuel Liedot, CEO, GRAITEC
Emmanuel LEROY, Chief Product and Strategy Officer, GRAITEC

title: Headless Civil 3D: Batch Exporting to NWC and IFC Without Ever Opening the Drawing
abstract: If you've ever opened 35 DWGs™ one at a time to extract corridors, surfaces, and pipe networks for Navisworks software, you know the pain—file locks, memory ceilings, and a week of clicking. Then the design updates … and you start again. This session will cover the batch-processing of Civil 3D models headlessly—scanning, extracting, and exporting without opening the UI. The pipeline includes: a Microsoft Excel manifest, headless discovery, solid extraction, surface meshing, pipe transfer, property attachment, and export via AcCoreConsole. We’ll also cover the five approaches that failed—Explode destroying pipe intelligence, ConvertToSolid crashing headless databases, wBlock corrupting styles, zero-triangle access violations, and PropertySet zombie objects. Each one cost days.
speakers: Sobeshan Pillay, Associate, WSP

title: Help Lead Autodesk Fusion into the Future
abstract: Join this interactive “Inside the Factory” session where your feedback will directly influence the future of Autodesk Fusion software. Explore emerging capabilities across AI-driven design, connected workflows, and advanced manufacturing—and gain early insight into product direction. Through guided discussions and hands-on exploration, you’ll share challenges, evaluate new features, and help prioritize what matters most. This collaborative session will connect real-world workflows to product development—ensuring Fusion evolves to meet your needs.
speakers: James Mann, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk
Peter Champneys, Principal Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk
Kyle Williams, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk

title: How to Build a Business Case for Reality Capture: Insights from the Nation's Biggest Builders
abstract: Reality capture technology promises to reduce rework, settle disputes, and give project teams eyes on site without being there. Getting support for this new technology internally can be an uphill battle. In this session, you’ll learn what it takes to make a successful business case for reality capture programs from leaders at some of America’s biggest construction companies. They'll cover what sparked their search for solutions, what use cases they were targeting, what got them past executive skepticism, and what KPIs they measure. You’ll leave with a practical framework for building your own business case, including the specific language, metrics, and project examples that moved the needle with leadership.
speakers: Roy Malcolm, Central Region VDC Leader, DPR Construction
Ahmad Sabbouri, Vice President of Customer Success, Cupix
Jonathan Caceres, VDC Manager, The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company

title: Immersive Design Reviews: Evaluating Informed Design Models in Workshop XR
abstract: This class would show how configurable, manufacturable content created through Informed Design can be reviewed at scale in Workshop XR, helping teams catch spatial clashes, access BIM data, and raise issues before construction. This would be especially suited to a Revit-to-review workflow for BIM/VDC teams because Workshop XR is built for collaborative model reviews, supports issue management, and connects directly to Autodesk Forma.
speakers: Shane McDonald, BIM Design Manager, Murphy
Matthew Lenehan, Mechanical Design Engineer, Murphy

title: Industrialized Construction, Prefabrication, Modular, and Informed Design: Meet Your Peers at AU 2026
abstract: Join fellow AU attendees for an informal meetup focused on industrialized construction, prefabrication, modular workflows, and Informed Design. This session will bring together owners, designers, builders, fabricators, and Autodesk Partners who are shaping the future of how buildings are designed and delivered. Whether you’re advancing off-site construction, exploring connections between design and manufacturing, or learning from peers across the ecosystem, this meetup will be a space to network, exchange ideas, and discuss challenges and opportunities across the AU community.
speakers: Clair Stone, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
James Youmatz, General Adoption Manager, Autodesk

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Productization Goes Global: Designing Scalable Entertainment Venues
abstract: How do you deliver iconic, high-quality venues at speed and scale? This session will explore how productization, systemization, and kit-of-parts strategies are transforming the design and delivery of large-scale entertainment venues. Drawing on global case studies—from temporary World Cup stadiums to immersive venues like Sphere—this talk will demonstrate how standardized components and platform-based approaches enable flexibility, performance, and rapid deployment. It will also examine how digital workflows, BIM, and data-driven design all support convergence between design, manufacturing, and operations. You’ll gain practical insight into applying industrialized construction principles without compromising experience or design quality.
speakers: Nathan Tobeck, Head of Digital APAC, Populous

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | From BIM to Factory: Turning Building Design into Scalable Manufacturing Systems
abstract: This session will explore the strategic shift from traditional construction to industrialized construction and what it means for the future of the built environment. Using DuPod as a case study, this session will examine how integrating engineering, digital platforms, and manufacturing creates a new delivery model for buildings—one based on productization, scalability, and predictable outcomes. Rather than treating buildings as one-off projects, industrialized construction applies manufacturing logic to create repeatable building systems and supply chains. This discussion will focus on how this shift can reshape productivity, risk, and value creation across the construction industry.
speakers: Ihab Ramlawi, Co-Founder & Managing Director, DuPod

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Industrialized Construction: What Will It Take to Reach the Tipping Point?
abstract: Industrialized construction is widely discussed but unevenly implemented. This panel will bring together perspectives from research, technology, academia, and industry to examine what it will take to scale prefabrication, productization, and design for manufacturing and assembly (DfMA). Drawing on new global research with Dodge Construction Network across five markets, the session will explore why fewer than half of organizations report scaled use despite strong intent. Panelists will test these findings against real-world experience, focusing on procurement, early design decisions, supply chain integration, and workforce capability to identify what must change to reach industry-wide adoption.
speakers: Donna Laquidara-Carr, Industry Insights Research Director, Dodge Construction Network
Ray Boff, National Prefab Leader, DPR Construction
Paul Drayton, Head of Digital, Laing O'Rourke
Martin Fischer, Professor, CIFE-Stanford
Az Jasat, Dir., Strategic Planning/Analytics, Autodesk

title: Industrialized Construction Summit | Design Once, Fabricate Many: Scaling Industrialized Construction with Bouygues Construction
abstract: Bouygues is industrializing construction with a multidiscipline modular landing shaft integrating water and electrical systems. We'll demonstrate how Autodesk Informed Design software connects BIM, fabrication, and installation into a seamless workflow. Using a modular MEP cabinet as a real-world case study, attendees will see how a single configurable design can generate fabrication-ready outputs, automate documentation, and ensure consistent quality across projects. We’ll explore the impact of the Informed Design approach: reducing coordination errors, accelerating installation, and enabling scalable prefabrication strategies. We'll highlight how design rules and structured data allow teams to move from project-based delivery to repeatable, productized construction.
speakers: Antoine MORIZOT, CAD Engineer, Bouygues Construction
Clair Stone, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage | Autodesk Forma Jeopardy!
abstract: Calling all game show enthusiasts—come participate in an Autodesk Forma-focused game of Jeopardy, where you can test your knowledge of the platform and pick up new tips and insights. We’ll cover AI capabilities, workflows from planning to operations, newly launched features, and more. This session is for everyone, from Forma novices wanting to learn more to seasoned experts eager to test their skills. Structured like the US game show, audience members can “buzz in” to answer questions, accumulate points, and compete for prizes. In this session, we’ll showcase Autodesk Forma capabilities in an interactive and fun format. Expect to walk away with fresh insights and practical applications to deliver your projects more efficiently.
speakers: Danielle Foss, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage I Hybrid Intelligence and a Pro-Social AI Future
abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping how we design, build, manufacture, and create. But as AI becomes more capable, the most important question isn't what AI can do, it's how people and organizations can use it to amplify human potential.
Autodesk’s Mike Haley (SVP, Research, Autodesk) and Heather McIntosh Cassano (VP, User Experience, AEC Solutions) will engage in a conversation with Dr. Cornelia Walther on how AI is rapidly changing the ways we work, collaborate, and what it means culturally as it's used to solve and innovate on increasingly complex challenges. The conversation will be moderated by Maxim Williams (VP, Global Culture and Belonging, Autodesk).
Together, the panel will explore the meaning of pro-social AI and hybrid intelligence, where combining human judgment with artificial intelligence can create better human centered outcomes for individuals, businesses, and society.
Attendees will leave with practical insights into how leaders, teams, and practitioners can navigate AI responsibly while maximizing its potential to unlock innovation, creativity, and opportunity.
This session is sponsored by Autodesk Global Culture & Belonging team.
speakers: Cornelia walther, Professor, Sunway University
Maxim Williams, VP, Global Culture & Belonging, Autodesk
Mike Haley, SVP, Research, Autodesk
Heather McIntosh Cassano, VP, User Experience, AEC Solutions, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage l AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma: A CAD Manager's Playbook for Connected Project Data
abstract: Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials is now included with stand-alone AutoCAD subscriptions, connecting desktop design workflows to unified, cloud-based project data without changing how your team works. In this technical deep dive, we’ll show CAD managers how to turn fragmented file management into integrated workflows that reduce friction and accelerate delivery for your teams. We’ll look at Connected Support Files for project-aware support files that load automatically, Connected References that fixes broken xrefs, Connected Sheet Set Manager, Checkout, and much more.
speakers: Amarjeet Sonkar, Senior Principal Experience Designer, Autodesk
Damian Willcox, Distinguished Experience Architect, Autodesk
