title: Innovators Stage | Skills to Pay the Bills: Creating Claude Skills for Autodesk Workflows
abstract: Claude skills provide a standard way to create reusable capabilities that help AI complete complex tasks. This session will focus on creating skills that automate design and project delivery workflows in Autodesk. You’ll learn what a skill is, when it should be used instead of prompts or Model Context Protocols (MCPs), how to design skills that interact with Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma, and how to adopt these automations across an organization. We’ll explore how skills can be used together with tools like MCP and custom scripts, and we’ll build practical examples such as querying BIM metadata, automating design data checks, and producing design documentation.
speakers: Poyraz Yildirim, Developer Advocate Manager, Autodesk
João Martins, Principal Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage | Skills to Pay the Bills: Creating Claude Skills for Autodesk Workflows
abstract: Claude skills provide a standard way to create reusable capabilities that help AI complete complex tasks. This session will focus on creating skills that automate design and project delivery workflows in Autodesk. You’ll learn what a skill is, when it should be used instead of prompts or Model Context Protocols (MCPs), how to design skills that interact with Autodesk Platform Services and Autodesk Forma, and how to adopt these automations across an organization. We’ll explore how skills can be used together with tools like MCP and custom scripts, and we’ll build practical examples such as querying BIM metadata, automating design data checks, and producing design documentation.
speakers: Anthony Sertorio, Principal Enterprise Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Inside Autodesk Certification: Strategies from the Exam Authors
abstract: Unlock the secrets behind Autodesk Certification. These exams are designed to validate real-world workflow skills required across the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Yet many candidates struggle to understand what’s truly being evaluated or how to prepare. Join exam authors for a behind-the-scenes look at how exams are designed to reflect industry practice and skills being tested. Learn from contributors to Certified Professional Exams in BIM Management and Revit Architectural, Structural, and Electrical Design. They will present certification-style examples inspired by real exam objectives and explore interpretation strategies. You’ll leave with a clearer understanding of how certification aligns with project workflows and how to improve skills needed to succeed.
speakers: ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM
Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim
Eric Wing, BIM Director, C&S Companies

title: Integrating Nature-Based Solutions in Civil 3D and InfraWorks for Resilient Infrastructure Design
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are reshaping how civil teams deliver resilient water infrastructure. Yet integrating watershed-scale insights into detailed design remains a challenge. This session will show how The Nature Conservancy applied targeted training and InfraWorks and Civil 3D software to connect regional watershed analysis with site-level engineering workflows. Learn how to translate watershed data into design inputs, develop NbS concepts into constructible models, and maintain data continuity across planning and design phases. See how connected workflows improved cross-team collaboration, enabled earlier decision making, and reduced project risk in real-world water infrastructure projects.
speakers: Carlos Rogeliz, Technical Director – N4W Facility, The Nature Conservancy
Jonathan Nogales, Science Associate, The Nature Conservancy

title: Integrating Structural Analysis Workflows in BIM with Revit
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll learn how to create, manage, and maintain analytical models in Revit for the purpose of structural analysis, BIM coordination, and design documentation. You’ll explore how to keep analytical and physical models coordinated as your design evolves, prepare your model for structural analysis, and bring analysis results back into your BIM workflow. By the end of the session, you’ll be able to close the loop between design and analysis, improving accuracy, efficiency, and collaboration in your structural projects. The session is for structural engineers and technicians who design and coordinate for BIM.
speakers: Catalin Lang, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Konrad Ociepka, Senior Product Owner, Autodesk

title: Keep Your Scanner. Unlock Your Point Clouds.
abstract: You own a survey-grade scanner. The point clouds it produces sit on a drive, hard to share and useless to anyone who is not a surveyor. This session will show you a different path. See how a point cloud from a Leica, FARO, Trimble, or other scanner becomes a navigable Matterport digital twin, then feeds Autodesk Forma, Revit, AutoCAD, or other design software through the integration your team already uses. You keep the hardware you bought. You make its output usable for the whole project team, not just the person who captured it. Through a live workflow, you’ll see Point Cloud Import turn a raw scan into a true 3D model with scan-to-BIM and scan-to-CAD output, and where that model fits against the photo-based documentation tools you may already run. You’ll leave able to map your own capture-to-coordination plan and put the scan data you’ve already paid for to work across design, construction, and closeout.
speakers: Sun-Yen Tan, Associate Product Manager, Matterport
Dominick Gallegos, Director of Product Marketing - AEC / FM, Matterport

title: Lessons from Cost Management Implementation Ninjas
abstract: Whether you're exploring Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build, actively using it, or pushing the limits as a power user, this session is for you! Join this 30-minute ask-the-experts session to connect directly with the Autodesk Forma Cost Management implementation experts. Get answers to your toughest questions, learn proven best practices, and hear how leading teams are optimizing cost workflows and enterprise resource planning (ERP) integrations to drive better outcomes. Discover practical tips and real-world strategies, and see how AI can help solve complex cost challenges. Plus, bring your scenarios to the table during an open Q&A and walk away with actionable insights you can apply immediately.
speakers: Nick Prato, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Tyler Patton, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Lunch
abstract: Midday is made for good food and good company. Join fellow attendees for lunch and enjoy a relaxed break before the afternoon sessions begin.

title: Lunch & Learn: Unleash Peak Performance: Optimizing Dell Pro Max Workstations for Autodesk and Local AI
abstract: • Discover how the new Dell Pro Max 14 and 16 mobile workstations—powered by AMD Ryzen™ processors for workstations —deliver desktop-class performance for demanding Autodesk workflows. In this session, we'll show you how to tune your laptop for maximum output, fine-tune Autodesk application settings for optimal responsiveness, and harness the power of agentic workflows and local AI to accelerate your everyday design and engineering tasks. Whether you're modelling in Revit, rendering in Arnold, or iterating in Fusion, learn practical tips to work faster, smarter, and untethered from the cloud.
speakers: Rob Jamieson, Senior ISV Manager-ADM, AMD

title: MASTERING MEGA PROJECTS: AN INFRASTRUCTURE BLUEPRINT TO PROJECT DELIVERY
abstract: Mega projects. How well do we understand them? As a Lead Design Consultant, let us try and get to the bottom of it. This session will focus through an Infrastructure lens on how to navigate these large scale, multi-disciplinary projects. Utilising Forma, we have to manage multiple stakeholders and consultancies with thousands of deliverables to constrained timeframes. Learn how we developed tools to decrease deliverable output times by 60%, created workflows to simplify coordination with other teams using Autodesk products and used live collaboration with Autodesk themselves to streamline solutions whilst live on the project. We will give you the blueprint on digital delivery with your own mega project.
speakers: Matt Keogh, Associate Technician, Buro Happold
Tom Ryder, CAD / Software Manager, Buro Happold

title: Maximizing the Value of InfoWorks ICM: A Model-Driven Approach to CSO Reduction
abstract:
Utilities managing combined sewer systems are increasingly challenged to reduce overflow events while controlling capital costs. This presentation highlights how the InfoWorks ICM hydraulic model was used as the foundation for advanced system optimization in the SUEZ SEVESC wastewater network in the western suburbs of Paris.
The calibrated InfoWorks ICM model enabled detailed simulation of network performance across a range of storm events, forming the analytical backbone for decision-making. Building on this, Optimizer™ (by Optimatics) was integrated to systematically evaluate thousands of operational and infrastructure scenarios, including regulator settings, pump operations, and real-time control (RTC) strategies.
speakers: Alexandre Gil, General Manager, SUEZ Optimatics
Josh Cantone, President, Optimatics
Joel Knight, NA Business Development, Optimatics

title: Measuring the Impact of Autodesk Forma Data Management on Design Applications
abstract: Transitioning from traditional network environments to cloud-based systems such as Autodesk Forma Data Management can be challenging. Understanding the advantages can be difficult without clear guidance for what works best. For this panel discussion, we’ll include industry-leading Autodesk experts to provide opinions and tips based on years of project and product experience. This session will start with a discussion on file management and move to Revit, Inventor, and Civil 3D tips for enhanced features when working in Forma Data Management. Next, we’ll cover content compatibility and end with recommendations for future projects to help your teams be as efficient as possible. Join us as we help you avoid many of the common challenges that accompany technology changes.
speakers: David Butts, Virtual Design and Construction Manager, Kimley-Horn
David Neill, Firmwide Forma Administrator, Kimley Horn
Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore
Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim

title: Meet Rhumbix: Connecting your Field-to-Finance Workflows
abstract: Join the Rhumbix team to discover how connected field and finance workflows can help construction teams turn jobsite activity into actionable insights. In this session, we’ll demo how Rhumbix streamlines the capture of labor, time, and production data from the field and connects it to downstream cost and financial workflows. And, share how better connections between the field and office can reduce manual processes and improve visibility into project performance.

title: Multi-AI-Agent BIM Orchestration: Building Autonomous Query. Check. Fix Loops for Revit.
abstract: What if your Revit model could check itself—and fix what it finds—autonomously? This session will introduce a multi-agent system where specialized AI agents collaborate in a loop: a Query agent will read model data via Model Context Protocol (MCP), a QC agent will check it against configurable standards, and a Design agent will propose corrections - each previewed, human-approved, and audited before any write. The cycle will repeat until the model passes. We’ll demo three live scenarios: Naming Convention Fix, Parameter Completeness, and Geometry Checking - built with Revit MCP Server, Forma MCP, Python, LangGraph, and configurable YAML rules. We'll also cover transaction management, convergence control, and the points where human oversight remains essential.
speakers: Phuc Le, Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: Nightmares in Motion: Animating the Creatures of IT in Welcome to Derry
abstract: Few characters in modern horror are as unpredictable as Pennywise, whose terrifying transformations lie at the heart of IT: Welcome to Derry. In this session, Rodeo FX Animation Supervisor Scott Holmes will reveal how the team used Maya software to design rigs and craft performances for Pennywise’s many monstrous forms. Through production examples and animation breakdowns, the talk will explore the creative process behind building creatures that can shift from subtle unease to full nightmare, while remaining believable, expressive, and terrifying on screen.
speakers: Scott Holmes, Animation Supervisor, Rodeo FX

title: No More “BIM Guy”: Driving Real Digital Transformation Across Construction
abstract: "That's the BIM guy's job." Whether you've heard it on a job site, in a coordination meeting, or in a boardroom, you know the gap this panel is here to close. An owner, a heavy industrial GC, a self-perform contractor, and a specialty MEP contractor join moderator Prateek Chitnis for an unfiltered conversation about what digital transformation actually costs across the construction ecosystem. No polished success stories. No vendor pitches. Just four practitioners from different seats at the table, each with a different definition of what "BIM adoption" means, and each with failures they haven't talked about publicly. Yet.
speakers: Danielle Dy Buncio, CEO, VIATechnik
Ravi Wood, BIM Director, Samsung Semiconductors
Prateek Shailesh Chitnis, BIM Manager, Dennis Group
Morgan Drivas, VDC Manager, JTM Construction
Brett Settles, VDC Director, Alberici Constructors, Inc

title: One Data‑Driven App to Rule BIM Documents and Automated Requirements Checks via ACC APIs
abstract:
Have you ever started a project with a BIM Execution Plan that slowly drifted away from real project? Documents become outdated, requirements fade, and no one can confirm that models and the common data environment still match what was agreed.

This class introduces a data‑driven approach where project requirements are not static documents but become active data in a single source‑of‑truth app (Power App). From that same data, it generates and updates project documents, runs checks across Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) and 3D models using APS APIs. AI helps interpret results and flag mismatches.

You’ll see an end‑to‑end demo and leave with a reusable pattern to keep what’s specified, documented, and modeled telling the same story.
speakers: Jérémy Mols, BIM Director, Artelia

title: One Platform, Zero Guesswork: Seamlessly Connecting 2D and 3D Takeoff with Estimation
abstract: A recent QuickBooks survey found that one in four construction companies risk closure if they make two or three inaccurate estimates. The estimation inaccuracy is caused by the complexity of 2D and 3D data and the frequent updates to bid packages. It’s compounded by siloed takeoff and estimation processes. Autodesk addresses this by seamlessly integrating takeoff and estimation within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). This lab will give you firsthand experience in workflows that improve takeoff accuracy and estimation using a unified, connected platform. You’ll link 2D and 3D takeoffs to cost data, enabling real-time estimation. Walk away with learnings to perform faster, data-driven takeoffs, and deliver predictable project estimates through a connected source of truth.
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk

title: One Shader to Rule Them All: Universal Lookdev with MaterialX and LookdevX in Maya
abstract: The era of "siloed" shading is over. As pipelines move toward OpenPBR and MaterialX, artists must learn to build materials that are platform-agnostic. This session will explore the power of LookdevX in Maya 2026 software for creating high-fidelity, universal shaders. We’ll break down how to move away from legacy shading networks toward a unified MaterialX workflow that ensures visual consistency across various renderers and applications. Explore the technical logic of LookdevX, learn how to use the new OpenPBR standard for both realism and stylization, and discover the secrets to "packaging" your lookdev so it survives the transition from Maya to the rest of your pipeline. Build once, render everywhere.
speakers: Kaan Zorlu, Lead 3D Artist, Leo Production

title: Operational Intelligence with Autodesk Tandem: Driving Maintenance ROI from Digital Twins
abstract: Digital twins offer operational insight, yet their value is often unrealized when data remains disconnected from daily operational workflows. Asset models exist, but maintenance decisions, cost analysis, and ticket creation still happen in separate systems, limiting adoption and measurable ROI. This session will explore how integrating Autodesk Tandem with maintenance operations transforms digital twins into practical decision-making tools. We’ll show how you can calculate maintenance ROI by correlating maintenance costs, downtime, and potential fault costs using AI, and how these insights accelerate maintenance ticket creation and support predictive, data-driven strategies.
speakers: Saverio Camillo Saviello, Sr Solution Architect, Autodesk

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Prestige NEXTRA: From Fragmentation to Control—Scaling 180 Million Square Feet of Real Estate with Autodesk Forma
abstract: Managing one of India’s largest RE portfolios, Prestige is transforming project delivery to address fragmented systems, siloed data, and limited cross-functional visibility. This session will introduce Prestige NEXTRA, an enterprise initiative to create a connected and standardized delivery ecosystem. We will showcase how Autodesk Forma integrates systems such as SAP, Primavera P6, procurement, and cost tools to improve information flow across design, planning, and execution. You will gain insights into enterprise rollout, governance, and adoption, along with key lessons from scaling digital processes across a large portfolio.
speakers: Vishesh Vishesh Kaul, Chief Information & Digital Officer, Prestige Group
Vishwajeet S. Patil, Engineering Transformation Head, Prestige Group

title: Procurement Without Chaos: Building Consistency with Best Practices and Connected Systems
abstract: Procurement issues cause roughly 50% of project delays, and using inconsistent, manual processes for planning/tracking is a recipe for cost overruns and missed deadlines. DPR Construction manages more than 2,000 projects annually, so the stakes couldn’t be higher. Success demands disciplined best practices across process, tools, and metrics. In this session, we’ll present a proven, measurable procurement planning and tracking approach using tools like Autodesk Forma, ConstructivIQ, and more. DPR has already implemented this across hundreds of projects—moving from disconnected workflows to a scalable, connected system. Join us to learn how you can apply the same principles within your own organization to drive more-predictable and efficient outcomes.
speakers: Sam Young, Solutions Architect, DPR Construction
Sadanand Sahasrabudhe, CEO, ConstructivIQ

title: Prompt to Procurement: AI Research at MIT on Closing the Render-to-Build Loop
abstract: Architects and BIM teams are generating AI images faster than ever. But outputs rarely connect back to real materials, specifications, or fabrication. This session will draw on three MIT Architecture and Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) research projects to show exactly where the design-to-build pipeline breaks down and what fixes it. What we’ll cover includes steering AI image generation with element-level references, matching rendered materials back into BIM specifications, and connecting natural language to robotic assembly—each finding maps to a workflow that practitioners can act on. You’ll leave with research-backed behavioral changes where AI tools genuinely add value in their pipelines and where the gaps need bridging.
speakers: Richa Gupta, Researcher and Forward Deployed Engineer, Massachusetts Institute of Technology |Nomic

title: ReCap Meshing for BIM Coordination
abstract: In this session, we’ll share a strategy discussion into ReCap software’s new mesh workflow for creating scan-derived meshes that perform reliably in Model Coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and Navisworks software. Using a confidential project case study, you will see how our team processed 1 TB of scan data across 1.2 million square feet and resolved repeated model crashes that disrupted access for virtual design and construction (VDC) engineers and trade partners. By moving from Leica Cyclone 3DR to ReCap-generated meshes, we improved mesh quality, stabilized performance, streamlined scan-to-coordination workflows, and enabled automated clash detection with existing conditions for more-reliable downstream delivery.
speakers: Gabriel Hernandez, VDC Project Manager, Turner Construction
Melinda Hoffman, Subject Matter Expert, Construction, Autodesk
Brad Lane, VDC Reality Capture Manager, Turner Construction

title: ReCap Pro Mesh to Revit Lab: Get Hands-On Structured Mesh and IFC Workflow for Faster Intelligent Modeling
abstract: Turning point clouds into reliable BIM inputs is still a challenge for many architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams. In this lab, you’ll execute a complete, field-tested ReCap Pro workflow that transforms scan data into structured, interoperable mesh models ready for enhanced design and collaboration. Guided by subject matter experts, you’ll apply automatic classification to generate clean meshes, standardize outputs using Template Manager, map Revit categories, and export IFC models for downstream BIM use. You’ll then use these outputs as modeling references in Revit and validate them through coordination workflows in Navisworks and Model Coordination. Walk away with a repeatable, end-to-end scan-to-BIM process that reduces manual remodeling and accelerates coordination across project teams.
speakers: Idoia Martinez, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk
Carlos Aquise, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Reimagining Facility Operations: A Client’s Strategy for a Living Digital Twin
abstract: A Confidential Client is redefining facility operations through an Autodesk Tandem-powered digital twin that transforms survey (ReCap software), scan-to-BIM (Revit and Civil 3D software), and project data into a living operational platform, not just documentation. Integrated with SkySpark and a CMMS, the twin enables machine-learning-driven fault detection and diagnostics, submetering analysis, and optimization control at the building level today—with a GIS-enabled, facility-wide decision layer on the horizon. The result: faster operational decisions, measurable efficiency gains, and a scalable model for AI-driven facilities management. Hear how a Client's digital delivery workflow became the foundation for continuous operational improvement, and see what it takes to get there.
speakers: Dan Kolimar, Vice President, NV5

title: Revit and CAD to Operational Digital Twins: Indoor GIS for Facilities Teams
abstract: Many owners have rich Revit and AutoCAD data—but after handoff, that information is often difficult for operations teams to use in workflows. This session will show how to turn design data into a floor-aware indoor geographic information system (GIS) that supports operations across campuses, airports, and other facilities. You’ll learn how to transform CAD/BIM data into an indoor system of record for maps, assets, spaces, safety, and occupants. We’ll walk through implementation patterns and data import methods from CAD/BIM into ArcGIS Indoors, using location as a framework to move from handoff to operational value. See real examples from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, where BIM data was converted into operational twins for assets, spaces, and situational awareness.
speakers: Adan Banda, Sr. Geospatial Data Manager, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
Will Isley, CTO - PS R&D Center, Esri
Gokce Ozcelik, Sr. Product Manager - Indoor GIS, Esri

title: Revit Community Meetup: Connect, Share, and Unwind
abstract: Join fellow Revit users for a casual, community-focused meetup during AU. This informal gathering offers a space to connect, share experiences, and engage in real conversations—no presentations or formal agenda. Step away from the busy schedule to swap stories, compare workflows, and meet others who understand the daily realities of working in Revit. Whether you're looking to expand your network or just recharge with like-minded peers, this session is for you. Autodesk team members will be there to listen, but the focus is on the community—you. Drop in anytime and stay as long as you’d like.
speakers: Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk
Scott D Davis, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk
Cesar Escalante, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Building Products, Autodesk

title: Revit in the Age of Agents: A Clear-Eyed Guide for the Perplexed
abstract: Dynamo scripts, Autodesk Assistant, Model Context Protocol (MCP) plug-ins, and embedded agents are four fundamentally different approaches to AI in Revit—all promising productivity, none interchangeable. This session is for BIM managers who don’t have a structured answer to the question, “Which one should we use?” We’ll walk through a practical evaluation framework: three questions that separate what each approach can and cannot do, demonstrated live inside Revit. You’ll leave with a comparison matrix you can use in your next vendor meeting, your next build-versus-buy discussion, or the next time someone on LinkedIn tells you the future is here.
speakers: Adi Shavit, CTO, SWAPP.AI

title: Revit MEP Fundamentals and New Tricks
abstract: Many teams still rely on outdated Revit MEP habits that slow coordination and create inconsistent models. This session will cover how to build a strong foundation in spaces, connectors, systems, circuits, and documentation. Then we’ll show how recent Revit improvements support better analysis, clearer panel and circuit workflows, improved analytical visibility for duct and pipe systems, and a smoother path from design to fabrication. We’ll share practical methods that help newer users build confidence and experienced users work faster, model more accurately, and reduce rework.
speakers: Matthew Collier, Technical Product Manager, IMEG Corp.
Sean Fruin, Mechanical Applications Product Owner, IMEG

title: Revit Structural Connections for Design Engineers
abstract: The Revit Structural Connections tool brings steel connections into the design environment, and using it as a structural design consultant might require borrowing strategies from detailing and fabrication workflows. This session will share lessons learned from developing connections for the Revit 2027 Snowden Towers Sample Project, focusing on how engineers can effectively use the tool in a design workflow. Through practical examples, we’ll explore approaches to connection modeling, as well as key considerations and ways to get useful results without overcomplicating the process. The goal is to help structural engineers understand where the tool fits, how to use it efficiently, and how to make it work within their projects.
speakers: Desiree Mackey, CFE, BD Mackey Consulting
Brian Mackey, Head Geek, BD Mackey Consulting

title: Right from the Start: Setting Up the Civil 3D Survey Environment
abstract: A successful Civil 3D survey workflow begins with a properly configured survey environment. This session will focus on configuring Civil 3D to support consistent and predictable movement of data from field crews to survey deliverables. Topics will include establishing the survey working folder, managing equipment databases, creating and maintaining figure prefix databases, configuring linework code sets, organizing description key sets, and structuring point groups. You’ll gain a clear understanding of how these components work together and why each setup decision matters, enabling better control over how field-collected data is interpreted in the office and translated into reliable survey drawings with minimal manual intervention.
speakers: Tom Richardson, Owner, T2 Consulting Services, LLC

title: Schedules That Talk: Connecting Data, Lean Planning, and Project Decisions
abstract: Most schedules don’t fail because of planning. They fail because they aren’t measured. In this session, you’ll discover how teams transform schedules into data-driven tools that improve coordination and alignment with project milestones. By integrating lean practices—such as weekly look-ahead planning—with plans, teams can automatically generate metrics through the built-in PPC summary, reducing reporting time by up to 40%. Discover how schedules data enables key metrics for supporting faster and more informed decisions. Walk away with practical strategies to connect schedules with plans within Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Join us in empowering project teams and creating better collaborative project delivery workflows.
speakers: Elizabeth Soto, BIM Manager, Grupo Hermosillo
Pablo Buensuceso, VDC Manager, Grupo Hermosillo

title: Semiconductor Factory Digital Twin: Information Foundations
abstract: This session will provide an overview of the foundational information that is used to develop a semiconductor factory digital twin, including data and formats, 2D graphical information, 3D spatial information, reality capture, and relevant ISO and SEMI industry data and information standards. This foundational information has a lifecycle that spans planning, engineering, fabrication, construction, operation, and manufacturing—and their related technology stacks and AI infrastructure.
speakers: Michael Potts, Director of Architecture & Engineering, Arcadis

title: Separating Hardware Reality from Hype
abstract: Join Lenovo with Intel’s global workstation user and segment lead for an inside look at the technologies transforming professional workstations. Discover how hardware is evolving, what’s driving other companies’ hardware decisions, and which key challenges today’s users face. We’ll also explore the three engines powering today’s System-on-a-Chip (SoC)—the CPU, GPU, and NPU—and how they work together to accelerate modern workflows, including AI. You’ll also learn how Intel develops and optimizes its graphics drivers, and how these innovations support Autodesk applications. Whether you're planning your next workstation upgrade or trying to separate AI hype from reality, this session will help you understand how workstation technology is changing and what it means for your Autodesk workloads.
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel

title: Shaping Low-Carbon Buildings from the Start: A Hands-On Lab with Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight
abstract: Today’s architects are integrating sustainability analysis early to reduce environmental impact and meet carbon targets. Yet early design has traditionally relied on intuition due to limited data. This hands-on lab will introduce an outcome-based workflow that brings actionable carbon insights into early-stage design. You’ll use Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Insight to move from conceptual massing with real-time operational and embodied carbon feedback to detailed analysis, including Energy Use Intensity (EUI) and carbon trade-offs across design options. Through dashboards, metrics, benchmarks, and simulation factors, you’ll learn to optimize carbon performance and enable cross-disciplinary, data-driven design decisions.
speakers: Giuseppe Ardito, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Corina Marinescu, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Justin Taylor, Sr Principal, AEC Solutions Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Small Business Roundtable - Design & Manufacturing
abstract:
Hosted by Jon den Hartog, Autodesk's VP of Product Development and Manufacturing Solutions, this session will bring together fellow entrepreneurs, builders, and creators for an intimate, conversation-driven roundtable designed exclusively for small business customers. Limited to under 50 attendees, this session creates space for honest, two-way dialogue—no slides, no pitches, just real talk.

 Share what's working well in your Autodesk experience, discuss the challenges you're navigating, and tell us what you'd love to see next. Autodesk leaders will be on hand not just to answer questions, but to genuinely listen and learn from the businesses that use our products every day.
speakers: Jon den Hartog, VP, Design, Autodesk

title: Solving 90% of Rebar Issues in Design: Construction Through Standards, Automation, and Co-Creation
abstract: A challenge faced in rebar construction was that many RFIs (requests for information) with architects emerged only during the construction phase. Limited early discussion with specialty contractors delayed issue resolution, leading to additional data creation and rework that increased rebar construction costs by over 6%. To resolve the problem, architects, engineers, and constructors adopted a collaborative workflow from design using Autodesk Forma to support a shared data environment. Rebar data was standardized for manufacturing, and automated placement was enabled by combining structural and rebar data during design. At the end, the early design-phase collaboration reduced construction inquiries by about 90%, nearly eliminated rework, and cut data preparation effort by around 90% through automation.
speakers: Hiromitsu 曽根, General Manager of Project, Maeda Corporation
Nobuya Watanabe, Manager, Maeda Corporation

title: Steel Design with Confidence: From Layout to Documented Connections
abstract: Structural engineers often skip steel connection tools because they don't want to model every fastener. This hands-on lab will prove they don't have to. You’ll configure connections by adjusting key parameters and watch geometry respond in real time, also discovering how Revit software now keeps consistent geometry and parameters when the workflow moves from design to steel connections. Toward the close of the session, we’ll tag plans, annotate detail views, assemble sheets, and build connection schedules. Whether you’re transitioning from 2D or looking to enhance your steel workflows, this session will equip you with hands-on skills to design with confidence.
speakers: Dumitru Berteanu, Senior Principal Product Owner, Autodesk

title: Sustainability and AI in Practice: Driving Better Outcomes with Connected Data, Workflows and Tools
abstract: Join professionals across industries for an engaging meetup exploring how sustainability is showing up in practice today and in the future. As design, make, and operate industries face growing pressure for more traceable, verifiable outcomes, teams are exploring new approaches. Connected data, workflows, and tools like agentic AI are playing a bigger role in decision making. This is an open conversation and networking opportunity to share and learn from peers. Discuss what’s working, challenging, and where opportunities lie across areas like carbon analysis, sustainable design, net zero, biodiversity, and water stewardship. By exchanging ideas and building relationships, we’ll explore how to tackle today’s challenges and scale impact.
speakers: Emily Edelstone, Impact Growth Enablement Manager, Content & Tools, Autodesk
John Locke, Sr Mgr, Research Science, Autodesk
Kat Mitchell, Senior Impact Growth & Engagement Manager, Autodesk

title: Tangled Up in Blue: Untangling a ProjectWise Migration to Autodesk Forma
abstract: When the project teams saw files taking up to 45 minutes to open and AutoCAD crashes becoming routine, they knew their platform was failing them and driving project costs higher. Adding to the pressure, the project was advancing from 60% to 90% plan submittals, a stage when most avoid major platform changes. Migrating off ProjectWise meant transitioning roughly 14,000 files and enabling more than 300 users and 10 subconsultants—while keeping design moving forward. This session will show how the Blue Line Light Rail project, a 13-mile corridor, was transitioned to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Learn how a strong proof of concept, Civil 3D workflows, Autodesk-developed tools (including the bulk migration tool), and external Civil 3D tools helped identify and resolve issues during a midproduction migration.
speakers: Andy Bosch, Designer, Kimley Horn
Sean Hulbert, Sr Principal, Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk

title: Tangled Up in Blue: Untangling a ProjectWise Migration to Autodesk Forma
abstract: When the project teams saw files taking up to 45 minutes to open and AutoCAD crashes becoming routine, they knew their platform was failing them and driving project costs higher. Adding to the pressure, the project was advancing from 60% to 90% plan submittals, a stage when most avoid major platform changes. Migrating off ProjectWise meant transitioning roughly 14,000 files and enabling more than 300 users and 10 subconsultants—while keeping design moving forward. This session will show how the Blue Line Light Rail project, a 13-mile corridor, was transitioned to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Learn how a strong proof of concept, Civil 3D workflows, Autodesk-developed tools (including the bulk migration tool), and external Civil 3D tools helped identify and resolve issues during a midproduction migration.
speakers: Andy Bosch, Designer, Kimley Horn
Sean Hulbert, Sr Principal, Professional Services Consultant, Autodesk

title: Technical Adoption of XR in Construction: Connecting VR, AR, and Autodesk Forma Workflows
abstract: Discover how VR and AR create a practical, end‑to‑end BIM workflow from design to construction. See how Autodesk Forma can be integrated with Autodesk Workshop XR to enable immersive design reviews and collaborative decision making in VR. Then discover real-life integration with GAMMA AR to validate installation, reduce errors, and connect design intent directly to construction for a seamless, circular, virtual design and construction (VDC) workflow.
speakers: Gary Cowan, Head of Digital Construction/VDC, Kane Group

title: The CDE Is Not Only Storage—It’s Decision Control
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to implement a common data environment (CDE) from scratch for teams using Autodesk Forma Data Management. Drawing on real-world experience with constantly changing projects, the session will address challenges such as version-control issues, rework, permission control, uncoordinated deliveries, and time wasted between disciplines. Participants will learn how to structure folders, define review workflows, assign responsibilities for each stage, and control the flow of information to reduce errors and accelerate decision making. We’ll also cover how to create a learning notebook to help avoid repeating the same mistakes in the future.
speakers: Gustavo Ubriaco Contreras, BIM Manager, The Palace Company
Didier Raphael Ramirez Darjo, Autodesk Expert Elite, Independent consultant

title: The Comeback Tour: How Barton Malow Rebuilt Trust in Desktop Connector
abstract: When your net promoter score (NPS) is –23 and nearly half your users are detractors, you don't just relaunch a tool—you rebuild a relationship. Starting with only 32% of 1,200 project delivery team members on Desktop Connector, Barton Malow's construction technology team launched a 14-month, three-phase adoption campaign—and finished at 92%, well past their 80% goal. In this session, we'll share the honest playbook: how we used survey data to make the business case, how we structured a phased rollout across a distributed workforce, how we built a support ecosystem to sustain momentum, and how we quantified 150,000 hours of potential annual savings. Transparency included.
speakers: Elizabeth Fox, Sr. Technology Implementation Manager, Barton Malow

title: The Electrical Design Triangle: Keeping Your Revit Model, Single-Line Diagram, and Calculations in Sync
abstract:
Every electrical project depends on three things agreeing: the Revit model, the single-line diagram, and the load calculations. In vanilla Revit they live in three places, and engineers keep them aligned by hand. Rename one panel, and you update it three times. Resize a transformer, and you update the single-line diagram, the upstream breaker size on the Revit panel schedule, and the voltage drop calculation.

Generating a diagram from the model once is the easy part. The cost shows up on revision twelve, when the model has moved and the diagram hasn't. This session presents a practical framework for treating the Revit model as the single source of truth, with the single-line diagram and calculations synchronized to it. Using real projects, we'll show which changes should propagate automatically instead of being redone by hand. You'll leave with a simple test for your own workflow: does a change propagate, or do you redo it by hand?
speakers: David Robison, Founder and President, Design Master Software

title: The Fun Hardware Talk
abstract: Don’t attend this session if you’re looking for yet another boring hardware session. This won’t be that. Join Lenovo with Intel’s global workstation user and segment lead for an engaging, (almost) vendor-agnostic look at how Autodesk workstations are evolving—and what it means for your projects and future investments. Is an AI PC good enough for Autodesk software? Are more CPU cores always better? Which upgrades deliver real value—and which just add cost? We'll cut through the hype to explore how Autodesk workflows use CPUs and GPUs, and we’ll examine how the NPU is used by other software, as well as for AI technologies. Learn how modern SoC architectures are reshaping visualization, simulation, rendering, and AI-enabled workflows. You'll also discover workstation buying trends, future technology directions, cost-saving opportunities, and critical security considerations often overlooked by professionals. Whether you're evaluating AI PCs, planning your next workstation refresh, or future-proofing your Autodesk environment, you'll leave with practical insights and a clear understanding of what matters most in the next generation of workstations.
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel

title: There Is Now a Level Zero: Getting Started with Autodesk Platform Services to Access Your Autodesk Forma Data
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services documentation, website, and sample files all assume the user is an experienced web developer. Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) professionals who want to take advantage of using Autodesk Platform Services to access their Autodesk Forma data are not web developers, and they need to understand how to start from level zero. This class will introduce a level zero approach for connecting Autodesk Platform Services to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll walk through creating an Autodesk Platform Services application, obtaining authentication, and connecting to Autodesk Forma. Once connected, we’ll retrieve basic project information, and we’ll review the structure of the Autodesk Forma data.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: The Truth Is Out There, but So Is the Nonsense: AI Tips and Tricks for iLogic and the Inventor API
abstract: You've seen how iLogic can tame tedious tasks and make you more efficient. Now AI promises to go even further, writing your rules, navigating the Inventor API, and transforming your automation overnight. Sounds great, right? Here's the truth: Great results from AI are out there, but so is the AI-induced nonsense. You might have seen AI confidently generate code that doesn't work. Or watched it invent API methods that don't exist. The promise is real. But so are the hallucinations, the dead ends, and the frustrations of vibe coding. Come to this session to cut through the hype with tips, tricks, and insights for getting real results from AI, knowing when to trust it, when to push back, and how to build automation that fulfills the prompt.
speakers: Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries

title: Top Firms Share How to Build Knowledge Infrastructure to Scale AI-Powered Digital Adoption
abstract: Hear from a panel of top firms including Jacobs, Tetra Tech, IDOM and HDR as they share best practices on building the human intelligence and knowledge infrastructure layer across the AI-enabled tech stack. Learn how to elevate human plus agentic AI workflows to close digital skills gaps to realize the ROI of improved performance, reduced rework and risk and a competitive edge to win more bids. Imagine the AI-powered digital adoption platform where information from trusted sources is instantly converted into consumable and actionable knowledge, personalized for every learner and delivered in the flow of work through mainstream applications connecting the field and office. GeT tangible data on knowledge gaps and skills matrices through organized learning content and skills challenges aligned with company workflows and project standards. Drive tech adoption at scale with AI-powered "just enough, just in time, and just for me" verified knowledge—because the best training is training your way. GeT IT Your Way.
speakers: Holly Brattberg, Founder & Chief Strategy Officer, Global eTraining
Susan Brattberg, Founder & Chief Customer Officer, Global eTraining

title: Transforming Construction Planning with Digital: Site Plans in Action with Laing O'Rourke and McCarthy
abstract: Join construction leaders from cmBuilder.io, Laing O'Rourke, and McCarthy Building Companies as they explore how digital site planning is transforming the way complex projects are won and delivered. Learn how empowering field teams with intuitive 3D and 4D planning tools is democratizing construction logistics—reducing reliance on specialists while enabling project managers, superintendents, and site teams to take ownership of planning and coordination. Discover how digital simulation of construction sequencing, logistics, and site operations helps teams validate plans before work begins, identify risks earlier, improve stakeholder communication, and optimize project execution. Through real-world case studies from major projects in the United Kingdom and North America, this session will demonstrate how digital site logistics plans are helping contractors win more work, improve collaboration, and deliver safer, more efficient projects.
speakers: Javier Glatt, Co-Founder, cmBuilder.io
Paul Drayton, Head of Digital, Laing O'Rourke
Khoi Pham, Sr. VDC Manager, McCarthy Building Companies, Inc.

title: Turning Data into a Strategic Advantage in AEC
abstract: The architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry is at a turning point. Firms have invested heavily in digital tools, yet most aren’t unlocking the full value of their data. Information remains fragmented across systems and phases, limiting visibility, slowing decisions, and constraining innovation. This session will explore a core idea: Data is becoming AEC’s most strategic asset, if it’s structured, connected, and activated. We’ll outline how leading firms are shifting to a data-first strategy, leveraging Autodesk Forma as a unifying foundation. You’ll leave with a practical framework to standardize, connect, and activate data—turning fragmentation into a measurable competitive advantage.
speakers: GB Cazes, President, Data Solutions, ATG USA
Kent Watson, VP Technology, ATG USA

title: Unified Production Environment: How AI and Data Transformed Ramboll’s Engineering
abstract: Ramboll is reinventing itself as a data-centered, AI‑powered engineering firm. Through its Together for Better Outcomes (T4BO) partnership with Autodesk, Ramboll has productized a unified production environment (UPE) to accelerate AI adoption. By embedding the Autodesk AI tool Autodesk Assistant into daily workflows, productivity increases while more-sustainable client value is delivered. This session will show how data-centered design and AI‑assisted engineering are transforming project delivery and ways of working, reinforcing Ramboll’s role as a partner for sustainable change. We’ll share tangible outcomes, such as higher delivery quality, deeper sustainability insights, and increased project capacity without adding headcount.
speakers: David Thomson, Principle Product Owner Digital Design, Ramboll
Marc Sleegers, Sr Principal, Business Consultant, Autodesk

title: Unlock the Power of AI for AutoCAD 2027 Toolsets
abstract: Unlock the full potential of AI in AutoCAD 2027 toolsets. Building on our AU 2024 award-winning class, this session will explore how AI-powered tools revolutionize CAD, driving unmatched efficiency. Experience how AutoCAD 2027 software’s AI automates complex workflows—from intelligent object recognition and predictive drafting to real-time generative design. With automated dimensioning, predictive error-correction, and material optimization, you’ll slash design cycles. Use AI-driven simulation to stress-test designs against real-world scenarios, ensuring peak performance. Transform your workflow with seamless, AI-enhanced interoperability that bridges multidisciplinary teams. Future-proof your craft with smarter, faster, and more creative CAD.
speakers: Hung Nguyen, Technical Consultant, SolidCAD
Lina El-Khoury, BIM Strategy & Digital Solutions Consultant, LEK

title: Using MCP to Build Self-Improving AEC Data Workflows
abstract: Most architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) data stays raw because processing it manually does not scale. This session will demonstrate a working pipeline where AI classifies documents, extracts structured information, enriches records, and validates outputs at every stage. Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI agents to Revit, Autodesk Platform Services, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), letting them read and write connected data across tools in a single workflow. A live walk-through of a real pipeline used on AEC projects will show how feedback loops capture user corrections so results improve with every iteration. You will leave with a reusable architecture pattern you can adapt to your own challenges, from tender analysis to intelligent models to construction submittals.
speakers: Nabil Sadeg, CTO, Nacorm

title: Vibe Coding for AECO Professionals—The Master Class
abstract: This comprehensive 90-minute presentation will cover the entire vibe-coding landscape for architecture, engineering, construction, and owner (AECO) professionals. We’ll provide platform-agnostic coverage of AI-powered development tools, prompt engineering, token economics, deployment strategies, and real-world AECO workflows—from proof of concept to production.
speakers: Charles Berteaux, VDC/Tech Manager, SSOE Group

title: Visual Context Intelligence: Empowering AI to Work Better in the Design Journey
abstract:
While AI has shown popularity and power in ideation and early concept, it still has issues with consistency and iteration. Design is a journey. It is collaborative and, most importantly, design accuracy absolutely matters.

In this session you will hear from Lumion's Head of Product on how Lumion is building a new process called Visual Context Intelligence into its AI tools in order to strengthen and refine AI in later stage visualisation. 

You’ll also hear Lumion’s thoughts on where and when AI should be used. You will go behind the curtain on Visual Context Intelligence, see it working in the latest AI tools, and hear what industry testing has shown so far about consistency and accuracy across iterations.
speakers: David Weir-McCall, Head of Product, Lumion

title: VRED to Flame using Python: Standardizing Image Pipelines from Render to Finishing
abstract: Rendering Autodesk VRED scenes can result in Open EXR sequences that require manual handling before they can be used in Autodesk Flame. This creates delays, inconsistencies, and avoidable errors in high-end commercial finishing workflows. This session will discuss example pipelines using both VRED and Flame Python tools to render Open EXR sequences from VRED and ingest them into Flame as clips. We will cover render jobs, structuring output, managing naming, and simplifying Flame imports. You should leave with a repeatable, production-ready workflow that reduces manual ingest and connects visualization to finishing with speed and reliability.
speakers: Mark Taylor, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
Ruediger Ambs, Sr Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk

title: What Owners Want: Honest Guidance on BIM, CDEs, and Becoming a Preferred Digital Partner
abstract: You’ve set up the common data environment (CDE). You’ve trained the team. You’ve delivered the models. So why does the owner still complain? Because owners do not think like consultants. In this candid 30-minute session, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MOEI) will share what an infrastructure owner actually expects from BIM deliverables, CDE workflows, and digital submissions. You’ll hear how we assess consultant performance, what builds trust, and which common mistakes immediately signal weak digital delivery capability. This is not a product demo or a generic case study. It’s an owner-side view of what really influences decisions, repeat work, and preferred-partner status on major government projects.
speakers: ahmed alwaeel, Director of planning and design, Ministry of energy and infrastructure
abdulrahman alkholy, Digital transformation lead & AI, Ministry of energy and infrastructure

title: What’s New in Revit 2027: AI, Data, and Connected Workflows
abstract: Revit 2027 software advances a more connected, data-driven BIM workflow, linking design, analysis, and documentation with the Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) ecosystem. In this session, Revit product managers will demonstrate how AI-powered assistance, extended cloud data, and collaborative carbon insights transform everyday production workflows. Learn how Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights connects Revit models to shared sustainability dashboards, how extended properties bring cloud-managed data directly into the model, and how automation and performance improvements accelerate documentation. See how connected workflows reduce rework, improve decision making, and align multidisciplinary teams from early design through detailed delivery.
speakers: Dan Peticila, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Cesar Escalante, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Building Products, Autodesk
Scott D Davis, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: What’s New in Revit 2027.x: AI, Data, and Connected Workflows
abstract: Revit 2027 software advances a more connected, data-driven BIM workflow, linking design, analysis, and documentation with the Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) ecosystem. In this session, Revit product managers will demonstrate how AI-powered assistance, extended cloud data, and collaborative carbon insights transform everyday production workflows. Learn how Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights connects Revit models to shared sustainability dashboards, how extended properties bring cloud-managed data directly into the model, and how automation and performance improvements accelerate documentation. See how connected workflows reduce rework, improve decision making, and align multidisciplinary teams from early design through detailed delivery.
speakers: Scott D Davis, Sr Territory Technical Lead, Autodesk
Dan Peticila, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Cesar Escalante, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Building Products, Autodesk

title: Where Innovation in Standards Takes Flight: How Massport Advances BIM, GIS, and EAM Integration
abstract: The Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) will share key lessons learned from its journey toward using BIM, geographic information system (GIS), and asset management for better project delivery and capital planning. Large project and asset owners will learn how Massport turns project, spatial, and asset data into actionable insights for better decision making. This session will highlight how Massport manages more than 200 capital projects across five airport/seaport campuses using BIM-enabled workflows. You’ll learn how Autodesk Forma is used as a common data environment to collaborate with design and construction teams, enable on-time digital delivery, and create a virtual campus as a single source of truth—supporting Massport’s broader digital transformation goals.
speakers: Jason Del Signore, VDC Manager, Massport

title: Whodunit? Building a System That Remembers Every Hand in the Work.
abstract: Creative work is always collaborative. But the record rarely reflects that. Fabricators, assistants, mentors, and technicians disappear from the story—while credit consolidates around whoever has the loudest voice. This session will introduce ETCH, a trust-based documentation platform built on a custom blockchain, designed to make invisible labor visible. We'll walk through the design problems that shaped the system and discuss how to document a messy, nonlinear process. How do you attribute equitably across skill types? How do you build trust without financial incentives? The answer is a working system built by a design student who got frustrated enough to build the thing they needed.
speakers: Renee Dua, student, srishti manipal institute of art deign and technology

title: Why Construction Needs World Models
abstract: Construction does not have a data shortage; it has a decision-support shortage. What project teams lack is a reliable way to continuously assemble the live state of a project across time, space, and cost, using that understanding to make better project decisions. This session will introduce the grounded world model as that missing layer, fusing multisensor site signals with previously siloed project evidence such as drawings, site photos, and BIM. Unlike a digital twin, which reflects current conditions, a world model can reason over relationships and support action when conditions start to shift, while supporting agentic issue detection. This points to a fundamentally different way of managing construction from a living model of the site.
speakers: Mo Han, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
Yuri Bartzis, Construction Industry Fellow, Autodesk
Xin Yang, Senior Research Scientist Construction, Autodesk

title: Why Operations Is Becoming AEC’s Next Competitive Advantage
abstract: Stephen Hooper, Senior Vice President of Autodesk Operations Solutions, and Chris Turlica, Head of MaintainX at Autodesk, join the Digital Builder podcast to explore why operations is emerging as a major opportunity in the built environment. The conversation examines connected operations, asset performance, maintenance, operational intelligence, AI, and how organizations can unlock greater value across the lifecycle of their buildings and infrastructure.

title: Year of the Owner: Owner and Contractor Collaboration Using Autodesk Forma
abstract: During this session, we’ll explore from an owner’s perspective how we’re collaborating with our contractors using Autodesk Forma. We’ll discuss lessons learned, how we overcame difficulties, and how we’ve laid out groundwork for continued and increased collaboration in future projects. Transitioning to Forma has allowed for processes to become more efficient, but it has also shown gaps where new checks were implemented to ensure delivery of a quality product.
speakers: Jacob Pfenning-Wendt, Solutions Manager, UPS

title: You Don't Know the Power of the API: Extending Inventor iLogic with API
abstract: You’ve taken your first steps into automation with iLogic. Now it’s time to expand your toolset and make The Force even stronger. This hands‑on classroom session will help you transport into the wider galaxy of API‑powered automation. Instead of diving deep into theory, we’ll focus on how to access the Inventor API, understand what’s possible, and confidently begin using it alongside iLogic. Using a guided example, you’ll learn to connect iLogic to the API, locate key objects, and extend automation across parts, assemblies, and drawings. While it might look like The Dark Side at first, this class will break it into simple concepts and practical examples. By the end, you’ll leave with the confidence and foundation to continue your automation voyage.
speakers: Chelsea Kastanek, Sr. Technology Consultant - Automation, Symetri

title: Your AI Is Only as Smart as Your Project Data
abstract: Every firm is piloting AI. Most pilots stall for the same reason, and it isn't the model. It's the data. Decades of drawings, RFIs, specs, and contracts sit scattered across servers, inboxes, and forgotten project folders. The firms winning with AI in 2026 treat project history as an asset. They make it findable, permissioned, and trusted before pointing AI at it. This talk  shows how to fix the data layer first: what to organize, how to govern access, and how to build the foundation that makes AI accurate and safe. You'll leave with fresh insights on how to turn scattered project data into firm knowledge your teams, and your AI, can actually use.
speakers: Philip Townsend, Principal Solutions Architect, Egnyte Inc.
Aaron Vorwerk, AEC Practice Leader, Architects + Owners, Egnyte

title: You’ve Heard About Autodesk Assistant in Revit. Now Here’s How to Actually Use It.
abstract: In this session, we’ll focus on how the new Autodesk Assistant in Revit fits into real modeling and documentation workflows inside Revit 2027. From making modeling easier to troubleshooting issues and supporting documentation, we’ll walk through practical examples you can apply right away. You’ll see how to ask better questions, how to refine the responses, and how to turn those responses into something useful. We’ll also discuss how AI can support and complement your design process, not replace it. We’ll cover where Autodesk Assistant works well, where it still falls short, and how to use it in a way that actually saves time. Come to this session to learn how to make Autodesk Assistant in Revit work for you, not against you.
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend
ARGELIA Barcena, Head of Regional Leads - North America, Women in BIM

title: 30 Autodesk Forma Features You Should Be Using—But Probably Aren’t
abstract: Are you getting the full value from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), or just scratching the surface? In this session, we’ll go through 30 features across the Autodesk Forma platform that can improve how you design, analyze, and manage your projects. Some of these are well known but underused, and others are hidden in plain sight. The goal is simple: show you what’s available today and how to start using it right away. We’ll cover a mix of well-known capabilities that are often underused, along with lesser-known tools that are easy to miss but highly impactful. Examples are grouped across design exploration, data-driven analysis, and project coordination, so you can see how they connect into a more efficient, end-to-end workflow.
speakers: Shir Rustici, BIM Program Manager, Turner & Townsend
Jonathan Hand, Technical Marketing Manager, Construction, UK, Autodesk

title: Accelerating Real Estate Development with Autodesk Forma and Revit
abstract: Early-stage real estate decisions are often constrained by slow, fragmented workflows between site analysis and building design. This session will demonstrate a tightly integrated workflow using Autodesk Forma Site Design and Revit software to rapidly generate, evaluate, and iterate development scenarios. You’ll learn how to move from contextual site intelligence to parametric building systems, enabling faster feasibility studies, improved stakeholder alignment, and data-informed decision making. The session will include live demonstrations, workflow diagrams, and implementation strategies for practice.
speakers: Joe BIMtucci, Senior Project Design Technologist, Cuningham
Emily Bisaga Dunne, Executive Director of Design Technology, Cuningham

title: A Dynamic Lab on AutoCAD Dynamic Blocks
abstract: Why should you be using dynamic blocks? Quite simply, dynamic blocks can greatly reduce the number of blocks in your library, improving your efficiency. While it does take a little more time up front to create a dynamic block, the time saved on the back end makes it well worth the effort. Even better news: If you’re a proficient AutoCAD user, you should have no problem converting those boring static blocks into shiny, new dynamic blocks.
speakers: Tracy Chadwick, Computer Drafting Professor/Coordinator, Hutchinson Community College

title: AECO Community Meetup
abstract: Connect with Autodesk’s AECO community, including members of The Big Room, Autodesk’s online AECO Community Hub. Join us for a special in-person meetup designed to bring industry peers, community connections, and online conversations to life.Enjoy an interactive icebreaker, win some swag, and connect with your peers IRL. Meet the people behind the ideas, posts, and conversations happening across the online AECO community!Whether you’re already part of The Big Room or simply looking to meet more AECO colleagues, you’re welcome here. Stop by to say hello, share ideas for future community activities, and help shape what’s next together.
speakers: Nicola Ianeselli, Senior Director of Technology, Chenmoore
Briani Carey, Construction Community Program Manager, Autodesk
Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk

title: AECO Roadmap: Data Solutions
abstract: The AEC Data Model is becoming the shared language that connects design, construction, and operations as AECO shifts from file-centric BIM to data-centric delivery. In this roadmap session, learn how Autodesk is unifying files, models, and granular data through Forma Data Management and the AEC Data Model, unlocking governance, automation, analytics, and data reuse. We’ll highlight what’s next across Content Catalog, Extended Properties, Model Analytics, Parameters Service, Forma Assets, Datum, and emerging capabilities such as Information Requirements, Asset Information Connector, and Asset Registry. The result? Teams can access, trust and connect data across the full asset lifecycle.
speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk
Shilpa Ghanmode, Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk
Paul Markovits, Senior Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk

title: AECO Roadmap: Data Solutions
abstract: The AEC Data Model is becoming the shared language that connects design, construction, and operations as AECO shifts from file-centric BIM to data-centric delivery. In this roadmap session, learn how Autodesk is unifying files, models, and granular data through Forma Data Management and the AEC Data Model, unlocking governance, automation, analytics, and data reuse.
