speakers: Eddy Krygiel, Sr. Manager, AEC Data Model Strategy, Autodesk
Shilpa Ghanmode, Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk
Paul Markovits, Senior Group Product Manager, AEC Data, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma—Admin, Standards, and Insight
abstract: Operational efficiency isn’t just about speed—it’s about consistency, control, and clarity. In this session, we’ll explore how the latest updates in Autodesk Forma are helping teams standardize processes, streamline administration, and turn project data into meaningful insights. We’ll cover recent enhancements and what’s coming next across Project and Hub Admin, Bridge, Templates, Library, Reports, Data Connector, Dashboards, and more. Learn how we’re reducing setup time, increasing governance, and unlocking insights across projects and portfolios. If you want to scale smarter and operate with confidence, this session will deliver a clear path forward.
speakers: Sheryl Yang, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Ash Gupta, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Ross Collinson, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk
Jonathan Hand, Technical Marketing Manager, Construction, UK, Autodesk
Avani Saxena, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Autodesk Forma for Preconstruction
abstract: Investing in preconstruction is one of the most effective ways to reduce risk and set projects up for long‑term success. Join this dynamic session with the Autodesk preconstruction product team to explore what’s new and what’s coming next for Autodesk Forma Takeoff, Autodesk Forma Estimate, Autodesk Forma Bid, BuildingConnected Pro, Bid Board Pro, and TradeTapp. You’ll get an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at our product strategy, major initiatives on the horizon, and the customer feedback that’s shaping our future. Bring your voice to the table and help influence the evolution of our preconstruction offerings. Whether you're a power user or just getting started, you won’t want to miss this session!
speakers: Chico Membreno, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk
Joel Feldman, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Cory Kintz, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Liam Murray, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Informed Design
abstract: Join the Autodesk Informed Design product team for a forward-looking session on how Autodesk is advancing industrialized construction. This session will showcase the latest developments and future roadmap for Informed Design—Autodesk’s platform tool that connects design intent to manufacturing execution. Learn how we’re helping architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) and manufacturing teams accelerate delivery, reduce rework, and unlock new levels of collaboration and efficiency.
speakers: Az Jasat, Dir., Strategic Planning/Analytics, Autodesk
Ryan McMahon, Sr. Dir. & GM, Manufacturing Informed Design, Autodesk
Andy Akenson, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: MEP
abstract: For MEP teams, reliability depends on how well analysis, system logic, and detailing stay aligned. In this session, Autodesk product leaders will showcase the latest updates and share what’s ahead for MEP engineers, detailers, and fabricators across Revit, the AEC Collection, and Autodesk’s cloud collaboration tools. You’ll get a first look at improvements to modeling workflows, new sustainability-driven capabilities, and emerging AI-powered design assistance. This roadmap session highlights how Autodesk is advancing its solutions to better support multi-disciplinary coordination and drive greater project efficiency. We’ll also open the conversation—sharing what’s coming while inviting your feedback on what should come next.
speakers: Ian Molloy, Director, Product Management, MEP, Autodesk
Martin Schmid, Prod./Prod. Line Mgr., Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Structures
abstract: Structural teams across design engineering, fabrication and construction face increasing pressure to deliver safe, sustainable, and highly coordinated outcomes on tighter schedules. Designers must produce accurate, analysis-driven models that inform decision-making, while fabrication and construction teams need detailed, buildable information for efficient execution. Discover how Autodesk is advancing model accuracy, enhancing analysis capabilities, and strengthening multi-disciplinary collaboration across the structural workflow, persona and project phases. You’ll also get an early look at features in development and get the opportunity to share your feedback directly with the team shaping the roadmap.
speakers: Dan Peticila, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Pawel Piechnik, Director, Product Management, Structures Product Line, Autodesk
Piotr Pysz, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: AEC Roadmap: Water
abstract: Water infrastructure is changing fast, and your tools need to keep up. Join Autodesk water experts to explore the latest innovations across InfoDrainage, InfoWorks ICM, InfoWorks WS Pro, InfoWater Pro, and Info360 Insight. Discover how you can streamline workflows for drainage design, hydraulic modeling, and asset management, alongside expanding integrations with Civil 3D and the Architecture, Engineering & Construction Collection. Discover what’s new, what’s coming next, and how it all connects. You’ll get a sneak peek at in-development capabilities, and you’ll have the chance to connect directly with the teams behind these solutions, ask questions, and share feedback that helps drive the roadmap forward.
speakers: Trevor English, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Water, Autodesk
Brian Deeley, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk
Mike Maylone, Sr. Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk
Brett Singley, Manager, Product Mgmt, Autodesk

title: Agentic AI for AEC: Orchestrating Autonomous Project Delivery with Autodesk
abstract: Agentic AI is rapidly changing how work gets done, moving beyond prompts into systems that can plan, act, and automate tasks across tools. This session will explore how to apply agent-based approaches using tools like Claude Code and Claude Cowork, Dispatch, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Autodesk Platform Services. In this session, you’ll learn how to connect agents to Autodesk data, manage authentication and permissions, and orchestrate workflows that automate design and project delivery tasks. Through practical examples, we’ll show how to combine agents, Claude skills, and APIs to move from isolated automations to scalable, end-to-end processes.
speakers: Irene Won, Customer Success, Anthropic
Adam Sheather, Sr Principal, Solution Architect – APAC Lead Technical Advisory, Autodesk

title: Ahead of the Curve: A VDC Leader's AI Playbook for When Your Organization Isn't Ready
abstract: AI isn't just changing how construction work gets done. It's changing how the best leaders plan, communicate, and develop their teams. Most organizations aren't keeping pace, leaving forward thinking VDC leaders navigating the gap alone. This session delivers a practical playbook for managers already ahead of their organization with AI. Planning decisions get sharper, team communication gets stronger, and coaching conversations improve. AI tools get matched to your department's real capability and fit, including what's already built into Autodesk Forma. Credibility for leading adoption gets built even when policy or access hasn't caught up. You will leave this session with high-value entry points you can use this week with zero approval required from your organization.
speakers: Blake Titus, VDC Manager-Planning, Miron Construction

title: AI Agents for Electrical Design: Driving Revit with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
abstract:
At the top of this session, I'll give an AI agent a real electrical design task: review the electrical system in a Revit model, determine what's circuited, identify what needs power, and circuit those loads. Along the way it will hit the questions an engineer actually has to answer. Do we add another panel, or work with what's there? How do we split the loads across panels?

While the agent works in the background, we'll look at how MCP connects AI to Revit, what tools an electrical engineer might give an agent, and where the engineer needs to stay in control.

You'll leave knowing what AI agents can and can't reliably do in Revit today, and how to start experimenting yourself. Whether the agent succeeds, stalls, or takes a wrong turn, you'll see exactly where the line falls.
speakers: David Robison, Founder and President, Design Master Software

title: AI Agents Meet Autodesk Platform Services: From Autodesk Forma Building Design to Operational Digital Twin
abstract: Most digital twin projects stall at the same point: There’s no 3D model. Point cloud scanning takes weeks—too heavy for operational use cases like workplace booking or shop-floor monitoring. But we’ve found a faster path: Design buildings in Autodesk Forma Building Design, process them server-side via the Autodesk Platform Services Automation API for Revit, then use agentic AI workflows via Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enrich the model with workplaces and connected production data. It takes hours instead of months. Through video walk-throughs and live demos, we’ll show two use cases we’re deploying this year—replacing our own third-party desk-sharing tool, and building a manufacturing digital twin. You’ll leave with a replicable pattern for AI-enabled design-to-operate workflows.
speakers: Frank Otto, Product Owner - Platform, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH
Hendrik Schön, Enterprise Architect, N+P Informationssysteme GmbH
Poyraz Yildirim, Developer Advocate Manager, Autodesk

title: AI-Assisted CAM for Prototype Shops: Accelerating Autodesk Fusion Workflows with CloudNC
abstract: Avalanche Energy operates a high-mix prototype shop where parts must move from design to machining in hours, not days. This session will show how the team uses the Autodesk Fusion Manufacture workspace with CloudNC’s CAM Assist to automate toolpath generation and accelerate CAD-to-CAM workflows. See how standardizing tooling, fixturing, and machining strategies enables consistent, repeatable programming across evolving designs. Learn how automation reduces programming time from hours to minutes, allowing programmers to focus on setup planning and process optimization. You’ll leave with practical workflows to identify high-impact automation opportunities, structure CAM setups, and scale fast, reliable part production.
speakers: Ryan Walker, Machine Shop Manager, Avalanche Energy

title: AI-Connected Workflows: Fusion, Claude, and MCP 101
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion, Claude, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) can work together to create smarter, more connected engineering workflows. This introductory session will explore how conversational AI can assist with design, automation, scripting, documentation, and workflow generation inside Fusion environments, while MCP enables secure connections between AI, tools, and data sources. Attendees will learn foundational concepts, practical integration examples, and real-world use cases that demonstrate how AI-driven workflows can improve productivity, collaboration, and decision-making across product development and manufacturing.
speakers: Brian Frank, Sr. Director, Product Management, Autodesk
Patrick Rainsberry, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk

title: AI Data Ready: From Design to Construction to Operations
abstract: Design and construction projects involve diverse tools and stakeholders across phases, creating fragmented, inconsistent data and documentation. This session will show how we establish an AI-ready data foundation from day one using the Autodesk Forma Assets module, enabling a continuous digital thread from design through construction to operations. We’ll demonstrate how standardized data from Revit models and equipment lists—aligned with CSI MasterFormat and UniFormat—connects design, procurement, project controls, commissioning, and operations. By treating models and metadata as lifecycle deliverables, we reuse and enrich data instead of recreating it—with Forma serving as the central platform for integrated, reliable, AI-ready project data.
speakers: Gilbert Kwan, BIM Business Process Owner, Amgen
Stacy Goins, Senior Manager, Engineering Projects, Amgen

title: AI in Construction Meetup
abstract: Join us as we connect owners, general contractors, and specialty contractors around the United States to exchange best practices, wins, and lessons learned that enhance the construction customer experience with AI. This will be a place to network with like-minded contractors and owners and share ideas and dive deeper into workflows you wouldn’t normally find on an Autodesk webinar. We want to connect you with your peers to elevate the way you manage your facilities, helping Autodesk create the most valuable tool for your needs—based on your feedback, presented by your peers.
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk
Mark King, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Ramya Palani, Senior Customer Success Manager - Team Lead, Autodesk

title: AI-Powered Digital Thread: Connecting Requirements, ALM, and PLM Across a Product's Lifecycle
abstract: Discover how Visure Solutions and Autodesk unite ALM and PLM to enable a seamless digital thread across software lifecycles and physical designs. This session will explore how integrating Visure’s strengths in requirements and traceability with the Autodesk Fusion Manage capabilities delivers end-to-end visibility—from concept to validation. Learn how AI enhances impact analysis, automates traceability, and supports smarter decision making. Through practical use cases, we’ll show how teams can reduce risk, accelerate development, and ensure alignment across engineering disciplines, while meeting the evolving expectations of modern product development.
speakers: Fernando Valera, CTO, Visure Solutions, Inc.

title: An Agentic Future-State of Embedded Certainty Through Autodesk Forma, Informed Design, and KOPE
abstract: Discover the future of productization in Autodesk Forma. Learn how connecting Forma to KOPE and Informed Design begins to deliver on the convergence of construction and manufacturing. This session will show you how to use AI agents to translate generic design intent in Forma into constructible building systems, like detailed partition wall assemblies in KOPE, while adding full manufacturing components from connections to fasteners in Informed Design. By instantly transitioning to high-fidelity models, you use fluid workflows in Forma with instant, quantifiable insights that drive certainty around design risk and cost drivers in preconstruction.
speakers: David Flynn, Co-Founder, KOPE
Mark Thorley, Co-Founder & CEO, KOPE

title: A New Era for Stadium Design and Construction: Huntington Bank Field
abstract: Modern stadiums are no longer just places to watch a game. They are year-round destinations that serve as community hubs, host diverse events, and deliver exceptional fan experiences. As expectations for performance, sustainability, and operational efficiency continue to rise, the complexity of designing, constructing, and operating these facilities has never been greater. Get an inside look at the Cleveland Browns' new stadium, a landmark project across North East Ohio that is redefining how modern sports and entertainment venues are planned, delivered, and operated. Learn how the team is using Forma to create a fully digital project from design through handover.
speakers: Phil Dangerfield, SVP, Operations, Haslam Sports Group
Sidharth Haksar, VP,  Construction Strategy and Industry Partnerships, Autodesk
Patrick Wipperman, AECOM

title: Ask the Vault Team
abstract: If you have any queries regarding the functionality and operation of Vault software, or if you would like to learn more about a specific feature, this session will offer an excellent opportunity to engage with the Vault team. The team comprises both the engineering and the product management teams, and they will provide candid and insightful responses to any inquiries you may have about Vault.
speakers: Senthil Kumar, Sr. Manager, Software Development, Autodesk
Jason Dai, Principal Engineer, Autodesk
Santhosh Palaniappan, Principal Software Development Engineer, Autodesk

title: A Tale of (Digital) Twin Cities. A Tale You'll Actually Want to Hear.
abstract: In this session, we’re going to take you through the entire process of creating a digital twin for a wastewater treatment plant that’s more than 80 years old. This will cover everything from laser scans of existing conditions to creating assets that show live data and allow scheduled maintenance and access to drawings—and loop diagrams it. Let's explore how to set up Revit, Civil 3D, GIS, Autodesk Forma Data Management, Autodesk Forma Build, and Autodesk Tandem software to be used in far more ways than you may have considered. Learn with us how we create a management system that our future workforce wants to use.
speakers: Allen Weed, BIM Analysist / GIS Tech III, City of Portland BES

title: AU Clubhouse
abstract:
Join the club.

 

What if networking felt more like collaborating than mingling? AU Clubhouse is an interactive networking experience where the AU community comes together through team-based games designed to spark conversation and collaboration.

 

Connect with architects, engineers, designers, manufacturers, and developers from across industries as you solve puzzles in Solvers Club, draw and decode in Decoders Club, or put your knowledge to the test in Trivia Club.

 

It’s networking reimagined for people who learn by doing, and do their best work together.

 

Drop in anytime - no sign-up required. Visit the AU Clubhouse Welcome Desk outside the Expo Hall to get started.

times.room: Venetian, Expo Hall C Foyer, level 2

title: AU Merch Store
abstract:
Take AU Home With You.

Visit the all-new AU Merch Store for exclusive Autodesk apparel, premium swag, and limited-edition AU collectibles. Celebrate the ideas, innovations, and connections that brought us together and grab a piece of the experience before it's gone.

Designed for the builders, makers, innovators, and visionaries shaping tomorrow.

title: AutoCAD Ask Me Anything
abstract:
What have you always wanted to ask the people behind AutoCAD?

Join Dan Whitcombe, Senior Group Product Manager; Prakriti Khanna, Senior Group Product Manager, Collaboration Product Line; host Shiva Kashalkar, Senior Director, Product Management, AIR; and special community guest Tom Richardson for a live, moderated Ask Me Anything.

This community-first session gives AutoCAD customers a direct line to product leaders and an experienced user voice. The team will answer pre-submitted questions and the audience’s most upvoted questions in real time, focusing on how customer needs are shaping AutoCAD today and influencing where it goes next. Topics may include workflows, product priorities, decision-making, and the broader challenges affecting how teams work.

Bring your questions, compare notes with the community, and hear practical answers from the people shaping AutoCAD.

title: AutoCAD Electrical Works—Once You Tell It How
abstract: AutoCAD Electrical software ships with powerful tools, but many teams struggle to move beyond the out‑of‑the‑box configuration into a setup that truly supports their design standards, workflows, and project scale. This class will focus on how to configure AutoCAD Electrical so it becomes a reliable production tool instead of a constant source of rework and work-arounds. Rather than focusing on schematic drafting basics, this class will emphasize configuration strategy, governance, and best practices that scale across teams and projects. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of what to configure, why it matters, and how to maintain a healthy AutoCAD Electrical environment over time.
speakers: Melissa Vrobel, Engineering Team Lead, FTI
Luke Van Hecke, CAD Technician II, Faith Technologies

title: AutoCAD Support Clinic
abstract: Join a panel of Autodesk product support experts as they share practical tips and proven techniques to boost your AutoCAD productivity. This interactive session will include a brief overview of Autodesk’s support organization, key resources available to customers, and introductions to the panelists. You’re encouraged to bring real-world challenges—our experts from Technical Support, QA, and Licensing will be available to provide live guidance and solutions. A workstation with AutoCAD will be set up for in-session problem demonstrations, making this a hands-on opportunity to get answers to your most-pressing issues.
speakers: Volker Cocco, Sr Technical Enablement Specialist - AutoCAD, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Forma at the Center: Designing a Real-World CDE for Multidiscipline Engineering
abstract: Many organizations adopt Autodesk Forma industry cloud as their common data environment (CDE) for BIM collaboration. But complex infrastructure projects rely on far more than BIM tools alone. Traffic modeling, hydraulic analysis, geotechnical simulations, and geographic information system (GIS) workflows often depend on specialized software that cannot operate effectively within cloud collaboration platforms. This session will show how Parsons implemented a practical CDE architecture with Autodesk Forma at the center of coordination while supporting discipline-specific production environments. You’ll learn how clear governance, ISO 19650 alignment, and defined workflows can unify multidisciplinary collaboration without constraining engineering delivery.
speakers: Rafael Lucero, Head of Digital Engineering EMEA, Parsons
Ian McGovern, VP Operations & Innovation, Parsons

title: Autodesk Fusion Manage Beyond Engineering: From Ideation to Realization
abstract: Autodesk Fusion Manage software is often positioned for engineering change and data management—but its real value emerges when extended across the broader product lifecycle. This session will show how manufacturing organizations use Fusion Manage to connect quality processes, supplier collaboration, ideation, and requirements management in a single system. Learn how to structure workflows for nonengineering teams, improve cross-functional visibility, and reduce delays caused by disconnected systems. You’ll leave with a practical framework to expand Fusion Manage beyond engineering and drive more-coordinated, traceable product development.
speakers: Michelle Stone, Sr Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Fusion Manage for Digital Factory ... What?
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore the complete factory asset lifecycle—from the initial procurement and commissioning of equipment to maintenance, optimization, and eventual decommissioning. You’ll learn how to use cloud-based PLM to gain real-time visibility into production readiness, track the health of your physical assets, and eliminate silos between engineering and the shop floor.
speakers: Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Dave Graves, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Matt Zielke, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Platform Services GraphQL in Production: AEC, MFG, and Data Exchange Patterns from Analytics to AI Agents
abstract:
Autodesk's Data Model APIs for AEC and MFG, along with Data Exchange GraphQL APIs, use GraphQL—unlocking richer integrations, workflow automation, and AI-powered workflows. But GraphQL differs from REST in ways that quietly break production systems.

Our team has shipped analytics dashboards, workflow automation, Data Exchange workflows, and MCP servers letting AI agents query live design data. We've hit the pitfalls so you don't have to.

This session delivers production-proven patterns: query design for AEC/MFG Data Models and Data Exchanges, partial-success error handling, enterprise authentication, mutation patterns, and AI agent enablement via MCP. We also highlight the underutilized GraphQL capabilities in the User Profile API.

Real examples. Real lessons. Patterns that work from day one.
speakers: Kevin Vandecar, Sr Mgr, Technology Consulting, Autodesk
Mayank Mridul, Senior Software Engineer, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Platform Services Viewer Reborn: A Developer’s Deep Dive
abstract: This session will explore the next-generation Autodesk Platform Services Viewer, redesigned for performance and extensibility. We’ll break down its WebGPU-first rendering pipeline, large model experience, and the new API for programmatic control over loaded content. Through code-level examples, you’ll see how to optimize rendering, stream data efficiently, and build advanced interactions directly in the viewer. This session is ideal for developers looking to push Autodesk Platform Services Viewer beyond out-of-the-box capabilities.
speakers: Petr Broz, Sr. Principal Developer Advocate, Autodesk
Alex Berner-Gandras, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Sebastian Dunkel, Sr. Principal Software Engineer, Graphics, Autodesk

title: Autodesk PRIDE & Mental, Inclusion, Neurodiversity, and Disability (MIND) Network Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.
speakers: Alexis Womble, Senior Security Program Manager, Autodesk
Madison Burnell, Executive Assistant, Autodesk
Jason Swenton, Director, AMER Go-To-Market & Customer Experience Talent Acquisition, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Product Lifecycle Management Hands-On Test Drive
abstract: Get a greater understanding of how businesses can unlock the full potential of Autodesk Fusion data management and PLM in this hands-on workshop. Learn how to connect design data, streamline workflows, and standardize processes across the product lifecycle. You’ll explore key capabilities of Autodesk Fusion Manage, helping you manage product data, improve collaboration, and reduce errors from design through production. This session will provide a clear introduction and practical insights for anyone looking to get more value from integrated data management and PLM within the Fusion platform.
speakers: Giancarlo Caldarella, Account Executive, Autodesk
Bas Claassen, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Ashley Hooper, Technical Specialist, Fusion PLM, Autodesk

title: Autodesk Tandem: What Early Digital Twin Deployments Taught Us About Real Value
abstract: What does it really take to make Autodesk Tandem software valuable beyond a demo? This session will share candid lessons learned from early Autodesk Tandem and digital twin planning efforts, including challenges around asset data, model readiness, contractor engagement, and owner expectations. You’ll gain insight into what should (and should not) be included in record models, how to align Autodesk Tandem with CMMS and operational data, and how to avoid common missteps that limit long-term adoption.
speakers: Robert Eckdahl Ii, VDDS Solutions Leader, Black & Veatch

title: Autodesk Young Professionals & Veterans Network Meetup
abstract: This meetup is sponsored by Autodesk Employee Belonging Groups (EBGs) to support connection and shared growth across communities. We bring employees and customers together through interactive, networking-focused experiences. Participants will engage in small-group conversations designed to encourage meaningful dialogue, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across teams, roles, and communities.
speakers: Shashwat Bhardwaj, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk
Kristina Poluyanova, Sales Specialist, Construction, Autodesk
Booth Staff, test

title: Automate the Last Manual Step: Scheduling MEP Fabrication Publishes with Stratus and Revit
abstract: Industrial contractors using AutoCAD Plant 3D already know how to publish DWG files to the Autodesk Construction Cloud/Forma. Now, the cloud-hosted model becomes the source of truth for Stratus as well, so VDC teams can access the full Stratus fabrication processing pipeline. You'll learn how this enables consistent model throughput from design to shop floor to field install, and avoids risk of spool fabrication teams working from stale PDFs, Isos, or 2D instructions.
speakers: Jake Olsen, CEO, Stratus

title: Automating Minimum Plumbing Fixture Calcs in Revit Using Schedules, Formulas, and Spatial Data
abstract: Minimum plumbing fixture (MPF) calculations are often inconsistent, time-consuming, and dependent on Microsoft Excel (and the users' capabilities within it). This session will demonstrate how to integrate MPF calculations directly within Revit software using repurposed area data, project parameters, key schedules, and formulas. You’ll learn how to implement piecewise functions to reflect code requirements, apply consistent rounding methods, and incorporate strategic overrides. This course will also introduce color scheme visualization to communicate fixture demand clearly to project teams and Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs). By the end, you’ll produce standardized, accurate, and code-compliant plumbing fixture calculations entirely within Revit, with a little help from Dynamo.
speakers: Gracey Carol, Practice Technology Project Leader, HED
Amanda Gioia, Practice Technology Computational Leader, HED

title: Automation API: The Execution Engine for Autodesk at Scale
abstract: The Automation API is evolving from a job-processing service into the execution layer for running Autodesk engine workloads at scale. This session traces that evolution, from reusable automation bundles toward flexible, agent-driven workflows, and where it is heading next. We will look at how the platform is being built for reliability at scale, how it provides dedicated, isolated compute and flexible compute options for demanding workloads, and how it is becoming the place where AI agents run Autodesk engine work: supporting always-on engine sessions for iterative agents, surfacing core desktop capabilities to agent-driven workflows, and enabling no-code workflow integration. Using real-world scenarios, we will connect these pieces into the broader Autodesk Platform Services story. This session is relevant whether you are building on Autodesk Platform Services or planning for the future of automation in your workflows.
speakers: Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Rami Kuret, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: A Year in Review: What You Might Have Missed in Autodesk Fusion
abstract: Over the past year, Autodesk Fusion software has continued to evolve across design, manufacturing, electronics, and data—delivering new capabilities that help teams move faster from concept to production. In this session, we’ll take a look at the most impactful updates introduced since last AU. You’ll see how recent enhancements connect design and manufacturing more seamlessly, expand electronics capabilities, and improve data management and collaboration. We’ll also highlight the strategic areas of investment shaping the Fusion future and what they mean for the way you work. Whether you’re a designer, machinist, engineer, or product developer, this session will help you understand where Autodesk Fusion is headed—and how to take advantage of what’s new.
speakers: Kyle Williams, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk
Bankim Charegaonkar, Director, Product Management, Autodesk
Richard Hammerl, Senior Customer Advocacy Manager - Electronics, Autodesk
Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Peter Champneys, Principal Customer Advocacy Manager - Design, Autodesk

title: Backstage Pass: System Variables Management
abstract: With more than 700 system and environment variables inside AutoCAD software, it’s difficult for anyone to know them all. This class will walk through the standard AutoCAD options for learning the system variables, and also provide a free LISP application to browse and change the variables in a dialog. By the time the class is finished, you will be able to find and change any of these variables easily.
speakers: Peter Jamtgaard, Principal Structural Engineer, Jamtgaard Structural Engineering, LLC

title: Beyond 4D: Resource-Based Construction Simulation with FlexSim
abstract: Traditional 4D workflows show sequence—but they rarely quantify how labor, equipment, and logistics decisions affect project performance. This technical deep dive will show how FlexSim extends construction simulation beyond schedule playback into resource-based decision support. Using a practical case study, you’ll learn how to connect schedule logic with crews, equipment, productivity assumptions, and site logistics. You’ll also see how to model the difference between resource-driven and time-bound activities. And you’ll understand how to compare workforce, equipment, and delivery scenarios before execution to identify bottlenecks and improve planning accuracy.
speakers: Anitha c, Junior project Associate, Desapex
AkshayKumar Pawar, Project Associate L2, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP

title: Beyond AEC: Designing a Climate-Resilient Agroforestry System with Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: What if the tools we use to design buildings could also save coffee farming? This session will present a real pilot from Colombia where Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services are used to design Climate-Resilient Agroforestry Systems. See a live Autodesk Forma Site Design demo of digital twin shade and microclimate simulations. Discover how to use Autodesk Forma Data Management to capture geolocated pest data, Brix readings, and reforestation tasks. And learn how Autodesk Platform Services connects it all into actionable farm intelligence. Outcomes include a 67% reduction in coffee berry borer infestation, and layout decisions that once required years now being validated in days. You’ll leave this session with a new mental model for where Autodesk platforms can drive sustainability impact beyond construction.
speakers: Juan David Hurtado Henao, Owner - General Manager, Blue Bird Coffee

title: Beyond Automotive: Scaling Autodesk VRED for Industrial Design Reviews
abstract: Autodesk VRED is well known in automotive, but the same real-time visualization workflow can accelerate collaboration across industrial manufacturing. This Technical Deep Dive shows how teams can use VRED, Python scripting, and immersive reviews to create shared virtual prototypes for switchgear, pumps, and engineered products. Attendees will see how to structure review sessions, add scripted interactions, validate design intent before physical build, and shorten feedback cycles across design, engineering, and program teams.
speakers: Prashant Kalyani, Jr Project Associate, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP
AkshayKumar Pawar, Project Associate L2, Desapex Engineering Consultants LLP

title: Beyond CAD: Where AutoCAD and Forma Connect
abstract: Join us for a fireside chat exploring the future of AutoCAD-to-Forma workflows. Learn how bringing the richness of AutoCAD data into Forma can unlock new design possibilities, extend familiar workflows, and help you deliver more value to your clients.

title: Beyond Digital Twins: How AI and Engineering Models Are Transforming the Built World
abstract: For years, digital twins have been presented as the ultimate goal of digital transformation. But today the conversation has evolved. The real value lies in creating a digital representation of an asset and enabling it to analyze, predict, and support better decisions via artificial intelligence. This session will explore how engineering models, BIM, reality capture, operational data, and AI combine to create intelligent digital ecosystems. We'll examine the evolution from traditional to AI-enabled digital twins. We’ll discuss the role of foundation and domain-specific engineering models. And we’ll explore how organizations can leverage existing digital assets to unlock new operational insights and automation. This session will provide a practical road map for those seeking to transform engineering and construction data into actionable intelligence. You’ll leave with a clear understanding of how AI complements digital twins and how technologies can drive measurable business value throughout the asset lifecycle.
speakers: mark king, Senior Product Manager - Reality Capture, Hexagon Multivista
Valerie Ashe, Sr. Account Executive, Hexagon Multivista
Mariano Franchini, Director of RC & Scan to Services, Hexagon Multivista

title: Beyond the Foundation: Scaling 10 Years of Legacy Code for the Next Generation
abstract: Opening a decade-old LISP file is like entering an ancient tomb: You half-expect a curse if you move a parenthesis—but, instead, you find how more than 1,300 people get work done. This "staple" launch sequence has been our firm's silent engine for more than 10 years, staying rock solid, even as we grew sixfold in size. In this case study, the original architect and a new innovator will share how we collaborated to honor this foundation while using AI to drive productivity. We’ll dive into modernizing legacy AutoCAD and Civil 3D code and providing IT with AI-enhanced detailed reporting and problem-solving. Join us to learn how to balance stable history with the future innovation required for the next decade.
speakers: Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.
R.K. McSwain, IT Customer Service Manager / CAD Manager, LJA, Inc.

title: Beyond the Tool: Aligning People, Process, and Technology in Cost Management
abstract: Inconsistent cost practices, unclear ownership, and fragmented financial workflows are common challenges for general contractors of all sizes. Fortis Construction will share how its cost management operating model was redefined through the implementation of Autodesk Cost Management, aligning roles, processes, and technology along the way. Rather than focusing on system functionality, this session will offer a deep dive into the strategic decisions, trade-offs, and lessons learned. You will leave with a practical framework for evaluating and structuring your own cost processes toward scalable, consistent, and risk-aware cost management in partnership with Autodesk Cost Management.
speakers: Randi Schieber, Sr. VDC Manager, Fortis Construction

title: BIM and VDC Professionals Meetup
abstract: Join this interactive meetup for BIM and virtual design and construction (VDC) professionals to exchange ideas and experiences in an open, peer-driven discussion. Together, we’ll explore how AI and automation are being applied in BIM workflows, the realities of scaling BIM across organizations, and the lessons learned along the way—both successes and challenges. This is a collaborative space for participants to share insights, ask questions, and learn from each other’s real-world experiences. Whether you're testing new technologies or leading BIM implementation, come ready to contribute to the conversation.
speakers: Antia Rodriguez, BIM Transformation Manager, Hitachi Energy
Mariangela Toscano, BIM Lead (Europe & Middle East), Grimshaw
David Gonzalez, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Braindate
abstract:
Find your people. Share your expertise. The best conversations at AU start with Braindate.

 

Create a topic or join one that sparks your interest, then meet onsite in the Braindate Lounge to dive into a focused 45-minute group conversation with like-minded peers, or connect 1:1 for 30 minutes with another attendee to build a meaningful new connection.

 

Share expertise, solve real-world challenges, discover new ideas, and make meaningful connections with attendees who are passionate about the same topics you are - from AI and automation to digital twins, BIM workflows, and more.

 

Visit My AU Portal to start Braindating!

times.room: Venetian, Expo Hall C - Braindate Lounge, level 2

title: Breakfast
abstract: Grab coffee and a bite to eat to fuel your final day at AU.

title: Breaking Data Silos: Connecting Design and Construction Insights with Power BI
abstract: Project data often lives in silos across design and construction, limiting visibility to real-time insights and slowing decision making. With the latest Power BI integrations, Autodesk is bringing together Data Exchange and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to enable unified, end-to-end project insights. In this session, you’ll learn how to combine granular model data from Data Exchange with project, issue, and asset data from Forma into Power BI to build actionable dashboards. Discover practical workflows, customer examples, and best practices that help teams connect data across phases, reduce risk, and drive better project outcomes.
speakers: Trupti Deshpande, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Juan Diego Aranda Yaulimango, LIDER BIM, V&V BRAVO
Vishwa Shah, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: Bridge Design Automation: From Alignment to BIM‑Ready Deliverables
abstract: Bridge teams face pressure to deliver faster, consistent, and low‑carbon outcomes. Yet, many bridge BIM workflows remain manual and hard to scale. This technical deep dive will demonstrate a workflow used on real projects to generate and compare bridge design options from a single alignment input. It will take you from option generation to coordinated models, carbon results, and a final decision point. The session will show how scalable, model‑based delivery enables faster optioneering and earlier sustainability decisions for engineers and project managers to drive better outcomes. In practice, this approach has delivered time savings on bridge projects, including the production of 20 bridge models within days.
speakers: Tatjana Somova, Senior Digital Designer, Mott MacDonald

title: Bridging CAD and GIS: A Streamlined Workflow for Faster, Smarter Proposal Development
abstract: Use Autodesk for fast drafting, quick design changes, and concept development. Then bring that DWG™ proposal data into your geodatabase to streamline integration with your existing geographic information system (GIS). Autodesk excels at rapid design, while GIS provides spatial context and publishing power. By designing in AutoCAD software and delivering through ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Online, you get both speed and accuracy for customer‑ready proposals.
speakers: Joan Rickard, GIS Manager, Areli Corp

title: Bridging the Gap: Custom Autodesk Forma Construction Connect Workflows for ERP and Owner Integration
abstract: Many firms struggle with "data silos" where project information is trapped between Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) and specialized enterprise resource planning (ERP) or owner systems. While off-the-shelf solutions exist, they often fall short of specific operational needs. In this session, Hawaiian Dredging Construction Company will share its journey of building custom integrations in Forma Construction Connect, with nCircle Tech as a consultant. We’ll dive into the technical architecture used to sync data between Forma and CMiC, and show how we automated reporting to owner portals. You’ll leave with a road map for evaluating custom versus out-of-the-box integrations as well as best practices for making Forma the central one-stop shop for field operations.
speakers: Christopher Baze, Director of Construction Technology, Hawaiian Dredging Construction Company
Varun Bhartiya, CEO and Co-founder, nCircle

title: Builders in the AI Loop: How We Accelerate Construction and Preserve Judgement
abstract: AI is increasing output across construction teams, but many leaders are seeing a quieter problem: more-polished work, less ownership. With more options come harder decisions. This strategy talk will use one concrete story and a practical framework to show how to adopt AI without eroding the judgment that experienced builders, designers, and owners have earned the hard way. You’ll learn how to separate AI-assisted production from the human decision making that takes decades to develop. We’ll discuss how leaders in the industry add thinking checkpoints within workflows that make teams faster while preserving their precious (and playful) cognition.
speakers: Richard Antczak, Senior Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Building MEP Automation Tools with pyRevit: Real Examples from High-Rise Project Delivery
abstract: As MEP engineers, we spend too much time on repetitive tasks that could be automated. In this session, we’ll show how we used pyRevit at KEO International Consultants to build custom automation tools inside Revit software, transforming our workflow on high-rise projects. Using two real tools as examples—a chilled water pipe autosizer based on pressure drop criteria (150-300 Pa/m) and a domestic water pipe autosizer following CIBSE Guide G—we’ll demonstrate how pyRevit can automate complex MEP tasks in a single click. This session is for MEP engineers and BIM managers who want to build their own automation tools, regardless of programming background.
speakers: Zaid Fahed, MEP BIM Manager, KEO International Consultants

title: Building the Intelligent Catchment: Using InfoWorks ICM and AI to Create Cleaner, More Resilient Water Environments
abstract: The Only Rainwater into Windermere project represents a system-level approach aiming to stop sewage and highway runoff from entering England’s largest lake. This joint presentation between the project director and the InfoWorks ICM product manager will explain how InfoWorks ICM was used to produce site-specific analytics and potential solutions to inform intervention planning. We’ll present the project timeline, key modeling and data pipelines, methods used, and how these outputs were embedded into decision support tools for key decision makers. You’ll see a short technical demonstration of InfoWorks ICM workflows, and get a peek into the future of using AI prediction capabilities. A discussion of practical outcomes for the water sector will follow.
speakers: Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
Tony Smithson, Storm Overflow Director UK, Mott MacDonald

title: Building the Intelligent Catchment: Using InfoWorks ICM and AI to Create Cleaner, More Resilient Water Environments
abstract: Building intelligent catchments requires a combination of high-quality data, hydraulic modelling and emergency AI capabilities to support better decisions and cleaner, more resilient water environments. This joint presentation between the project director and the InfoWorks ICM product manager will explain how InfoWorks ICM was used to produce site-specific analytics and potential solutions to inform intervention planning. We’ll present the project timeline, key modeling and data pipelines, methods used, and how these outputs were embedded into decision support tools for key decision makers. You’ll see a short technical demonstration of InfoWorks ICM workflows, and get a peek into the future of using AI prediction capabilities. A discussion of practical outcomes for the water sector will follow.
speakers: Tony Smithson, Storm Overflow Director UK, Mott MacDonald
Samer Muhandes, Senior Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: Building Tomorrow: Mastering Project Delivery in the Age of Technology
abstract: As Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) continues to navigate its digital transformation, the team is using Autodesk Forma as the digital backbone for their Project Delivery Collaboration Center (PDCC). Capitalizing on the flexibility and interoperability of the Forma environment, PennDOT is able to connect legacy system data. Learn how PennDOT uses Forma to manage design and construction projects, as well as for its connectivity to other off-the-shelf solutions. Learn how processes are being streamlined, time’s being saved, and project transparency is all accomplished through the rollout of PDCC. To showcase its benefits, PennDOT will be sharing the current use of PDCC on its projects and the road map to the future.
speakers: Kelly Barber, Chief Engineer, PennDOT

title: Building What the Industry Won't: Running Your Digital Practice Like a Tech Start-Up
abstract: What happens when off-the-shelf software limits your vision? At Heatherwick Studio, Revit and Rhino software are our core engines. But true innovation requires breaking out of closed files. This session will reveal how to run your digital practice like a tech start-up by building cloud ecosystems that democratize data. Instead of waiting for vendors, we build tangible tools to expand our impact. Take “Nessie”: We bypassed the Revit UI so nonusers can access and modify data across multiple files at once, straight from the cloud. We’ll explore how to use machine learning (ML) and AI for automated QA/QC, how to deploy AutoDocs, and how to use DIGIPIN for collaborative review. Learn to architect an open, data-rich future that empowers your entire studio.
speakers: Alfonso Monedero, Digital Practice, Heatherwick Studio

title: Build Your Firm's AI Adoption Plan in 90 Minutes
abstract: Most architecture firms know they need an AI strategy, but few have one written down. In this hands-on lab, you will build a clear 30-day AI adoption plan during the session, including owners, simple guardrails, and one measurable pilot. Participants will complete a quick readiness check, audit where knowledge gets stuck on a recent project, and draft a one-page AI policy plus a 30-day action plan they can start using Monday morning.
speakers: KENTON GRANT, Fractional CTO & Technology Advisor, Kenton Grant Consulting
Evan Troxel, Director, TRXL

title: Built on Trust: How Autodesk and Multiconsult Accelerated Revit Performance at Scale
abstract: What happens when mega projects push Revit beyond its limits? For Multiconsult, 30+ minute open and sync times became a critical barrier across multidisciplinary teams working on highly detailed healthcare projects. In this session, we’ll show how Autodesk and Multiconsult partnered to expose performance bottlenecks by analyzing journal data, model structures, and sync patterns. Together, we optimized linking strategies, streamlined sync workflows, and strengthened model health practices, turning insights into targeted Revit hotfixes addressing scalability challenges in loading and regeneration. This collaboration built trust and delivered shared value. Discover how this work is driving scalable, cloud-centric workflows and how to apply it.
speakers: Casandra Armeanu, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk
Thea Marie Danielsen, Head of BIM for Buildings and Properties, Multiconsult Norge AS
Stian Ingvaldsen, VP Digital Engineering Solutions, Multiconsult Norge AS

title: Catching Procurement Risk Before It's a Delay: Closing the Supply Chain Gap
abstract: Procurement risk rarely shows up early enough to act on. Most GCs find out about a lead-time problem when a submittal comes back rejected or a delivery date slips — by then, the schedule has already absorbed the hit. This session reframes the procurement log from a record of what happened into a signal for what's about to go wrong. We'll unpack what "proactive" actually means in practice: knowing critical lead items before design is finished, prioritizing submittals by schedule impact rather than spec order, and catching a delivery shift the same day it happens — not weeks later at the next OAC meeting. With switchgear lead times now stretching past a year and tariff-driven cost escalation, procurement has stopped being a construction activity and become a development-phase decision. We'll discuss what it takes to move that decision upstream — and why the construction "data leaders" already doing this see meaningfully higher profit growth as a result.
speakers: Klas Berghede, VP Production & Innovation, Boldt
Eshan Don, CEO & Founder, Krane
Jared Christman, Vice President of Innovation and Technology, Hays Electrical Service

title: Civil 3D Corridor Chaos Meets Control: A Hands-On Lab
abstract: Corridor modeling in Civil 3D can be a beautiful, efficient thing—or a nightmarish mire. If you’ve ever lost a late night trying to change one tiny end condition in a sea of them, this hands-on lab is for you. You’ll build and compare corridor models in Civil 3D software using a single-baseline, single-region approach with spiderweb-like conditionals. Then you’ll use a multiple-baseline, multiple-region approach with limited conditionals. You’ll test switching end conditions in corridor parameters; you’ll test how the workflows respond to design changes; and you’ll learn how a better-structured model reduces friction and rework, improves flexibility and design review, and supports faster, more informed project decision making at concept or final design.
speakers: Kristen Liggett, Senior Project Engineer, VHB

title: Civil BIM Runway Digital Twin
abstract: See how more than a decade of standardized design projects have been aggregated into a digital twin runway for one of the world’s busiest airports. How can owners use verified utility designs to drive maintenance and regulatory compliance? In Denver, we’re tracking sanitary sewer, storm sewer, aircraft de-icing fluid delivery and recovery, jet fuel, water, electrical duct banks, airfield lighting and signs, and pavement models to inform future design and current operations. As the puzzle comes together, see how we can visualize a clear picture of our infrastructure.
speakers: Clint Davis, Sr. Civil BIM Project Manager, Denver International Airport

title: Civil BIM Runway Digital Twin
abstract: See how more than a decade of standardized design projects have been aggregated into a digital twin runway for one of the world’s busiest airports. How can owners use verified utility designs to drive maintenance and regulatory compliance? In Denver, we’re tracking sanitary sewer, storm sewer, aircraft de-icing fluid delivery and recovery, jet fuel, water, electrical duct banks, airfield lighting and signs, and pavement models to inform future design and current operations. As the puzzle comes together, see how we can visualize a clear picture of our infrastructure.
speakers: Clint Davis, Sr. Civil BIM Project Manager, Denver International Airport

title: Collaborative Multi-Agents for AEC: A New Way to Navigate Design Decisions
abstract: Achieving net-zero carbon in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) at scale can be complex, often requiring trade-offs between cost and carbon reduction goals, as well as new design approaches and workflows. Collaborative multi-agent systems (MAS) can unlock new opportunities for these kinds of multi-objective problems. At Autodesk Research, we’re developing and testing agentic-based capabilities for design decision making, including defining design representations for automated design exploration, navigating metrics trade-offs, and sharing design tasks. This talk will present our findings and demonstrate how they can be applied to real-world projects, as demonstrated through our partnership with LA28.
speakers: Lorenzo Villaggi, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
Nikita Klimenko, Senior AI Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: Collaborative Multi-Agents for AEC: A New Way to Navigate Design Decisions
abstract: Achieving net-zero carbon in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) at scale can be complex, often requiring trade-offs between cost and carbon reduction goals, as well as new design approaches and workflows. Collaborative multi-agent systems (MAS) can unlock new opportunities for these kinds of multi-objective problems. At Autodesk Research, we’re developing and testing agentic-based capabilities for design decision making, including defining design representations for automated design exploration, navigating metrics trade-offs, and sharing design tasks. speakers: Nikita Klimenko, Senior AI Research Scientist, Autodesk
Lorenzo Villaggi, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: Concept-to-Consumer in 60 Minutes: Rapid Conceptual Design for Consumer Products with Autodesk Fusion and Vizcom
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Fusion and Vizcom radically shorten conceptual design cycles for consumer products by pairing the Fusion parametric engineering and lifecycle controls with Vizcom’s real-time photoreal visualization and AI-driven variant generation. Learn how rapid ideation, material/finish sweeps, and perceptual testing produce validated visual states that automatically feed CAM snapshots, BOM and version updates, and manufacturability acceptance gates, preserving traceability and minimizing rework. The talk will include demos, concrete integration patterns, and data-contract best practices for the Fusion-Vizcom workflow. We’ll also cover a one-click pilot activation that turns validated concepts into prioritized production pilots with measurable POC outcomes.
speakers: Jared Teiger, Community Manager, Vizcom
Kaelan Richards, CTO, Vizcom
Nicolas De Peyer, Product Expert Team lead, Vizcom

title: Connect AutoCAD to the Cloud: Reduce File Chaos for Small Teams with Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials
abstract: Discover how Autodesk Forma Data Management Essentials enhances AutoCAD workflows for small teams through a live demonstration of a centralized, cloud-connected project workspace. Included with AutoCAD, Revit, and Civil 3D subscriptions, Forma Data Management Essentials enables teams to organize, view, and share project data directly from the desktop. See how to reduce version confusion, improve collaboration, and connect design workflows without disruption. This session will also demonstrate how to get started, how to compare Forma Data Management Essentials to common file-sharing tools, and how to share project standards across teams.
speakers: Volker Cocco, Sr Technical Enablement Specialist - AutoCAD, Autodesk

title: Connected Carbon Data for Construction: API-Powered Decisions at Scale
abstract: Construction teams face growing pressure to make early, data-driven carbon decisions. Yet fragmented regional data sets limit consistency and scalability across tools. This session will explore how TBI, a leading construction firm, is advancing end-to-end carbon assessment by connecting data across planning, design, and preconstruction workflows. Using Autodesk Forma Carbon Insights (Autodesk Forma, Revit, and Forma Takeoff) and the Sustainability Data API, TBI will demonstrate how API-powered strategies enable early-stage carbon comparisons across multiple regions, reduce manual data handling, and scale assessments across projects. You’ll gain a strategic framework for driving better, data-informed decisions through connected, scalable carbon workflows.
speakers: Dick van Ginkel, Technical Innovation Manager, TBI_WOONlab
Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk

title: Connected Preconstruction: BuildingConnected Workflows in Autodesk Forma
abstract: BuildingConnected has long been the backbone for bid management and subcontractor qualification at Miller Davis. As early beta users, Miller Davis has worked closely with Autodesk to test workflows that bring BuildingConnected into Autodesk Forma alongside Autodesk Forma Takeoff and Autodesk Forma Estimate. The Miller Davis team will share how Forma Bid helps reduce tool fragmentation and keeps preconstruction work connected within a single environment. We’ll discuss lessons learned from early adoption, and we’ll walk through familiar workflows reimagined in Forma—including RFP management, multiple proposals per project, bidder recommendations, qualification insights, bid leveling, and flexible reporting. The Autodesk product team will join to support the discussion.
speakers: Cory Kintz, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk
Ariel Castillo, Subject Matter Expert, Preconstruction, Autodesk

title: Connected Preconstruction: BuildingConnected Workflows in Autodesk Forma
abstract: BuildingConnected has long been the backbone for bid management and subcontractor qualification at Miller Davis. As early beta users, Miller Davis has worked closely with Autodesk to test workflows that bring BuildingConnected into Autodesk Forma alongside Autodesk Forma Takeoff and Autodesk Forma Estimate. The Miller Davis team will share how Forma Bid helps reduce tool fragmentation and keeps preconstruction work connected within a single environment. We’ll discuss lessons learned from early adoption, and we’ll walk through familiar workflows reimagined in Forma—including RFP management, multiple proposals per project, bidder recommendations, qualification insights, bid leveling, and flexible reporting. The Autodesk product team will join to support the discussion.
speakers: Ariel Castillo, Subject Matter Expert, Preconstruction, Autodesk
Cory Kintz, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk

title: Connecting AECO Workflows End-to-End with the Autodesk Forma Industry Cloud
abstract: See how architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) teams connect planning, design, coordination, and construction workflows in a single AI and data-driven environment using the Autodesk Forma industry cloud. This technical and practical deep dive will walk through real workflows—from site planning in Autodesk Forma to design in Revit software, coordination in Forma Design Collaboration, and execution in Forma Build. Learn how data flows through Autodesk Data Management as a common data environment, preserving decisions across phases with practical examples. Explore practical AI-powered use cases such as rapid design iteration, automated analysis, and model-based coordination. And discover how to reduce manual work, improve collaboration, and implement connected workflows across the AECO lifecycle.
speakers: Alejandra Beaujon, Sr Implementation Consultant, Autodesk
Joey Matla, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Connecting a Nation: How MOEI Unified Infrastructure Delivery Across the UAE Using Autodesk Forma
abstract: When the United Arab Emirates set its Net Zero 2050 target, the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MOEI) faced a critical challenge: Project data was spread across disconnected systems in seven emirates, creating delays, inconsistency, and poor visibility. This session will share how the MOEI moved to a connected delivery model using Autodesk Forma, scaled ISO 19650-aligned BIM standards nationally, created a single source of truth, and used AI-powered environmental analysis to support better design decisions. We’ll also share what failed, how we handled resistance, and the lessons learned. You’ll leave with a practical road map you can apply to government and institutional projects immediately.
speakers: Moza Neimi, CEO for AI MOEI, ministry of energy and infrastructure
abdulrahman alkholy, Digital transformation lead & AI, Ministry of energy and infrastructure

title: Content Creators Community Meetup
abstract: Join us for an enriching Content Creator Community Meetup. This event is designed for those keen on enhancing their craft, networking with fellow content creators, and discussing effective strategies for building engaging content and growing their impact. Whether you're a seasoned creator or just starting your journey, this meetup is your chance to connect, share insights, and learn from a supportive community of Autodesk experts and enthusiasts.
speakers: Neil Cross, Autodesk Software Consultant, Tech3D
Chris Benner, Community Manager, Autodesk

title: Continuous Versus Periodic Clash Detection: Can Model Coordination and Autodesk AI Replace Navisworks?
abstract: Is the Navisworks silo holding your project back? For 20 years, coordination was a "once a week" event locked on a desktop. No more. This session will explore the leap to continuous, cloud-native coordination in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll dive into how Model Coordination democratizes BIM, using Autodesk AI and Autodesk Assistant to validate clashes against specs in real time. Learn to ditch static PDF reports for a closed-loop workflow that connects designers directly to fixes. We’ll settle the debate: Where does Model Coordination win, and when do you still need the Navisworks "power user" kit? Join us to build a road map for a faster, AI-augmented and integrated future. Stop clashing. Start coordinating.
speakers: Karan Singh, Digital Delivery Manager, Burns & McDonnell India
Stephen Brooke, Digital Delivery Manager, Burns & McDonnell

title: Customer Case: Explore Autodesk Workshop XR implementation in Wartsila
abstract: This session demonstrates how implementing Autodesk XR has delivered direct business value through faster issue detection and improved collaboration. By bringing project teams into a shared XR environment, design errors and conflicts are identified earlier, reducing rework, cost, and decision lead times. We will outline the workflow from Autodesk Construction Cloud (Forma) to XR ready VR models and show how XR is used in live new build projects to support joint reviews, stakeholder alignment, and informed decision making. The session also highlights future plans to further enhance value through GAMMA AR for extending the experience to construction site.
speakers: Johann Ackermann
Thomas Mård, IT Manager, Wärtsilä Finland Oy
Fredrik Rasmus, Senior Project Engineer, Wärtsilä Finland Oy

title: Data Exchange in the Real World: Customer Stories, Lessons Learned, and What's Next
abstract: What does Data Exchange look like when it’s solving real problems on real projects? In this session, you’ll first hear directly from teams using Data Exchange today and learn how they’ve connected disparate tools, reduced manual handoffs, and built more-reliable cross-discipline workflows. These are live production use cases demonstrating interoperability with measurable impact on delivery. Then, the Data Exchange product management team will connect these stories to what’s next, sharing road map priorities, upcoming capabilities, and the ways that customer feedback is shaping the platform. Leave with practical ideas to apply in your own workflows and a clear view of where Data Exchange is headed.
speakers: Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Gaurav Bhamre, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Anna Baranova, Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk

title: Design and Make Celebration
abstract:
You spent the week building the future. Now let’s celebrate it. 

 

On Thursday night, AU takes over The LINQ Promenade for a festival-style finale filled with live music, comedy, DJs, food, drinks and experiences around every corner. 

 

See Rebelution live at Brooklyn Bowl, with Party Pupils bringing the yacht-rock energy before the show. Dance outside with TOKiMONSTA and XANDRA. Catch Josh Johnson, Chris Turner, Liz Glazer and Leonard Ouzts at Jimmy Kimmel’s Comedy Club. Bowl a few frames, explore VR and live art, or take a spin on the High Roller, where select pods will feature surprise entertainment of their own. 

 

This is not a traditional single-headliner concert. The celebration stretches across The LINQ, so check the schedule, pick your own festival adventure, and explore the full footprint. 

 

Individual venues have their own capacities, and popular experiences may fill. If one venue is full, another great experience is just steps away. 

 

Before you head to The LINQ:  

 

	Wear your AU badge. It is required for entry.
	Leave laptops, backpacks, and large bags at your hotel.  
	Small purses are permitted.  
	Bring a government-issued photo ID for bar service.  
	Check the app for set times and the festival map.  
	Individual venues have their own capacities and may fill.  
	Wear comfortable shoes and plan to explore.

title: Design and Manufacturing Industry Deep Dive
abstract: Explore the trends, challenges, and technology shifts shaping the future of design and manufacturing. This session will examine how organizations are connecting data, people, and processes across the product lifecycle to increase agility, improve sustainability, and accelerate innovation. Gain practical insights into evolving industry priorities and the opportunities they create for business transformation.
speakers: Sanjay Aggarwal, Vice President, D&M Industry Strategy, Autodesk
Vik Vedantham, Sr. Director, D&M Business Intelligence & Strategy, Autodesk

title: Design and Manufacturing Tech Admin Meetup: Connect, Share, and Learn with CAD, PDM, and PLM Manager Peers
abstract: Are you a CAD manager, PDM/PLM admin, technology leader, or CAD geek supporting design and engineering teams? If you manage Autodesk software, data, standards, and/or users, you know the role can feel isolated. Meetups at AU are casual networking opportunities designed to help you find like-minded people and make meaningful connections. Join your technology manager peers across CAD, PDM, and PLM to connect, share experiences, and consider common challenges together. Discuss what’s working and what’s not, and get a fresh perspective on how others are managing their technology environments to meet business objectives. Leave with new ideas, practical insights, and a support network you can rely on long after AU.
speakers: Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk
Ron Hyman, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Designing the Future Workforce Together: Connecting Education Outcomes with Industry Expectations
abstract: Education and industry must work together to prepare the next generation of designers and makers, but how do we get there? What’s one skill students are missing today, and how do we help prepare them to design and make for tomorrow? This interactive session invites you to move beyond casual mingling into purpose-driven connection-building between educators and industry professionals. Engage in guided discussions, share challenges and insights, and uncover opportunities to better align curriculum with real-world needs. Walk away with meaningful connections, fresh perspectives, and actionable ideas. Join us and help shape the future workforce together.
speakers: Michael Brackney, Senior AEC Customer Success Manager, US, Autodesk
Jason Roth, Principal Account Manager, US, Autodesk

title: Design Like a Rocket Scientist: Generative Design Versus Topology Optimization in Autodesk Fusion
abstract: What’s the difference between topology optimization and generative design—and why does it matter when you're building components with strict safety factors and manufacturing requirements? In this session for both CAD beginners and pros, we’ll explore the tools and workflows that helped Elara Aerospace design a launch-ready, record-breaking rocket capable of surviving the extreme forces of space. You’ll work through guided exercises in Autodesk Fusion software, learning how to apply both generative design and topology optimization to reduce mass, increase strength, and improve overall performance under tight constraints. By the end of the session, you’ll have built and optimized a component ready for spaceflight-level performance.
speakers: Roman Stoma, Student Structural Engineer, Elara Aerospace

title: Design, Make, and Move: Real‑World Workflows on Slim Mobile Workstations Powered by Intel
abstract: Design and Make teams are under pressure to deliver more-complex projects, faster, from anywhere. In this session, a frontline “super user” from industry joins Intel to show how Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, and Revit come together on slim mobile workstations powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 and Intel Arc B390 graphics to meet that challenge. You’ll see how the speaker’s organization moved from traditional, desk‑bound workflows to a flexible, AI‑enabled setup that keeps designers, engineers, and BIM teams productive—whether they’re in the office, on the shop floor, or on the jobsite. Revit drives rich intelligent models and documentation. AutoCAD handles detailed 2D and 3D work that still anchors many projects. Autodesk Fusion connects design, generative exploration, and manufacturing in a single environment. All of it runs on slim, professional mobile workstations—with integrated Intel Arc graphics and on‑device AI acceleration—without sacrificing performance or reliability.
speakers: David Butts, Virtual Design and Construction Manager, Kimley-Horn
Lindsay M Benjamin, ISV Partner Marketing Manager, INTEL CORPORATION

title: Design Without Disruption: Solving Electronics Obsolescence at the Source
abstract: At Avnet, our mission is to accelerate the adoption and seamless supply of new technologies. We understand the challenges engineers face when bringing innovative designs to life, and we’re here to help. Our latest app is designed to empower engineers by providing direct access to critical resources, streamlining the design process, and optimizing the supply chain. This session will be an engaged demonstration of Autodesk Fusion Electronics and Avnet’s App to solve for the most-challenging obsolescence problems within your electronics supply chain
speakers: Rogelio Gonzalez, GCET Apps Engineering Manager, Avnet

title: Developing Reinforcement Shop Drawings for Viaducts and Station Buildings Using Revit: A Case Study
abstract: This session will look at a case study on delivering reinforcement shop drawings for viaducts and station buildings using Revit software at metro scale. SYSTRA India adapted building-centered workflows to infrastructure precast through a template-to-transmittal strategy which included: standardized content and shared parameters; parametric rebar families aligned to fabricator shape codes; and automation for numbering, scheduling, and batch sheet creation. Rule‑based QA checks, strict revision control, and ERP‑ready exports ensured traceability from model to yard. Results included 30% to 40% faster turnarounds.
speakers: Matias Mantilla, Sr Technical Account Manager, Autodesk
Lovneet MAHAJAN, Head of Department, SYSTRA MVA Consulting India Pvt. Ltd.

title: Digital Twin Meetup (Volume 2): Digital Twins Meet AI
abstract: Following last year’s digital twin meetup, this second edition will explore how digital twins are evolving with AI and reality capture across infrastructure and construction. Discover how BIM, geographic information system (GIS), and reality capture enable connected, data-driven environments that support simulation, prediction, and informed decision making. This interactive meetup will focus on real-world challenges, lessons learned, and practical strategies for scaling digital twins. Join an open discussion to exchange ideas, explore what’s working today, and understand how to move from static models to dynamic digital twin solutions.
speakers: Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD
Viv Devadas, AI Solutions Manager, Mott MacDonald
Mostafa Elashmawy, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Digital Twins and the Missing Middle: Strategies for Filling the Lifecycle Data Gap in Large Projects
abstract: Architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) teams excel at BIM for construction, but a "missing middle" exists between handover and operations where high-fidelity data often rots. For owners of 200MW+ mission-critical assets, this data gap creates massive operational risk. How do we bridge this divide to ensure a living digital twin? This session will deconstruct the missing middle using a data-first framework. We’ll explore how to use Owner Data Delivery Requirements (ODDR) and ISO 19650 to align design with operations from inception. Learn the technical workflows to migrate and validate data from Revit software and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll also preview how AI agents can automate QA/QC, transforming static models into actionable digital currency for the entire building lifecycle.
speakers: Benjamin Wills, Senior Digital Delivery Program Manager, VEC
Bryan Blas, Digital Delivery Program Manager, VEC
Tadeh Hakopian, Program Manager, Digital Delivery, VEC

title: Digital Twins: Hot Takes and Cold Truths
abstract: The audience for this session will be polled beforehand on digital twin hot takes and cold truths. Based on the results, former virtual design and construction (VDC) professionals working in the digital twin technology space will share a hot take and cold truth from their experiences. For example, a hot take is: "You can build a digital twin with poor data quality, set goals with an emphasis on 3D visualization over operational outcomes, and do many pilot projects without scaling into broader operations." We’ll identify opportunities and share anecdotes on empowering owners, operators, and their design and construction partners to connect capital delivery and facilities operations through digital twins.
speakers: Iria Carreira, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Karina Cardenas, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
