title: Ditching the Bloat: Re-Engineering MEP High-Density Modeling with Revit DirectShapes to Save Model Health
abstract: A major crisis facing the VDC industry is model bloat. On large scale projects, placing thousands of dynamic, deeply nested native Revit hangers or small components triggers endless CPU parametric calculations that cripple model health, max out workstation RAM, and freeze synchronization times. To break this bottleneck, our product team chose a disruptive approach: pivoting away from standard Revit Families (.rfa) entirely and adopting Revit DirectShape technology. In this session, we will deep dive into the strategic evaluation behind moving the parametric engine outside of Revit to process calculations externally. We will demonstrate how injecting raw geometry directly into the project environment bypasses the family constraint solver, turning slow CPU-bound processing into fluid, GPU-driven visualization. Finally, learn how we map standard Shared Parameters to these elements to retain 100% of required BIM scheduling and tagging data.
speakers: Michael Schinn, Director of BIM for DEWALT, DEWALT / MSUITE

title: Don't Just Imagine the Future—Build It: How Information Became the Infrastructure of Interior Construction
abstract:
The future of construction is often discussed in terms of new materials, technologies or products. Yet the industry's biggest challenges stem from an older problem: disconnected information. Every day, project teams recreate data, translate intent and manage friction when design, specification, manufacturing and construction operate separately. As expectations for speed, flexibility and sustainability increase, this fragmented approach is difficult to sustain.
In this session, Diane will draw from real-world examples, including the development of 4SPACE Rooms and a partnership with Autodesk. You will explore how connected data,manufacturable intelligence, AI and integrated workflows are changing not only how spaces are designed, but how ideas move from concept to reality.
Learn why information is a foundational layer of the built environment, how digital workflows reduce friction across a project lifecycle and what organizations must do to bridge gaps between innovation and adoption.
speakers: Diane Turnwall, Architectural Solutions  Director, Haworth

title: Don’t Wait, Non-Revit Developers! Create Your Own Revit Add-Ins Using AI and the Revit API.
abstract: Many Revit users have workflow wish list items that could automate repetitive tasks or add missing functionality. This class will show how to create Revit add-ins. Aimed at non-developers, we will cover add-in basics. We’ll also show how AI can help generate and refine code while users stay in control. You’ll learn enough to review results, test behavior, and improve tools step by step. No programming experience is required. By the end, you’ll understand how Revit add-ins work and how AI can help turn everyday workflow problems into useful custom tools.
speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: Don’t Wait, Non-Revit Developers! Create Your Own Revit Add-Ins Using AI and the Revit API.
abstract: Many Revit users have workflow wish list items that could automate repetitive tasks or add missing functionality. This class will show how to create Revit add-ins. speakers: Marcello Sgambelluri, Director of Advanced Design Technology, AG&E

title: Do You Trust Me? Building Trustworthy AI for Design and Engineering Workflows.
abstract: As AI becomes embedded in design and engineering tools, the question isn’t just what it can do—it’s whether you can trust it. This session will cover practical ways to make AI more reliable, including handling proprietary versus common design data—and validating outputs. You'll learn practical tactics for increasing the trustworthiness of AI models, with a focus on real-world challenges like distinguishing proprietary intellectual property from common design elements and validating the accuracy of AI-generated outputs. We’ll explore assessing inputs, adding safeguards, and creating feedback loops to improve performance over time—so you can adopt and build AI responsibly without sacrificing quality or compliance.
speakers: Ousama Lakhdar-Ghazal, Director, Trusted AI & Privacy, Autodesk
Nicolas Bonnet, Head of AI Trust, Autodesk

title: Drawing from Experience: CAD Management Is More Than Being a CAD Expert
abstract: This award-winning panel is back again with new topics to discuss and insights to share. This year, the panel will feature some familiar faces and some new ones—all gathered to discuss things important to a CAD manager. Topics will range from technology and data to the even more challenging human aspects of teams and workflows. Learn from this panel of diverse CAD managers who are widely respected as leaders in their field. Hear their unique perspectives and discover solutions to challenges faced by CAD managers from organizations of all sizes and backgrounds. You won’t want to miss this chance to hear the important lessons they’ve learned from decades of experience.
speakers: R.K. McSwain, IT Customer Service Manager / CAD Manager, LJA, Inc.
Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching
Robert Green, Owner, Robert Green Consulting
Kate Towne, Lead IT Applications Specialist, TYLin
Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+

title: Empower Your Designs: Combine Third-Party Models with Inventor Automation
abstract: Are you overwhelmed by the variety of 3D models from vendors, suppliers, or OEMs? Formats like STP, SAT, IGS, CGR, and OBJ may showcase product shapes, but they often lack features needed for effective use in complex CAD environments. In this session, you’ll learn how to use advanced templates and techniques combined with iLogic automation to create useful models in Inventor software. These templates will define connection points, establish constraint frameworks, set BoM descriptions, and even create accurate CoG work geometry on models that lack material properties. Join us for an engaging exploration of tips, tricks, and modeling strategies that will empower you to achieve your automation goals and elevate your design process.
speakers: Coy Pannell, Senior Designer, Subsea 7
Anthony Muzzillo, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: Engineering Out Resonance: Practical Modal and Frequency Response Workflows in Inventor Nastran
abstract: Unwanted vibration can lead to equipment failure, structural fatigue, and costly downtime. In this technical deep dive, we’ll walk through a practical modal and frequency-response workflow in Inventor Nastran software using a fully generic vibrating‑machine model. You’ll learn how to identify natural frequencies, interpret resonance behavior, tune stiffness, shift critical modes, and validate safe operating ranges. This session will deliver a repeatable, production-ready simulation workflow for engineers working with vibrating systems across mining, manufacturing, and machinery design.
speakers: Diego Ramirez, Director, D.R. Engineering Solutions Pty Ltd

title: Every Project Builds the Next: How Agentic AI Turns Design Projects into Software
abstract: Every design project starts almost from scratch — zoning analysis redone, energy models rebuilt, hard-won design logic left behind in last year's project folder. What if each previous project made the next one better? This session will present Autodesk Research's prototype system for agentic Design and Make. As you work through the different phases of a project, from conceptual design with physical models to collaborative design reviews with clients and engineers, the system captures your workflows and design knowledge as reusable software that compounds over time. When a new commission arrives with different requirements, that software comes with you, automatically adapting. Your firm doesn't just deliver results — it builds bespoke software that makes every project smarter than the last.
speakers: Brian Lee, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk
Ray Wang, Principal Research Scientist, Autodesk

title: Expo
abstract:
This is where AU comes to life.

Step inside the AU Expo and experience the future of design and make in motion. See live demos of Autodesk’s newest product offerings, connect with the Autodesk Community, recharge and network in our lounges, and explore breakthrough solutions from hundreds of innovative sponsors.

Whether you’re shaping buildings, infrastructure, teams, or transformation strategies, the Expo is your place to discover what’s next—and meet the people making it happen.

And don’t miss the AU Quest: a fun, interactive way to explore, connect, and uncover the best of the Expo.

Come curious. Leave inspired.

title: Ford Racing Generative Design for Suspension Components
abstract: Join us for a conversation and presentation on the application of Autodesk Fusion Generative Design at Ford Racing. Learn about the how, the why, and the results. We’ll showcase process, testing, and a workflow of collaboration between Ford and Autodesk. In addition, come find out how engineering and design can work better together.
speakers: Jeff Smith, Fusion Sr. Sales Specialist,  Enterprise, Autodesk
Dave Friske, Ford Performance Engineer, Ford Motor Company

title: Forma CS Summit l The Autodesk Forma Admin & Standardization Roundtable: Building a Scalable Data Foundation
abstract: Join this interactive Forma Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, focused on Forma administration and standardization strategies. Designed for Forma admins, platform owners, and operations leaders, this session uses facilitated peer discussion to explore governance and scalable adoption that enable streamlined, standardized practices. Engage directly with Autodesk Product and SMEs as active contributors and partners, alongside industry peers sharing knowledge and real‑world insight in a collaborative, feedback‑driven environment. Attendees leave with actionable strategies, expanded peer networks, and stronger partnership with Autodesk.
speakers: Will Marinos, Director of Design Technologies, Hazen and Sawyer
Ross Collinson, Dir., Product Management, Autodesk
Neree Croteau, Principal Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: Forma CS Summit l The Autodesk Forma Ecosystem Roundtable: Building Successful Projects Through Connected Teams and Data
abstract: The most successful projects are built on aligned stakeholders, shared visibility, and strong partnerships. Join this interactive Autodesk Forma Ecosystem Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for owners, GCs, subcontractors, architects, and engineers looking to maximize the value of Autodesk Forma throughout project delivery. Through facilitated peer discussion with Autodesk Product, SMEs, and industry peers, explore how others are leveraging Autodesk Forma to connect teams, workflows, and project data to strengthen stakeholder engagement and project experiences. Bring your perspectives, learn from the Autodesk Forma community, expand your network, and leave with new ideas for driving long-term, collaborative project success.
speakers: Tawnya Reitz, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk

title: Forma CS Summit l The Forma AI & APIs Roundtable: Connected Data, AI, and Business Transformation
abstract: AI is everywhere—but where is it delivering real business value? Join this interactive Forma AI & APIs Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for platform owners, administrators, innovation leaders, and digital transformation teams. Through facilitated peer discussion and engagement with Autodesk Product, SMEs, and industry peers, explore how connected data, AI, APIs, Autodesk Assistant, and intelligent automation are transforming workflows and business outcomes. Exchange ideas, learn from real-world experiences, explore Autodesk's vision for AI, and help inform the future opportunities and priorities shaping innovation across the Forma platform.
speakers: Jordan McKeown, Director of Operations, Pankow Builders
Matt Racher, Senior Customer Success Manager, Autodesk
Edmundo Herrera, Principal Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Forma CS Summit l The Forma Data & Insights Roundtable: Turning Data into Strategic Impact
abstract: What separates organizations that collect data from those that use it to drive meaningful impact? Join this interactive Forma Data & Insights Roundtable, hosted by Autodesk Customer Success, for leaders focused on reporting, analytics, digital transformation, and operational excellence. Through facilitated peer discussion, engage with Autodesk Data & Insights leaders, Product experts, and industry peers to explore how connected, standardized data within Forma is enabling elevated reporting, dashboard-driven visibility, and more informed decision-making. Share experiences, gain practical insights, and help shape future reporting and analytics priorities while building stronger connections across the Forma community.
speakers: LaShawn Hodge, Principal Account Services Rep, Autodesk
Brad Buckles, VP, Technology and Innovation, Charles Perry Partners, Inc.
John Prior, Sr Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk

title: Fragmentation to Flow: How Vanderlande Connects Design, Delivery, and Operations with Autodesk Forma
abstract: Fragmented data, disconnected tools, and inconsistent workflows continue to limit visibility and slow decision making across complex projects. Vanderlande’s projects span design, construction, and operations, and maintaining reliable and aligned information is increasingly challenging. In this session, discover how Vanderlande is transforming project delivery across both airport and parcel logistics projects using Autodesk Forma as a unified platform. While airport projects require tailored approaches for each customer, parcel programs demand scalable, repeatable workflows across multiple sites. Explore how this approach replaces fragmented systems, improves collaboration, and enables consistent delivery across diverse project types.
speakers: Matthew Rowland, Engineering Senior Manager, Vanderlande

title: From 1893 to the Digital Twin: Revolutionizing Bilbao’s Century-Old Sewer Network with ICMLive
abstract: How do you transform Bilbao’s 130-year-old, 740-kilometer sewer network into a proactive, data-driven utility? By integrating InfoWorks ICM and ICMLive into Acciona’s "NETWIN" ecosystem, the city has moved from reactive maintenance to real-time predictive management. We’ll dive into the technical journey of creating an operational digital twin capable of simulating tidal influences and intense Atlantic rainfall (+20% projected) to mitigate combined sewer overflows (CSOs). You’ll learn how this integration provides a scalable road map for aging urban infrastructure, ensuring compliance with the new European Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (2024/3019) while delivering long-term value beyond temporary subsidies.
speakers: Frank Zamora, C.I.O. AGUA, Acciona
Paloma Akerman, Principal, Sales Specialist, Water, Autodesk

title: From 2D Layout to 3D Simulation: A Digital Factory Hands-On Lab
abstract: In this hands-on lab, you’ll experience a connected digital factory workflow by executing it in real time. Starting with a 2D factory layout in AutoCAD using Factory Design Utilities, you’ll convert it into a 3D model in Inventor with a single click and bring it into FlexSim for simulation. The lab will also demonstrate how design changes are synchronized across AutoCAD, Inventor, and FlexSim, ensuring a connected workflow and reducing manual rework. You’ll gain practical skills to move from layout to simulation in minutes.
speakers: Dave Graves, Sr Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Mike jolicoeur, Sr Sales Specialist, Flexim, Autodesk
Harshit Gole, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: From AI Concept to Product Development: Partner Innovation in Autodesk Fusion
abstract: AI is changing how products are imagined, explored, and developed from the earliest stages. In this partner panel, Vizcom, Avnet, and Naya Studio will show how their Autodesk Fusion integrations bring AI and intelligent automation into conceptual design and the early stages of product development. Attendees will learn how Vizcom connects AI-powered concept visualization with Fusion design workflows; how Avnet supports electronics decisions, BOM insight, and early supply-chain awareness; and how Naya Studio connects Fusion models with the briefs, sketches, feedback, and approvals around them while turning Fusion geometry into early cost and sustainability insight. Together, these partners help product design teams turn early ideas into informed concepts and make smarter decisions before downstream development begins.
speakers: Grace Chang, D&M Strategic Partnerships Ecosystem Manager, Autodesk
Christopher Jackson, Vice President, Global Engineering, Avnet
Casey Morgan, Strategic Business Developer Dir., Autodesk
Kaelan Richards, CTO, Vizcom
Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio

title: From Asset Data to Digital Twin: How Rivian Builds a Trusted Asset Backbone
abstract: What does it take to turn project data into a digital twin teams can actually trust? Rivian shares how it treats asset data as a product, connecting Autodesk Forma, Autodesk Tandem, ERP, and CMMS systems into a reliable asset backbone. Hear how data standards, ID strategies, integrations, and lessons from manufacturing pilots are helping connect design, construction, operations, maintenance, and finance.

title: From AutoCAD Toolsets to Inventor: Enabling Connected Workflows with Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma
abstract: This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD Electrical electromechanical workflows, AutoCAD Mechanical linked with Inventor software, and factory design workflows for seamless data exchange. Learn how to integrate layouts and models across tools, enabling accurate coordination from schematics to 3D design. Discover how cloud-based solutions like Desktop Connector and Autodesk Forma improve collaboration, maintain data continuity, and reduce rework. Through practical examples, see how connected workflows enhance efficiency and accelerate project delivery.
speakers: Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Bid to Build: Unified Cost Management with Autodesk Forma and the Tech Ecosystem
abstract: Cost management doesn’t happen in one phase—it spans preconstruction, risk, contracting, and field execution. In this hands-on lab, experience how Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build directly integrates with BuildingConnected Pro, TradeTapp, DocuSign, and Rhumbix to break down silos, accelerate workflows, and increase transparency for stronger cost control. You’ll explore how teams can reduce risk, accelerate buyout, and streamline contract execution through integrated workflows. You’ll also explore how field data flows back into cost management, delivering real-time visibility and enabling more-informed decisions. Walk away with practical, repeatable skills you can apply immediately to implement cost workflows across your projects.
speakers: Tyler Patton, Principal Implementation Consultant, Autodesk

title: From Budget to Final Fee: Cost Forecasting Without the Guesswork
abstract: Unlock cost forecasting by exploring the range of tools in Cost Management in Autodesk Forma Build. In this interactive lab, you’ll immerse yourself in a real-world project, learning to create accurate cash-flow forecasts, manage revenue projections, and link budgets and schedules in one seamless workflow. Guided step by step, you’ll apply the new 3-Point Fee Enhancement to compare plans, forecasts, and fee goals. You’ll walk away with practical skills to identify fee risks early and forecast contract value with confidence.
speakers: Heather Soderquist, VP, Construction Innovation, Jacobsen Construction

title: From Content to Control: Structuring MEP BIM Production with Content Catalog
abstract: Have you ever tried using Content Catalog to structure MEP content during construction stages? This session will show you how to use metadata to manage content for QA/QC and use granular search to organize it by phase and construction status. Going beyond traditional libraries, this cloud-based system treats assets as connected data, supporting coordination, production, and fabrication workflows. Learn how to reduce content search time by up to 30% and minimize rework by using Content Catalog as a control system—guiding modeling, improving coordination, and integrating automated quality process into production. You’ll gain a practical framework to implement workflows and enable faster decisions across design and fabrication teams.
speakers: Florencia Kossman, Job Captain MEP, ENG
Valentín David, Project Manager, ENG

title: From Data to Decisions: Putting AI to Work in Construction
abstract:
The AEC industry has invested heavily in BIM, cloud collaboration, fabrication technology, and connected project platforms. Yet many teams still face the same challenge: turning all that project data into clear, actionable insight.

This session explores how AI can close the gap, connecting existing project data to surface insights faster, identifying risks earlier, tracking progress more effectively, and supporting better decisions across design, fabrication, and field operations.

Beyond the technology, attendees will learn what it takes to put AI to work in real construction environments, including implementation, governance, and lessons learned. Participants will leave with a practical framework for improving project visibility, streamlining reporting, and getting more value from the data they already have.
speakers: Ralph Schoch, Technology Manager, Victaulic

title: From Design to Decision: Automating Multimodal Corridors with Civil 3D and Dynamo
abstract: Delivering a multimodal corridor requires more than geometry alone; it demands coordination across design, drainage, automation, and visualization. This session will show how ICON Engineering applied a connected approach on the 124th Avenue corridor in Thornton, Colorado. Civil 3D software served as the backbone of the design, while Dynamo, InfoDrainage, and InfraWorks software systems were integrated into a single pipeline. Dynamo automated alignments, profiles, and utility coordination tasks; stormwater design was developed and validated in InfoDrainage; and the design was brought into InfraWorks for visualization and stakeholder communication.
speakers: Jacob Marquez, CAD Manager / Project Engineer, ICON Engineering Inc
Sean Fahey, Senior Project Engineer, Shrewsberry & Associates
Elijah Shoulders, Project Engineer, ICON Engineering Inc

title: From Design to MAKE at ITT Flow Technologies: Building a Connected Digital Manufacturing Strategy
abstract: ITT Flow Technologies designs highly configurable equipment. But as with many manufacturers, the digital thread breaks as data moves from engineering to programming, production, and the shop floor. Disconnected CAD, CAM, and manufacturing systems reduce traceability and drive manual work-arounds, delays, and rework. This session will show how ITT Flow Technologies is reconnecting design and manufacturing using Inventor, Vault, and Autodesk Fusion software. We’ll review a real-world approach to creating a connected data flow across the product lifecycle. And we’ll assess digital maturity, identify high-impact opportunities, and build a phased road map that delivers early value while improving collaboration, productivity, quality, and efficiency.
speakers: Trevor Mallaber, Designer, ITT Flow Technologies
Daniel Mills, Engineering Applications Manager, ITT Flow Technologies

title: From Design to Reality: How Avnet's AI Tools Are Making Better Engineering Decisions Earlier
abstract: Product development is evolving beyond traditional CAD workflows. Join Avnet and Autodesk to see how AI-powered engineering experiences are helping engineers move from concept to manufacturable products faster while making smarter decisions earlier in the design process. Learn how Avnet's component intelligence—including real-time pricing, availability, lifecycle data, alternate part recommendations, and engineering content—integrates directly into Autodesk Fusion. Discover how AI-assisted design workflows combined with supply chain insights enable teams to evaluate feasibility, manufacturability, and sourcing tradeoffs from the start. By connecting AI-driven design with real-world component and procurement intelligence, engineering teams can reduce redesigns, improve collaboration between engineering and sourcing, and accelerate the path from idea to production-ready products.
speakers: Christopher Jackson, Vice President, Global Engineering, Avnet
Rogelio Gonzalez, GCET Apps Engineering Manager, Avnet

title: From Dirt to Data: Automating Site Design with Dynamo as a Service and Autodesk Forma
abstract: This technical deep dive will present an automated site-development workflow linking Civil 3D, Revit, Autodesk Forma Site Design, and Dynamo as a Service (DaaS). First, Civil 3D extracts the contextual data from a Forma project, analyzes grading limits, and generates back in Forma hatched “buildable pad” areas (max flat footprint without major walls/earthwork). Next, a Dynamo graph reads building program data from a spreadsheet. Then, the user selects the site boundary and pad outline in DaaS. And a Python node places buildings based on editable criteria (daylight, sun angle, wind, noise, orientation) to rapidly generate and compare options.
speakers: Aaron Coffman, Senior Architect, SSOE
Daniel Drennen, VDC Technical Leader, SSOE Group

title: From Handover Chaos to Operational Certainty: What Changes When Data Becomes Usable
abstract: Infrastructure owners often face a gap between project delivery and operations, where asset data exists but is fragmented, inaccessible, and effectively invisible to operations teams. This leads to uncertainty, rework, and delayed readiness. While many approaches focus on how digital twins are built, this session will focus on what changes for operations once data becomes visible and usable. Through a real-world case from Lantis, learn how Autodesk Tandem software enables operational certainty from day one, reducing handover rework by roughly 30% and accelerating maintenance readiness by up to six months.
speakers: Cristina Ispas, BIM Lead, Beheersmaatschappij Antwerpen Mobiel
Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: From Ideas to Outcomes with Autodesk Platform Services
abstract:
AI is changing how people build with Autodesk Platform Services (APS). Instead of learning APIs, stitching together integrations, and manually orchestrating workflows, you'll now be able to describe the outcome you want and let APS find, connect, and execute the capabilities needed to achieve it.
See how new AI-powered experiences are making APS more approachable for everyone - from experienced developers to Design and Make professionals who have never built with APS before. Learn how APS works with the AI interface of your choice, helping turn natural language into governed, repeatable workflows built on trusted Design and Make data and Autodesk capabilities. Whether you're new to APS or already building with it, you'll leave with a clear understanding of how AI is transforming the APS experience and how you can use it to deliver business outcomes faster, with greater consistency and at scale.
speakers: Rami Kuret, Product Manager, Autodesk
Vasini Govindarajan, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk
Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: From Innovyze to Autodesk Tandem: Digital Twins and AI for Climate‑Resilient Water Infrastructure
abstract: Water infrastructure is entering a decisive decade. In 2026, utilities face climate volatility, aging assets, regulatory pressure, and rising expectations for resilient, transparent service. Traditional approaches based on static hydraulic models and reactive operations are no longer sufficient. This keynote will explore how connected digital twins and AI are reshaping water infrastructure across the full lifecycle—from planning and design to operations and maintenance. It will present a practical workflow showing how Innovyze modeling outputs evolve into a live operational digital twin in Autodesk Tandem software, enabling continuity from design to asset maintenance, and supporting predictive, risk‑based decision making.
speakers: Priyanka Talkal, Associate-Water, WSP
Parthasarathi Mishra, Associate, WSP Global

title: From Model to Trust: Making BIM Reliable for Construction
abstract: Digital delivery only works when models are reliable enough to build from. Yet many teams still struggle with trust, alignment, and inconsistency expectations. This session will share lessons from a large-scale structural project where model reliance became critical during the transition from design to construction. We’ll walk through what worked, what didn't, and how expectations shifted across architects and contractors. You’ll leave with a practical framework to improve model reliability and reduce coordination risk.
speakers: Debora Machado, BIM Manager, Walter P Moore
Edward Leonard, Senior Technical Modeler II, Walter P. Moore
Jesse Young, BIM Integration Manager, Walter P Moore

title: From Office Data to Smarter Decisions: Digital Twins for Workplace Optimization
abstract: Office relocations are often driven by assumptions rather than data, leading to inefficient space use, unnecessary asset procurement, and missed energy optimization opportunities. This session will present a real-world case study from BDP showing how digital twins created with Autodesk Tandem software connect occupancy, energy, and asset data to drive smarter workplace decisions. By making existing data visible and usable, the team avoided £600,000 in furniture spend, enabled reuse of 71% of assets, and reduced required floor area by 27%. Learn how to integrate sensor data, structure asset information, and apply digital twin insights to reduce cost, improve sustainability, and optimize real estate decisions.
speakers: Elliott Crossley, Director Digital Delivery, BDP
Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: From Outsourced to In-House: How Product Teams Are Rebuilding Manufacturing with Autodesk Fusion
abstract: Offshore manufacturing used to be the cheapest option … until it wasn’t. As shipping costs rose by more than 200%, offshore rework rates soared three to five times higher, and lead times stretched by up to 30%, many manufacturers started to rethink offshoring and consider bringing production closer to home. This class will show how Autodesk Fusion software helps teams address the often-overlooked costs of offshoring by connecting design and manufacturing workflows in one platform. Through practical examples, you’ll see how Fusion reduces rework, improves process control, speeds iteration, and streamlines computer numerical control (CNC) programming to support more-agile and efficient in-house production.
speakers: Christopher Gill, Technical Sales Specialist, Fusion, Autodesk

title: From Pilot to Portfolio: Scaling Digital Twins Across a University Campus
abstract: Many digital twin initiatives succeed at the pilot stage but fail to scale across portfolios. This session will present a real-world case from the University of Exeter, showing how a structured facility template enabled digital twins to scale across four buildings—covering both new build and retrofit projects. By standardizing asset data and workflows, the team reduced handover activation effort by 60% to 70%, enabled CAFM-ready asset activation within two to three days, and improved access to operational data by 40%. Learn how to create reusable templates and governance models to scale digital twins across campuses and capital programs.
speakers: Leejo Johney, Head of Digital Estate, University of Exeter
Siva Koppula, Customer Success Manager, Autodesk

title: From Pilot to Practice: How Lake Flato Evaluates and Scales New Tools
abstract: Many firm leaders can name the software tools they bought last year. Fewer can say which ones are still in use. Dan Stine, Director of Design Technology at Lake Flato, walks through how his team decides what tools are worth evaluating, what they measure during a pilot to know whether a new tool is achieving its objectives, and what it takes to roll out a tool firmwide, including the parts that did not go as planned. He is joined by Ross Wagner, a former architect and Head of Product Strategy at Pirros, on the patterns that separate the rollouts that take hold from the ones that fall out of use after a few months. Attendees will learn how industry-leading firms evaluate the ROI of new software and incorporate new technology into existing workflows.
speakers: Daniel Stine, Director of Design Technology, Lake Flato
Ross Wagner, Head of Strategy, Pirros

title: From Plan to Pour: Aurigo Primus Plan and Autodesk Forma for Asset Owners
abstract: Bridge the gap between capital planning and project execution. Led by Aurigo's director of product, this technical deep dive will explore Primus Plan and its powerful integration with Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). We’ll showcase our AI-powered what-if scenario planning, demonstrating how to optimize multi-year capital portfolios before pushing them to downstream construction management. Walk through the technical architecture and data flows that move infrastructure projects from early-stage planning straight into execution within Autodesk Forma. Learn how to eliminate data silos, maximize funding, and maintain total visibility across the entire project lifecycle.
speakers: Johann Potgieter,  Director of Product, Aurigo Software Technology

title: From Preparation to Production in Autodesk Fusion: Serial Additive Manufacturing for Automotive and Aerospace
abstract: This session will focus on serial additive manufacturing using Autodesk Fusion software, with practical insights into designing and producing functional parts. We’ll cover real-world use of FDM and SLA technologies, including workflows with UltiMaker and Formlabs printers, and working with high-performance, flame-retardant, and rigid materials. Key topics will include defining proper tolerances and clearances, optimizing designs for repeatable production, and preparing parts for testing and certification requirements. Special attention will be given to early-stage design decisions—including integration of assembly fixtures and quality control features—considering material behavior and process limitations.
speakers: Vasyl Tymoshchuk, Project Manager, Yamaha Motors Europe
Dmytro Mukhin

title: From Prompt to Production: Designing Furniture at the Speed of AI with Autodesk Fusion
abstract: Designing and manufacturing furniture often relies on disconnected tools and repetitive work. This session will explain how to create a connected, end-to-end workflow using the Autodesk Fusion platform. Starting from simple prompts, Autodesk Assistant accelerates design and enables fast creation of parametric furniture models. This workflow will show how models are refined for engineering, prepared for manufacturing with integrated CAM tools, and transferred to production using Autodesk Fusion Operations software—while Autodesk Fusion Manage ensures process and data continuity from request to delivery. It will also highlight how design intent is preserved and how a single data environment reduces errors.
speakers: Melike Ozdemir, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Quantity to Cost: Streamline Takeoff-to-Estimate Workflows with Autodesk Preconstruction
abstract: Preconstruction teams often lose time when takeoff, pricing, and estimate updates are managed across disconnected processes. Manual quantity transfers, revision checks, and pricing adjustments can create inefficiencies, rework, and risk. In this hands-on lab, you’ll work through a connected Autodesk preconstruction workflow from 2D and 3D takeoff to estimate generation and cost refinement. You’ll learn how to capture quantities, apply formulas, push results into Estimate, manage updates, and use libraries, templates, and cost markups to standardize your process. By the end of the class, you’ll be able to create a more consistent, scalable process for turning quantities into cost insights with greater speed and confidence.
speakers: Dhruvesh Shah, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
Ovais Mattoo, Principal Technical Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Reality to Production: ReCap Mesh Workflows and Model Coordination at Porsche
abstract: Learn how Porsche uses ReCap software, mesh extraction, and Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to create accurate “last stand” models of production factories before retooling. In high-cost environments where production downtime must be minimized, existing Revit models of assembly lines are compared with current as-built conditions using lightweight, segmented meshes. This enables precise adjustments or extensions of production lines with reduced risk. This session will cover mesh generation, semantic segmentation, and integration into Model Coordination, with real project insights and best practices for large-scale manufacturing environments.
speakers: Anastasia Thoma, Sr Solution Architect, Autodesk

title: From Single Client to Multi-Tenant: Forma Data Management Architecture for APS App Store Success
abstract: When an independent software vendor (ISV) submits an app to the Autodesk App Store with a single Client ID, all customers share identical credentials—creating data leakage risks. This session will introduce the "robot-per-tenant" pattern: provisioning unique robot email addresses per customer (for example, acme-mep-robot@clientid.com), which ensures token scope isolation at the identity level. We'll cover onboarding flows, three-legged OAuth (3LO) token management scoped per tenant, Hub/Project membership automation, and audit trail design. Even application logic errors cannot breach tenant boundaries. Drawing from production deployments with Forma Data Management and Forma Admin APIs, learn how to scale from 10 to 1,000 tenants.
speakers: Matt Mason, Director, Software Development, IMAGINiT Technologies
Michael Beale, SWE, AWS

title: From Sketch to Toolpath: Reducing Design-to-Manufacturing Time Using Connected Autodesk Workflows
abstract: Disconnected workflows between 2D design, 3D modeling, and manufacturing often lead to delays and reduced productivity. This session will demonstrate how to connect AutoCAD, Inventor, and Autodesk Fusion software into a seamless design-to-manufacturing workflow, supported by cloud platforms like Autodesk Desktop Connector for data management and collaboration. Learn how to transform 2D drawings into parametric models and generate computer numerical control (CNC) toolpaths while maintaining data continuity. Through real-world examples, discover how connected workflows reduce errors, minimize rework, and accelerate delivery from design to production.
speakers: Sagar G S, Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk
Chaitanya Belsare, Sr Associate, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: From Source to Farm: Digital Twins for End-to-End Irrigation with Autodesk Water Infrastructure
abstract: Irrigation systems are often managed in silos: Reservoirs, canals, and farm distribution lack integrated visibility, leading to inefficiencies and water losses. This session will demonstrate how Autodesk water infrastructure solutions can create a connected, data-driven irrigation system. InfoWorks ICM is used to model river basins and canal hydraulics, while InfoWorks WS Pro simulates pressurized distribution networks. InfoAsset Manager structures irrigation assets for seamless integration, and Info360 Insight enables real-time monitoring and operational decisions. In this session, you will learn practical workflows to improve water allocation, reduce losses, and enable demand-based irrigation using simulation, asset intelligence, and analytics.
speakers: Rajeshwari Mynepalli, Technical Specialist, Water, Autodesk
Ayyer Sadal, Assistant Manager, Product Sales, CSTech AI

title: From Superpowers to Payoff: Turning MCPs into Real Business Value in Construction
abstract: In this session, we share how Heijmans and Autodesk moved MCPs from innovation pilots to real business value in the construction industry. After 1.5 years of working with Autodesk Model Context Protocol (MCP), Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), and custom MCP clients, we focus on what it takes to scale MCPs in daily workflows. Attendees will learn how we combined custom-built and off‑the‑shelf MCP servers to reduce administrative tasks, connect data across systems, and support engineers and site teams with a personal assistant (JARVIS). We’ll discuss architectural decisions, key challenges, lessons learned, and show live examples of MCPs delivering measurable value on real projects.
speakers: Dustin Bolte, Senior Consultant Informationmanagement, Heijmans
Piotr Kruczkowski, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk

title: From Sustainability Intent to Spatial Decisions: Integrating Environmental Performance into Autodesk Forma
abstract: The future of sustainable design isn't about creating more data - it's about transforming fragmented information into connected intelligence that helps teams make better decisions, earlier. In this panel discussion, leaders from VINCI Construction and Autodesk will explore how AI, digital platforms, and connected workflows are helping project teams access the right data, in the right context, at the right time. Drawing on major infrastructure and building projects, biodiversity research, and digital transformation initiatives, the panel will examine how project requirements, environmental intelligence, and organizational knowledge can be brought together into one layered system to inform design decisions from the earliest stages of a project.
speakers: Marta Bouchard, Dir., Sustainability Solutions, Autodesk
Armelle Langlois, Head of Sustainable Performance, VINCI Construction

title: From Vague to Precise: Write AI Prompts That Actually Work in AutoCAD and Civil 3D
abstract: Discover how better prompts can transform the way you work with Autodesk Assistant in AutoCAD and Civil 3D software. The feature just landed as a tech preview, but users who get value from it share one thing: They know how to ask. Most people type something vague, get a poor result, and move on. As the product team behind this experience, we’ve seen where the gaps are—ambiguous scope, missing context, overly broad requests. This session will use live before/after demos to show you how prompts with clear tasks, contexts, and constraints turn frustrating results into reliable outcomes for workflows like standards checks, counts, queries, and style changes. Whether you’re a drafter or CAD manager, you’ll leave with a prompt template library your team can adopt right away.
speakers: Stella Zhou, Senior Experience Designer, Autodesk
James(Jinan) Xue, Principal Software Tester, QA, Autodesk

title: Fusion + Naya: End-to-End Workflow for Physical Products
abstract: The next decade of physical product design will be defined by what teams choose to automate. Modern design tools should not just make things happen faster. They should free teams to focus on taste-making, creation, and human intuition, while quietly handling the repetitive work no one wants to do. This session explores how end-to-end product workflows, powered by AI and human collaboration, are enabling teams to design faster, more efficiently, and better for the world. See how Autodesk Fusion and Naya complement each other across the full design process, from first concept to manufacturing, and walk away with a strategic view of how Fusion and Naya enable a better design process, and where the next year of AI and workflow is heading.
speakers: Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio
David Gerber, VP of Business Development and Partnerships, Naya Studio
Saad Rajan, CEO & Co-founder, Naya Studio

title: Get certified at AU!
abstract:
Turn your AU 2026 experience into recognition you can use right away. Complimentary onsite Autodesk certification testing gives eligible* attendees the opportunity to validate their expertise, showcase real-world skills, and earn an industry-recognized digital credential.

 

Whether you're looking to advance your career, strengthen your team's capabilities, or set yourself apart from the competition, certification is a meaningful way to invest in your future.

	Autodesk Certified Professional in Revit for Structural Design
	Autodesk Certified Professional in BIM Management for Building Design

title: Get the Water to the Pond: Use Drainage Design and Analysis in Civil 3D
abstract: In this session, we’ll walk through what you need to perform a pipe-to-pond drainage study in Civil 3D software, beginning to end. If you have to pipe the stormwater to the proposed detention pond or get it there by overland channel, you’ll see what it takes to create the study. This session will be fast and furious, but you’ll leave with the step-by-step process to perform the design. Hope to see you there!
speakers: John Sayre, Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Infrastructure Products, Autodesk
Charlie Ogden, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk
Prince Trinidad-Rhodius, Technical Marketing Manager, Water, Autodesk

title: HKS Is Making Autodesk Data Exchanges Real at Stadium Scale
abstract: Autodesk data exchanges only create value when exchange structure, naming, versioning, and downstream use are governed as part of delivery. In this technical deep dive, HKS will show how selective exchange logic, federated model handling, metadata preservation, validation, and stadium-scale export optimization support world-class facade delivery. You’ll leave with a production-minded framework for moving from oversized handoffs to controlled, traceable, downstream-ready exchange workflows.
speakers: Brian Nickel, Firmwide Practice Technology Specialist II, HKS Inc.
Bear Pope, Digital Practice Leader, HKS
Melvin Williams, Digital Practice Leader - Venues, HKS, Inc.

title: How Digital Preservation Is Securing Fallingwater's Future
abstract: Justin Gunther, Vice President and Director of Fallingwater, Touf Hassoun, President & CEO of CASE Technologies, and Mark Dietrick, Director of Services at CASE Technologies, join the Digital Builder podcast to discuss how one of the world's most iconic buildings is being digitally documented and preserved. The conversation explores the intersection of historic stewardship and emerging technology, and what the Fallingwater project reveals about the future of managing, understanding, and protecting important built assets.

title: IFC’d Around and Found Out: Model-Based Quantity Takeoffs for Linear Civil Projects
abstract: Model-based takeoff for linear civil projects sounds great, until Civil 3D-to-IFC exports leave out the quantities and metadata needed to actually price the work. In this session, Kyle Field and Josh Boardman from ISL Engineering will show how they used Civil 3D, Dynamo, and Autodesk Forma Takeoff software to bridge that gap. You will see how custom Civil 3D property sets can turn 3D solids into takeoff-ready bid items by embedding missing length and area data, carrying standardized bid item information, and making model objects easier to isolate and quantify. The result is a more scalable workflow with less retracing, stronger QA/QC, and cleaner estimating outputs for linear civil projects.
speakers: Kyle Field, Construction Technology Lead, ISL Engineering and Land Services
Joshua Boardman, CAD Management Specialist, ISL Engineering

title: iLogic in Practice: A Panel of Experts on Rule Management and Automation Excellence
abstract: Join experienced contributors from the Autodesk Community Inventor Customization forum as they compare their real-world approaches to organizing and managing iLogic rules. This panel is designed for intermediate-to-advanced Inventor users and CAD managers who want to take their iLogic implementations to the next level. Panelists will share their real-world insights on internal versus external rules, the advantages of maintaining a centralized iLogic rule library, and proven approaches for structuring rule logic across parts and assemblies. The discussion will also tackle the pros and cons of event triggers and practical techniques for controlling rule execution more effectively.
speakers: Jerry Berns, Design Technology Specialist, Newell Machinery Co.
Brandon Bibelhauser, Mechanical Engineer/Software Developer, FORTNA
Tiffany Hayden, Application Developer, KETIV Technologies Inc.
Paul Munford, Principal Technical Onboarding Architect - D&M, Autodesk
Curtis Waguespack, Design Automation Solutions Architect, Topper Industries

title: Industrialized Construction at Scale: Data-Driven Sustainability for Modular Systems
abstract: How can industrialized construction, intelligent data, and integrated workflows turn sustainability from a reporting burden into a scalable design strategy? In this session for architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) leaders and delivery teams, Max Bögl Group will share how one company manages the value chain—from raw material sourcing and design to off-site production, delivery, assembly, and maintenance—to deliver modular buildings and bridge systems with measurable sustainability outcomes. As we use projects from Germany and the Netherlands, you’ll see how standardized, parametric products, connected models, and automated assessments help teams compare options faster, respond to strict European requirements, and build the data foundation for future AI-supported design decisions.
speakers: Mergim Hoti, BIM Specialist, Max Bögl Nederland B.V.

title: Industrialized Revit: How We Turned Tilt-Up and Precast into a Productized Delivery System
abstract: Industrialized construction relies on repeatable systems, not hero modeling. In this session, we’ll show how Hermosillo applied that mindset to productize Revit delivery for tilt-up and precast projects. By combining standards, clearly defined deliverables, and end-user involvement, a core innovation team of designers (with no prior programming experience) used AI-assisted workflows, Dynamo, and the Revit API to build production-ready automation. The result: a system capable of generating hundreds of views, sheets, facades, and renders in under 50 minutes, reducing documentation time by over 90% and compressing weeks of work into hours. You’ll leave with a blueprint to replicate this approach and scale automation across your projects.
speakers: Josue Balderrama, Core Innovation Lead, Grupo Hermosillo
Pedro Alejandro Bermea Leynes, CORE Innovation Specialist, Grupo Hermosillo

title: Information Management Strategies at the World’s Busiest Airport
abstract: Let’s talk about implementing a comprehensive information management strategy as it relates to BIM, digital twins, and asset data. In this session, you’ll hear about the new information management strategy created for the Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) Planning and Development department.
speakers: Chris Harman, BIM Program Lead, WSP / ATLNext

title: Informed Design API from Autodesk in Action: Real Workflows with Gaylor Electric
abstract: In this session, Gaylor Electric, a leading US electrical contractor, will share how it’s using the Informed Design API as part of its prefabrication and project delivery workflow. The team uses Informed Design to rapidly configure and generate design outputs early in the project lifecycle, enabling estimation, coordination, and planning before full project setup. You’ll see how these workflows work in practice and how configurable design approaches can support more-scalable project delivery.
speakers: Jack Atkinson, Engineering Manager, Gaylor Electric, Inc
James Cotter, Production Innovation Center Manager, Gaylor Electric, Inc

title: Innovators Stage | From Reality Capture to BIM: Preserving Fallingwater with Autodesk—Panel Discussion
abstract: Explore how one of the world’s most iconic buildings—Fallingwater—is being preserved for the next century using Autodesk technology. This session will walk through an end-to-end digital preservation workflow—from reality capture using LiDAR, drones, and photogrammetry to BIM development in Revit and collaboration in Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Learn how integrated data enables deeper insight, supports conservation decisions, and lays the foundation for digital twins. Discover how teams are transforming heritage stewardship through connected workflows, innovation, and scalable digital strategies.
speakers: Mark Dietrick, Director of Services, Case Technologies
Justin Gunther, Director of Fallingwater, Fallingwater
Touf Hassoun, President/CEO, Case Technologies
Dan Lohmeyer, VP, AutoCAD, Building, and Infrastructure (ABI) Solutions, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage | I'll Take "Clash Detected" for 400: An AECO Jeopardy Challenge
abstract: Think you know architecture, engineering, construction, and operations (AECO) workflows? Prove it. In this Jeopardy-style session, architects, engineers, contractors, and BIM managers will go head to head across categories like "Clash Detected," "Connect the Platforms," "Coordination Gone Wrong," and "Who Owns the Data?" Audience members will compete live for a prize. And everyone will walk away with sharper cross-discipline instincts and a better understanding of where handoffs break down—and how integrated workflows fix them. Equal parts fun and educational, this session will turn real workflow pain points into a room full of engaged, competitive learners.
speakers: Tanmay Bhalerao, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk
Fabiane Amorim, Sr Field Marketing Manager, AMER AECO, Autodesk
Erica Bowman, Account Based Marketing Manager, Autodesk

speakers: Fabiane Amorim, Sr Field Marketing Manager, AMER AECO, Autodesk
Erica Bowman, Account Based Marketing Manager, Autodesk
Tanmay Bhalerao, Sr Account Technical Lead, Autodesk

title: Innovators Stage | Whose Model Is It Anyway? (Comedy Show)
abstract: Step into the hilarious side of CAD and BIM in this 30-minute comedy show! Hear stories of mysterious warnings, impossible client requests, chaotic models, and the kinds of design mishaps that make you laugh, wince, and nod in recognition. Packed with jokes, relatable chaos, and surprise twists, this show will celebrate the absurd, unpredictable, and sometimes ridiculous moments that happen behind every model. Whether you’re a designer, engineer, or project manager, you’ll leave entertained—and maybe even inspired to look at your own files a little differently.
speakers: Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.
Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek
Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD
Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+
Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk

Packed with jokes, relatable chaos, and surprise twists, this show will celebrate the absurd, unpredictable, and sometimes ridiculous moments that happen behind every model.
