speakers: Dzan Ta, Autodesk Technical Specialist, Symetri
Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.
Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek
Steven Bloomer, BIM & Information Management Lead, GHD
Alex Eckhart, Principal Marketing Specialist, Autodesk
Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+

title: Integrated Real-Time MIDP Using Reviews in Autodesk Forma and Autodesk Platform Services
abstract: Keeping a Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP) accurate on live projects is one of the biggest challenges for BIM managers and project managers. Issuing incomplete or unreviewed deliverables puts contracts at risk. In this class, we’ll show how Autodesk Platform Services Webhooks and the Reviews tool in Autodesk Forma transform the MIDP into a live system that validates deliverable metadata against information requirements and confirms review status before submission. Using real project examples and proven metrics, we’ll show how this ensures 100% compliance with contractual deliverables, eliminates manual tracking, and mitigates the risk of noncompliant submissions. Join us to learn how to build a QA/QC system that keeps your MIDP accurate, connected, and audit ready.
speakers: Mateusz Lukasiewicz, Associate Director - Digital Technology, KEO International Consultants

title: Integrating Company Policies in Autodesk Assistant: AI-Driven Governance and Automation in Autodesk Forma
abstract: Explore how Arcadis and Autodesk embedded Arcadis policies and standards into Autodesk Assistant as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). This integration delivers tailored, policy-driven responses for cross-project maturity checks, quality control, and workload distribution. Learn how Autodesk Assistant proactively triggers issue creation and review workflows aligned with Arcadis governance, while seamlessly interacting with external systems to generate support desk tickets and schedule Microsoft Outlook meetings. Discover the architecture, AI insights, and automation patterns enabling smarter, policy-compliant project delivery at scale—improving compliance, reducing manual oversight by 40%, and doubling cross-region worksharing efficiency.
speakers: Rodney Dsilva, Principal Solution Architect, Autodesk
Mark Kroezen, Senior Consultant (BIM Manager), Arcadis Nederland B.V.
Freek Matheij, Global AI Platform Director, Arcadis

title: Integration Workflows in a Stadium—Autodesk Forma As a Communication Bridge
abstract: GIA successfully delivered the new Oaxaca Warriors baseball stadium, covering 40,934 square meters, in just 12 months using BIM methodology and the integration of Autodesk Forma into office and field workflows. Faced with a tight 12-month deadline, complex coordination, and a large volume of project data, the team adopted a common data environment (CDE) to centralize information and optimize collaboration between the office and the field. This digital approach allowed for process automation, improved traceability, and optimized real-time decision making. The result was a high-quality project delivered on time, demonstrating how cloud platforms are transforming efficiency and collaboration in Mexico’s construction industry.
speakers: Oscar Uriel Hernandez, BIM Specialist, GIA

title: International Perspectives on Open Standards and Adoption
abstract: This session explores the critical role of open standards in accelerating digital transformation across the global AECOO industry. As the demand for interoperability grows, the collaboration between buildingSMART International and Autodesk becomes a cornerstone for seamless data exchange and sustainable project delivery. Featuring a panel of buildingSMART Chapter leaders and Autodesk executives, we will dive into regional adoption trends, the evolution of open standards, and real-world strategies for implementing openBIM. Attendees will gain insights into how open standards drive efficiency, support regulatory compliance, and empower stakeholders to own their data.
speakers: ERIC BUGEJA, Chair / Director, buildingSMART Australasia/International
Calvin Kam, CEO / Chapter President, SBI / buildingSMART USA
Claudia Cozzitorto, Director of Digital Practice, KPMB Architects
Jugal Makwana, Senior Business Development Executive, Autodesk
Najib Najib, Director, Head of Digital Delivery / Vice Chair, JESA /  buildingSMART Morocco

title: I Shall Call You C3PO: A Guide to Using Autodesk Assistant for Revit As Your Production Sidekick
abstract: With today’s AI tools, science fiction truly meets reality. We can all have a handy “droid” by our side. But instead of calling it Siri, Claude, or Gemini, we can call it: C3PO! Can Autodesk Assistant for Revit tell you the odds of outrunning an Imperial Star Destroyer? Perhaps not. But it can tell you how many chairs are in an auditorium or the size of a room, or it can even create a floor plan and apply a view template. Want advice on what kind of space to put in an empty retail unit? It can do that, but don't ask it to draw the layout—that's on you! In this lab, we'll explore this new tool that brings AI directly into your Revit workspace. And if you want to call it by everyone's favorite droid name, it probably won't mind.
speakers: Kimberly Fuhrman-Jones, Community Manager, Autodesk
Paul Aubin, Author/Consultant, Paul F Aubin Consulting Services, Inc.
Harlan Brumm, Director, Product Management, Revit Core Capabilities & Collaboration Services, Autodesk

title: Leakage Modeling Workflows for Calibrating Water Distribution Models
abstract: Water utilities increasingly rely on hydraulic models to improve water-loss management. Yet, explicitly representing real losses remains a common challenge. This session will present a practical, repeatable workflow for modeling leakage using InfoWater Pro software. You will learn how to go beyond traditional water-loss representations and incorporate system pressures, SCADA data, and district metered areas into calibrated models to quantify and spatially allocate real losses. We’ll demonstrate how pressure-dependent leakage formulations can improve calibration accuracy and identify high-leakage zones. Real-world examples will show how, when calibrated, these models support operational decision making, targeted leak detection, and capital planning.
speakers: Chris Adams, engineer, Arcadis
Ben Chenevey, Principal Water Engineer, Arcadis
Nathan Gerdts, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Learn How to Use Autodesk Forma Building Design by Recreating a Modernist Classic Design
abstract: This hands-on lab will teach a repeatable early-stage design workflow using Autodesk Forma Building Design through a controlled case study of a famous, modernist, residential icon. Using a shared reference model reduces project complexity and allows participants to focus on workflow, not design invention. Participants move from site context and massing to environmental analysis and iteration—then to facade and plan design options evaluated on daylight and solar performance, orientation, and layout design. The workflow supports continuity into Revit software, reducing rework and improving coordination.
speakers: Jesper Staahl, Senior Technical Marketing Manager, Forma, Autodesk
Arne Bjelland, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: "Level 4" Live "What-If" Digital Twins for Manufacturing Using FlexSim
abstract: Flex has more than 100 facilities in more than 30 countries worldwide, manufacturing a wide range of products across seven different categories. To extend our forecasting capabilities, Flex GISE (global industrial and system engineering) simulation teams developed a web-based comprehensive (Level 4) digital twin application that users can adapt to support different types of manufacturing. The tool combines the FlexSim web server and advanced data-acquisition capabilities to deliver accurate, real-time forecasting and scenario-based decision support. It combines live production data with simulation, enabling users—even those with limited simulation expertise—to perform “what-if” analyses through an intuitive interface.
speakers: Gergely Popovics, Simulation Engineering Manager, Flex Ltd.
Diana Ceballos, Simulation Engineering Manager, Flex

title: Link It Up: Using the Electromechanical Link Between AutoCAD Electrical and Inventor
abstract: Curious about how to link your schematics in AutoCAD Electrical software to your models in Inventor software? Get an understanding of the functionality that links these two programs together. This session will cover the key elements you’ll need to know to bridge your design between AutoCAD Electrical and Inventor.
speakers: Bryan Fields, Subject Matter Expert, IMAGINiT

title: Lunch
abstract: Midday is made for good food and good company. Join fellow attendees for lunch and enjoy a relaxed break before the afternoon sessions begin.

title: Maximizing Autodesk Platform Services Value: Smarter Usage, Greater Control, AI-Ready Scale
abstract: Autodesk Platform Services continues to evolve to better support how customers build, scale, and optimize applications in an increasingly AI-driven world. APIs and Model Context Protocols (MCPs) are becoming foundational to agentic AI workflows, making it more important than ever to understand and optimize Autodesk Platform Services use. This session will highlight the features Autodesk Platform Services is building to help you make the most of cloud APIs and MCPs, whether developing directly on Autodesk Platform Services or integrating through third-party applications. You’ll also see new capabilities that provide greater visibility and control, including Autodesk Platform Services reporting, cost management tools, and AI-powered usage prediction through Autodesk Assistant. Join us to learn how to scale with confidence and maximize value from Autodesk Platform Services.
speakers: Dwanill Mehta, Product Manager, Autodesk

title: MCP on the Autodesk Platform: Three Production Servers Across the Full Stack
abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the layer that lets AI agents access Autodesk tools, data, and APIs through a standardized interface. The firms building this infrastructure today will define the standard—not just use it. This session will go deep on three production MCP servers: revitDeploymentMCP (CI/CD pipeline as four AI-callable tools), a Dynamo MCP server (exposing Dynamo scripts for AI orchestration), and an Autodesk Platform Services Data Pipeline server (chaining the Model Derivative API, the Data Management API, and the Design Automation API without auth failures or silent webhook drops). Each server is examined at the architecture, implementation, and deployment levels. You’ll receive complete implementation patterns for all three.
speakers: Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap
Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap

title: Measuring Perceptions of Trust: How to Turn Trust into Tangible Results
abstract: In this interactive session, you’ll learn how to apply to your organization some frameworks for measuring and building trust. You’ll learn strategies for assessing trust across customer and employee experiences, and you’ll learn how to identify gaps and prioritize high-impact opportunities. Through guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll map trust drivers—capability, reliability, transparency, and humanity—to key workflows, products, and culture. The session will conclude with a practical action plan to build trust, improve outcomes, and drive measurable business results.
speakers: Kate Adam, Director, Customer Trust & Engagement, Autodesk
Mariluz Blandon, Director, Global Belonging Strategy​, Autodesk

title: Meet Rhumbix: Connecting your Field-to-Finance Workflows
abstract: Join the Rhumbix team to discover how connected field and finance workflows can help construction teams turn jobsite activity into actionable insights. In this session, we’ll demo how Rhumbix streamlines the capture of labor, time, and production data from the field and connects it to downstream cost and financial workflows. And, share how better connections between the field and office can reduce manual processes and improve visibility into project performance.

title: Megaproject Scheduling Reimagined: How Boldt Aligns Field and Office with Outbuild and Autodesk Forma
abstract: Megaprojects don't just require more resources. They require a fundamentally different approach to planning, communication, and accountability. When hundreds of trades converge on a single site over years of construction, the gap between the schedule on paper and the field can compound into costly delays. Klas Berghede (VP of production and innovation at Boldt) and Michael Wong (head of customer success at Outbuild) share how Boldt integrated Outbuild with Autodesk Forma to bring structure, real-time visibility, and field alignment to Boldt’s most complex projects, connecting master schedules with weekly lookaheads and field data with the office to drive faster, more confident decisions at scale.
speakers: Mike Wong, VP of Customer Success, Outbuild
Klas Berghede, VP Production & Innovation, Boldt

title: MEP Content Editor: Product Updates and Live Demos
abstract: Join this session to explore the latest updates to the MEP Content Editor and see how they can enhance your fabrication workflows. We’ll walk through new features, improvements, and real-world applications, followed by live demonstrations that showcase how to efficiently create, modify, and manage fabrication content. In addition, we’ll cover how fabrication content connects with Revit models through cloud-based workflows, including syncing between centralized cloud environments and desktop fabrication databases. Whether you're maintaining a database or building content from scratch, this session will provide practical insights to help you work smarter and more effectively.
speakers: Louie Mdanat, Solutions Consultant II, ARKANCE
Craig Farish, Principal Product Owner, Autodesk

title: MEP Early, Not Late: Using Autodesk Forma, Revit Systems, and AI to Influence Design Before It’s Locked
abstract: Autodesk Forma Site Design isn’t just for architects. This session will show how MEP engineers can use Forma Site Design analytics to influence early-stage design, and carry design intent into Revit MEP through structured data and AI-assisted evaluation. Instead of reacting to fixed architectural geometry, MEP teams use Forma Site Design to inform early massing, orientation, and program decisions. We’ll use real project examples to demonstrate how early metrics such as area, volume, and orientation are interpreted from an MEP perspective and translated into system assumptions that feed Revit MEP workflows. AI-driven analysis supports option comparison, capacity estimation, and risk identification, resulting in fewer late redesigns and earlier MEP ownership of decisions.
speakers: Dagmara Romaniak, Architect Design Automation & BIM Specialist, Jacobs
Dawid Szczerba, BIM & Design Automation Specialist, Jacobs

title: Miami Dade InfoWorks ICM Model and Master Plan
abstract: As part of the Miami-Dade County Water and Sewer Department (WASD) Integrated Master Plan, Hazen calibrated one of the largest and most hydraulically complex wastewater models developed in InfoWorks ICM. It represented 1,038 pump stations, 3,200 miles of gravity sewer, and 980 miles of force main conveying approximately 310 MGD to three regional wastewater treatment plants that serve more than 2.3 million residents. The effort included long-term simulation and calibration using the InfoWorks ICM Ground Infiltration Model (GIM) to represent groundwater influence, detailed pump station simulation and verification, Ruby-script-based QA/QC and RDII calculations, and the use of the InfoWorks ICM model to simulate wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) hydraulics as part of an integrated system evaluation.
speakers: Ethan Hypes, Senior Principal Engineer, Hazen and Sawyer
Dimitry Lebedev, Senior Associate, Hazen and Sawyer

title: Modular Data Center: Innovation and Performance with a Connected Workflow Powered by Autodesk
abstract: In this session, we’ll explore the challenges and strategic solutions involved in the transition of the Modular Data Center from Dassault SolidWorks to Inventor software, along with the implementation of Vault PLM software and integration with Revit and Autodesk Forma. This change required us to overcome technical and operational obstacles, including compatibility with legacy data, migration of custom properties, and user adoption. We’ll demonstrate how we addressed these challenges and present the gains in performance and efficiency, highlighting the advantages of a connected workflow in delivering complex projects.
speakers: Carlos Silva, Mechanical Engineer, Modular Data Centers
Paulo Santos, Head of Design and Manufacturing, NTI Brazil

title: Naya AI and Autodesk Fusion for Physical Product Development: Estimation, Workflow, and Sustainability
abstract:
Naya is an AI Product Development Platform for physical goods, from footwear to furniture, working with MillerKnoll, Adidas, Google, and hundreds of other brands. Naya connects to Autodesk Fusion.
Attendees will learn how Naya Estimation AI helps teams determine manufacturing cost within minutes instead of weeks from a Fusion model, Sketch, BOM, drawing, or CAD, move quicker through product development, negotiate better, and get more products to market at target price. With features for value engineering and scenario planning, teams can make more informed design decisions.
Attendees will also see how, from the same Sketch, BOM, drawing, or CAD, Sustainability AI generates a full environmental footprint in minutes: carbon, water, energy, and plastics, so teams can weigh trade-offs before committing to production.
Workflow AI brings briefs, BOMs, CAD, drawings, and more into one place so teams move faster, maintain accountability, and unlock greater creative potential.
speakers: David Gerber, VP of Business Development and Partnerships, Naya Studio
Saad Rajan, CEO & Co-founder, Naya Studio
Vivek Haligeri Veerana, CTO & Chief of AI, Naya Studio

title: Next-Gen Rebar in Revit 2027: Bridges and Buildings
abstract: This hands-on lab will introduce the next-generation rebar workflows in Revit 2027 software, focusing on placement, editing, and validating reinforcement in 2D and 3D views. The class will use practical exercises to address real-world situations, including bridge components and standard building structures. It will show how to model reinforcement with uniform geometry distributed within complex structural elements; manage changes to the bars and models; and extract fabrication information using tags, bending details, and rebar schedules.
speakers: Ovidiu PAUNESCU, Senior Principal Product Owner, Autodesk

title: No More Blind Spots: Autodesk MCP Driving AI Across Multi-CDE Platform Projects
abstract: On a live transport megaproject, a major infrastructure contractor recovered 37 days of lost labor and $137,000 in the first week—anchored by Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). Most major projects don't run on a single common data environment (CDE). Autodesk Forma sits at the center, but teams still operate across ProjectWise, Aconex, Microsoft SharePoint, and others. That's where coordination breaks down and no one sees the risk coming. This panel will bring together Autodesk, UTS, and Utopia Digital—co-investigators on Australia’s Economic Accelerator research program. Together we're building SyncSight: an AI governance layer that uses Autodesk's Model Context Protocol (MCP) to extend the Autodesk Forma intelligence across every CDE on a project—detecting coordination failures before they become delays.
speakers: Aaron Traylen, Utopia Digital / University of Technology Sydney

title: One Platform, Global Ambitions: Bridging the Gap Between CDE Vision and Reality
abstract: Common data environments (CDEs) promise a single platform to manage construction workflows—but how do they perform on real international projects? At Bouygues Construction, we deployed Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) from tender to construction across multiple autonomous projects. This session will share what worked, what didn’t, and why. Learn how field teams actually used the platform, where gaps required complementary tools (for example, progress tracking and document control), and why centralized governance models fell short. Discover how a shift toward an enablement-driven approach improved adoption, and gain a practical framework to assess CDE platforms, design realistic governance, and support digital adoption in decentralized environments.
speakers: Maxence BOUTIN, Project manager - Collaborative Platform, Bouygues Construction IT
Aurélien DESCHAMPS, Head of BIM / Interior Design / XR, Bouygues Batiment International

title: One Standard, Many Offices: Managing Electrical Revit at Scale
abstract: Managing electrical BIM standards across multiple offices can be one of the most challenging aspects of scaling Revit workflows. Differences in regional practices, project types, and team experience often lead to inconsistencies, inefficiencies, and rework. This class will explore a proven framework for developing, implementing, and maintaining electrical Revit standards across geographically distributed teams. You’ll learn how to balance standardization with flexibility, how to structure shared parameters and templates, and how to create governance models that drive consistency without slowing production.
speakers: Matt McCarthy, East Coast Regional BIM Manager, Syska Henessy Group

title: openBIM and Interoperability Workflows at Autodesk: 2026 Edition
abstract: Workflows based in openBIM enable interoperability and collaboration among different software applications and stakeholders in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry using neutral, industry-standard formats. These workflows center around Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), an open and neutral data format for BIM. In a continuing series, you'll learn about the Autodesk strategy around IFC and openBIM, the newest and future capabilities of Revit, and other AEC products supporting openBIM workflows. And you’ll learn how these standards are being used in defining the AEC Data Model API and granular cloud data workflows. As a bonus, we'll also offer some insights for Revit users to optimize their IFC usage.
speakers: Angel Velez, Distinguished Engineer, Autodesk
Lejla Secerbegovic, Group Product Manager, Product Data, Autodesk
Janina Sánchez, Senior Product Manager - Revit Data Workflows, Autodesk

title: Orchestrating Industrialized Construction with AI Agents: Connecting Product and Project Workflows
abstract: Industrialized construction requires coordination across design and manufacturing workflows, but today these processes remain fragmented. This session will explore how AI agents can help connect product and project workflows, enabling earlier decision making and improved constructability. You’ll see how validation and specification workflows can be applied today within Autodesk tools, along with a phased view toward configuration, productization, and continuous improvement. A real workflow example will demonstrate how teams can move from disconnected automation to coordinated execution.
speakers: Andy Akenson, Distinguished Architect, Autodesk

title: Overcoming the Seven Deadly Sins of Civil 3D Project Performance
abstract: All you did was click “Open.” Now your fans are spinning at Mach 3D, and if your laptop were slightly more aerodynamic, it would likely defenestrate itself. Your Civil 3D project didn't slow down on its own. It was sinned against. None of it felt wrong at the time. Seven structural decisions are buried in your data management, file setup, and modeling workflows that Civil 3D punishes quietly and without warning until your 13-minute regen hits 42 minutes and sincity.dwg is due tomorrow. Donnie Gladfelter, Autodesk Expert Elite and AU Top Speaker, names the sins, earns each one its absolution—and sends you home with a project built the way Civil 3D actually wants to work. From first alignment to final handoff. Your laptop will thank you.
speakers: Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek

title: Overcoming the Seven Deadly Sins of Civil 3D Project Performance
abstract: All you did was click “Open.” Now your fans are spinning at Mach 3D, and if your laptop were slightly more aerodynamic, it would likely defenestrate itself. From first alignment to final handoff. Your laptop will thank you.
speakers: Donnie Gladfelter, Design Technologist, The CAD Geek

title: PM Break
abstract: Recharge, refuel, and reconnect during our afternoon break. Enjoy light refreshments designed to give you an energy boost, spark fresh conversations, and help you return to the next session ready to dive back in.

title: Powering Paperless Contractor Submissions and Tracking Across 50 Million Square Feet with Autodesk Forma and Data Analytics
abstract: Disconnected contractor submissions and manual tracking reduce visibility, slow approvals, and limit scalability. In this session, you’ll learn how a paperless submission framework was deployed across a 50-million-square-foot portfolio using Autodesk Forma. Integrated workflows were established using Submittals, RFIs, and Forms to standardize contractor interactions, enable consistent data capture, and ensure full traceability. Through APIs, disparate data sources were unified and transformed into intelligent data models that power advanced dashboards. Discover how this approach delivers real-time submission tracking, improved transparency, and faster data-driven decisions—providing a scalable blueprint for digital transformation at an enterprise level.
speakers: Ritesh Mittal, General Manager, DLF Limited
Japneesh Singh, Deputy Manager, DLF

title: Prefab Promised a Lot. Here's Why It Underdelivered.
abstract: Prefabrication promises better quality, safer jobsites, reduced costs, and compressed schedules. But those gains only materialize when what you build in the shop connects precisely to what happens in the field. For many firms, accurate field layout is the hidden bottleneck between prefab strategy and prefab results, no matter what you build. In this session, hear from two firms that used automated layout to fully realize their prefab strategies across very different sectors. One brings experience from hyperscale data center construction, where prefab modules must meet tight tolerances across massive floorplates. The other operates in high-volume residential construction, where speed, repeatability, and cost drive everything—and where a misstep in framing snowballs into delays for every trade that follows. What unites them is how automated layout changed the relationship between the shop and the site. What they've learned will challenge how you think about your own prefab potential.
speakers: Josh Lewis, Chief Operations Officer, FrameTec
Kaushal Diwan, WND Ventures Leader, DPR Innovation and R&D Sponsor, WND Ventures by DPR Construction
Scott Nyborg, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Dusty Robotics

title: Preparing LAX for the 2028 Olympics: AI-Powered Digital Twins with Autodesk Tandem MCP
abstract: With the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) is modernizing to handle millions of visitors. Managing billions in capital assets across disconnected BIM, CMMS, and GIS systems is no longer viable. In this session, Mingxun Zou, James Awe and Michael Beale will reveal how Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) built an AI-powered digital twin platform. We'll demonstrate the following: An Autodesk Tandem MCP server enabling natural language queries, a Python/Grasshopper automation extracting asset attributes to GeoJSON, and a real-time MapLibre visualization. Building on an Esri Dev Summit 2026 presentation, we'll show the evolution from manual CAD exports to AI-driven facility intelligence. Through live coding, you'll build the same integrations—preparing LAX for its Olympic moment.
speakers: Mingxun Zou, BIM Administrator, Los Angeles World Airports
James Awe, Sr Distinguished Architect, Head of Tandem Connect, Autodesk
Michael Beale, SWE, AWS

title: Prompting for Fusion: AI basics for Autodesk Assistant in Fusion
abstract: Learn how to use effective prompting techniques to accelerate script execution and add-in creation in Autodesk Fusion. This introductory session will cover prompt engineering fundamentals, practical workflows for generating and refining code with AI, and best practices for working with Fusion APIs and automation tools.
speakers: Sualp Ozel, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk
Luke Mihelcic, Senior Manager,  Product & Technical Marketing - Design, Autodesk

title: RACING AHEAD WITH DATA: Delivering a F1 Circuit with Autodesk Forma
abstract: This session demonstrates an advanced workflow for linear infrastructure using Autodesk Forma, Dynamo, and Power BI, focusing on automation, interoperability, and data-driven decision-making. Participants will learn how to use a civil alignment as a parametric driver to automate asset placement through Dynamo, leveraging coordinate logic (X,Y) and terrain adaptation. The workflow integrates generated assets into Revit with structured data and parameter control. During construction, Autodesk Build enables asset tracking and status management. Finally, Power BI dashboards provide real-time insights, KPIs, and lifecycle visibility, improving coordination, efficiency, and project outcomes.
speakers: Jesus Fuentes, BIM Manager, EIFFAGE CONSTRUCCIÓN
Irene Ruiz-Castillo, BIM Manager, ACCIONA CONSTRUCCIÓN

title: Reality Capture Now and Next: The Power of Point Clouds and Mesh Modeling
abstract: Laser scanning has become indispensable for capturing existing conditions, yet getting that data into Revit efficiently remains a challenge for many firms. This class will show a proven real-world workflow—from registering point clouds in ReCap software to structuring and linking RCS files into Revit across a cloud-connected team in Autodesk Forma. Beyond today's best practices, we'll explore how the ReCap 2026 scan-to-segmented mesh capabilities and classification features can fundamentally transform the scan-to-BIM pipeline. As meshes increasingly replace raw point clouds as the geometry reference standard, you’ll leave with both a time-tested workflow you can implement immediately and a clear-eyed view of where this technology is headed.
speakers: Olivia Morgan, BIM Specialist, SmithGroup
Mike Deacon, Product Management Engineer/Mgr, Autodesk

title: Real-Time Digital Twin with iWG/iCG and InfoWorks WS Pro and InfoWorks ICM: An Italian Water Utility Case Study
abstract: In this session, we will look at 3,300 kilometers of water supply networks serving 344,000 inhabitants, 155 district metered areas (DMAs), and more than 400 monitoring stations—with one digital twin keeping it all together. Piave Servizi used Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP) to enhance water supply operational efficiency by adopting iWG, a web platform by Idrostudi. Integrating InfoWorks WS PRO advanced modeling engine, iWG digital twin creates precise virtual replicas of water supply networks (WSNs), enabling simulations, what-if scenarios, and pressure analyses—accessible to all operators, no modeling expertise required. By providing instant, data-driven insights, the iWG digital twin empowers water utilities to cope with daily challenges. And the journey continues: the iCG digital twin with InfoWorks ICM is bringing the same power to sewerage management.
speakers: Luca Serena, Principal, Sales Specialist, Water, Autodesk
Raffaele Marciano, Engineering Head Officer, Piave Servizi S.p.A.
Davide Russo, CEO & Technical Director, Idrostudi s.r.l.

title: Reimagining Stadium Delivery Through a Digital-First Approach
abstract: Phil Dangerfield, SVP of Operations at Haslam Sports Group, joins the Digital Builder podcast to discuss the Cleveland Browns' new Huntington Bank Field and the decision to make BIM a contractual deliverable for a major sports venue project. The episode explores digital delivery, owner priorities, long-term operations, fan experience, and lessons that could influence the future of major venue development.

title: Rendering Reality: The Rise of Gaussian Splats
abstract: Join industry experts from design visualization and VFX as they explore how Gaussian Splats and solutions from Autodesk Interactive Media & Entertainment are transforming digital workflows. Learn what these techniques are, how they enable highly accurate digital twins and immersive world building, and where they fit in real-world production pipelines. Through examples and firsthand insights, speakers will share what excites them about this approach—along with the practical pros, cons, and challenges of adopting it.
speakers: Logan Foster, Product Owner, Autodesk
Aaron Dabelow, Senior Technical Lead & Producer, MAKE
Mark Kauffman, Asst. VP/Technical Lead, WSP

title: Residential by Design: Building the People, Templates, and Tools That Make Area Data Work
abstract: Residential area data seems straightforward until multiple definitions come into play. Sellable, zoning, gross, usable, net leasable, supply, and target—they each serve different stakeholders and follow different rules. This session will present KPF's approach, starting with a cross-disciplinary committee that established shared standards and templates. At its core is an expanded area framework that extends Revit capabilities through Dynamo automation and parameter-based logic to produce reliable outputs directly from the model. Custom tools and dashboards streamline presentation plans, while light and air analysis tools support local compliance. Project examples from the United States, Korea, and Singapore show how these workflows scale across markets.
speakers: Rachel (Se Won) Min, Senior BIM Specialist, Kohn Pedersen Fox (KPF)

title: Revit Cloud Worksharing Migration Has Arrived—But Linked Models Still Need a Control Plane
abstract: Many customers are struggling to migrate high volumes of existing Revit Cloud Worksharing models from BIM 360 to Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud). The process is often manual, slow, and difficult to scale. Autodesk Platform Services now offers developers a batch workflow that can automate this migration using Autodesk APIs. In this session, Zhong Wu, Autodesk developer advocate, will show what the new Autodesk Platform Services migration capability makes possible, while Moses Scott, platform architect at Woolpert, will show why linked-model scenarios still require preflight diagnostics, user-visible link-state guidance, and control-plane thinking before migration proceeds.
speakers: Moses Scott, Director of Platform Architecture & Data Insights, Woolpert
Zhong Wu, Principal Developer Advocate Engineer, Autodesk
João Martins, Principal Systems Integration Consultant, Autodesk

title: Rivian’s Digital Twin Strategy: Turning Asset Data into a Product, Not a Byproduct
abstract: Rivian is bridging the gap from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to a full-scale digital twin by treating asset data as a product—not a byproduct. In this session, we’ll show you how assets are structured in Autodesk Forma, live-linked to model elements in Autodesk Tandem using Tandem Connect, and integrated with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) systems to form a single, reliable asset backbone. We’ll break down the data standards, ID strategy, and integration patterns that connect design, construction, and operations. Using real examples unique to Rivian manufacturing plants, we’ll share lessons learned from early pilots, and we’ll describe how we manage change so teams across design, field ops, maintenance, and finance can all trust and use the same digital twin.
speakers: Derek Milz, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Rivian’s Digital Twin Strategy: Turning Asset Data into a Product, Not a Byproduct
abstract: Rivian is bridging the gap from Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) to a full-scale digital twin by treating asset data as a product—not a byproduct. speakers: Derek Milz, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk
Alex Barilov, Lead, Production Facilities VDC, Rivian Automotive LLC

title: Save Time and Improve Quality: Dynamic Factory Design with Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim Integrations
abstract: Discover how combining Factory Design Utilities, Revit, and FlexSim software transforms facility design through seamless integration of 2D layouts, 3D models, and process simulation. This case study will demonstrate significant time savings by eliminating redundant updates across platforms and enabling engineering teams to make objective, data-driven decisions with less rework. This class will present the end-to-end Factory Design Utilities workflow, showing how AutoCAD, Inventor, Revit, and FlexSim software work together to enable rapid, realistic simulations and models. Engineers from Jacobs will share real project examples demonstrating ROI, cost savings, and how simulations validate designs, communicate decisions, and extend value into production planning and continuous improvement.
speakers: Tyler Morrison, Industrial Systems Global Principal, Jacobs
Justin Freeman, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk

title: Scaling iLogic Architecture Without Chaos
abstract: Large Inventor iLogic environments often suffer from duplicated code, fragile “Call External Rule” workflows, and rules that become difficult to maintain as teams grow. This session will share a production-tested approach for building a centralized iLogic function library that behaves like native Inventor functionality. You will learn how to structure reusable VB-based subroutines, enable IntelliSense across internal and external rules, and apply versioning and governance patterns that allow automation to scale safely. You’ll see real-world examples that show how this approach reduced duplication, improved consistency, and accelerated engineer-to-order development in Inventor.
speakers: Brandon Bibelhauser, Mechanical Engineer/Software Developer, FORTNA

title: Scaling Rail Data at MRS Logística: From Fragmented Workflows to Real-Time Intelligence
abstract: In a reality of more than 200 railway infrastructure projects running simultaneously, data fragmentation is not a risk—it’s inevitable. This technical deep dive will show you how MRS Logística tackles this challenge by refining BIM requirements and building a standardized common data environment (CDE) in Autodesk Forma. From issues and daily reports to audits, model coordination, cost, and schedule, workflows are structured and connected at scale. Discover how Autodesk Assistant enables structured analysis and how the Insight Builder tool turns connected data into real-time intelligence—driving consistency, reliability, and faster decision making across projects.
speakers: Camila Kfouri, Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk
Paulo Renato, Digital Engineering Leader, MRS Logística

title: Small Business Community Meetup
abstract: Whether you’re running your own studio, building products, or designing across disciplines, this will be a space to share experiences, exchange ideas, and meet others shaping their own paths. Come connect, collaborate, and be part of a growing network of independent creatives.
speakers: Eric DeLeon, Founder & Principal Consultant, DeLeon Consulting & Coaching
Deborah Lilley, Sr Mgr, Community Strategy & Advocacy, Autodesk
Sam Karas, Program Manager - Community, Autodesk

title: Small Business Roundtable - AECO
abstract:
Hosted by Marcus O'Brien, Autodesk's VP of Product Development, AutoCAD, Infrastructure, and Reality Capture Solutions, this session will bring together fellow entrepreneurs, builders, and creators for an intimate, conversation-driven roundtable designed exclusively for small business customers. Limited to under 50 attendees, this session creates space for honest, two-way dialogue—no slides, no pitches, just real talk.

 Share what's working well in your Autodesk experience, discuss the challenges you're navigating, and tell us what you'd love to see next. Autodesk leaders will be on hand not just to answer questions, but to genuinely listen and learn from the businesses that use our products every day.
speakers: Marcus O'Brien, VP AutoCAD, Infrastructure and Reality Capture, Autodesk

title: Small Business Roundtable - Media & Entertainment
abstract:
Hosted by Nikola Todorovic, Autodesk's VP of Emerging Technology and Co-Founder of Autodesk Flow Studio, this session will bring together fellow entrepreneurs, builders, and creators for an intimate, conversation-driven roundtable designed exclusively for small business customers. Limited to under 50 attendees, this session creates space for honest, two-way dialogue—no slides, no pitches, just real talk.

 Share what's working well in your Autodesk experience, discuss the challenges you're navigating, and tell us what you'd love to see next. Autodesk leaders will be on hand not just to answer questions, but to genuinely listen and learn from the businesses that use our products every day.
speakers: Nikola Todorovic, VP, Emerging Technology, Autodesk

title: Streamlined Stormwater Design with InfoDrainage
abstract: Many stormwater design teams rely on workflows that bounce between multiple programs, require repeated file transfers, and depend on clunky spreadsheets. This approach is inefficient, prone to error, and difficult to scale across an organization. InfoDrainage, on the other hand, allows for robust stormwater design all in one place, and easily round-trips with Civil 3D software. In this class, we’ll show where Kimley-Horn teams saw meaningful efficiency gains in generating RCNs and round-tripping storm drain networks. Drawing on Kimley-Horn’s collaboration with Autodesk, we’ll discuss how real-world needs shaped InfoDrainage to benefit both project teams and the industry more broadly. Mike Pizzino, InfoDrainage expert at Autodesk, will co-present.
speakers: John Neff, Civil Engineer, Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc
Mike Pizzino, Technical Account Specialist, Autodesk

title: Structural Engineering at the Core: Integrated Digital Delivery at Foster + Partners
abstract: By showcasing several case studies, we’ll explore how the in-house structural engineering team at Foster + Partners successfully delivers high-complexity, global projects through an integrated design approach. We’ll highlight how deep engineering expertise is combined with advanced digital workflows and close multi-disciplinary collaboration through Autodesk products, enabling efficient, innovative, and architecturally expressive outcomes. Central to this success is the team’s ability to ensure that design-informed decisions are data-driven, coordinated, and efficiently communicated across all project stakeholders.
speakers: Andrea Colombo, BIM & Design Systems Coordinator, Foster + Partners
Ash Rahman, Structural BIM Lead/Manager, Foster + Partners

title: Stuck? Unlock Solutions with Autodesk Expert Elites.
abstract: Got a challenge you just can’t crack? Bring it with you! In this interactive “Ask an Expert” session, you’ll engage in group conversations led by Autodesk Expert Elites to troubleshoot real-world issues together with your peers. Whether you’re dealing with a stubborn assembly, broken references, animation problems, or unclear workflows, this is your chance to get unstuck. There’s no formal presentation—just collaborative problem-solving, shared insights, and practical guidance tailored to the questions in the room. Come with your toughest issues, learn from others, and leave with actionable solutions.
speakers: Deepak Maini, Principal Business Consultant, Autodesk
Gil Cordle, Digital Design Manager / Autodesk SME, LJA, Inc.
Todd Rogers, Civil Administration, Walter P Moore
Kristina Youngblut, BIM Manager, CIMA+
Cary Mandell, Principal Customer Advocate, Autodesk

title: The Adoption Flywheel: Lessons from the Bain and Co. Deployment of Autodesk Forma at a Leading Indian Developer
abstract: Most digital transformation efforts share one struggle: The platform is live, but users stick to legacy systems. Working with a leading Indian real estate developer, Bain embedded Autodesk Forma as the operating backbone for its preconstruction workflows. The adoption flywheel included the following: Bain focused on strategy before deployment, co-creating more than 40 workflows and 150 decision rights. Then role-specific dashboards were customized for individuals and management. Following that, the focus shifted to change management, considering management mandates, weekly leaderboards (project and user), and focused communication. Contextualized knowledge materials and hands-on training (in-house and external) completed the picture. This session is designed for executives and implementation agencies who want a replicable approach to closing the deployment-adoption gap.
speakers: Shubika Sardana, Associate Partner, Bain and Company
Shradha Vaid, Partner, Bain & Company
Yashaswi Sharma, Management Consultant, Bain and Company

title: The Future of Product Design with Inventor Professional
abstract: Join this session as Dan Szymanski shares the development roadmap and product strategy for Inventor Professional software. Dan will cover recent and planned functionality that will add value to everyday workflow needs. We encourage you to engage the Inventor product team members with questions and feedback during and after the session.
speakers: Dan Szymanski, Principal Product Manager, Autodesk

title: The Preconstruction Meetup: Ideas, Insights, and What’s Working
abstract: Preconstruction is evolving fast—and the way teams bid, qualify, and estimate work is changing with it. This meetup will bring together preconstruction professionals to connect with peers, exchange real-world strategies, and explore how leading teams are using data to make smarter, faster decisions. From improving bid accuracy to strengthening go/no-go decisions, join the conversation to hear what’s working, what’s not, and where the industry is headed. Whether you’re refining your current approach or looking for fresh ideas, this session is your chance to learn from others facing the same challenges—and winning.
speakers: Kellie Herring, Customer Success Manager, ACS, Autodesk
Aaron Jech, Technical Success Manager, Preconstruction (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk
Samira Tily, Sr. Product Marketing Manager, PreCon Products, Autodesk

title: The Re‑Emergence of the CPU for Your Workloads: From Traditional CAD/BIM to Agentic AI
abstract: This session will answer a simple question for AU attendees: “In a world obsessed with GPUs, where should I actually spend my money across CPU, GPU, and NPU for my design, make, and emerging AI workloads?” For years, workstation buying has been “GPU‑first.” Agentic AI and modern Autodesk workflows are pushing CPU back to center stage as the orchestrator for both traditional and AI workloads. Traditional workloads (Revit model updates, AutoCAD drafting, Autodesk Fusion modeling, simulation, office, and collaboration) are still heavily CPU‑bound. Piling on GPU does not fix a starved CPU. Agentic AI and AI assistants add a new control layer that is CPU‑intensive orchestration: planning, tool calls, APS integration, retrieval, evaluation, and logging. The right answer is a balanced portfolio of CPU, GPU, and NPU—mapped to how AU customers actually work, not just to spec sheets.
speakers: Jamie Gwilliam, WW User & Industries Lead, Workstations, Intel

title: The Scan-to-Build Playbook: The Walsh Group’s Success with Autodesk Reality Capture
abstract: Join us for an insightful session on how The Walsh Group is transforming construction processes using Autodesk Forma and ReCap Pro reality capture. This session will explore the full journey from initial scanning to the final build phase, showcasing how advanced capture technologies improve accuracy, efficiency, and collaboration. Speakers will demonstrate real-world applications of reality capture within a connected platform, highlighting benefits like enhanced visualization, streamlined workflows, and reduced rework. You’ll gain practical information about integrating capture data into Forma to support better decision making and project delivery.
speakers: Emmanuel Graves, Technical Specialist, Construction, Autodesk
Rhett Rutherford, Construction Technology Manager, The Walsh Group

title: The Superb Guide to Easy Revit Rides On!
abstract: The award-winning Superb Team continues with enhanced insights into the ever-expanding world of Revit software and its friends. Our lively conversation spiced with weird, wild, witty, and wonderful war stories will energize you with the latest and greatest developments in Revit 2027 and Autodesk Forma industry cloud. Discover wild and wonderful things to do with Revit using native tools or third-party software for reality capture, visualization, and AR/XR. Use interoperability with add-ins and other authoring and visualization software. Get a glimpse of the future with innovative use cases using AI. Discover more ways and means to enhance productivity. Join us for wise and fun pointers on how to be a fearlessly productive Revit Warrior.
speakers: Rina Sahay, BIM Lead, Wade Trim
Nauman Mysorewala, Design and Engineering Technology Manager, GFT Infrastructure

title: Trust Enthusiasts Unite
abstract: Join us for a meetup focused on cybersecurity, privacy, risk management, and responsible AI. Open to all experience levels, from students to professionals, this event will bring together a diverse community, including Autodesk Trust Org members. Connect with peers, share knowledge, and explore current trends and challenges shaping the digital landscape. Whether you’re new or experienced, you’ll gain practical insights, exchange ideas, and build meaningful connections. Join us for an evening of discussion, learning, and networking while contributing to a more secure and responsible digital world.
speakers: Sebastian Goodwin, SVP, Chief Trust Officer, Autodesk
Mary Wing, Dir., Chief of Staff Trust, Autodesk

title: Turning BIM into AI-Powered Digital Twins: Real-Time Predictive Maintenance with IoT
abstract: Intelligent models are often underused after design, remaining static and disconnected from real-world operations. This session will present a real-world deployment in a metropolitan rail system, where BIM is transformed into a live, AI-powered predictive maintenance platform. Using IFC-based workflows derived from Revit software, models are converted into lightweight, web-ready formats and integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data at the asset level. An AI layer enables anomaly detection and failure prediction, reducing unplanned downtime and improving maintenance efficiency. You will gain a practical understanding of how to extend BIM into an operational digital twin and implement scalable, data-driven maintenance strategies.
speakers: Beril Oytun Çetinkaya, Architect, Metro İstanbul
Tolga Bozkurt, AI Digital Twin & IoT Specialist, Metro Istanbul

title: Turning Curtain Walls into Configurable Products with Revit, Dynamo, and Informed Design
abstract: Coordinating Revit curtain wall layouts with configurable manufactured panel units is often manual, slow, and difficult to validate at scale. In this hands-on lab, you will use custom Dynamo nodes backed by the Informed Design API to connect a Revit curtain wall layout to a configurable unitized panel. Starting from a prepared model and scaffolded graph, participants will extract panel dimensions, send geometric data to the Informed Design API, and generate a complete manufacturing data set with shop drawings and parts lists. We’ll generate a report highlighting supported, unsupported, and changed panel conditions in Revit. And we’ll unpack the API concepts behind the nodes so you can adapt the workflow to your own products.
speakers: Daniel Noviello, Customer Adoption Specialist, Autodesk

title: Turning Site Design into Quantifiable Flood Resilience with InfoDrainage and Civil 3D
abstract: Early‑stage flood resilience design relies on simplified assumptions, limiting understanding of how site-design decisions influence flood performance. This session will present an InfoDrainage‑led workflow to quantify flood resilience at site scale through coordinated parametric design and hydraulic modeling. The session will show how InfoDrainage, Autodesk Civil 3D, Subassembly Composer, and Dynamo software are used together to drive parametric site design and generate inputs for 1D‑2D flood simulation. Rule‑based design logic enables rapid, repeatable generation of site grading and flood mitigation solutions using Dynamo Player. The resulting BIM‑ready terrain and surface models support scenario testing across exceedance and climate change scenarios.
speakers: Juan Aguirrebengoa, Principal Civil Engineer CEng MICE, Mott MacDonald

title: Ultimate Convergence Throwdown: Revit Versus Civil 3D Project Alignment with Model Coordination
abstract: There are multiple workflows that result in Revit and Civil 3D projects aligning correctly in the Autodesk Forma Model Coordination tool—but which is best? This session will end the ambiguity around best practices for spatially aligning Civil 3D site information with Revit. We'll cover what’s changed in Revit in recent releases that makes site coordination easier. For anyone who’s encountered surprise units, survey feet translation problems, or Revit footprints in far-off coordinates, this session will clear up the confusion. You'll find out if the Shared Reference Point tool is needed and when to Acquire Coordinates.
speakers: Louisa Holland, Principal Business Consultant- Infrastructure, Autodesk
Misha Shanley, Principal Technical Support Specialist, Autodesk

title: Unlocking Autodesk Assistant: Secrets of World-Class Data Management with Vault, Common Data, and PLM
abstract: World-class implementations don’t happen by accident—they’re built on deep knowledge of how to make Autodesk tools work together intelligently. In this no-fluff session, Allen Gager will reveal the secrets every expert knows for maximizing Autodesk Assistant across the Autodesk platform while building a robust common data environment (CDE) powered by Vault and Vault PLM software. Discover how to use Autodesk Assistant (now integrated in Vault 2027, Autodesk Fusion, AutoCAD, Autodesk Forma, and beyond) as your always-on, context-aware AI partner. Learn natural language techniques to find files faster, automate routine tasks, get in-context guidance, query project data, and even drive simple automations—without ever leaving your workflow.
speakers: Tyson Copa, Platform Specialist, IMAGINiT Technologies
Allen Gager, Applications Expert - MSD, Rand

title: Unlocking Enterprise Content: Real-World Content Catalog Strategies That Work
abstract: As organizations scale, managing digital content becomes increasingly complex. Fragmented assets, inconsistent metadata, and inefficient search workflows slow teams down and limit reuse. This session—co-presented with the Content Catalog product manager—will introduce the software’s latest capabilities, which are designed to bring structure, discoverability, and intelligence to content at scale. You’ll learn how new features enable better organization, faster search, and improved collaboration. Through a real-world implementation, slantis will show how Content Catalog is applied, from initial setup and governance decisions to daily workflows and measurable outcomes. We’ll also share lessons learned and strategies for driving adoption.
speakers: Paula Rama, BIM Consultant, slantis
Mahzad Fasih, Senior Product Manager, Autodesk

title: Unlocking GIS Data for Early-Stage Planning with Esri ArcGIS and Forma Site Design
abstract: Discover how to enhance your early-stage planning workflows by unlocking GIS data from Esri within Autodesk Forma Site Design. See how the ArcGIS for Autodesk Forma extension brings real-world spatial context directly into your projects, helping you assess site conditions, streamline workflows, and make more accurate decisions from day one.

title: Unlocking the Power of Reality Capture: The Leica CloudWorx Seamless Integration with Autodesk Software
abstract: Reality capture has been in the industry since the late 1990s, evolving from its tripod-based roots to encompass many different forms of modern data capture. One could easily make an argument that reality capture has also grown from a handful of sensors to a wide variety of processes today. Regardless of where the data comes from, there has been one consistent and constant challenge that professionals still face: what to do with the volumes of data reality capture creates and how to make meaningful deliverables. This session will provide insight on how Leica CloudWorx continues to provide powerful tools for converting massive point cloud data into meaningful 3D models, 2D CAD drawings, and topographic deliverables. Furthermore, many tools in Leica CloudWorx serve as enhancements to the standard CAD tools that are in the Autodesk suite of software packages.
speakers: Michael Harvey, Sr. Product Manager – Reality Capture, Leica Geosystems

title: Unlock Smarter Construction: AI Workflows in Autodesk Forma
abstract: AI is transforming how work gets done across the industry. In this hands-on lab, you’ll discover how Autodesk Forma Build enables AI-powered, intelligent data and integrated workflows to power transformation in construction outcomes. You’ll explore practical use cases on Construction Intelligence and AI Automated Workflows. Learn how AI in action can streamline coordination, reduce manual effort, and support more-connected, informed decision making across the project lifecycle.
speakers: Snow - Snezhina Shukina, Principal Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk
Sarah O' Sullivan, Senior Customer Success Manager, Construction, Autodesk

title: Using Autodesk Forma Build and Autodesk Forma Assets for Heritage Rehabilitation
abstract: The Centre Block Rehabilitation is the restoration and renovation of Canada's seat of Parliament, including the removal, repair, and reconditioning of the building’s heritage assets. Using point cloud data, Autodesk Forma Build, Revit, and Dynamo software, the construction manager's virtual design and construction (VDC) team modeled every heritage asset requiring tracking and repair. Through Forma Build, the heritage team efficiently tracks and manages stonework for approximately 1,000,000 assets. This approach reduced costs by 40% while meeting schedule requirements. Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud) centralizes issue tracking, scope changes, shop drawings, and asset management, streamlining the entire process using connected data and integrated workflows.
speakers: Andrew Macdonald, Senior VDC Manager, EllisDon
Arturo Baselli Gutierrez, VDC Manager, EllisDon

title: Vault on Autopilot: AI-Driven PDM Automation Across Lifecycle, Revisions, and ERP
abstract: Vault Professional software manages thousands of engineering workflows—but property assignment, lifecycle transitions, revision management, approval routing, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) synchronization remain manual. Every operation is predictable and rule-governed. This session will deliver AU 2026's Intelligent Data theme in practice: an AI agent connected to the Vault API monitoring product data management (PDM) events and executing the right action autonomously via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent loop. The large language model (LLM) interprets PDM state against business rules, and the API executes without manual intervention. In controlled workflows, this has reduced administrative overhead by up to 70%. You’ll leave with an ROI-prioritized implementation road map.
speakers: Jose Baquero, Senior Consultant MGF - AI Solutions, Avant Leap
Enrique Galicia Tovar, Director of Innovations and AI, AvantLeap

title: Visualization as Design Practice: How CannonDesign Is Thoughtfully Incorporating AI to Rethink Design Workflows
abstract: The relationship between design and visualization is undergoing a fundamental shift. For years, the rendering pipeline demanded a separate skill set—one that pulled architects away from design and toward modeling, tracing, and asset hunting. By integrating AI-enabled functionalities across workflows, CannonDesign stopped treating visualization as a downstream step and rebuilt it as part of the design process. This session will explore how real-time rendering and AI-enabled workflows are collapsing the distance between design intent and finished imagery, eliminating the 3D model-to-visualization handoff, and allowing architects to work directly on content rather than a representation of it. It's a new approach to design where clients engage with designs early, deliverables are experiences rather than static files, and architects invest more time developing strong design concepts. To illustrate the modern workflows outlined, the session will conclude with a D5 demo by Jeff Espinoza.
speakers: Andrew Petty, Director - Design Technology, CannonDesign
Jeff Espinoza, Director of Customer Success and Services, D5

title: What Airport Restrooms taught us about Smarter Asset Data.
abstract: At Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, restroom operations presented a familiar challenge: plenty of activity, plenty of data, but not enough trusted visibility into what was happening across the spaces, assets, supplies, and vendor work.  Not a new problem. An invisible one. This session will break down how Sea-Tac cut through the “smart restroom” hype by fixing the foundation first—structured asset and space data. Space IDs and Asset IDs were defined in Revit, carried through Build Assets, verified in the field, and connected through Autodesk Tandem and IBM Maximo. That’s when everything changed. Restrooms became measurable. Vendor work became verifiable. Operations became controllable. Because smart doesn’t start with sensors. It starts with data you can trust.
speakers: Liliana Martinez, Senior Manager, Design Technology, Port of Seattle
Mark Mergenschroer, Technical Success Manager (NAMER Adoption), Autodesk

title: What Structural Engineering Taught Two Start-Up Founders About Building Software
abstract: Architects and engineers are often asked to adopt tools that fundamentally change how they work, without having had a voice in how those tools were designed. That disconnect can turn new technology into another process teams have to work around. Before founding Pirros, Peter Johann and Ari Baranian worked as structural engineers and experienced that disconnect firsthand. Using the development of a new QA/QC product as a case study, they will describe how their engineering experience helped them identify problems with traditional QA/QC processes, and how they partnered directly with Pirros clients to design, test, and refine the new product. Attendees will learn how architecture and engineering firms can provide feedback that shapes product decisions and how software teams can involve clients more effectively throughout development. Both sides will leave with practical ways to build stronger working relationships, and create tools that better reflect real project workflows.
speakers: Ari Baranian, CEO and Co-Founder at Pirros, Pirros
Peter Johann, Co-Founder & COO at Pirros, Pirros

title: Why GIS Is Essential to Design, Construction, and Operations in AEC
abstract: Michael Davidson, Senior Product Manager at Esri, joins the Digital Builder podcast to explore how geographic information systems (GIS) are reshaping the built environment. The conversation examines how location intelligence connects design, construction, and operations workflows, why GIS is becoming foundational for digital twins, and how emerging technologies including AI and open standards are changing the way organizations make decisions about the assets they build and manage.

title: Winning the Enterprise: How Brown and Caldwell Replaced ProjectWise with Autodesk Forma and Egnyte
abstract: Discover how Brown and Caldwell (BC) transformed its design delivery by moving away from the rigid constraints of Bentley ProjectWise. In this real-world case study, BC will share how the firm unified its design and business ecosystems using Egnyte and Autodesk Forma, keeping systems natively in sync without friction. We’ll explore how BC achieved true platform freedom, allowing every user type to work exactly where they’re most comfortable, while ensuring central governance and auditability. Whether an engineer is modeling in Autodesk Forma or a project partner is collaborating directly in Egnyte, files stay completely mirror-matched across all formats—from DGN and DWG™ to XLSX—with absolutely no compromises. Designed for BIM/VDC and IT leaders, this session will provide the real-world reference architecture and checklist that BC used to maximize engineering speed and data integrity.
speakers: Nick Decker, Director of Engineering Segment, AEC, Egnyte
Jeremiah Dunn, National Specialty Leader - BIM/VDC, Brown and Caldwell
Michael Rybacki, Project Owner, Brown and Caldwell

title: “Works on My Machine” Isn’t a Strategy: Controlling AutoCAD Xrefs, Standards, and Sheet Set Manager in Forma Data Management
abstract: Managing AutoCAD projects in shared environments often leads to broken references, inconsistent templates, and file conflicts. This session will focus on workflows using AutoCAD and Autodesk Forma Data Management (formerly Autodesk Docs) to bring control and consistency to multi-user projects. You’ll learn how to structure projects, manage permissions, maintain reference integrity using Connected References, and manage multi-user editing using checkout workflows. This session will also demonstrate how to deploy project-aware standards using Connected Support Files, coordinate deliverables using the new Connected Sheet Set Manager, and apply repeatable workflows to improve consistency and reduce errors across teams.
speakers: Satheesh Kumar, Technical Sales Specialist, Autodesk
Dhananjai Gopika, Manager, Technical Support, Autodesk

title: Your Bottlenecks Are Showing: 10 Lessons from Thousands of Product Design and Development Companies
abstract: Designing great products is difficult. Successfully taking those products to market on time and under budget is even harder. After working with thousands of product design and engineering businesses, clear patterns have emerged between teams that struggle and those that consistently deliver. In this fast-paced 30-minute session, we’ll break down 10 key lessons that separate successful teams from the rest. We’ll dive into what worked for them as well as what didn’t. You’ll leave with practical strategies to reduce delays, improve alignment, and move from concept to production with greater speed and increased confidence. If you’re a business owner or business leader who wants to fast-track your company’s success, this session is for you.
speakers: Jason Lichtman, Principal Technical Specialist,  Fusion, Autodesk

title: Community watching party: Day 1 Keynote in German
abstract:
Hallo zusammen!
<

Im Namen der deutschsprachigen Community laden wir euch herzlich ein, gemeinsam mit der Community die Autodesk University General Session anzusehen – mit Live-Kommentaren auf Deutsch.

Gemeinsam mit mehreren Mitgliedern des Autodesk Expert Elite-Programms sowie dem Community Manager der deutschsprachigen Autodesk Community, Dmytro Mukhin, treffen wir uns in einem Zoom-Raum, um die Session gemeinsam zu verfolgen und uns live im Chat auszutauschen.

Wir freuen uns auf euch!

title: Community watching party: Day 2 Keynote in Ukrainian
abstract:
Привіт всім!
Від імені україномовної спільноти запрошуємо вас приєднатися до перегляду "Industry Keynote" в рамках  Autodesk University 2026 разом із спільнотою та з коментарями українською мовою.
Разом із кількома учасниками програми Expert Elite, а саме – Юрієм Подольчуком, Олександром Канівцем, Олексієм Соколовським, Анастасією Фещенко, Антоном Васильєвим, Олександром Черніковим, Андрієм Гуменюком та менеджером україномовної спільноти Autodesk, Дмитром Мухіним, приєднуйтесь до Zoom-кімнати, де ми разом подивимось цю сесію та поспілкуємося в чаті наживо.
До зустрічі!
speakers: Anton Vasyliev, senior researcher, NTU «KhPI»
Oleksandr Kanivets, ASKansulting

title: Discover our Media and Entertainment Community - Creators
abstract: Want to connect with other creators, get inspired, and learn how to become more involved in the Autodesk community? Join our session to discover community initiatives, programs, and opportunities to participate, collaborate, and grow. Hosted by Joaquim Moral, Senior Community Manager at Autodesk for EMEA, LATAM, and M&E.
speakers: Felipe Fierro, Film Director - Autodesk Expert Elite, Pigmalion Animation Studio

title: Discover our Spanish and Portuguese Community & Groups (Sesión en Español con soporte en Portugués)
abstract: Want to connect with other creators, get inspired, and learn how to become more involved in the Autodesk community? Join this session, hosted in Spanish by Joaquim Moral, Senior Community Manager at Autodesk for EMEA, LATAM, and M&E. Portuguese support will also be available during the session.
